Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.T:: Stores rules for a particular object in a background region.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Name: Editor-facing label for this object type. Only the object's `ToString` returns it, so it appears in the background editor's object list and nowhere in the rendered background.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Count: Number of instances of this object placed per background region. A value is rolled from the range for each region tile, so the density scales with how many regions the camera view spans. Region size is set by the style's [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#RegionSize|RegionSize]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.TextureFiles: Sprite images for this object. All entries across every style are packed into the shared background atlas, and each placed instance picks one entry at random. Files that don't tile cleanly are canvas-padded up to the atlas mip alignment.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Size: Base on-screen dimensions of the sprite before [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#Scale|Scale]] is applied. A vector is rolled per instance, so a range gives a spread of widths and heights.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Scale: Per-instance multiplier applied to [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#Size|Size]]. Both the maximum Size and maximum Scale feed the object's culling radius, so overly large ranges widen the region padding needed to avoid pop-in.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Z: Parallax depth of each instance, rolled per instance. `0` sits at the near plane and higher values recede toward the far plane, moving more slowly as the camera pans. The minimum of the range also scales the object's culling radius against the style's near and far plane distances.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.Rot: Range of starting orientations. Each instance is given a random direction within the arc when spawned.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.RotSpeed: Continuous spin applied to each instance, rolled per instance. The shader animates the quad's rotation over time from this value.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.ColorHue: Hue in degrees (0 to 360, wrapped) for the per-instance random tint. Combined with [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorSat|ColorSat]], [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorVal|ColorVal]] and [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorAlpha|ColorAlpha]] into an HSVA color multiplied onto the sprite.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.ColorSat: Saturation (0 to 1) of the per-instance random tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorHue|ColorHue]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.ColorVal: Value or brightness (0 to 1) of the per-instance random tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorHue|ColorHue]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.ColorAlpha: Opacity (0 to 1) of the per-instance random tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#ColorHue|ColorHue]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.TwinkleInterval: Period of the twinkle animation, rolled per instance. Each instance also gets a random phase offset within its own interval so they don't pulse in unison. Paired with [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#TwinkleAddColor|TwinkleAddColor]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.TwinkleAddColor: Color added to the sprite at the peak of each twinkle cycle, rolled per instance. Zero disables the effect. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#TwinkleInterval|TwinkleInterval]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.PerlinProbability: Perlin noise field that biases where instances are placed. When set, candidate positions are rejected unless a random draw falls under the noise value at that point, clustering objects in high-noise areas. When absent, positions are uniformly random within the region.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRu.PerlinRandExponent: Shapes the random draw used against [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#PerlinProbability|PerlinProbability]]. The unit random is raised to this power before being remapped to -1..1, so values above `1` push placement toward the strongest parts of the noise field. Has no effect without a PerlinProbability.

Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.T:: Stores rules for the procedural game backgrounds.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.Styles: Every background style the game knows about. Styles flagged [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#InGameBackground|InGameBackground]] become selectable in-game, and those also flagged [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#IsDefault|IsDefault]] form the default rotation. All of their object sprites are packed together into one shared atlas at load.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.AtlasTextureParams: Post-processing and sampling parameters for the shared background sprite atlas built from every style's object textures. Controls mip levels and sample mode of the packed texture.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.ShroudMaterial: Material used to draw the shroud pass that darkens space outside the ship's line of sight. It samples the captured background so fogged regions still show a dimmed starfield, and the minimap reuses it for the same effect.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.SightMaskScale: Resolution multiplier for the sight-mask render target relative to the screen. Below `1` renders the fog-of-war mask at reduced resolution for softer, cheaper edges.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.SightMaskEdgeSize: Thickness of the feathered edge drawn around sight circles, in world units before camera scaling. Sets the outer sight-circle line thickness and the same value drives the minimap's sight edge.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules.StaticBackgroundTextureSize: Pixel dimensions of the texture generated from a style's [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#StaticBackgroundTexture|StaticBackgroundTexture]] generator. Styles without a static texture ignore this.

Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.T:: Stores rules for a particular style of procedural background.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.ID: Identifier used to look this style up. A [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundRules#BackgroundStyle|MenuBackgroundRules.BackgroundStyle]] reference and every saved background key resolve back to the style through this ID.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.NameKey: Localization key for the style's display name. The in-game "set background" menu uses it as the label text for this style's entry.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.InGameBackground: Marks the style as one players can select while playing. Only styles with this set appear in the in-game background list. Others are reserved for menus or specific scenes.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.IsDefault: Marks an in-game style as part of the default rotation. Only applies to styles that also set [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#InGameBackground|InGameBackground]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.BaseColor: Solid color the framebuffer is cleared to behind the background objects. When unset, no clear color is applied and whatever the scene already holds shows through.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.StaticBackgroundTexture: Generates a large tiling texture drawn behind the parallax objects, sized by [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundRules#StaticBackgroundTextureSize|StaticBackgroundTextureSize]] and seeded per background. It is placed at a random rotation and scrolls with the deepest parallax layer. Omit for a plain background.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.GlobalAmbientLight: Scene-wide ambient light color uploaded to the lighting shader each frame. Adds a flat light contribution to every part regardless of light sources.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.GlobalDiffuseLight: Scene-wide diffuse light color uploaded to the lighting shader, applied to surfaces facing the global light direction.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.GlobalMinDiffuseLight: Lower bound for the global diffuse term uploaded to the lighting shader, so surfaces facing away from the light are never fully dark.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.GlobalSpecularLight: Scene-wide specular highlight color uploaded to the lighting shader for the global light.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.RegionSize: World-space size of each background region tile. Objects are placed and cached per tile, so larger regions spread the same [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#Count|Count]] over more area.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.NearPlaneDistance: Camera distance of the nearest parallax plane. Together with [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#FarPlaneDistance|FarPlaneDistance]] it sets how strongly object depth ([[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules#Z|Z]]) translates into parallax motion.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.FarPlaneDistance: Camera distance of the farthest parallax plane. The ratio of far to near distance determines the parallax spread across the depth range. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules#NearPlaneDistance|NearPlaneDistance]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.Material: Material the object quads are drawn with. Its texture is replaced at load with the packed background atlas, so a mod supplies the shader and blend state here rather than the sprite image.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRul.Objects: The object types populating this style. Each is placed, tinted and animated independently. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundObjectRules|BackgroundObjectRules]].

Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules.T:: Stores rules for rendering a grid to the camera.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules.LineColor: Color of the grid lines and crosses. As the camera zooms and the grid changes resolution the game cross-fades two levels by scaling this color's alpha, so it also serves both the lines and crosses grid styles.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules.DesiredLinesAcross: Target number of grid divisions across the view. The spacing is chosen so roughly this many lines fit the larger of the view's width and height, then quantized to a power of [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules#ResolutionIncrementFactor|ResolutionIncrementFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules.ResolutionIncrementFactor: Factor by which grid spacing snaps between zoom levels. Spacing steps in multiples of this factor and the two nearest levels are blended, so a value of 2 doubles or halves the grid density at each transition.
Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules.MinViewSize: Floor on the view size used to compute grid spacing. When the view is smaller than this, spacing stops getting finer, keeping the grid from becoming too dense when fully zoomed in.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletComponentRules.T:: One piece of a projectile's behaviour, such as its collider, its homing, its hits or its sprite. A modder writes one of the concrete component types under a bullet's `Components` group.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.T:: Defines one projectile a weapon can fire, giving it a range, a speed and the named `Components` that supply its physics, hits and visuals.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.ID: Identifier that must be unique across the game.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.OtherIDs: Legacy identifiers. You shouldn't normally need these.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Range: How far the target can be when the projectile is shot at it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.IdealRange: The range from which the AI will try to use this weapon.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.IdealRadius: The target radii, in tiles, that map onto [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.IdealRange]]. Against a target no larger than the minimum radius the AI prefers the near end of the ideal range, against one at least the maximum radius the far end, interpolating for sizes in between. Has no effect unless [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.IdealRange]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Speed: How fast the projectile moves forward when spawned.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.ReceivableBuffs: The buff types the projectile inherits from the part that fired it. Buffs not listed here are dropped when the projectile spawns, so a buff must be listed for buffable values such as [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Range]] and [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Speed]] to respond to it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.ForgetTarget: Whether the projectile discards the firing weapon's target when it spawns. Components and effect filters that check the projectile's target or targeted ship then treat it as having none.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.RandomRotation: Whether the projectile spawns facing a random direction.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathR.T:: Shared by the components that can kill their own bullet and run its `OnDeath` hit and media effects when they do. A modder writes one of the concrete kinds.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathR.OnDeath: The hit effects and media effects played at the bullet's position when this component kills it. The effect point honors the hit rules' `Offset` (rotated with the bullet) and `FrameOfReference`, though `HitObject` is not allowed for death components. The vanilla deployed mine spawns its 16 shrapnel bullets from here.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathR.FactorEffectsWith: The ID of a sibling bullet component whose current factor multiplies the intensity of the [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathRules.OnDeath]] hit and media effects. A `DamagePool` reports its remaining damage fraction, a `Targetable` its remaining health fraction, and a `DeathByEnemyProximity` its accumulator mapped through [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.OutputFactorRange]]. The vanilla mine's deploy death uses `FactorEffectsWith = Targetable` so a damaged mine deploys with weaker effects.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByDam.T:: Kills the bullet as soon as the `DamagePool` component it names has spent all of its damage.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByDam.DamagePool: The ID of the sibling `DamagePool` component to watch. The bullet dies as soon as that pool's remaining damage reaches 0, checked when the bullet activates and whenever the pool's value changes. The vanilla overclocked deck cannon and railgun shots use this so the projectile disappears once its damage budget is spent.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByDis.T:: Kills the bullet once it has flown `Distance`, falling back to the bullet's own `Range` when no distance is given.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByDis.Distance: How far the bullet travels before dying, in tiles, rolled randomly between Min and Max when the bullet spawns. Travel is measured relative to the bullet's frame of reference, so drifting along with a moving battle frame does not count. When unset, the distance is the bullet's [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Range]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByDis.HasTarget: Restricts when this death component is attached at all. True attaches it only to bullets fired with a target, false only to bullets fired without one, and leaving it unset attaches it always.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.T:: Detonates the bullet when an enemy ship or bullet stays within `Range` long enough to pass `AccumulateThreshold`, which is how proximity mines work.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.Interval: The time between proximity checks, in seconds. The first check runs one interval after the bullet spawns, and the timer restarts after every check. The vanilla deployed mine checks every 0.1 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.Range: The radius, in tiles, of the circular detection area around the bullet. Any valid ship or bullet intersecting this circle counts as a detection for that check.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.StartDelay: The arming delay, in seconds, after the bullet spawns during which no proximity checks run at all. The vanilla deployed mine arms after 0.5 seconds and drives its arming animation from this value.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.AccumulateThreshold: The accumulator value at which the bullet dies, defaulting to 1. Each check that detects something adds [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.AccumulateRate]] and each empty check subtracts [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.DeaccumulateRate]]. With all three at their defaults of 1, a single detection triggers death immediately.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.AccumulateRate: The amount added to the accumulator by each proximity check that detects a valid ship or bullet, defaulting to 1. Values below [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.AccumulateThreshold]] make the bullet require sustained proximity across several checks before dying.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.DeaccumulateRate: The amount subtracted from the accumulator by each proximity check that detects nothing, defaulting to 1. The accumulator never drops below 0.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.DetectsShips: Whether ships trigger detection. A ship counts when it is an enemy of the bullet's source ship, or when it is the bullet's target ship and can be damaged by the source. Nothing is ever detected when the bullet has no source ship.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.DetectsBullets: Whether other bullets trigger detection, off by default. Only bullets with a `Targetable` component count, and only when the bullet's source ship would target them, so friendly and allied bullets are ignored.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.DetectsBulletCategories: Limits bullet detection to targetable bullets whose [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetableRules.TargetCategory]] matches one of the listed IDs. When unset, any enemy targetable bullet triggers detection. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.DetectsBullets]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEne.OutputFactorRange: The factor span this component reports when another component references it via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathRules.FactorEffectsWith]], defaulting to 0..1. The current accumulator's progress toward [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByEnemyProximityRules.AccumulateThreshold]] is mapped linearly from Min to Max.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByLif.T:: Kills the bullet after `Lifetime` seconds, defaulting to the time it needs to fly the bullet's own `Range`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByLif.Lifetime: How long the bullet lives, in seconds, rolled randomly between Min and Max when the bullet spawns. When unset, the lifetime is the bullet's [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Range]] divided by its speed, so the bullet expires right at its nominal range.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByLif.HasTarget: Restricts when this death component is attached at all. True attaches it only to bullets fired with a target, false only to bullets fired without one, and leaving it unset attaches it always.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByPre.T:: Kills the bullet at the distance where it predicts it will meet its target, offset randomly by `RandomOffset` for an airburst spread.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByPre.RandomOffset: A random extra distance, in tiles, added to the predicted impact distance, rolled between Min and Max when the bullet activates. Defaults to 0. The component estimates how far the bullet must fly to reach the target's predicted intercept point and dies after traveling that far plus this offset, and if there is no target or no intercept can be computed it never triggers.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathBySpe.T:: Kills the bullet once its speed drops below `MinSpeed` or rises above `MaxSpeed`, which is how a mine settles and arms.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathBySpe.MinSpeed: The speed, in tiles per second, below which the bullet dies. Checked every fixed update. The vanilla mine shot uses `MinSpeed = 30` so the launched mine deploys once drag has slowed it down enough.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathBySpe.MaxSpeed: The speed, in tiles per second, above which the bullet dies. Checked every fixed update.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathBySpe.RelativeToFrameOfReference: Measures the bullet's speed relative to its frame of reference instead of as absolute world speed, so a bullet drifting along with a moving battle frame counts as stationary. Off by default.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByTar.T:: Kills the bullet once it comes within `Proximity` of its target, without needing to collide with it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BulletDeathByTar.Proximity: The distance, in tiles, to the target's center below which the bullet dies, checked every fixed update. Defaults to 0. Does nothing when the bullet has no target.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.T:: Draws a looping frame animation on the bullet, with its own offset, spin, render bucket and fade timing.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.Animation: The animated sprite drawn on the bullet, defining the frame atlas, frame count, and playback rate. Frames advance automatically while the bullet exists. When [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]] is set, every frame that declares no shader of its own gets the game's lit-sprite shader.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.NormalsTexture: A normal-map texture that makes the sprite lit by the simulation's dynamic lighting. Setting it binds the texture as the normals shader constant on every animation frame, switches frames without their own shader to the lit-sprite shader, and enables the extra [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.DiffuseShader]] and [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.NormalsShader]] render passes.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.NormalsShader: The shader used for the extra render pass into the scene's normals target. This pass only runs when the sprite is lit via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]]. Falls back to the game's standard sprite-normals shader when unset.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.DiffuseShader: The shader used for an extra render pass into the scene's diffuse target. This pass only runs when the sprite is lit via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]]. Nothing extra is drawn when unset.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.IsLight: Renders the sprite into the simulation's light buffer instead of the regular scene, so it contributes to dynamic lighting rather than being lit itself. Vanilla shots use this for their additive glow sprites.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.Offset: The sprite's position relative to the bullet's center, in tiles, in the bullet's own rotated frame. When the sprite is scaled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.LerpScaleFrom]] or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.ReduceScaleWith]], the offset shrinks and grows with the scale.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.RotOffset: The sprite's rotation relative to the bullet's facing, in degrees.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.Spin: Continuous rotation applied to the sprite every frame, in degrees per second. The spin turns only the sprite's own node, not the bullet itself.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.Z: The Z height written into the sprite's vertices, used by the lighting shaders as the sprite's height above the 2D plane. It does not affect draw order, which comes from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.RenderBucket]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.RenderBucket: The named effect bucket, defined in the game rules' `EffectBuckets` lists, that decides the render-order layer the sprite draws in. Defaults to `default_bullet`. Vanilla shots layer their sprites with buckets such as `BulletLower1` and `BulletUpper2`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.ReduceScaleWith: ID of a sibling bullet component whose factor multiplies the sprite's scale every frame, raised to [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.ReduceScaleExponent]]. Factor sources include hit components (remaining penetration fraction), `DamagePool` (remaining damage fraction), and `Targetable` (remaining health fraction), all in 0..1. The vanilla railgun bullet shrinks with `ReduceScaleWith = Hit`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.ReduceScaleExponent: Exponent applied to the factor read from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.ReduceScaleWith]] before it multiplies the sprite's scale. Values below 1 make the shrinking more gradual. The vanilla railgun bullet uses `0.5`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.LerpScaleFrom: The sprite's starting scale as X and Y multipliers, interpolated linearly to full size over [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.LerpTime]] after the bullet spawns.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.LerpTime: The duration, in seconds, of the grow-in interpolation from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.LerpScaleFrom]] to full scale.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.LerpIntervalWith: ID of a sibling bullet component whose factor continuously re-maps the animation's frame interval within [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.IntervalLerp]], so the animation speeds up or slows down as that factor changes. The fractional progress through the current frame is preserved when the interval changes.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.IntervalLerp: The range of per-frame intervals, in seconds, that the factor from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.LerpIntervalWith]] is mapped onto. A factor of 0 yields the Min interval and a factor of 1 yields the Max.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.StartTime: Time after the bullet spawns, in seconds, before the sprite starts rendering. Together with [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.EndTime]] this defines a visibility window, and the animation only plays while the sprite is visible. The vanilla deployed mine uses this to swap its sprites when it arms.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.EndTime: Time after the bullet spawns, in seconds, at which the sprite stops rendering and the animation pauses. Defaults to forever. See [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimatedSpriteRules.StartTime]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.AnimationOffset: Initial frame time, in seconds, that the animation starts with when the bullet spawns, beginning playback partway into the animation instead of at the first frame.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletAnimate.CaptureBackBuffer: Captures the current back buffer right before the sprite draws and binds it as the captured-back-buffer shader constant, letting the sprite's shader distort or refract whatever is behind it.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.T:: Plays particles, sounds and other media on the bullet for as long as it lives, such as a missile's thruster plume.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.MediaEffects: The set of media effects (particles, sounds, lights) played continuously on the bullet for as long as it exists. The effect node is attached to the bullet at [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEffectsRules.Offset]] and inherits the bullet's velocity and frame of reference each physics tick. The vanilla railgun bullet attaches its trail particle effects this way.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.Offset: The position, in tiles, where the effects are attached relative to the bullet's center, in the bullet's own rotated frame.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.Rotation: The rotation of the attached effects relative to the bullet's facing, in degrees.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.MediaEffectsScale: The base intensity multiplier for the played effects, defaulting to 1. It is a modifiable value evaluated against the bullet's buffs and effect scale, so it can react to buffs. The vanilla railgun bullet multiplies it by the `RailgunShot` buff to grow the trail with charge.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.FactorEffectsWith: ID of a sibling bullet component whose factor (a 0..1 value such as a damage pool's remaining-damage fraction or `Targetable`'s remaining-health fraction) multiplies the effect intensity every physics tick on top of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEffectsRules.MediaEffectsScale]]. The vanilla nuke missile's first stage uses `FactorEffectsWith = Targetable` to fade its effects as the missile takes damage.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEf.FactorEffectsExponent: Has no effect. The game stores the value but never reads it, so the [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletMediaEffectsRules.FactorEffectsWith]] factor is always applied linearly. The working equivalent for sprites is [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.ReduceScaleExponent]].

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.T:: Draws a still image on the bullet, with its own offset, spin, render bucket and optional normals for lighting.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.Sprite: The sprite drawn on the bullet, including its texture, size in tiles, vertex color, blend mode, and optional custom shader. When [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]] is set and the sprite declares no shader of its own, the game's lit-sprite shader is applied automatically.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.NormalsTexture: A normal-map texture that makes the sprite lit by the simulation's dynamic lighting. Setting it binds the texture as the sprite's normals shader constant, switches the sprite to the lit-sprite shader unless it declares its own, and enables the extra [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.DiffuseShader]] and [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.NormalsShader]] render passes.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.NormalsShader: The shader used for the extra render pass into the scene's normals target. This pass only runs when the sprite is lit via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]]. Falls back to the game's standard sprite-normals shader when unset.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.DiffuseShader: The shader used for an extra render pass into the scene's diffuse target. This pass only runs when the sprite is lit via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.NormalsTexture]]. Nothing extra is drawn when unset.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.IsLight: Renders the sprite into the simulation's light buffer instead of the regular scene, so it contributes to dynamic lighting rather than being lit itself. Vanilla shots use this for their additive glow sprites, such as the PD shot's `GlowSprite`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.Offset: The sprite's position relative to the bullet's center, in tiles, in the bullet's own rotated frame. When the sprite is scaled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.LerpScaleFrom]] or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.ReduceScaleWith]], the offset shrinks and grows with the scale.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.RotOffset: The sprite's rotation relative to the bullet's facing, in degrees.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.Spin: Continuous rotation applied to the sprite every frame, in degrees per second. The spin turns only the sprite's own node, not the bullet itself.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.Z: The Z height written into the sprite's vertices, used by the lighting shaders as the sprite's height above the 2D plane. It does not affect draw order, which comes from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.RenderBucket]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.RenderBucket: The named effect bucket, defined in the game rules' `EffectBuckets` lists, that decides the render-order layer the sprite draws in. Defaults to `default_bullet`. Vanilla shots layer their sprites with buckets such as `BulletLower1` and `BulletUpper2`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.ReduceScaleWith: ID of a sibling bullet component whose factor multiplies the sprite's scale every frame, raised to [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.ReduceScaleExponent]]. Factor sources include hit components (remaining penetration fraction), `DamagePool` (remaining damage fraction), and `Targetable` (remaining health fraction), all in 0..1. Vanilla bullets shrink as they penetrate with `ReduceScaleWith = Hit`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.ReduceScaleExponent: Exponent applied to the factor read from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.ReduceScaleWith]] before it multiplies the sprite's scale. Values below 1 make the shrinking more gradual. The vanilla railgun bullet uses `0.5`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.LerpScaleFrom: The sprite's starting scale as X and Y multipliers, interpolated linearly to full size over [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.LerpTime]] after the bullet spawns. The vanilla PD shot grows its tracer from `[.25, 1]` over 0.05 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.LerpTime: The duration, in seconds, of the grow-in interpolation from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.LerpScaleFrom]] to full scale.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.StartTime: Time after the bullet spawns, in seconds, before the sprite starts rendering. Together with [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.EndTime]] this defines a visibility window, which the vanilla deployed mine uses to swap sprites when it arms.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.EndTime: Time after the bullet spawns, in seconds, at which the sprite stops rendering. Defaults to forever. See [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteRules.StartTime]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Graphics.BulletSpriteR.CaptureBackBuffer: Captures the current back buffer right before the sprite draws and binds it as the captured-back-buffer shader constant, letting the sprite's shader distort or refract whatever is behind it. The vanilla tractor beam and the nuke shockwave use this for their distortion effects.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletDamagePoolR.T:: Gives the bullet a budget of damage that hit effects draw from until it runs out, so a penetrating shot weakens as it goes.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletDamagePoolR.Damage: Damage capacity of the pool, scaled by the projectile's effect scale. `Damage` hit effects that reference the pool drain it as they deal damage, other components can read the remaining fraction through their `FactorEffectsWith` field, and a `DeathByDamagePool` component can destroy the projectile once the pool is empty. The overclocked large flak field uses a 400 point pool shared by its bullet hits and beam attenuation.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.T:: Lets the bullet punch into a ship and keep going, with separate effects for the first hit, each part passed through and the exit.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.Penetration: The projectile's total penetration capacity. Each part it passes through subtracts that part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InitialPenetrationResistance]] (or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ContinuingPenetrationResistance]] for further cells of the same part), scaled by the penetration factor fields, and the projectile is destroyed once the capacity is used up. At `0` the projectile stops at the first thing it hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetrationSpeed: Speed, in tiles per second relative to the hit ship, that the projectile slows to when it hits an operational part and starts penetrating. Left unset, the projectile keeps its normal flight velocity while penetrating.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesOperational: Whether the projectile can penetrate into operational parts. When false it expends all remaining [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] on the first operational part it hits and is destroyed there.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesStructural: Whether the projectile can penetrate into structural parts such as armor and structure. When false it expends all remaining [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] on the first structural part it hits and is destroyed there.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesShields: Whether the projectile can pass through shields. When true a hit shield subtracts its penetration resistance times [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.ShieldPenetrationFactor]] from the remaining [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]]. When false the projectile is stopped by the first shield it hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesFriendlies: Whether the projectile keeps flying after hitting a ship it cannot damage, such as a friendly ship. When false it is destroyed at the point of that hit. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.FriendlyShipLowCollisions]] or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.FriendlyShipHighCollisions]] allow the collision to happen at all.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PartCategoryPenetrationFactors: Extra multipliers on penetration resistance for parts in specific part categories. Every listed category the hit part belongs to multiplies the resistance subtracted from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]], on top of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.OperationalPenetrationFactor]] or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.StructuralPenetrationFactor]]. Values below 1 penetrate such parts more easily.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.OperationalPenetrationFactor: Multiplier on the penetration resistance of operational parts. Values below 1 let the projectile penetrate deeper through them, values above 1 drain [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] faster.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.StructuralPenetrationFactor: Multiplier on the penetration resistance of structural parts such as armor and structure. Values below 1 let the projectile penetrate deeper through them, values above 1 drain [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] faster.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.ShieldPenetrationFactor: Multiplier on the penetration resistance of shields the projectile passes through. Only applies when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.PenetratesShields]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.FriendlyShipLowCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the low (ordinary) part colliders of ships it cannot damage, including the ship that fired it. Setting this false lets the shot fly over friendly ships while still hitting their high colliders, which is how the deck cannon's bullet fires over its own ship.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.FriendlyShipHighCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the high part colliders of ships it cannot damage. High colliders are those marked `IsHigh` on raised parts such as the deck cannon turret or sensor array.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.NonFriendlyShipLowCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the low (ordinary) part colliders of ships it can damage. Setting this false makes the shot pass over enemy ships and only interact with their high colliders.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.NonFriendlyShipHighCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the high part colliders of ships it can damage. High colliders are those marked `IsHigh` on raised parts such as the deck cannon turret or sensor array.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.SourcePartCollisionDelay: Time, in seconds after spawning, during which collisions with the part that fired the projectile are ignored. Vanilla missiles and mines use about 1.5 physics ticks so they can leave their launcher without immediately hitting it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.ShieldCollisions: Filter deciding whose shields the projectile collides with. Defaults to enemy shields, plus a friendly ship's shields when that ship is the deliberate target, but never the firing ship's own shields. Allowed shield hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitShield]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.BulletCollisions: Filter deciding which other targetable projectiles this projectile can collide with. Collisions are off by default. Allowed hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitBullet]], and whether the projectile survives is controlled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.PenetratesBullets]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesBullets: Whether the projectile keeps flying after hitting another projectile. When false it is destroyed on the spot. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.BulletCollisions]] allows bullet hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.CrewCollisions: Filter deciding which crew in space the projectile collides with. Collisions are off by default. Allowed hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitCrew]], and whether the projectile survives is controlled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.PenetratesCrew]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratesCrew: Whether the projectile keeps flying after hitting a crew member in space. When false it is destroyed on the hit. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.CrewCollisions]] allows crew hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.FactorEffectsWith: Name of another component on the same projectile, such as a `Targetable` or `DamagePool`, whose remaining-strength factor scales this hit's effect intensity. The penetrating hit in turn exposes its own factor, the remaining fraction of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]], for other components to reference.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitOperational: Effects applied the first time the projectile hits an operational part. Further operational parts along the penetration path use [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.PenetratingOperational]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitStructural: Effects applied the first time the projectile hits a structural part such as armor or structure. Hitting an operational part also counts as the first structural hit, so further structural parts use [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.PenetratingStructural]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratingOperational: Effects applied to each further operational part the projectile penetrates after the first hit that triggered [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitOperational]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.PenetratingStructural: Effects applied to each further structural part the projectile penetrates after the first hit that triggered [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitStructural]] or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitOperational]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.FinishedPenetratingOperational: Effects applied when the projectile runs out of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] inside an operational part, its final stop. If that part is also the first operational part hit, [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitOperational]] plays instead.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.FinishedPenetratingStructural: Effects applied when the projectile runs out of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] inside a structural part, its final stop. If that part is also the first part hit, [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.HitStructural]] plays instead.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitShield: Effects applied when the projectile hits a shield allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.ShieldCollisions]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitFriendly: Effects that replace the normal hit rules whenever the struck ship cannot be damaged by the projectile's source, such as a friendly ship. When unset, friendly hits use the regular hit rules.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitBullet: Effects applied when the projectile hits another projectile allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.BulletCollisions]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitCrew: Effects applied when the projectile hits a crew member in space allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.CrewCollisions]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.HitsFriendlyStructure: Whether structural hit effects also trigger on ships the projectile cannot damage. When false, hitting a friendly ship's structural parts applies no effects.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetrating.CalculateWorldHitNormals: Whether the hit will calculate world-space part hit normals.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.T:: Stops the bullet at the first thing it touches and applies the matching effects for a shield, a part, another bullet or crew.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.FriendlyShipLowCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the low (ordinary) part colliders of ships it cannot damage, including the ship that fired it. Setting this false lets the shot fly over friendly ships while still hitting their high colliders, as the deck cannon's bullet does. Also accepted under the alias `SourceShipLowCollisions`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.FriendlyShipHighCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the high part colliders of ships it cannot damage. High colliders are those marked `IsHigh` on raised parts such as the deck cannon turret or sensor array. Also accepted under the alias `SourceShipHighCollisions`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.NonFriendlyShipLowCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the low (ordinary) part colliders of ships it can damage. Setting this false makes the shot pass over enemy ships and only interact with their high colliders.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.NonFriendlyShipHighCollisions: Whether the projectile collides with the high part colliders of ships it can damage. High colliders are those marked `IsHigh` on raised parts such as the deck cannon turret or sensor array.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.SourcePartCollisionDelay: Time, in seconds after spawning, during which collisions with the part that fired the projectile are ignored. Vanilla missiles and mines use about 1.5 physics ticks so they can leave their launcher without immediately hitting it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.ShieldCollisions: Filter deciding whose shields the projectile collides with. Defaults to enemy shields, plus a friendly ship's shields when that ship is the deliberate target, but never the firing ship's own shields. Allowed shield hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.HitShield]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.BulletCollisions: Filter deciding which other targetable projectiles this projectile can collide with. Collisions are off by default, and the point defense shot enables them for the `missile`, `mine` and `bullet` categories to shoot ordnance down. Allowed hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.HitBullet]], and whether the projectile survives is controlled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.PenetratesBullets]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.PenetratesBullets: Whether the projectile keeps flying after hitting another projectile. When false it is destroyed on the spot. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.BulletCollisions]] allows bullet hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.CrewCollisions: Filter deciding which crew in space the projectile collides with. Collisions are off by default, and allowed hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.HitCrew]]. Due to a quirk, the physics category for crew collisions is only enabled when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.BulletCollisions]] also allows at least one allegiance, so crew hits require bullet collisions to be enabled as well, as the point defense shot does.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.PenetratesCrew: Whether the projectile keeps flying after hitting a crew member in space. When false it is destroyed on the hit. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.CrewCollisions]] allows crew hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.FactorEffectsWith: Name of another component on the same projectile, such as a `Targetable` or `DamagePool`, whose remaining-strength factor scales this hit's effect intensity and media intensity.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitOperational: Effects applied when the projectile hits an operational part. Unless [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.Bounce]] is set the projectile is destroyed at the hit point.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitStructural: Effects applied when the projectile hits a structural part such as armor or structure. Structural parts are only collided with at all when the projectile's deliberate target is structural, unless [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.IgnoreStructureUnlessTargeted]] is disabled or [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.HitsFriendlyStructure]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitShield: Effects applied when the projectile hits a shield allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.ShieldCollisions]]. Unless [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.Bounce]] is set the projectile is destroyed at the shield.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitFriendly: Effects that replace the normal hit rules whenever the struck ship cannot be damaged by the projectile's source, such as a friendly ship. When unset, friendly hits use the regular hit rules. Vanilla missiles use it to play their impact visuals and sound without dealing any damage.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitBullet: Effects applied when the projectile hits another projectile allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.BulletCollisions]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitCrew: Effects applied when the projectile hits a crew member in space allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.CrewCollisions]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.HitsFriendlyStructure: Whether structural hit effects also trigger on ships the projectile cannot damage. Enabling it additionally makes the projectile collide with structural parts even when they are not its deliberate target, overriding [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.IgnoreStructureUnlessTargeted]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRu.IgnoreStructureUnlessTargeted: Whether the projectile ignores structural parts such as armor and structure unless its deliberate target is a structural part. When true, a shot aimed at an operational part flies over bare armor and structure instead of detonating on it.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.T:: Turns the bullet into a volume that damages other bullets passing through it and drains beams, the way the flak field does. It only works on a bullet with `CirclePhysics`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.BulletCollisions: Filter deciding which targetable projectiles the volume reacts to, defaulting to those of enemies. Volume hits only ever interact with targetable projectiles (and beams via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRules.BeamAttenuationDamagePool]]), never with ships or crew. Allowed hits trigger [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRules.HitBullet]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.FactorEffectsWith: Has no effect. The volume hit never connects the reference to its internal effect factor, which therefore stays at 1, unlike the working [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletSimpleHitRules.FactorEffectsWith]] on simple and penetrating hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.BeamAttenuationDamagePool: Name of a `DamagePool` component on the same projectile. When set, the volume also attenuates beam weapons that cross it. Each beam is weakened by up to the pool's remaining damage and the pool is drained by the amount absorbed, which is how the overclocked large flak field blocks beams.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.FactorEffectsByDistance: Whether the effect scale of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRules.HitBullet]]'s hit effects is multiplied by the length, in tiles, of the hit projectile's path through the volume during the physics tick. Projectiles that clip the edge are then affected less than ones passing through the middle.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.FactorMediaIntensityByDistance: Whether the intensity of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRules.HitBullet]]'s media effects is multiplied by the length, in tiles, of the hit projectile's path through the volume during the physics tick.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRu.HitBullet: Effects applied to each projectile allowed by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletVolumeHitRules.BulletCollisions]] that passes through the volume. Media effects are swept along the chord of the target's path instead of playing as a one-shot. The collision itself destroys nothing, so any harm comes from the hit effects, typically pooled `Damage`.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletS.T:: Spawns a smaller bullet for every `DamagePerSplit` points a hit takes out of the named damage pool, splitting a shot into fragments.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletS.DamagePool: Name of the `DamagePool` component on the same projectile whose drain is measured. The number of fragments spawned is derived from how much the pool drops while the owning hit's effects run, and damage that falls short of a full split carries over to later hits.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletS.DamagePerSplit: Pool damage consumed per fragment spawned. Each hit spawns one fragment for every full `DamagePerSplit` points it drained from [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletSplitRules.DamagePool]], then the remaining pool is divided evenly between the original projectile and the new fragments.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletS.SpawnEffect: The `SpawnBullets` effect that creates each fragment, run once per split at the hit point. Its effect scale is set to the fragment's share of the remaining pool relative to the pool's base damage, so each fragment carries a proportional slice of the parent's strength.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.T:: A bundle of hit effects and media played for one kind of impact, such as striking a shield, penetrating a part or dying.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.HitEffects: Gameplay effects such as `Damage`, `ExplosiveDamage` or `SpawnBullets` run at the hit point when this hit triggers. They receive whatever was hit, a part, shield, projectile or crew member, as their target.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.HitEffectsScale: Multiplier on the effect scale passed to [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.HitEffects]], default 1. Stacks with the projectile's own effect scale and any `FactorEffectsWith` factor, and accepts value modifiers so buffs can change it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.MediaEffects: Purely audiovisual effects such as particles, sounds and screen shake played at the hit point. Volume hits play them continuously along the target's path through the volume instead of as a one-shot.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.MediaEffectsScale: Multiplier on the intensity of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.MediaEffects]], default 1. Accepts value modifiers, which the overclocked railgun shot uses to grow its impact effects with the overclock buff.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.DamagePoolBulletSplitting: Splits the projectile into fragments spawned by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.DamagePoolBulletSplitRules.SpawnEffect]] whenever this hit's effects drain enough damage from a `DamagePool` component. Only hits of a `PenetratingHit` component apply it. The overclocked railgun shot uses it to shed fragment bullets as it penetrates.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.ReduceEffectsByPenetration: Scales this hit's effect scale and media intensity by the fraction of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.BulletPenetratingHitRules.Penetration]] the projectile has left, so deeper hits are weaker. Only hits of a `PenetratingHit` component honor it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.Bounce: Whether the projectile ricochets off instead of being destroyed by this hit. When true the collision is handed back to the physics engine so the projectile bounces away after the effects play. No vanilla shot uses it.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.FrameOfReference: Velocity frame the spawned effects inherit, so particles drift along with the chosen object. When unset, `HitObject` is used, which takes the velocity of whatever was hit at the hit point. `Bullet` uses the projectile's velocity, `Inherit` the frame of reference the projectile itself inherited, and `Grid` the stationary world frame.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Hits.HitRules.Offset: Offset in tiles added to the hit point before effects are placed, rotated to the projectile's facing. The point defense shot uses `[-0.15, 0]` to pull its impact effects slightly back along the shot. Volume hits ignore it.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelera.T:: Speeds the bullet up or slows it down over time, along its facing, its velocity or the line to its target.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelera.Acceleration: The acceleration, in tiles per second squared, applied to the bullet every physics tick. Interpolated from Min to Max as the bullet's age moves through [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelerationRules.AccelerationOverTime]], and a plain single value applies constantly. Negative values brake the bullet.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelera.AccelerationOverTime: The lifetime window, in seconds since spawn, over which [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelerationRules.Acceleration]] interpolates from its Min to its Max. Defaults to `[0, 0]`, making the acceleration constant. Vanilla missiles use a second component with `Acceleration = [-90, 0]` and `AccelerationOverTime = [0, .75]` to bleed off inherited launch velocity.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletAccelera.Direction: The direction the acceleration pushes in. `Bullet`, the default, pushes along the bullet's facing, `Target` toward its current target, `Velocity` along its velocity, and `FrameOfReferenceVelocity` along its velocity relative to its frame of reference. With `Target` and no living target no force is applied.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletBoxPhysi.T:: Gives the bullet a rectangular collider of the given `Size`, suited to long shapes like missiles.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletBoxPhysi.Size: The dimensions, in tiles, of the bullet's rectangular physics collider, with X along the bullet's facing. Vanilla missiles use `[1.5, .5]`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletBoxPhysi.Density: The mass density of the collider, giving the body a mass of the rectangle's area times this value. Mass mainly matters when bullets physically collide via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsRules.CollidesWithBullets]].

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletCirclePh.T:: Gives the bullet a round collider of the given `Radius`, the usual choice for shells, bolts and mines.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletCirclePh.Radius: The radius, in tiles, of the bullet's circular physics collider. Vanilla laser bolts use a tiny `0.01` while the mine body uses `.3`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletCirclePh.Density: The mass density of the collider, giving the body a mass of the circle's area times this value. Mass mainly matters when bullets physically collide via [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsRules.CollidesWithBullets]].

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.T:: Common movement and collision settings for a bullet's body, including damping and how long it keeps the firing ship's velocity. A modder writes `BoxPhysics` or `CirclePhysics`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.LinearDamping: Viscous drag coefficient slowing the bullet toward its frame-of-reference velocity rather than toward a dead stop. At 0, the default, the bullet keeps its speed. The deployed vanilla mine uses `.5` together with [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsRules.FrameOfReferenceDuration]] `0` to brake to a halt in space.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.AngularDamping: Viscous drag coefficient on the bullet's spin. At 0, the default, rotation is undamped.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.CollidesWithBullets: Lets the bullet's physics body collide and bounce off the bodies of other bullets that also enable it. By default a bullet's body physically collides with nothing. Vanilla mines use this so they bump off each other.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.FrameOfReferenceDuration: Seconds over which the frame-of-reference velocity the bullet inherited at spawn, usually the firing ship's velocity, fades linearly to zero. Until it fades, [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsRules.LinearDamping]] and other frame-relative behavior measure against that velocity instead of the fixed grid. Defaults to infinity so the frame never fades, while the deployed vanilla mine sets `0` to drop it immediately.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletPhysicsR.RandomExtraSpeed: Extra speed, in tiles per second, rolled uniformly between Min and Max and added to the bullet's base [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Speed]] at spawn. Vanilla shrapnel uses ranges like `[-5, 5]` to vary fragment speeds.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.T:: Pulls the bullet towards nearby ships and bullets, or pushes it away when `Acceleration` is negative, which is how mines spread out.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.Range: The radius, in tiles, of the circle around the bullet that is searched every physics tick for ships and bullets to accelerate toward. Objects at the edge of this radius contribute nothing, with influence growing toward the bullet per [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximityAccelerationRules.Falloff]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.Acceleration: The acceleration, in tiles per second squared, applied along the combined pull of everything in range. Negative values repel instead, as the deployed vanilla mine uses `-10` to push away from other mines.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.Falloff: Exponent shaping how each object's pull weakens with distance. The per-object weight runs from 1 at the bullet's location to 0 at the edge of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximityAccelerationRules.Range]] and is raised to this power, so values above 1 concentrate the pull at close distances.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.AccelerateTowardsShips: Whether ship parts in range pull the bullet. Each part is weighted by its physical area times its density, so massive parts attract more strongly.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.AccelerateTowardsBullets: Whether bullets in range pull the bullet. Only bullets with a `Targetable` component count.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.AccelerateTowardsBulletCategories: Restricts the bullet pull to bullets whose [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetableRules.TargetCategory]] is in this list. When unset every targetable bullet counts. The deployed vanilla mine uses `[mine]` so mines only repel each other.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.AccelerateTowardsFriendlies: Whether non-hostile objects contribute to the pull. For ships this means ships the bullet cannot damage, and for bullets it means bullets the firing ship would not target.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximit.AccelerateTowardsEnemies: Whether hostile objects contribute to the pull. For ships this means ships the bullet can damage, and for bullets it means bullets the firing ship would target.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.T:: Turns the bullet towards its target at `TurnVelocity` and steers it around obstacles, which is what makes a missile home.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.TurnVelocity: The maximum rate at which the bullet turns toward its target, written with a `d` suffix for degrees per second. Each physics tick the bullet's angular velocity is capped at this rate, so lower values give wider homing arcs. Vanilla missiles use `240d`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.ModifiesLinearVelocity: Redirects the bullet's velocity relative to its frame of reference along its facing every tick, keeping the speed unchanged, so the bullet actually changes course as it turns. When false, the default, homing only rotates the bullet and its flight path is left to other components.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.Delay: Seconds before homing kicks in, during which the bullet flies straight with no turning. The countdown only runs while the bullet has a live target. Vanilla missiles use `.1` so they leave the launcher before curving.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidanceRaycastDistance: The length, in tiles, of the look-ahead raycasts used to steer around ships other than the target ship. When greater than 0 the bullet probes its desired heading, then offsets of 45, 90, 135, and 180 degrees to either side, and flies the first clear direction, preferring the one closest to its current facing. If every direction is blocked it does not steer that tick. The `Avoids` fields choose what counts as an obstacle.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.TargetLeadPrediction: Aims at a predicted intercept point computed from the target's motion and the bullet's current speed instead of the target's current center. Falls back to the center when no intercept solution exists.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.VelocityCompensation: Blends the bullet's velocity relative to the target into its steering, so it turns to cancel sideways drift instead of merely pointing at the target. Higher values weight the drift correction more strongly, and 0, the default, disables it. Vanilla missiles use `60%`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidsEnemies: Whether the avoidance raycasts treat ships hostile to the firing ship as obstacles. The target ship itself is never avoided. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHomingRules.AvoidanceRaycastDistance]] is greater than 0.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidsFriendlies: Whether the avoidance raycasts treat ships not hostile to the firing ship as obstacles, so homing shots steer around allies. The target ship itself is never avoided. Only relevant when [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHomingRules.AvoidanceRaycastDistance]] is greater than 0.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidsJunk: Whether the avoidance raycasts treat junk that does not block weapon line of sight as an obstacle. Junk whose ship rules set [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.JunkBlocksWeaponLOS]] is instead handled by [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHomingRules.AvoidsEnemies]] and [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHomingRules.AvoidsFriendlies]].
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidsStructural: Includes structure colliders in the avoidance raycasts, so bare structure blocks a probed direction. Off by default, letting homing shots fly over structure.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletTargetHo.AvoidsOperational: Includes operational (non-structure) part colliders in the avoidance raycasts, so those parts block a probed direction.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletSameSh.T:: Sends the bullet after another part of the same ship when the part it was aimed at is destroyed.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.T:: Lets a bullet with no target look for one within `Range`, trying ships, parts, bullets and crew in the order listed.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.Interval: Seconds between search attempts. The countdown only runs while the bullet has no living target, and the first search happens this long after spawning.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.Range: The radius, in tiles, of the circle around the bullet searched for new targets.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.TargetTypesByPriority: The kinds of target tried in order until one is found. `ShipParts` picks a random part of the closest attackable ship, `ShipCenters` targets that ship itself, `Bullets` targets the closest matching targetable bullet, and `Crew` the closest targetable crew floating in space. The remaining `WeaponTargetType` values are not supported by bullets and crash the game.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.BulletTargetCategories: Restricts `Bullets` searches to bullets whose [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetableRules.TargetCategory]] is in this list. When unset any targetable bullet the firing ship would target qualifies.

Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.T:: Gives the bullet health so point defense can shoot it down, and a `TargetCategory` label that other bullets filter on.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.Health: Hit points the bullet has against weapons that shoot at bullets, such as point defense. Incoming damage reduces it, and at 0 the bullet dies and plays its [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Death.BaseBulletDeathRules.OnDeath]] effects. Hit components that set `FactorEffectsWith` to this component scale their effects by the fraction of health remaining.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.TargetCategory: A category label compared by equality wherever bullet categories are filtered, such as a weapon's `BulletTargetCategories`, effect filter bullet categories, [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Physics.BulletProximityAccelerationRules.AccelerateTowardsBulletCategories]], and [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetSearchRules.BulletTargetCategories]]. A bullet with no category never matches any filter list. Vanilla uses the labels `missile`, `mine`, `laser`, and `bullet`.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.ExplosiveDamageAbsorption: The fraction, 0 to 1, of an explosion's remaining damage pool that can be applied to this bullet when it is caught in explosive area damage. Lower values let more of the explosion continue past the bullet to objects behind it. Defaults to 1, absorbing the full share.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.DamageResistances: Resistance per damage type against hits on this bullet, each a 0 to 1 fraction subtracted from incoming damage. A ranged value interpolates from Min at full health to Max as the bullet nears destruction. Vanilla laser bolts use `shrapnel = 50%` to survive flak better.
Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTarget.ExplosiveDamageResistance: Legacy shorthand that inserts its value as the `explosive` entry of [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetableRules.DamageResistances]]. Ignored when that map already contains an `explosive` entry.

Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules.T:: Stores rules for a single text and/or image entry on a codex page.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules.Image: Sprite shown for this entry. When paired with [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules#TextKey|TextKey]] it sits to the left of the text at its native size, otherwise it stands alone as an image-only block. An entry with neither field renders nothing.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules.TextKey: Localization key for this entry's body text, rendered as a left-aligned label with XML formatting enabled. Shown beside an [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules#Image|Image]] when both are set, or as a standalone paragraph on its own.

Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.T:: Stores rules for a single codex page.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.ID: Unique identifier for this codex page. Used as the key under which the player's per-page state (shown, seen, hidden) is persisted in settings, so it must stay stable across versions to preserve progress.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.TitleKey: Localization key for the page's title, shown as the heading of its popup window and as the label of its entry in the codex list.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.TabNameKey: Localization key naming the codex tab this page is grouped under. Pages sharing a resolved tab name are listed together on the same tab in the codex dialog.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.ShowCondition: Python expression evaluated against the current game (with `game`, `stats`, and `sim` in scope) that, when true, permanently marks the page as shown so its button appears on the HUD and stays in the codex. Only evaluated while the page is not already shown.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.TempShowCondition: Python expression evaluated each update that shows the page only while it returns true. Unlike [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules#ShowCondition|ShowCondition]] this does not persist, so the page's button disappears again once the condition goes false.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.OnSeen: Python script run once the first time the player sees or dismisses the page. Runs a single time only (guarded by a persisted flag) and has a `SetSetting(name, value)` helper in scope for writing static game settings.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.AutoOpen: When true the page's popup window opens automatically the moment the page first becomes visible, rather than waiting for the player to click its HUD button.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.AutoPause: When true the game is paused (via a multiplayer-safe input) at the moment [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules#ShowCondition|ShowCondition]] first fires and the page becomes shown. Only takes effect through that permanent show path.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.IsTip: Marks the page as a tip, collecting it into the game's tips pool shown by the startup Tips dialog rather than treating it as a regular tutorial codex page.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.CenterScreen: When true the page's popup window is positioned in the center of the screen when it opens instead of near its originating HUD button.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules.Entries: Ordered list of text and image blocks that make up the page's body, laid out top to bottom. See [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageEntryRules|CodexPageEntryRules]] for how each entry combines an image and text.

Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexRules.T:: Stores the rules for all of the game's codex.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexRules.CodexPages: Full set of codex and tutorial pages in the game. Each is evaluated against game state to decide when it appears, and pages flagged with [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules#IsTip|IsTip]] are additionally gathered into the tips pool.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexRules.NewTutorialSound: Sound effect played on the interface audio group whenever a new codex page becomes visible on the HUD, alerting the player that a tutorial or tip is available.
Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexRules.TipsRequiredTutorials: Set of codex page [[Cosmoteer.Codex.CodexPageRules#ID|IDs]] that must all have been seen before the startup Tips dialog is allowed to appear. Gates tips behind finishing the core tutorials, unless tutorials are disabled in settings.

Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.T:: Stores rules about the crew on ships.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.CostPerCrew: The credits charged for each crew member hired. Also counts toward a ship's total value based on its crew capacity.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.MaxHealth: The hit points a crew member has while flying in space. Weapons that target crew subtract from it, and the crew dies when it reaches 0.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.BaseSpeed: Walking speed aboard a ship, in tiles per second. Multiplied by each part's crew speed factor and by the carried resource's `CarrySpeed`. Also used to turn path distances into travel-time estimates when crew pick resource sources.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.DoorOpenDistance: How close, in tiles, a walking crew must get to the door ahead of it before it holds that door open. Works with [[Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.DoorCloseDistance]].
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.DoorCloseDistance: How far, in tiles, a crew keeps holding a door open after passing through it. Beyond this distance the door is released and can close.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.JobAssignmentsPerSecond: How many queued normal-priority jobs per second a ship recomputes crew assignments for. Higher values make crew react to new work faster at more CPU cost. Low-priority jobs use [[Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.LowPriorityJobAssignmentsPerSecond]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.LowPriorityJobAssignmentsPerSecond: How many jobs per second from the ship's low-priority queue get their crew assignments recomputed. The normal queue uses [[Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.JobAssignmentsPerSecond]].
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.ResourceSearchesPerSecond: How many resource sinks per second re-search the ship for possible supply sources. Rate-limits the expensive source search that feeds resource-delivery jobs.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.ManualTransferJobExpensiveCheckInterval: How often each pending manual resource-transfer job runs its expensive validity check (completion and source reachability). Despite the name it acts as a rate, roughly this many checks per job per second, spread round-robin over all pending jobs.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.SalvageJobExpensiveCheckInterval: How often each active salvage or deconstruction job runs its expensive finished check, including sight and distance tests. Like [[Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.ManualTransferJobExpensiveCheckInterval]] it acts as roughly this many checks per job per second, spread round-robin.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.MaxCrewSearchIterations: Cap on pathfinding iterations when searching outward from a job for the nearest available crew. Limits how far the search expands before giving up.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.EqualPriorityJobDistanceThreshold: Distance bias, in tiles, in favor of a crew's current job. When two jobs have equal priority, a crew is only pulled onto the new job if its current job's remaining distance exceeds the distance to the new job by more than this.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.OffShipEqualPriorityJobDistanceThreshold: The equivalent of [[Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.EqualPriorityJobDistanceThreshold]] applied to crew that are currently off their ship.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.TotalPathTrafficIncrease: Traffic cost added to the cells along each walking crew's registered path, and removed again when the path is released. Path searches that account for traffic then prefer less congested routes.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.CrewUpdatesPerSecond: How many times per second each crew member's movement and job logic runs, staggered across ticks. Its inverse is the timestep a job receives each time a crew works on it.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.SourceRefreshesPerTick: How many crew per physics tick re-validate their assigned crew source (the quarters part housing them), cycling round-robin through all crew in the simulation.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.HomelessWanderDistance: Radius, in tiles, around the spot where a crew became homeless within which it picks random wander destinations.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.FollowShipDistance: How far, in tiles, beyond the home ship's bounding circle idle or waiting crew in space position themselves, for example while idling outside or waiting for an oxygen refill.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.NewHomeSearchDistance: Radius, in tiles, a homeless crew searches for a ship of its player with spare crew capacity. The nearest such ship becomes its new home.
Cosmoteer.Crew.CrewRules.NewHomeSearchInterval: Minimum and maximum seconds a homeless crew waits between searches for a new home ship. Each wait is randomized within the range.
