Cosmoteer.Game.PartColorGuiRules.SortOrder: Orders this button among all the trigger, targeter, toggle and color buttons on a part's command card. Lower values are placed first.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartColorGuiRules.ShowWithShipCommands: Also shows this picker on the ship command card, not just on the parts card for the selected parts.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartColorGuiRules.ShowInEditor: Makes the picker available in the ship designer, so the player can set the color while placing parts and on parts selected with the select tool.

Cosmoteer.Game.PartStatRules.T:: Stores rules for a part statistic.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartStatRules.ID: Identifies this stat. A part's `Stats` and `StatCategories` maps supply values under this id, and stat bars and icon widgets in the build toolbox refer to it. Position in the game's `PartStats` list also decides the order stats appear in a part's tooltip, not the order the part declares them.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartStatRules.FormatKey: Localization key for the line printed in the part tooltip. The stat's values are passed in as the format arguments, so a stat holding two numbers such as `Size` uses a key with two placeholders.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartStatRules.DefaultBuiltinStat: Fills this stat from a value the engine already knows about when a part does not declare it explicitly, for example `Cost`, `MaxHealth` or `CrewCapacity`. Several of these are converted for display rather than passed raw. `Size` and `PhysicalSize` are multiplied by the ship scale to give two values in meters, `ExplosiveDamageAbsorption` and the crew speed factors are multiplied by 100 to give percentages, and the penetration resistances have 1 subtracted so they read as the extra resistance above normal. Some builtins are also skipped when they would be uninteresting, for example a penetration resistance of 1 or below, or a crew capacity of zero.

Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.T:: Stores rules for a particular part button that gives the part a target.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.TargeterID: The name this targeter is known by. A part joins the targeter by carrying a `UITargeter` component with the same `TargeterID`, and the button only appears while at least one selected part or ship owns such a component. The id is also the key under which the player's rebound hotkeys are saved and under which the hotkey's display name is looked up as `Inputs/PartTargeters/<id>`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.ButtonTextKey: The localization key of the caption drawn on the targeter button on top of `ButtonSprite`. The text is rendered with XML formatting enabled, so markup tags work. Vanilla's targeters are icon only and leave this unset.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.ButtonToolTipKey: The localization key of the tooltip shown when hovering the targeter button, for example `PartTargeters/TractorBeam`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.ButtonSprite: The icon of the targeter button in the command card. Leaving it unset gives a button with no image, so pair that with `ButtonTextKey`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.HasCancelButton: Whether a second button that clears the targets of every matching weapon is placed next to the targeter button. It also gates hotkey registration, so `DefaultCancelHotkey` is ignored when this is false. The cancel button only becomes clickable while at least one matching weapon actually has an explicit target.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.CancelButtonTextKey: The localization key of the caption drawn on the cancel button, rendered with XML formatting like `ButtonTextKey`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.CancelButtonToolTipKey: The localization key of the tooltip shown when hovering the cancel button.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.CancelButtonSprite: The icon of the cancel button. Vanilla's tractor beam uses a dedicated image while the headlight reuses the generic halt icon.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.Cursor: The mouse cursor shown for as long as the targeting mode is active, applied every frame in both the main view and the miniview. Leaving it unset keeps whatever cursor the game would otherwise show.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.TargetObjectCursor: The cursor shown instead of `Cursor` while the mouse is over a ship or part that this targeter can actually target. It is never applied in `ShipLocalPoint` mode, since free points are not objects.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.OverrideTentativeTargetNineSlice: The frame drawn around the part currently under the cursor, replacing the shared `Commands/WeaponTarget/TentativeTargetNineSlice`. When this override is used the frame is drawn at plain white rather than the player's configured enemy color, so any tint has to be baked into the sprites, as vanilla's tractor beam does with a blue `VertexColor`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.OverrideTentativeTargetCircle: The circle drawn around the ship currently under the cursor, sized to the ship's bounding radius and replacing the shared `Commands/WeaponTarget/TentativeTargetCircle`. As with `OverrideTentativeTargetNineSlice`, the override is drawn white instead of the player's enemy color.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.TentativeTargetLine: The preview line drawn from each participating weapon to the point or object under the cursor, in the player's configured enemy color. No preview line is drawn at all when this is unset, which is what vanilla's tractor beam does.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.DefaultHotkey: The key combination that activates this targeter out of the box, written as the whole chord such as `[PlatformCmdCtrl, T]`. It is registered in the ship command input context when `ShowWithShipCommands` is true and in the parts control context otherwise, and the player can rebind it in the controls settings.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.DefaultCancelHotkey: The key combination that clears this targeter's targets out of the box. Only registered when `HasCancelButton` is true.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.SortOrder: The ascending sort key that positions this targeter's buttons among all part command buttons in the card, shared with part triggers, toggles and color pickers. The targeter button and its cancel button both carry this value, and buttons with equal values keep their creation order.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.ShowWithShipCommands: Whether the button also appears on the ship command card, which is the card shown when whole ships rather than individual parts are selected. It additionally decides the input context the hotkeys live in, so a targeter meant to be usable with a ship selected needs this true for its hotkey to fire.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.TargetTypes: Which kinds of things clicking can pick as the target. The flags are evaluated in a fixed order regardless of how they are listed, and the `SelectParts` modifier, Control by default, switches between them. With `Ships` and `Parts` both set, ships are targeted normally and holding the modifier targets individual parts. With `Parts` and `ShipLocalPoint` both set, parts are targeted normally and holding the modifier drops to a free ship-relative point.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.TargetPartCategories: Restricts part targeting to parts that list one of these categories in their `TypeCategories`. Leaving it unset lets any part be targeted, and it has no effect on `Ships` or `ShipLocalPoint` targeting.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.AllowAppend: Whether holding the `AppendSelection` modifier, Shift by default, adds the clicked target to the weapons' existing target list instead of replacing it. With this false the modifier is simply ignored and every click replaces the target.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.AllowSameShipTarget: Whether the targeter may pick a target on the same ship it lives on. With this false, such targets are skipped when validating the click, so the button also stops showing a tentative highlight over them. The targeting part can never target itself either way.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.SnapToAngles: The directions, relative to the targeting part's own facing, that a `ShipLocalPoint` target snaps onto. The point snaps to the nearest ray cast from the first weapon's ship location along one of these directions, and holding the `SelectParts` modifier suppresses snapping so the point can be placed freely.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTargeterGuiRules.SnapToAngleDistance: How close, in tiles, the cursor's ship-relative point must be to one of the `SnapToAngles` rays for it to snap onto that ray. Nothing snaps when the nearest ray is further away than this.

Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.T:: Stores rules for a particular choice in a part toggle setting.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.ChoiceID: Identifies this choice. The game registers one rebindable hotkey per choice id, and the player's saved binding is stored under `PartToggles/<ChoiceID>` in the input settings, so renaming an id loses existing bindings.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.ButtonTextKey: Localization key for the label drawn on the toggle button while this choice is displayed, and on this choice's row in a `Popout` style list. The label is rendered with XML formatting enabled. Note that the game blanks the button's label again whenever `ButtonToolTipKey` is absent, so a choice that wants a visible label should set both keys.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.ButtonToolTipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown while this choice is displayed on the button, and on this choice's row in a `Popout` style list.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.ButtonSprite: The image drawn on the toggle button while this choice is the displayed mode, and the icon on this choice's row in a `Popout` style list.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.DefaultHotkey: The out of the box key combination that switches the toggle to this choice, written as the list of keys that must be held, for example `[PlatformCmdCtrl, Shift, D]`. Players can rebind it, and choices within the same toggle are allowed to share a binding without being reported as a conflict.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.AllowHotkeyRevert: Makes pressing this choice's hotkey while the toggle is already in this mode send the affected parts back to whichever mode they were in before, instead of leaving them unchanged. Useful for a momentary mode such as an override that should snap back on a second press.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.CreateHotkey: Registers a rebindable hotkey for this choice. Set it to false for a choice that should only be reachable by clicking, which also keeps it out of the key bindings list.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.Mode: The mode number this choice corresponds to on the part's `PartUIToggle`, which is what the part's own rules match against. When omitted, the choice's index in `Choices` is used, so an explicit value is only needed when the part expects numbers that are not 0, 1, 2 and so on. Vanilla's fire mode toggle uses -1 for hold fire.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleChoice.SelectedSound: Plays when the player switches the toggle to this choice by cycling the button or by picking it from a popout list. It does not play for mode changes made in the ship designer.

Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.T:: Stores rules for a particular part setting that can be toggled between multiple choices.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.ToggleID: Identifies this toggle. A part opts into the toggle by declaring a `PartUIToggle` component whose `ToggleID` matches, and the button then drives every matching toggle on the selected parts or ships. Vanilla ids include `"on_off"` and `"fire_mode"`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.Style: Picks the widget built for this toggle. `CycledButton` is a single button that steps through the choices, `Switch` is an on/off switch, `OffAlertSwitch` and `OnAlertSwitch` are the same switch with the off or on state drawn in the alert color, and `Popout` opens a list of all choices.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.MultipleModesDisplayOrder: Decides which choice the button displays when the selected parts are not all in the same mode. `First` shows the earliest choice in `Choices` that any selection uses, `Last` shows the latest.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.Choices: The modes this toggle can be in, in the order they are cycled and listed. The button starts on the first entry, and a choice without an explicit `Mode` takes its list index as its mode number.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.NoChoicesToolTipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown when the toggle is greyed out because fewer than two choices are available to the selection, for example when a game mode has locked the other choices. Also accepted under the old name `DisabledToolTipKey`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.NonOperationalToolTipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown when choices exist but none of the selected parts are operational enough to change mode, for example an unpowered or destroyed part.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.SortOrder: Orders this button among all the trigger, targeter, toggle and color buttons on a part's command card. Lower values are placed first, and vanilla gives the on/off toggle -1 so it comes before everything else.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.ShowWithShipCommands: Also shows this toggle on the ship command card, not just on the parts card for the selected parts. It also puts the choices' hotkeys in the general command input context instead of the parts control context.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartToggleGuiRules.ShowInEditor: Makes the toggle available in the ship designer, so the player can preset the mode while placing parts and on parts selected with the select tool.

Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.T:: Stores rules for a particular part trigger that can be activated by the player.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.TriggerID: Identifies this trigger. A part opts into it by declaring a `PartUITrigger` component whose `TriggerID` matches, and clicking the button fires every matching trigger on the selected parts, or on the selected ships when no individual parts are selected. Vanilla defines `"detonate"`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.DefaultHotkey: The out of the box key combination that fires the trigger, written as the list of keys that must be held. Vanilla's detonate trigger uses `[PlatformCmdCtrl, Shift, D]`. Players can rebind it, and the binding is stored under `PartTriggers/<TriggerID>`.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.ButtonTextKey: Localization key for the label drawn on the trigger button. The label is rendered with XML formatting enabled.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.ButtonToolTipKey: Localization key for the trigger button's tooltip.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.ButtonSprite: The image drawn on the trigger button in the command card.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.SortOrder: Orders this button among all the trigger, targeter, toggle and color buttons on a part's command card. Lower values are placed first.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.ShowWithShipCommands: Also shows this trigger on the ship command card, not just on the parts card for the selected parts. It also puts the hotkey in the general command input context instead of the parts control context.
Cosmoteer.Game.PartTriggerGuiRules.OnlyOne: Fires just one of the matching parts instead of all of them. The candidates are shuffled first, so the part that fires is picked at random among those that are operational.

Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.T:: Stores rules related to customizable UI colors.
Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.DefaultPlayerColor: The color used for the local player's own ships and crew in the interface, applied to selection outlines, ship logos, minimap icons and text markup. It is only a fallback, so a player who picks a color in the accessibility settings overrides it. Vanilla is a green `[10, 212, 98]`.
Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.DefaultEnemyColor: The interface color for hostile ships and targets, used for target reticles, targeting lines and enemy markers. Overridden by the accessibility settings, and vanilla is a red `[246, 49, 42]`.
Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.DefaultAllyColor: The interface color for friendly ships that the player does not control. Overridden by the accessibility settings, and vanilla is a cyan `[10, 212, 212]`.
Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.DefaultNeutralColor: The interface color for ships and objects that are neither friendly nor hostile. Overridden by the accessibility settings, and vanilla is a grey `[153, 153, 153]`.
Cosmoteer.Game.UIColorRules.ColorblindPresets: The presets offered in the accessibility settings drop list. Picking one writes all four of its colors into the player's settings at once, and the drop list re-selects a preset automatically when the player's four colors happen to match it exactly.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.T:: Spreads the listed factions over a generated galaxy and hands whatever is left to `RemainderFaction`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.Factions: Factions to place, each with its own territory rules. Homeworld locations for all of them are computed first, then each faction's territory is grown outward from its homeworld.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.RemainderFaction: Optional faction that fills in nodes left weakly claimed. After the main factions spawn, any node whose total faction strength is below [[RemainderFactionThreshold]] gets this faction added to make up the difference.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.RemainderFactionThreshold: Total faction strength a node must reach before the remainder faction stops filling it. Nodes below this are topped up by [[RemainderFaction]] up to this value. Default 0.5.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.MinRemainderFactionStrength: Minimum strength the remainder faction must contribute at a node. If the top-up amount would be smaller than this, the node is left as is.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.AvoidIterations: Number of relaxation passes that push faction homeworlds apart and away from the map edge, using each faction's [[Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSpawner+FactionSpawnRules#AvoidOtherFactionsStrength]] and [[Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSpawner+FactionSpawnRules#AvoidEdgeStrength]]. Default 10.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.T:: Stores rules for how to spawn a faction's territory.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.FactionID: Faction whose territory this entry places.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.TerritoryRatio: Fraction of the map's total nodes this faction claims, rounded up. Territory grows outward from the homeworld until this many nodes are covered.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.AvoidOtherFactionsStrength: How strongly this faction's homeworld is pushed away from other faction homeworlds during the relaxation passes controlled by [[Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSpawner#AvoidIterations]]. Default 0.2.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.AvoidEdgeStrength: How strongly this faction's homeworld is pulled toward the map center, away from the edge, during the relaxation passes. Default 0.2.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.FactionStrengthExponent: Exponent shaping how faction strength falls off from the homeworld to the territory edge, where strength is the remaining-node fraction raised to this power. The default of 1 gives a linear falloff, higher values a steeper one.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.FactionsSp.MinFactionStrength: Nodes whose computed strength falls below this are not assigned to the faction, trimming the faint outer edge of its territory.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.GalaxyGene.Spawners: Ordered list of spawners run in sequence to populate the galaxy map. Each spawner rolls its own [[Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.GalaxySpawner#SpawnChance]] before running.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.GalaxySpaw.T:: The base class for classes that spawn into the galaxy map.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.GalaxySpaw.SpawnChance: Probability from 0 to 1 that this spawner runs. A value of 0 or a failed roll skips it entirely, and the default of 1 always runs it.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.Count: Range for the number of nodes to spawn. A random integer in the range is chosen at spawn time.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.Distance: Range for how far each new node is placed from an existing node. The minimum of the range also acts as the minimum spacing between nodes, so any candidate closer than that to an existing node is rejected.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.ConnectionRadius: Radius around a new node within which it is connected to existing nodes, skipping any connection that would visually cross an existing one.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.PerlinNoise: Optional 2D noise field constraining where nodes may spawn. A candidate location is rejected unless its noise value falls inside [[NoiseRange]].
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.NoiseRange: Allowed range of [[PerlinNoise]] values for a valid node location. Default 0 to the maximum float. Has no effect unless PerlinNoise is set.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.MapNodesSp.NameGenerator: Optional generator producing each node's name, capped at 30 characters. Nodes are left unnamed when absent.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.RandomNode.T:: Picks a random controlling faction for each galaxy map node.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.RandomNode.FactionStrengths: Per faction strength ranges. At each node every listed faction rolls a random strength from its range and is assigned wherever the roll is positive. When omitted, every faction instead rolls a strength from -1 to 1 and is assigned on a positive roll.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Galaxies.RandomNode.GuaranteeFactions: When true a node is re-rolled until at least one faction ends up with strength there, so no node is left without a faction. Default true.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.CharacterSequ.T:: Generates a letter followed by numbers, example "E-423.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.CharacterSequ.AvailableCharacters: Pool of characters the name is built from. Each position draws one character uniformly at random from the whole string, so repeats are possible and every character has equal odds.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.CharacterSequ.Length: Number of characters in the generated name, each drawn independently from [[AvailableCharacters]].

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MarkovGenerat.T:: Generates random names using a Markov chain.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MarkovGenerat.MinLength: Shortest name the generator will accept. Candidates shorter than this are discarded and regenerated. Default 1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MarkovGenerat.MaxLength: Longest name the generator will accept. Candidates longer than this, or longer than the caller's own limit, are discarded and regenerated. Default unbounded.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MarkovGenerat.MaxConsecutiveConsonants: Longest run of consecutive consonants a name may contain before it is discarded and regenerated. Vowels a, e, i, o, u reset the run. Default unbounded.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MarkovGenerat.MarkovFile: Path to the pre-built binary Markov chain file loaded when the generator is read. The chain drives the letter-by-letter name generation.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.T:: Generates a name using a sequence of sub-generators.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.SubGenerators: Ordered list of sub-generators whose outputs are concatenated into one name. Each entry runs in turn subject to its own [[Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGenerator+Entry#Chance]], with [[AddComma]] and [[AddSpace]] deciding the separator between parts.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.AddComma: When true a comma is inserted before each part after the first. Default false.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.AddSpace: When true a space is inserted before each part after the first, following the comma if [[AddComma]] is also set. Default true.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.T:: One sub-generator of a `Multi` name generator, with the chance that its piece of the name is included at all.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.MultiNameGene.Chance: Probability from 0 to 1 that this sub-generator contributes to the name. The default of 1 always includes it, lower values include it only on a passing roll.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.NameGenerator.T:: The base class for objects that generate random names.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.NameListGener.T:: Picks a name at random from a list of names.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Names.NameListGener.Names: Pool of names to draw from. One is chosen at random, retrying until it fits within the caller's length limit.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetHaloG.T:: A planet layer that renders a procedurally-generated halo.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetHaloG.OuterThickness: Width of the halo band outside the planet edge, sent to the shader divided by [[Scale]]. Default 0.1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetHaloG.InnerThickness: Width of the halo band inside the planet edge, sent to the shader divided by [[Scale]]. Default 0.1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetHaloG.AnimateSpeed: Speed at which the halo animates, sent directly to the shader. Default 1.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.T:: The base class for a single layer on a generated planet.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.Name: Display label for the layer, shown in the planet generator editor. Falls back to the class name when blank and has no effect on rendering.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.Enabled: When false the layer is skipped entirely and never created. For probabilistic skipping instead see [[Chance]].
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.Seed: XORed into the seed passed to the layer so that two otherwise identical layers with different Seed values generate different content. Combined further with [[LayerParamsSeed]] for the layer's random parameters.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.Chance: Probability from 0 to 1 that the layer is created at all. A value of 0 always skips it, the default of 1 always creates it, and values in between roll against the layer seed each time the planet is generated.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.Scale: Size of the layer's quad relative to the planet rectangle, so values below the default 0.9 inset the layer and values above 1 overflow it. Ring, halo, shadow and penumbra widths are divided by this value.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.LayerParamsSeed: XORed with the layer seed to seed the layer's random parameters such as [[LayerSpin]], independent of the texture content seeded by [[Seed]].
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.LayerSpin: Range for the layer's own rotation speed, added on top of the planet's spin. A random value in the range is chosen and its direction is randomly flipped.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.DiffuseDarkness: Strength of the terminator shading from 0 to 1 sent to the planet shader, higher values darkening the unlit side more. Negated when [[InvertDarkness]] is set. Default 0.96.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.DarknessExponent: Exponent applied to the diffuse darkness falloff in the shader, shaping how sharply the lit side transitions into shadow.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.InvertDarkness: Negates the [[DiffuseDarkness]] value sent to the shader, shading the near side instead of the far side. Suited to atmosphere or cloud layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.SpecularStrength: Strength of the specular highlight from 0 to 1 sent to the shader. Default 0, meaning no highlight. Paired with [[SpecularShine]].
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetLayer.SpecularShine: Specular exponent sent to the shader, higher values giving a tighter highlight. Default 5.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.T:: A planet layer that renders a procedurally-generated ring.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.RingThickness: Width of the ring band, sent to the shader. Default 0.2.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.Resolution: Pixel resolution of the generated ring texture, passed as the texture size to the ring's texture generator. Default 1 by 128.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.Tilt: Range for the ring's tilt angle. A random angle in the range is chosen and its sine and cosine are sent to the shader. Default 45 degrees.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.Angle: Range for the ring's rotation around the planet. A random angle in the range is chosen and added to the planet's rotation. Default 0 to 360 degrees.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.ShadowSphereRadius: Radius of the planet sphere that casts a shadow onto the ring, sent to the shader divided by [[Scale]]. Default 0.9.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRingG.Penumbra: Softness of the ring shadow's edge, sent to the shader as the shadow light radius divided by [[Scale]]. Default 0.3.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.T:: Stores general rules for all planets.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.Styles: Named collection of planet styles keyed by ID. A planet doodad selects its style from this map by its StyleID, and each style is a set of layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.DefaultPlanetMaterial: Material used as the default for a texture layer's Material when the layer does not specify one.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.DefaultWavesMaterial: Material used as the default for a waves layer's Material when the layer does not specify one.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.DefaultHaloMaterial: Material used as the default for a halo layer's Material when the layer does not specify one. Halo layers also clear their generator layers and use a white base color.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetRules.DefaultRingMaterial: Material used as the default for a ring layer's Material when the layer does not specify one.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetStyle.T:: A collection of planet layers to together create a single style of planet.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetStyle.HeightMaps: List of height map generators for the style, each generated at twice the planet's horizontal pixel size and keyed by its Name so layers can reference it. Only enabled generators run.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetStyle.Layers: Ordered list of layers making up the style. Each enabled layer is drawn front-to-back, preceded by a reverse-order background pass. Entries are polymorphic, so a layer can be a texture, waves, halo or ring generator.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetStyle.Spin: Range for the planet's rotation speed. A random value in the range is chosen, its direction randomly flipped, then scaled by the caller's spin factor. Default 0.0025 to 0.005.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetTextu.T:: A planet layer that renders a procedurally-generated texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetTextu.Generator: Texture generator that produces the layer's diffuse texture, assigned to the material. When it has no layers a 1 by 1 texture is used. See [[NormalsGenerator]] for the matching normal map.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetTextu.NormalsGenerator: Texture generator that produces the layer's normal map, bound to the material as its normals shader constant. When it has no layers a 1 by 1 texture is used. Defaults to a flat normal color (127, 127, 255).
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetTextu.Material: Material the layer is rendered with, receiving the generated diffuse texture and normal map. Defaults to a copy of DefaultPlanetMaterial from the planet rules.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetWaves.T:: A planet layer that renders animated waves by lerping between normal maps.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetWaves.Interval: Seconds each normal map is shown before the animation cross-fades to the next entry of [[NormalsGenerators]], wrapping around at the end. Default 1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetWaves.Generator: Texture generator producing the waves' diffuse texture, assigned to the material. When it has no layers a 1 by 1 texture is used.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetWaves.NormalsGenerators: List of texture generators producing the normal maps the animation cycles through, cross-fading from one to the next every [[Interval]] seconds and wrapping around. Two flat normal maps are provided by default.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Planets.PlanetWaves.Material: Material the waves layer is rendered with. Defaults to a copy of DefaultWavesMaterial from the planet rules.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.GeneratorStag.T:: The base class for a single stage of a ship generator. Given an input ship, modifies it in preparation for the next stage.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.GeneratorStag.Name: The human-readable name of this GeneratorStage.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.GeneratorStag.IsEnabled: Whether this particular stage is enabled and will generate parts.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.ShipGenerator.T:: Contains a number of generator stages that, when combined, generate a random ship according to set parameters.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.ShipGenerator.Stages: A modifiable list of generator stages that are used to produce the random ships.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.ShipGenerator.ShipRulesID: Ship class whose part set this generator builds from. Resolved to the matching ship rules when the generator is loaded and written back out when it is saved.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.T:: Fills deposits of parts within an asteroid.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.Parts: The type of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.ReplaceableParts: The list of part types that may be replaced by this stage.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MinPartsFraction: The minimum number of parts to add.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MaxPartsFraction: The maximum number of parts to add.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MinPartsPerDeposit: The minimum number of parts to add per deposit area.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MaxPartsPerDeposit: The maximum number of parts to add per deposit area.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.T:: Places random parts in the shape of an asteroid.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.Parts: The type of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MinParts: The minimum number of parts to add.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.MaxParts: The maximum number of parts to add.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.T:: Places wedge parts on the exterior of an asteroid to make it look more natural.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.WedgeParts: The type of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Astero.ReplaceableParts: The list of part types that may be replaced by this stage.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.T:: The base class for generator stages that place parts within a pre-defined ship shape. Parts are placed according to a priority defined by the subclass.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.ReplaceableParts: The list of part types that may be replaced by this stage.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.ContiguousPathSearchLength: The maximum length to check to make sure contiguous paths won't be disconnected.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.T:: Stores the weight of each possible part rotation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotZeroWeight: Weight of the unrotated orientation (0 degrees) in the weighted-random ordering of orientations the stage tries. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotOneWeight: Weight of the 90 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering the stage tries. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotTwoWeight: Weight of the 180 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering the stage tries. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotThreeWeight: Weight of the 270 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering the stage tries. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotZeroFlippedWeight: Weight of the horizontally mirrored, unrotated orientation in the weighted-random ordering. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotOneFlippedWeight: Weight of the horizontally mirrored 90 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotTwoFlippedWeight: Weight of the horizontally mirrored 180 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.BasePl.RotThreeFlippedWeight: Weight of the horizontally mirrored 270 degree orientation in the weighted-random ordering. A weight of 0 excludes it, higher weights make it more likely to be tried first. Editor slider runs 0 to 10.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.T:: Converts one type of part to another.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.Conversions: The mapping from original part type to converted part type.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.ChanceAtCenter: The chance that the conversion will happen at the center of the ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.ChanceAtEdge: The chance that the conversion will happen at the edge of the ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.ChanceExponent: The exponent applied to the chance after the base value is calculated from the part's distance to the center.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.T:: One part swap a ship generator applies, replacing every `From` part on the ship with the `To` part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.From: Existing part type that this entry converts. Every part of this type on the ship is a candidate for conversion.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Conver.To: Part type that a matching [[From]] part is replaced with, keeping its location, rotation and flip.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Enlarg.T:: Enlarges existing ship parts into larger parts.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Enlarg.ReplaceableParts: The list of part types that may be replaced by this stage.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Enlarg.LargerParts: The type of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Enlarg.RandomizeReplaceOrder: Whether the parts should be replaced in random order.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillGa.T:: Fills in small gaps of the ship's structure.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillGa.Part: The type of part to fill the gaps with.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillGa.FillMode: The logic used to determine which cells should be filled.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillGa.ScanRange: The distance in each direction to scan when determining whether an empty cell should be filled.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillGa.Iterations: The number of iterations of the algorithm to run.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillWi.T:: Fills all available cells of the ship with a particular type of part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillWi.Part: The type of part to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillWi.Iterations: The number of iterations of the algorithm to run.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.FillWi.FillOrder: The order in which the cells are filled.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.T:: Generates a grid of random size and random number of rows and columns, all of a particular part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.Part: The type of part to add.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MinColumns: The minimum number of columns to generate.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MaxColumns: The maximum number of columns to generate.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MinRows: The minimum number of rows to generate.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MaxRows: The maximum number of rows to generate.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MinWidth: The minimum width of each cell.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MaxWidth: The maximum width of each cell.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MinHeight: The minimum height of each cell.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.MaxHeight: The maximum height of each cell.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.GridSt.UniformCellSize: Whether or not each cell is of the same size.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Modula.T:: Generates the basic structure of a ship by randomly assembling various structural modules together.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Modula.MinModules: The minimum number of modules with which the create the ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Modula.MaxModules: The maximum number of modules with which to create the ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Modula.Modules: The modules from which the ship may be built.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceD.T:: Adds additional doors to locations where a door would significantly reduce the travel distance between two sides of the wall.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceD.Door: The type of part to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceD.MinTravelDistance: If the distance between two sides of the wall are greater than this number, then a door will be added to the wall.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: Places a single kind of part in proximity to other kinds of parts.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.SearchRange: The maximum distance from a potential new part location that an existing part can be and still count as being "near" the potential location.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.PlaceNear: The parts near which the new parts should be placed.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Avoid: Avoids putting additional parts near parts of these types.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: Associates an existing type of part that the new part wants to be near with a weight of how important it is to be near that part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Part: Existing part type the new parts should be placed near. Defaults to the ship class's first part type when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Weight: How strongly nearness to this part type is favored when scoring candidate locations. Higher weights pull new parts closer to parts of this type, and closeness matters more the nearer the part is within the search range. Default 1.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: A simple stage that places some number of a single type of part. May be extended to optimize the parts' locations.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Part: The type of part to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.MinParts: The minimum number of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.MaxParts: The maximum number of parts to place.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: A stage that places some number of a single type of part according to a particular placement strategy.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.PlacementStrategy: The strategy to use when picking an optimal location for the part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.UseWeightedRotationFlips: Whether to pick a desired rotation based on weight.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.RotationFlipWeights: The weights by which to pick the desired rotation/flip, if UseWeightedRotationFlips is true.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: A stage that places multiple types of parts, each with a defined score, up to a maximum score. May be extended to optimize the parts' locations.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.MinScore: The minimum total score of parts to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.MaxScore: The maximum total score of parts to place.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: Associates a score and random weight for a particular part type.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Part: Part type this entry can place. Defaults to the ship class's first part type when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Score: Amount each placement of this part subtracts from the stage's remaining score budget, so higher-scored parts are placed fewer times. A part is only eligible while its score fits the remaining budget. Editor slider runs 1 to 10.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Weight: Selection weight among the currently affordable parts, higher weights making this part more likely to be chosen for each placement. Editor slider runs 0 to 100.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: A stage that places multiple types of parts, each with a defined score, up to a maximum score. Optimizes the parts' locations according to a specified strategy.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.PlacementStrategy: The strategy to use when picking an optimal location for the part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.UseWeightedRotationFlips: Whether to pick a desired rotation based on weight.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.RotationFlipWeights: The weights by which to pick the desired rotation/flip, if UseWeightedRotationFlips is true.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.T:: Places a particular type of part to cover all perimeter cells.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Part: The type of part to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceP.Iterations: The number of iterations of the algorithm to run.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceW.T:: A stage that places multiple types of weapons, making sure that they their line of sight isn't blocked by other parts of the ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceW.UseWeightedRotationFlips: Whether to pick a desired rotation based on weight.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.PlaceW.RotationFlipWeights: The weights by which to pick the desired rotation/flip, if UseWeightedRotationFlips is true.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.T:: A structural module generator that creates a circle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MinRadius: The minimum radius of the circle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MaxRadius: The maximum radius of the circle.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.T:: A structural module generator that creates a rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MinWidth: The minimum width of the rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MaxWidth: The maximum width of the rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MinHeight: The minimum height of the rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.MaxHeight: The maximum height of the rectangle.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.T:: The base class for a single structural module generated by the ModularStructureStage of a ship generator.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.RandomWeight: The random weight that this module will be selected.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.AllowedFromDirections: The directions from which this module may be added, or null to allow from any direction.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Struct.Part: The type of part to add.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Surrou.T:: Surrounds all occurrences of a particular type of part with another type of part.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Surrou.PartToAdd: The type of part to place.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Surrou.PartToSurround: The type of part to surround.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Ships.Stages.Surrou.Layers: The number of layers to surround the parts with.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.T:: Spawns doodads into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.ScaleFactor: Size multiplier applied to each spawned doodad, drawn uniformly from this range and then multiplied by the value selected by `ScaleMode`. A value of 1 is the doodad's authored size.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.ScaleMode: Selects a dynamic value that the drawn `ScaleFactor` is multiplied by, for example `AreaRadiusKM` to make doodads grow with the size of the play area. `None` leaves the drawn scale alone.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.DoodadType: A single doodad type to spawn, written either as a bare doodad ID or as a `DoodadTypeInfo` group. Any parameters the doodad type itself defines are read from the spawner's own group, and one of `DoodadType` or `DoodadTypes` has to be present.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.DoodadTypes: The candidate doodad types, one of which is drawn per spawned object by a lottery weighted on their `ChanceWeight`. Ignored when `DoodadType` is also given.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.T:: Stores information about a type of spawnable doodad.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.Type: The doodad to spawn. Its `SpawnRadius` becomes the spawned object's radius for all the distance checks, and its own tags are attached to the object on top of the spawner's `Tags`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.ChanceWeight: Relative weight of this entry in the lottery that picks which doodad type to spawn. It is multiplied by the faction strength lookup when `Faction` is set.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.DoodadSp.Faction: Scales `ChanceWeight` by how strong this faction is at the map node being generated, so faction-flavoured doodads only turn up in that faction's territory. A faction with no strength at the node makes the entry unpickable.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.FtlGateS.T:: Spawns one FTL gate for every connected node of the generated map.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.T:: Specifies parameters for how to search for multiple spawned objects.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.Mode: How the spawned objects will be searched for.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.Tag: The tag of the spawned objects to search for.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.Max: The maximum number of spawned objects to find.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.LimitToBatch: Whether only the spawned objects belonging to the same batch as the first spawned object will be found.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.LimitToFleet: Whether only the spawned objects belonging to the same fleet as the first spawned object will be found.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.Distance: The maximum distance that the spawned objects can be from the search location.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.OnlyFactions: If not null, only objects belonging to these factions will be found.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.MultiSpa.OnlyOpposingFactions: Whether only objects with opposing factions should be returned.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.T:: Spawns a nebula into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.NebulaType: The nebula type painted onto the triangle grid. Whatever was in a triangle before is overwritten, subject to `OnlyReplaceNebulaTypes` and `DontReplaceNebulaTypes`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.NebulaRadius: Radius in world units of the circle the nebula is generated inside, before `MultiplyNebulaRadius` and `AddNebulaRadius` are applied. In splat mode the circle also caps how far the splat may grow.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.MultiplyNebulaRadius: Selects a dynamic value that `NebulaRadius` is multiplied by. `None` leaves the radius alone.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.AddNebulaRadius: Selects a dynamic value added to `NebulaRadius`, applied after `MultiplyNebulaRadius`. `None` adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.NebulaSplatTriCount: Switches the nebula to splat mode and gives the number of triangles to try, drawn uniformly inclusive. A splat grows outward from the centre triangle rather than testing every triangle in the circle, which produces compact blobs instead of a full circular cloud.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.UseIrregularSplatShape: Gives every triangle on the splat's growth front the same chance of being chosen next. Without it a triangle's chance rises with the number of neighbours already taken, which rounds the blob out, so turning this on yields stringier and more ragged shapes. Only meaningful together with `NebulaSplatTriCount`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.MaxDistanceFromWorldOrigin: Maximum distance in world units from the world origin at which nebula triangles may be placed. Vanilla ties it to the career mode unexplored radius so nebulas stop at the edge of the map.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.ContiguousPathCheckSearchIterations: How many breadth-first steps are spent checking that filling a triangle does not cut the open space around it into disconnected pockets. A triangle whose free neighbours cannot be reconnected within this many steps is left empty, which keeps a nebula from sealing off flyable corridors. Vanilla uses 20 for ion storms and supernova nebulas.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.OnlyReplaceNebulaTypes: Restricts painting to triangles whose current nebula type is in this set. Triangles holding anything else are left untouched.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.DontReplaceNebulaTypes: Prevents painting over triangles whose current nebula type is in this set. Checked after `OnlyReplaceNebulaTypes`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoise: A 2D Perlin noise field sampled once per triangle to decide whether that triangle joins the nebula, which is what gives nebulas their cloudy outline. It is sampled at the triangle's offset from the nebula centre divided by the nebula radius, so the field scales with the nebula rather than with world units.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoiseRange: The band of noise values that count as inside the nebula, tested after `PerlinNoiseEdgeOffset` and `PerlinNoiseCenterOffset` have been added. Perlin output is clamped to -1..1 by default, so the default lower bound of 0 keeps roughly the upper half of the field.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoiseEdgeOffset: Added to the noise value at the nebula's outer rim and faded to nothing at its centre, so a negative value thins the cloud out towards the edge. The shape of the fade is set by `PerlinNoiseEdgeOffsetExponent`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoiseEdgeOffsetExponent: Exponent applied to the 0..1 distance from the nebula centre before it is used to blend in `PerlinNoiseEdgeOffset`. Values above 1 squeeze the offset into a narrow band right at the rim.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoiseCenterOffset: Added to the noise value at the nebula's centre and faded to nothing at its rim, so a negative value hollows the cloud out in the middle. Vanilla pairs -1 with an exponent of 4 to punch a hole in the cloudy nebula.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.PerlinNoiseCenterOffsetExponent: Exponent applied to the 0..1 distance from the nebula's rim before it is used to blend in `PerlinNoiseCenterOffset`. Higher values confine the offset to a tighter core.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.UsePolarPerlinCoordinates: Samples the noise field in polar coordinates, feeding the angle around the nebula centre in as X over a 0..1 range per full turn and the distance from the centre in as Y, instead of plain X and Y offsets. Pairing it with a `Repeat` on the noise's X axis makes the nebula outline wrap around seamlessly.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NebulaSp.MinPerlinNebulaTris: Discards connected clumps of nebula smaller than this many triangles, restoring whatever those triangles held before, which cleans up the speckle a noisy Perlin field leaves behind. Values of 1 or less turn the pass off, and it never runs in splat mode.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.NoneSpaw.T:: Spawns nothing itself. It exists so sub-spawners can hang off an imaginary spawn location.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.Resource.T:: Stores rules controlling how a spawned ship's resource loadout will be determined for a particular type of resource.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.Resource.ResourceType: The resource dropped into a flexible storage tile when this entry wins the loadout lottery.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.Resource.RandomWeight: Relative weight of this entry in the lottery, which is rolled once for every unpinned flexible storage tile on the ship. Weights only mean anything relative to the other entries of the same `ResourceLoadout`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.Resource.Quantity: How many units go into the tile, drawn uniformly inclusive and then clamped to the resource's own maximum stack size. It defaults to the largest possible integer at both ends, so tiles are filled right up to the stack limit.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.T:: Spawns ships into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.AIByTag: Maps a built-in ship tag to the AI given to ships carrying that tag. The picked ship's tags are tried in order and the first match wins, and the entry under the empty tag, which is what the `AI` shorthand creates, is the fallback for everything else.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Features: Extra roles attached to the spawned ships, combinable as flags: station, operational station, landmark, FTL point, hidden until discovered, and invulnerable. `Station` and `OperationalStation` also make the ship get stocked by the sector's trade route rules when no `ResourceLoadout` is given. The station, landmark and invulnerability components themselves are only attached when a ship is built out of stasis, so a ship the generator places directly into the live simulation does not get them until it has been through stasis once.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Allegiance: Who owns the spawned ships. `Player` is player 0, `Neutral`, `Barbarian` and `Junk` are the fixed negative player indexes, `FactionMilitary` and `FactionCivilian` read the index off the ship's own faction and throw if the ship has none, and `Unique` allocates a fresh player index per ship in career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.InitToMax: Fills the ship's resource storage and resource grids to capacity and moves the crew to their assigned stations at spawn time. With false the ship starts with whatever the blueprint stored.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.SpawnCrew: Whether the ship is created with the crew its blueprint calls for. With false the ship spawns empty, which is how derelicts and abandoned ships are made.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.RememberPhysicalState: Keeps a full snapshot of the ship, including damage and part layout, when it is pushed into stasis, so that it comes back exactly as the player left it. Without this an altered ship is rebuilt from its blueprint when it respawns.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.RememberResourcesAndCrew: Remembers the stackable resources and crew of an unaltered ship when it is pushed into stasis and restores them when it comes back. Ignored when `RememberPhysicalState` already snapshots the whole ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.NameGenerator: The generator used to invent a name for each spawned ship, replacing the name stored in the blueprint. Without it the blueprint's own name is kept.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.MaxNameLength: The character limit handed to `NameGenerator`. It does nothing on its own.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Fame: Base fame the player earns for destroying one of these ships, before any `FamePerTier` bonus is added. Fame is only recorded in career mode and only when the total comes out above 0.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.MaxFame: The player fame level at which these ships stop being worth anything. The actual reward is the smaller of the ship's fame and `MaxFame` minus the player's current fame, so a famous player earns progressively less from the same ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.FamePerTier: Extra fame per built-in ship tier, drawn uniformly from the range listed for the tier of the ship that was actually picked and added on top of `Fame`. Tiers with no entry add nothing.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.MaxFamePerTier: Per-tier override for `MaxFame`, drawn uniformly from the range listed for the tier of the ship that was actually picked. The lower of that roll and `MaxFame` is used, and tiers with no entry leave `MaxFame` alone.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.RandomHealthRange: Randomizes the health of every part on the spawned ship, as a fraction of that part's max health drawn uniformly between the two ends. Parts never drop below 1 health, and without this field ships spawn undamaged.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.ResourceLoadout: Fills the ship's flexible resource storage with a random mix, rolling the loadout lottery once per storage tile. Tiles whose resource type is pinned by the blueprint are left alone, and setting this also replaces the station trade-stocking pass that `Features` would otherwise trigger.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Labels: Free-form text labels attached to the spawned ships. Codex and tutorial conditions can test for them with `sim.HasShipWithLabelInSight('...')`, which is how vanilla drives the abandoned ship tutorial off the `abandoned` label.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.InitialShipCommandByTag: Maps a built-in ship tag to the order the spawned ship is given the moment it appears. The picked ship's tags are tried in order and the first match wins, with the entry under the empty tag, which the `InitialShipCommand` shorthand creates, as the fallback. Ships that spawn straight into stasis get no command at all.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Ship: A single built-in ship to spawn, written either as a bare ship ID or as a `ShipInfo` group. Exactly one of `Ship`, `Ships` or `ShipCriteria` has to be present, and `Ship` takes precedence if more than one is given.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Ships: The candidate built-in ships, one of which is drawn per spawned object by a lottery weighted on their `ChanceWeight`. The list must not be empty, and it is ignored when `Ship` is also present.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.ShipCriteria: Selects ships out of the built-in ship database by faction, tier, difficulty and tags instead of naming them. Only consulted when neither `Ship` nor `Ships` is given.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.AI/Type: The ship AI to attach to every ship this spawner creates. Reading it registers an `AIByTag` entry under the empty tag, so a per-tag entry in `AIByTag` wins over it for ships that match one.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.AI: The AI parameters, written directly inside the `AI` group next to `Type`. They are copied per ship whenever a patrol origin or a fleet leader has to be filled in, so the same parameters can be shared by a whole fleet.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.AI/PatrolOriginTag: A search for an already-spawned tagged object whose centre becomes the AI's patrol origin, overriding whatever the AI parameters hold. Generation throws if nothing matching the search has been spawned yet.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.InitialShipCommand: The order given to every ship this spawner creates as soon as it appears. Reading it registers an `InitialShipCommandByTag` entry under the empty tag, so a per-tag entry wins over it for ships that match one.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.T:: Stores information about the AI to use for a ship.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Type: The ship AI rules to run on ships that match this entry's tag.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.PatrolOriginTag: A search for an already-spawned tagged object whose centre becomes the AI's patrol origin, overriding whatever the AI parameters hold. Generation throws if nothing matching the search has been spawned yet.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.T:: Stores criteria for selecting what ship to spawn from the built-in database.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Type: What the spawned ship is ordered to do. `Follow` and `Attack` need the search to land on an actual ship and do nothing when it finds something else, while `MoveToLocation` only uses the found object's position.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.TargetsTag: Which already-spawned object the order targets, written as a tag plus a search mode. Generation throws if nothing carrying the tag has been spawned yet.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.InitialSpeed: The speed the ship is launched at, aimed straight at whatever `TargetsTag` found, in world units per second. Zero leaves the ship stationary, and vanilla uses 100 for ambushers charging the player.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.SuppressNoTagTargetFound: Has no effect. The value is read from the rules, but the only code that consults it is an empty branch left over from a developer warning, fired when a `Follow` or `Attack` order resolves to something that is not a ship, that is compiled out of release builds.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.T:: Stores criteria for selecting what ship to spawn from the built-in database.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Factions: Limits the candidate ships to these factions. When `UseLocalFactionWeights` is on it acts as the pool the single local faction is drawn from instead, and it is bypassed entirely once an enclosing `SynchronizeFactions` has already locked a faction in.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.UseLocalFactionWeights: Draws one faction at random, weighted by each faction's strength at the map node being generated, and then searches only within that faction. Factions with no presence at the node cannot be drawn, and `Factions` still restricts which ones are eligible.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Tier: The range of built-in ship tiers that may be picked, compared against each ship's `SpawnTier` falling back to its `Tier`. `UseLocalTier` and `UseTierField` shift this range rather than replacing it.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.UseLocalTier: Adds the career map node's own tier range to `Tier`, so a `Tier` of [0, 1] means the node's tier up to one above it. Career mode only, and combining it with `UseTierField` throws.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.UseEvenTierDistribution: Spreads the objects of a single spawn evenly across the tier range instead of drawing each ship's tier at random, so four ships over tiers 1 to 4 give one of each. Tiers at either end of the range that no ship matches are trimmed off first.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.UseTierField: Adds the career tier field value sampled at the spawn position to `Tier`, so ships get stronger the deeper into a dangerous region they appear. Career mode only, and combining it with `UseLocalTier` throws.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.AllowTierRangeExpansion: Widens the tier range by one in each direction and searches again whenever nothing matches, instead of failing. Without it a spawner asking for a combination no built-in ship satisfies throws and aborts sector generation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Difficulty: The range of built-in ship difficulty ratings that may be picked. Left unset any difficulty is accepted.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.Tags: Only built-in ships carrying every one of these tags are considered. Vanilla uses tags such as `combat` to keep civilian hulls out of a fight.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.UseEvenShipTypeDistribution: Walks the matching ships in database order instead of drawing at random, so a spawn of several ships cycles through the different hulls rather than repeating one. The starting offset is randomized once per spawner run.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.FleetTierRemapTable: Replaces the one ship a spawn would have produced with a whole fleet of weaker ships. Each entry is keyed on the original tier and lists alternative fleets, one of which is drawn at random, and every number in the chosen fleet spawns one ship of that tier. The tier has to resolve to a single value, otherwise generation throws.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.T:: Stores information about a type of ship to spawn.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.ShipID: The built-in ship blueprint to spawn. A `ShipInfo` written as a bare value is read as just this field, which is why `Ship = cosmoteer.some_ship` works.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.ShipSpaw.ChanceWeight: Relative weight of this entry in the lottery that picks one ship out of the spawner's `Ships` list for each object. It has no meaning for a lone `Ship`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.T:: The base class for classes that spawn objects into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.Tags: Labels attached to every object this spawner creates, so that later spawners can refer to them through `RootLocationTag`, the `MinDistanceFromTags` family, and the tag searches used by ship AI and initial ship commands. Doodads also contribute the tags declared on their own doodad rules.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SpawnChance: Probability from 0 to 1 that this spawner runs. The roll happens once for the whole spawner, so a failed roll skips every object it would have made and every sub-spawner below it.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.ForEachRootMax: The maximum number of tagged root locations to repeat the whole spawn at when `RootLocation` is `Tag`. Everything from `Count` downwards happens once per chosen root, and the field does nothing for the other `RootLocation` modes.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.Count: How many objects to spawn, drawn uniformly between the two ends inclusive. Both ends are first multiplied by the value selected by `MultiplyCount` and rounded up.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.Retries: How many extra candidate positions are tried when a spawn position is rejected by the distance, angle and nebula constraints, so each object gets `Retries` + 1 attempts. Once an object runs out of attempts the spawner gives up on it and on all remaining objects of the same `Count`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MultiplyCount: Selects a dynamic value that both ends of `Count` are multiplied by, for example `AreaSquareKM` to scale the population with the size of the play area. `None` leaves `Count` alone.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.Distance: The range of distances in world units from the root location at which objects are placed. Candidates are drawn with uniform area density across the ring rather than uniform radius, and both ends are scaled by `MultiplyDistance` and then offset by `AddDistance`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SortByDistanceToSpawnPoint: Sorts the chosen positions by distance to the career map node's player spawn point before the objects are actually created. That order is what the index in a sub-spawner's `ParentIndex` condition refers to, so it lets you treat the nearest object specially. Ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.RootLocation: The point that `Distance` and `Angle` are measured from. `Parent` is the object that spawned this spawner, `Grandparent` is one level above that, `WorldCenter` is (0,0), `Tag` uses objects found through `RootLocationTag`, and `MinTierGate` uses the lowest-tier FTL gate in career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.RootLocationTag: The tag whose already-spawned objects serve as root locations when `RootLocation` is `Tag`. Up to `ForEachRootMax` of them are used, chosen at random unless `RootLocationFarthestFromTag` is set, and the spawner does nothing when no object carries the tag.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.RootLocationFarthestFromTag: Makes the choice of tagged root locations deterministic instead of random by preferring the candidate that is farthest from the nearest object carrying this second tag. Only used when `RootLocation` is `Tag`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MultiplyDistance: Selects a dynamic value that both ends of `Distance` are multiplied by, for example `ParentToGrandparent` to place objects in proportion to how far the parent orbits out. `None` leaves `Distance` alone.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.AddDistance: Selects a dynamic value added to both ends of `Distance`, applied after `MultiplyDistance`. `None` adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromSiblings: Minimum gap in world units between this object and every other object placed by the same spawner run. The gap is measured between the objects' spawn circles, so their radii already count against it, and any negative value disables the check.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromSiblingOrbits: Minimum difference in orbital radius, meaning the distance out from the root location, between this object and each sibling. Use it to keep objects that share a root on visibly separate rings. Any negative value disables the check.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinAngleFromSiblings: Minimum angular separation, seen from the root location, between this object and each sibling. Any negative value disables the check, which is what the default of -360 degrees does.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromCousins: Minimum gap in world units between this object and every object already spawned by the other spawners that share the same parent object. Measured between spawn circles like `MinDistanceFromSiblings`, and disabled by any negative value.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromCousinOrbits: Minimum difference in orbital radius from the root location between this object and each cousin. The cousin version measures from circle centres rather than circle edges, unlike `MinDistanceFromSiblingOrbits`. Any negative value disables the check.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinAngleFromCousins: Minimum angular separation, seen from the root location, between this object and each cousin. Any negative value disables the check, which is the default.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromTags: Pairs of tag and distance in world units. A candidate position is rejected when it comes closer than the given distance to any already-spawned object carrying that tag, measured between the spawn circles.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MaxDistanceFromTags: Pairs of tag and distance in world units. A candidate is only accepted when, for every entry, at least one already-spawned object carrying that tag lies closer than the given distance. A tag that nothing carries yet rejects every candidate.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromTagOrbits: Pairs of tag and distance in world units. A candidate is rejected when its orbital radius comes within the given distance of a tagged object's orbital radius. Both radii are measured from the world origin here, not from the spawner's root location the way `MinDistanceFromSiblingOrbits` does it.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinAngleFromTags: Pairs of tag and angle. A candidate is rejected when its direction comes within the given angle of a tagged object's direction. Both directions are taken from the world origin, not from the spawner's root location.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MaxDistanceFromNebulas: Pairs of nebula type and distance in world units. A candidate is only accepted when it is inside, or within the given distance of, at least one of the listed nebula types. A distance of 0 means the candidate has to be inside the nebula itself.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.MinDistanceFromNebulas: Pairs of nebula type and distance in world units. A candidate is rejected when it is inside, or within the given distance of, any of the listed nebula types.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.Angle: The arc around the root location that candidate directions are drawn from, written as a near edge direction plus a width. It defaults to the full 360 degrees, and `SpawnsPerSlice` subdivides whatever arc is given here.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SpawnsPerSlice: Splits `Angle` into `Count` / `SpawnsPerSlice` equal slices, rounded up, and puts that many objects in each slice so they come out evenly spread instead of clumped. Zero turns slicing off, and when the arc is a full 360 degrees the whole slice pattern also gets one random rotation per spawner run.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SpawnSlicePadding: The fraction of each slice's width kept clear at both of its edges, so the usable arc is the slice width minus twice the padding. Vanilla uses values between 25% and 45%, and anything at or above 50% leaves no usable arc at all.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SuppressLocationAssertions: Has no effect in the shipped game. The value is read from the rules, but the only code that consults it is an empty branch left over from a developer assertion, fired when no valid position could be found within `Retries` attempts, that is compiled out of release builds.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SubSpawners: Spawners run once for each object this spawner successfully places, with that object as their parent. Their `Conditions` are evaluated against the parent object's index and position, and `RandomSubSpawnerCount` can cut the list down to a random subset.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.RandomSubSpawnerCount: Limits how many of the `SubSpawners` actually run per parent object, drawn uniformly from this inclusive range. Which ones get dropped is decided by a lottery weighted against each sub-spawner's `RandomWeight`. Without this field every sub-spawner whose conditions pass runs.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SynchronizeFactions: Locks every ship spawned anywhere below this spawner to a single faction. The first ship chosen decides the faction and the rest are then restricted to it, and the lock is released once this spawner finishes. Only affects ship spawners that select by `ShipCriteria`, since an explicit `Ship` or `Ships` list does not pick by faction.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimObjec.SynchronizeAllegiance: Locks every ship spawned anywhere below this spawner to a single player index. The first ship resolves its `Allegiance` normally and every later ship reuses that index, which matters most for `Unique` allegiance where each ship would otherwise get its own index. The lock is released once this spawner finishes.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.T:: The base class for classes that spawn anything into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.Conditions: Gates whether this spawner runs at all. The check is made by whoever owns the spawner, the `SimulationGenerator` for top-level entries and the enclosing `SimObjectSpawner` for entries in its `SubSpawners`, and a spawner whose conditions fail is skipped along with everything under it.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.RandomWeight: Relative likelihood of surviving the cut when the parent spawner uses `RandomSubSpawnerCount` to keep only some of its sub-spawners. The game feeds the reciprocal of this value into the removal lottery, so a higher weight makes a sub-spawner less likely to be dropped. It is ignored completely when the parent has no `RandomSubSpawnerCount`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.T:: Stores the conditions that must be met for a spawner to spawn.
