Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.OnlySectorTypes: Limits the spawner to career sectors whose sector type appears in this set. The test is skipped in game modes other than career, so the spawner still runs there.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.ExcludeSectorTypes: Blocks the spawner in career sectors whose sector type appears in this set. Like `OnlySectorTypes` it is ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.RequireSpawnFlags: Every flag listed here must be among the spawn flags that sector generation was started with, otherwise the spawner is skipped. Vanilla uses flags such as `binary_sun`, `no_sun` and `no_standard_nebulas`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.ProhibitSpawnFlags: Skips the spawner if any one of these flags is among the sector's spawn flags. The mirror image of `RequireSpawnFlags`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.IsInitNode: Requires the career map node being generated to be the player's starting node when true, or any other node when false. Ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.ParentIndex: Restricts the spawner to sub-spawner runs whose parent object has an index inside this inclusive range, counted from 0 in the order the parent spawner placed its objects. Top-level spawners always see index 0, so a range that excludes 0 never fires there.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.MinNodeTier: The career map node must reach at least this danger tier. The node is rejected only when the top of its tier range falls below the value, and the test is ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.MaxNodeTier: The career map node must not start above this danger tier. The node is rejected only when the bottom of its tier range exceeds the value, and the test is ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.MinParentFieldTier: The lowest tier field value allowed at the parent object's location. Tier fields are the career-mode danger gradient spread across the sector, and the test is ignored outside career mode.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.MaxParentFieldTier: The highest tier field value allowed at the parent object's location. See `MinParentFieldTier` for how tier fields are sampled.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SimSpawn.RequiredFame: The player's current career fame must be at least this much for the spawner to run. Ignored outside career mode, and the default of 0 lets everything through.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.Simulati.Spawners: The top-level spawners that populate a freshly generated simulation, run in the order they are listed. Each one only runs if its `Conditions` pass, is given the generator's root location as its parent, and everything deeper in the sector comes from their `SubSpawners`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnPoi.T:: Sets the progression origin point based on a desired strategy.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnedO.T:: Specifies parameters for how to search for a spawned object.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnedO.Mode: How the spawned object will be searched for.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnedO.Tag: The tag of the spawned object to search for.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnedO.OnlyFactions: If not null, only objects belonging to these factions will be found.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.SpawnedO.OnlyOpposingFactions: Whether only objects with opposing factions should be returned.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Simulation.TierFiel.T:: A spawner that emits a "tier field" around its location that influences the tier of spawned ships in its vicinity.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.T:: The base class for decal-like heightmap layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Seed: A per-layer seed XORed with the generator's seed to produce this layer's random number stream. Changing it gives a different random arrangement of decals without affecting other layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.MinScale: The minimum size of a decal, as a fraction of the heightmap's dimensions along each axis. Each decal picks a random scale between `MinScale` and `MaxScale`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.MaxScale: The maximum size of a decal, as a fraction of the heightmap's dimensions along each axis. Each decal picks a random scale between `MinScale` and `MaxScale`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Count: The number of decals to place, chosen randomly between the range's min and max. If min is not less than max, exactly min decals are placed. Each placement can still fail if no valid location is found within `Tries` attempts.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field sampled at each candidate decal location to bias where decals appear. The sampled value is passed through `EdgeEffects` and then the `Probabilities` ramp to get a placement probability.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the sampled `PerlinNoise` value based on proximity to the heightmap edges, before it is converted to a placement probability.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Probabilities: A curve mapping perlin noise values to decal placement probabilities. Each point pairs a noise value (`Position`) with a probability, and values between points are interpolated linearly. Points are kept sorted by `Position`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.WrapX: When true, a decal that extends past the left or right edge wraps around to the opposite side of the heightmap instead of being clipped.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.WrapY: When true, a decal that extends past the top or bottom edge wraps around to the opposite side of the heightmap instead of being clipped.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Tries: The maximum number of random locations tried when looking for a valid spot for each decal before that decal is skipped.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.T:: Stores a probability along with its position on the height curve.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Probability: The decal placement probability, from 0 to 1, at this point on the ramp.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Position: The perlin noise value at which this probability applies. A sampled noise value between two points interpolates their probabilities linearly, and points are kept sorted by `Position`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.T:: The base class for decal-like texture layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Seed: A per-layer seed XORed with the texture generator's seed to produce this layer's random number stream. Changing it gives a different random arrangement of decals without affecting other layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.MinScale: The minimum size of a decal, as a fraction of the texture's pixel dimensions along each axis. Each decal picks a random scale between `MinScale` and `MaxScale`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.MaxScale: The maximum size of a decal, as a fraction of the texture's pixel dimensions along each axis. Each decal picks a random scale between `MinScale` and `MaxScale`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Count: The number of decals to place, chosen randomly between the range's min and max. If min is not less than max, exactly min decals are placed. Each placement can still fail if no valid location is found within `Tries` attempts.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field sampled at each candidate decal location to bias where decals appear. The sampled value is passed through `EdgeEffects` and then the `Probabilities` ramp to get a placement probability.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the sampled `PerlinNoise` value based on proximity to the texture edges, before it is converted to a placement probability.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Probabilities: A curve mapping perlin noise values to decal placement probabilities. Each point pairs a noise value (`Position`) with a probability, and values between points are interpolated linearly. Points are kept sorted by `Position`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.WrapX: When true, a decal that extends past the left or right edge wraps around to the opposite side of the texture instead of being clipped.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.WrapY: When true, a decal that extends past the top or bottom edge wraps around to the opposite side of the texture instead of being clipped.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.ReadClippingMaskProbability: When true, the clipping mask value at a candidate location scales its placement probability, and locations where the mask is zero are rejected outright. When false, the clipping mask is ignored when choosing decal locations.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Tries: The maximum number of random locations tried when looking for a valid spot for each decal before that decal is skipped.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.T:: Stores a probability along with its position on the color curve.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Probability: The decal placement probability, from 0 to 1, at this point on the ramp.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseDecals.Position: The perlin noise value at which this probability applies. A sampled noise value between two points interpolates their probabilities linearly, and points are kept sorted by `Position`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseNormal.T:: The base class for texture generator layers that create normal maps from heights.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseNormal.HeightFactor: Scales the height differences between neighboring pixels when computing surface normals. Higher values produce steeper, more pronounced normals, and lower values flatten the resulting normal map.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.T:: The base class for texture generator layers that map a value to a color.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.Interpolate: How colors are blended between adjacent `Colors` points. `Off` uses the lower point's color with no blending, `Rgb` interpolates in RGB space, and `Hsv` interpolates in HSV space.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.Colors: The color ramp that maps the layer's computed pixel value to a color. Each point pairs a value (`Position`) with a `Color`, and a pixel's value is looked up along this ramp. Points are kept sorted by `Position`.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.T:: Stores a color along with its position on the color curve.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.Color: The color at this point on the layer's value ramp.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.BaseValueM.Position: The value at which this color sits on the ramp, matched against the layer's computed pixel value (typically in the -1 to 1 range). Points are kept sorted by `Position`, and values between two points are blended per the layer's `Interpolate` mode.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.T:: A texture generator layer that shifts the colors of the layer underneath.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.Seed: A per-layer seed XORed with the generator's seed to pick the random shift amounts. Changing it produces a different color shift.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.HueShift: The range from which a single hue offset in degrees is chosen. That one offset is added to every pixel's hue (wrapping at 360), so the whole underlying layer is rotated in hue by the same amount.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.SatShift: The range from which a single saturation offset is chosen and added to every pixel's saturation, clamped to 0 to 1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.ValShift: The range from which a single brightness (value) offset is chosen and added to every pixel's value, clamped to 0 to 1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.ColorShift.AlphaShift: The range from which a single alpha offset is chosen and added to every pixel's alpha, clamped to 0 to 1.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.T:: A texture generator layer that stamps decals at random over the texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.DecalFiles: The image files that can be stamped as decals. One file is chosen at random for each decal placed. Loaded files are cached and shared across layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.Hue: The range of hues, in degrees, from which each decal's tint hue is randomly chosen. The decal's pixels are multiplied by the resulting HSVA color, so the tint shifts the decal toward that hue.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.Sat: The range from which each decal's tint saturation is randomly chosen, clamped to 0 to 1. A saturation of 0 leaves the decal's own colors mostly intact.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.Val: The range from which each decal's tint brightness (value) is randomly chosen, clamped to 0 to 1. Defaults to 1, which preserves the decal's original brightness.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.DecalsText.Alpha: The range from which each decal's tint alpha is randomly chosen, clamped to 0 to 1. Defaults to 1. Lower values make the stamped decal more transparent.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GradientTe.T:: A texture generator layer that creates a simple color gradient across any axis.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GradientTe.GradientDirection: The direction the gradient runs, as an angle. Each pixel's distance is measured along this direction, so the mapped value goes from the ramp's low end at the trailing corner to the high end at the leading corner. Defaults to pointing right.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GradientTe.GradientScale: A divisor applied to each pixel's distance along the gradient before it is normalized onto the color ramp. Because the corner distances used to normalize the range are not scaled, values above 1 shift and compress the gradient toward the ramp's low end rather than simply stretching it.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GridTextur.T:: A texture generator layer that draws grid lines.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GridTextur.VerticalLines: The number of evenly spaced vertical grid lines drawn across the texture. Lines are drawn one pixel wide in white.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.GridTextur.HorizontalLines: The number of evenly spaced horizontal grid lines drawn across the texture. Lines are drawn one pixel wide in white.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapG.T:: Generates random heightmaps using individual layer generators.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapG.Name: The name of the generated heightmap.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapG.Enabled: Whether the heightmap should be generated.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapG.BaseValue: The base value of the heightmap before the layers are applied.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapG.Layers: The layers that are used to generate the heightmap.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.T:: The base class for heightmap generator layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.OpacityInRange: A range of values of the existing heightmap data in which this layer's opacity will ramp from 0 to 1.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.OpacityOutRange: A range of values of the existing heightmap data in which this layer's opacity will ramp from 1 to 0.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.Name: The name of this layer. Only used in the generator editor interface.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.BlendMode: Specifies how this layer will be applied to the previous layer's results.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapL.HeightScale: The factor applied to the values of this layer.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.T:: A texture generator layer that maps heightmap values to a color range.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.HeightExponent: The exponent applied to each sampled height before it is mapped through the layer's `Colors` ramp. Values above 1 emphasize higher areas and values below 1 flatten the distribution.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.HeightMapName: The name of the heightmap, from the generator's set of named heightmaps, used as the value source. If no heightmap with this name exists, values are treated as zero.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.T:: A texture generator layer that converts a heightmap to a normal map.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.HeightExponent: The exponent applied to each sampled height before the normal map is computed. Values above 1 exaggerate tall features and values below 1 flatten them.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.HeightMapT.HeightMapName: The name of the heightmap, from the generator's set of named heightmaps, used as the height source. If no heightmap with this name exists, heights are treated as zero.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.T:: A heightmap generator layer that distorts the heights of pixels underneath using perlin noise.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.Distortion: The magnitude of the height displacement, as a fraction of the heightmap size. Each output cell is sampled from a source position offset by the perlin noise value times this amount, so larger values smear the heightmap more.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field that drives the displacement. It is sampled once for the horizontal offset and again with the seed bitwise-inverted for the vertical offset. Displaced samples always wrap around the heightmap edges.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the displacement noise based on proximity to the heightmap edges, letting the distortion fade toward the borders.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.T:: A texture generator layer that distorts the pixels of the layer underneath using perlin noise.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.Distortion: The magnitude of the pixel displacement, as a fraction of the texture size. Each output pixel is sampled from a source position offset by the perlin noise value times this amount, so larger values smear the image more.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.Wrap: When true, pixels whose displaced source falls past an edge sample from the opposite side of the texture. When false, sampling is clamped to the texture bounds.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field that drives the displacement. It is sampled once for the horizontal offset and again with the seed bitwise-inverted for the vertical offset, so the two axes are displaced independently.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinDist.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the displacement noise based on proximity to the texture edges, letting the distortion fade toward the borders.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinHeig.T:: A heightmap generator layer that is created using perlin noise.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinHeig.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field sampled once per cell to produce this layer's height values.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinHeig.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the sampled noise based on proximity to the heightmap edges, before it becomes the cell's height.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.T:: Stores modifications that should be applied to perlin noise values near the edges of the texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.LeftAdd: Added to the perlin noise value near the left edge of the texture, weighted by proximity to that edge. The weight is 1 at the left edge and falls to 0 at the right edge, shaped by `LeftExponent`. This addition is applied before `LeftMultiply`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.LeftMultiply: Scales the perlin noise value near the left edge. The noise is multiplied by a factor interpolated from 1 at the right edge to `LeftMultiply` at the left edge, so the default of 1 leaves it unchanged. Applied after `LeftAdd`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.LeftExponent: The exponent applied to the left-edge weight (the fraction of distance from the right edge). Values above 1 concentrate `LeftAdd` and `LeftMultiply` closer to the left edge, values below 1 spread them further inward. 1 gives a linear falloff.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.RightAdd: Added to the perlin noise value near the right edge, weighted by proximity to that edge. The weight is 1 at the right edge and falls to 0 at the left edge, shaped by `RightExponent`. Applied before `RightMultiply`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.RightMultiply: Scales the perlin noise value near the right edge. The noise is multiplied by a factor interpolated from 1 at the left edge to `RightMultiply` at the right edge, so the default of 1 leaves it unchanged. Applied after `RightAdd`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.RightExponent: The exponent applied to the right-edge weight. Values above 1 concentrate `RightAdd` and `RightMultiply` closer to the right edge. 1 gives a linear falloff.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.TopAdd: Added to the perlin noise value near the top edge, weighted by proximity to that edge. The weight is 1 at the top edge and falls to 0 at the bottom edge, shaped by `TopExponent`. Applied before `TopMultiply`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.TopMultiply: Scales the perlin noise value near the top edge. The noise is multiplied by a factor interpolated from 1 at the bottom edge to `TopMultiply` at the top edge, so the default of 1 leaves it unchanged. Applied after `TopAdd`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.TopExponent: The exponent applied to the top-edge weight. Values above 1 concentrate `TopAdd` and `TopMultiply` closer to the top edge. 1 gives a linear falloff.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.BottomAdd: Added to the perlin noise value near the bottom edge, weighted by proximity to that edge. The weight is 1 at the bottom edge and falls to 0 at the top edge, shaped by `BottomExponent`. Applied before `BottomMultiply`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.BottomMultiply: Scales the perlin noise value near the bottom edge. The noise is multiplied by a factor interpolated from 1 at the top edge to `BottomMultiply` at the bottom edge, so the default of 1 leaves it unchanged. Applied after `BottomAdd`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNois.BottomExponent: The exponent applied to the bottom-edge weight. Values above 1 concentrate `BottomAdd` and `BottomMultiply` closer to the bottom edge. 1 gives a linear falloff.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNorm.T:: A texture generator layer that uses perlin noise to generate a heightmap and then uses that heightmap to generate a normal map.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNorm.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field sampled per pixel as a height field, from which the layer derives a normal map by comparing neighboring heights.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinNorm.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the sampled noise heights based on proximity to the texture edges, before normals are computed.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinText.T:: A texture generator layer that maps perlin noise values to a color range.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinText.PerlinNoise: The perlin noise field sampled once per pixel to produce the value that is mapped through the layer's `Colors` ramp.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.PerlinText.EdgeEffects: Modifications applied to the sampled noise based on proximity to the texture edges, before it is mapped to a color.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.T:: A heightmap generator layer that remaps a range of existing height values to a different range of height values.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.InputRange: The range of existing height values that is remapped. A value at `InputRange` min maps to `OutputRange` min and a value at `InputRange` max maps to `OutputRange` max.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.OutputRange: The range of height values that `InputRange` is remapped onto.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.ClampInputValue: When true, input values outside `InputRange` are clamped to it before remapping, so they map to the ends of `OutputRange`. When false, the mapping is extrapolated for values outside the range.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.ClampOutputValue: When true, the remapped result is clamped to `OutputRange`. When false, results can fall outside `OutputRange` when the input falls outside `InputRange`.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.RemapRange.IgnoreOutsideInputRange: When true, height values outside `InputRange` are left untouched instead of being remapped.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SolidColor.T:: A texture generator layer that simply draws a solid color.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlHeigh.T:: A heightmap generator layer that "swirls" the underlying heightmap.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlHeigh.SwirlAmount: The amount of rotation at the center of each swirl, measured in full turns. The cell at a swirl's center rotates by `SwirlAmount` times 360 degrees, and the rotation decreases to zero at the swirl's edge.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlHeigh.SwirlExponent: The exponent controlling how the swirl's rotation falls off from center to edge. Values above 1 concentrate the twist near the center, and 1 gives a linear falloff.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlTextu.T:: A texture generator layer that "swirls" the underlying texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlTextu.SwirlAmount: The amount of rotation at the center of each swirl, measured in full turns. The pixel at a swirl's center rotates by `SwirlAmount` times 360 degrees, and the rotation decreases to zero at the swirl's edge.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.SwirlTextu.SwirlExponent: The exponent controlling how the swirl's rotation falls off from center to edge. Values above 1 concentrate the twist near the center, and 1 gives a linear falloff.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureGen.T:: Generates random textures using individual layer generators.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureGen.SampleMode: The sample mode of the texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureGen.BaseColor: The base color of the texture before the layers are applied.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureGen.Layers: The layers that are used to generate the texture.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.T:: The base class for texture generator layers.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.Name: The name of this layer. Only used in the generator editor interface.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.BlendMode: Specifies how this layer will be applied to the previous layer's results.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.ColorScale: The per-channel color scaling applied to this layer's color before it is blended onto the previous layer's results.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.ReadClippingMask: If true, the effects of this layer will be clipped to the alpha channel of the previous layer that has this set to false.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.WriteClippingMask: If true, this layer's alpha values will be written to the clipping mask.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.WriteTexture: If true, this layer will write to the texture.

Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.T:: A texture layer that combines multiple sub-layers into a single texture.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.ImportClippingMask: When true, the group starts with a copy of the incoming clipping mask so its sub-layers can read it. When false, the group's internal clipping mask starts empty.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.BaseColor: The color the group's internal texture is cleared to before its sub-layers are applied. Defaults to black.
Cosmoteer.Generators.Textures.TextureLay.SubLayers: The texture layers rendered into the group's own texture, in order, before the combined result is blended onto the layer below. Disabled sub-layers are skipped.

Cosmoteer.Gui.LatencyLevel.T:: Stores rules for a particular latency level.
Cosmoteer.Gui.LatencyLevel.MaxLatency: The upper ping bound this level covers, in seconds. The multiplayer lobby and scoreboard pick the first level in the list whose `MaxLatency` is at or above a player's measured latency, so order the list from lowest bound to highest. The default of positive infinity makes a level the catch-all for any ping.
Cosmoteer.Gui.LatencyLevel.Sprite: The signal-strength icon shown next to a player whose ping falls in this level's [[Cosmoteer.Gui.LatencyLevel.MaxLatency]] band.

Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.T:: Stores information about a planet rendered in the background of a menu screen.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.DoodadID: Planet doodad drawn in the menu background. Must resolve to a planet doodad rules entry, which is instantiated once behind the logo ship.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.Seed: Random seed passed to the planet doodad, so a fixed value reproduces the same planet appearance every time the menu loads.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.Location: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. The planet is instead positioned at the logo ship's bounding-box center, or the origin when there is no logo ship.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.Rotation: Orientation applied to the planet doodad.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules.Scale: Size multiplier passed to the planet doodad as its origin scale.

Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundRules.T:: Stores information about a menu background.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundRules.BackgroundStyle: Background style shown behind the menu. Resolved to a [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.BackgroundStyleRules|BackgroundStyleRules]] and rendered with a fresh random seed each time the menu opens.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundRules.Planet: Optional planet drawn in front of the background. Omit for a background with no planet. See [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundPlanetRules|MenuBackgroundPlanetRules]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuBackgroundRules.LightSource: Direction the scene light comes from. Only the X and Y components are used: they are negated and normalized, then combined with a fixed Z of `0.75` for the final light normal, so the Z you supply here has no effect.

Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.MainMenuBackgrounds: The backdrops available behind the title screen, each with its own background style, light direction, and planet. The title screen shows one at a time and steps through this array when the player cycles backgrounds or when the cycle-background setting advances it on each game launch.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.CreditsBackground: The backdrop shown behind the credits screen. Only its background style is used, without a planet or logo ship.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShip: The ship that flies in the title screen background, arriving and leaving with FTL jump animations. Vanilla points this at the ship carrying the game logo.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.MasterVolumeAdjustSound: Plays as feedback when the master volume slider in the audio settings changes, so the player hears the new level.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.EffectsVolumeAdjustSound: Plays through the effects audio group as feedback when the effects volume slider in the audio settings changes.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.InterfaceVolumeAdjustSound: Plays through the interface audio group as feedback when the interface volume slider in the audio settings changes.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.CountdownBeepSound: Plays on each tick of the game-start countdown in the multiplayer setup screen and Build Battle.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ChatMessageSound: Plays when a message arrives in the multiplayer chat box.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShipFlyInSound: Plays when the [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShip]] jumps into the title screen background.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShipFlyOutSound: Plays when the [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShip]] jumps out of the title screen background.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.MultiplayerJoinedSound: Plays when another player joins the multiplayer game setup lobby.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.MultiplayerLeftSound: Plays when a player leaves the multiplayer lobby or a game in progress.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShipFlyOutDelay: Seconds between [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShipFlyOutSound]] starting and the [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LogoShip]] actually jumping out. Vanilla uses 0.3.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ShipColorSprite: The ship image shown on the color chooser buttons in the accessibility settings tab, where the player overrides the player, enemy, ally, and neutral ship colors.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.PlayerInGameSprite: Icon shown in the multiplayer player list next to players who are currently in a game.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ContinueGameIcon: Icon on the title screen Continue button that loads the most recent save.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.NewGameIcon: Icon on the title screen New Game button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LoadGameIcon: Icon on the title screen Load Game button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.MultiplayerIcon: Icon on the title screen Multiplayer button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ExitIcon: Icon on the title screen Exit button. Also reused for the unstash button in Build Battle.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.NewsIcon: Icon on the title screen News button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.SettingsIcon: Icon on the Settings button of the title screen and multiplayer lobby screens.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ModsIcon: Icon on the Mods button of the title screen and multiplayer lobby screens.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ShipLibraryIcon: Icon for the Ship Library entry in the title screen menu. Also reused in the PvP scoreboard and Build Battle gui.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.CodexIcon: Icon for the Codex entry in the title screen menu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.RoadmapIcon: Icon for the Roadmap entry in the title screen menu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.CommunityIcon: Icon for the Community submenu in the title screen menu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.FeedbackIcon: Icon on the title screen Feedback button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.CreditsIcon: Icon on the title screen Credits button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.DiscordIcon: Icon for the Discord entry in the title screen Community submenu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.SteamIcon: Icon for the Steam entry in the title screen Community submenu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.RedditIcon: Icon for the Reddit entry in the title screen Community submenu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.BackIcon: Icon on the back button of the multiplayer lobby and game setup screens.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.OnlineIcon: Icon on the Online tab of the multiplayer lobby browser, which lists Steam lobbies.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LanIcon: Icon on the LAN tab of the multiplayer lobby browser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.DirectConnectIcon: Icon on the direct connect button of the multiplayer lobby browser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.SearchIcon: Icon displayed inside text search fields throughout the gui.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LockIcon: Icon marking password-protected games in the multiplayer game list.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.HostIcon: Icon marking the hosting player in the game setup screen and PvP scoreboard.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.AiIcon: Icon marking AI-controlled players in the game setup screen and PvP scoreboard.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.ObserverIcon: Icon marking observers in the PvP scoreboard.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.DisconnectedIcon: Icon shown in the PvP scoreboard for players who have left or disconnected from the game.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.WaitingIcon: Icon shown in the PvP scoreboard for players the game is currently waiting on.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.RefreshIcon: Icon on the refresh button of the Steam lobby list.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.InCommsIcon: Icon shown in the PvP scoreboard next to players who are currently in the comms menu.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.Spinner: The sprite used as the animated busy indicator wherever the gui shows a loading spinner. Rotates continuously at [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.SpinnerSpeed]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.SpinnerSpeed: Degrees per second the [[Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.Spinner]] rotates. Vanilla uses 360, one full revolution per second.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LatencyLevels: Thresholds mapping a player's measured latency to a connection quality icon in the multiplayer game list and scoreboard. Levels are checked in order, and the first whose `MaxLatency` in seconds is not exceeded supplies the sprite shown.
Cosmoteer.Gui.MenuRules.LobbyNameGenerator: Generates the random code appended to Steam lobby names when hosting an online game. Vanilla produces a three character sequence of letters and digits.

Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.T:: Stores the templates for various different kinds of widgets.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.PulsingTextShader: Shader applied to a label's text renderer to make it pulse for attention, used on the build toolbox vital-part warning message. Vanilla points it at pulsing.shader.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.RightClickCursor: Cursor shown while hovering a widget that offers an alt-click or right-click context action, such as items in the ship library, mods dialog, resource toolboxes and crew roster. Vanilla uses cursor_right_click.png.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.InvalidCursor: Cursor shown while the pointer is over a target where the current action cannot be performed, such as an unaffordable or out-of-range FTL jump, an invalid salvage target, or an invalid crew placement. Vanilla uses cursor_invalid.png.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.GoodTextColor: Green color used for positive or success text, applied to labels and buttons like download-complete notices, victory messages and valid crew counts. Vanilla aliases [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MoneyRefundTextColor]] to it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BadTextColor: Red color used for negative, error, or warning text, applied to failure and conflict labels, defeat messages, floating warning text, and warning indicator arrows.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MoneyTextColor: Cyan color used when displaying credit amounts the player can afford, applied to inline money text and to affordable ship-cost labels.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.InsufficientMoneyTextColor: Color used for credit amounts the player cannot afford, applied to money text and disabled purchase labels when funds are too low. Vanilla aliases it to [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BadTextColor]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MoneyRefundTextColor: Color used for positive credit changes such as refunds and payouts, applied to money text prefixed with a plus sign and the money icon. Vanilla aliases it to [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.GoodTextColor]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FameTextColor: Blue color used when displaying fame amounts in formatted UI text.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.InsufficientFameTextColor: Color used for fame amounts the player cannot afford, applied to fame text when the requirement is not met. Vanilla aliases it to [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BadTextColor]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FuelTextColor: Blue color used when displaying affordable fuel amounts in formatted UI text.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.InsufficientFuelTextColor: Color used for fuel amounts the player cannot afford, applied to fuel text when the available amount is short.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.LimitedTextColor: Orange color used to mark a value that is capped or limited, applied to resource transfer max labels and resource limit fields and stars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ResizerTLBRIcon: Sprite intended as the top-left to bottom-right diagonal resize handle, the counterpart to [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ResizerTRBLIcon]]. Vanilla points it at widgets_resizer_tlbr.png, though no read site appears in the current game code.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ResizerTRBLIcon: Sprite drawn as a corner resize handle, used for the resize grip in the ship Miniview window. Vanilla points it at widgets_resizer_trbl.png.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MoverIcon: Sprite intended as a drag-to-move handle. Vanilla points it at widgets_mover.png, though no read site appears in the current game code.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DialogOpenSoundEffect: Sound effect played on the interface audio group whenever a dialog opens. Vanilla plays sounds/dialog_open.wav at volume 0.25.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DialogCloseSoundEffect: Sound effect played on the interface audio group whenever a dialog closes. Vanilla plays sounds/dialog_close.wav at volume 0.25.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DragAndDropCompleteSoundEffect: Sound effect assigned as the drop sound of drag-and-drop targets, played when a dragged item is successfully dropped such as reorganizing ships into folders.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DisabledIconShader: Shader applied to a button's image sprite to dim it while the button is disabled, used on undo, redo, build, repair, copy, cut, paste, delete, and similar toolbar icons when their action is unavailable. Vanilla points it at disabled.shader.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.PulsingIconShader: Shader applied to an icon sprite to make it pulse for attention, used on the repair-tool overlay sprite of the ship build button. Vanilla points it at pulsing.shader.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.GrayscaleIconShader: Shader applied to an icon sprite to desaturate it, used for part buttons that are locked in the demo or that the player cannot currently afford, and for grayed-out scoreboard icons. Vanilla points it at grayscale.shader.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BlurShader: Shader used to blur the background behind a widget, producing the frosted-glass effect behind dialogs, tooltips, menus, context menus, and drop lists when fancy UI effects are enabled. Runs once per pass counted by [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BlurPasses]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BlurPasses: Number of blur iterations applied behind a widget with [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BlurShader]]. Each iteration blurs horizontally and then vertically, so the draw count is twice this value. Vanilla sets it to 4.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BlurFallbackMaterial: Material used to tint the area behind a widget instead of blurring it when fancy UI effects are disabled, giving a flat translucent backing behind dialogs and menus.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DefaultFont: Engine-wide default font. Every widget and text renderer that does not specify its own font uses this one. Vanilla loads the Play and Microsoft YaHei faces with fixed-width digits.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ShadowFont: Font that renders text with a soft black drop shadow, applied throughout the UI to labels and buttons that need to stay readable over busy backgrounds such as build, crew, ship name, chat, and title-screen text. Vanilla derives it from [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DefaultFont]] with a blurred black shadow pass.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.GlowFont: Font that renders text with a soft glow, applied to attention labels such as input-binding conflict warnings and the wishlist prompt. Vanilla derives it from [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DefaultFont]] with a blur pass behind the foreground.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ShadowGlowFont: Font that renders text with both a black shadow and a glow pass, applied to the build toolbox vital-part warning message. Vanilla derives it from [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DefaultFont]] with a shadow pass and a glow pass.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DefaultCursor: Engine-wide default mouse cursor, shown whenever no widget or tool overrides the pointer. Vanilla uses cursor_arrow.png.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.Widget: Base template for every GUI widget, holding position and the set of attached components. Plain widgets copy their initial settings from this template, and through the chain of other default templates it seeds the baseline for every widget class in the game.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.StaticWidget: Default template for widgets drawn with a nine-slice background that do not react to input. Static widgets copy their settings from this template, and the vanilla version establishes the grey semi-transparent box look that boxes, labels and images build on.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DynamicWidget: Default template for widgets that swap their nine-slice depending on interaction state such as normal, highlighted and pressed. Interactive widgets copy their settings from this template, and the game wires the default highlight and click shader-time animations onto it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SimpleBox: Default template for containers that hold child widgets without arranging them. Simple boxes copy their settings from this template, which inherits the [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.StaticWidget]] box background in vanilla.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.LayoutBox: Default template for containers that automatically arrange their children according to a chosen layout mode. Layout boxes copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ScrollBox: Default template for layout boxes that show scroll bars when their children overflow the box. Scroll boxes copy their settings from this template, and vanilla wires the fade and scale animations onto its scroll bars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ListBox: Default template for scroll boxes that track the selection state of their children and by default stretch them horizontally from top to bottom. List boxes copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.WindowBox: Default template for scroll boxes with a title bar that the user can move and resize. Window boxes copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabBox: Default template for containers whose child pages are switched between using tab buttons. Tab boxes copy their settings from this template, with the buttons and pages coming from [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabButton]] and [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabPageBox]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabButton: Default template for the clickable button in a tab strip that selects a page of a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabBox]]. Each tab button copies its settings from this template, which vanilla inherits from [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SelectableButton]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabPageBox: Default template for the scrollable page container that a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabBox]] shows for the selected tab. Each tab page copies its settings from this template, and the game wires the slide animation played when switching tabs onto it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.Label: Default template for widgets that display a simple text label. Labels copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.Image: Default template for widgets that display a single customizable image. Images copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.Button: Default template for clickable text buttons that react to hover and press. Buttons copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SelectableButton: Default template for buttons that the user can select. Selectable buttons copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToggledImageButton: Default template for selectable buttons that carry two full sets of state nine-slices for their unselected and selected looks plus a sprite. Such buttons copy their settings from this template, and vanilla builds its on and off switch buttons on it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ImageButton: Default template for clickable buttons that show an image with text on top. Image buttons copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ListItem: Default template for selectable buttons that highlight their background when selected, used for rows in list boxes. List items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ImageListItem: Default template for selectable list items with an image and text on top. Such items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TreeItem: Default template for selectable items in a tree view that can hold collapsible sub-items. Tree items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToggleCheckButton: Default template for toggle buttons that show a check sprite when selected. Check toggles copy their settings from this template, which vanilla draws as a filled or empty check box.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToggleRadioButton: Default template for toggle buttons that show a radio sprite when selected. Radio toggles copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToggleExpanderButton: Default template for toggle buttons that show an expander sprite for collapsing and expanding a section. Expander toggles copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DropButton: Default template for buttons that display another widget near them when clicked. Drop buttons copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DropList: Default template for list boxes opened by clicking a button and shown as a drop-down beneath it. Drop-down lists copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HorizontalScrollBar: Default template for horizontal scroll bars whose value is changed by dragging a paddle or clicking increment and decrement buttons. Horizontal scroll bars copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.VerticalScrollBar: Default template for vertical scroll bars, the vertical counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HorizontalScrollBar]]. Vertical scroll bars copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HorizontalSlider: Default template for scroll bars styled as a draggable horizontal slider. Sliders copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressBar: Default template for progress bars, a static widget with an overlay sprite clipped according to a value. Progress bars copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SingleLineTextEditField: Default template for single-line editable text fields. Single-line fields copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SingleLinePasswordTextEditField: Default template for single-line editable fields that mask the entered text. Password fields copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MultiLineTextEditField: Default template for multi-line editable text fields. Multi-line fields copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MultiLineWrappedTextEditField: Default template for multi-line editable fields that word-wrap their text. Wrapped multi-line fields copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuBar: Default template for bars meant to dock to the top of the window and hold menu categories. Menu bars copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuItem: Default template for buttons meant to appear inside a menu category. Menu items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuToggleCheckItem: Default template for checkable menu items. Such items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuToggleRadioItem: Default template for radio-style menu items. Such items copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuCategory: Default template for the list of menu items reached by clicking a header item. Menu categories copy their settings from this template, and the game wires the open animation of its menu box.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuSubCategory: Default template for the list of menu items reached by mousing over an item in another menu. Submenus copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MenuSeparator: Default template for the line that separates items within a menu category. Separators copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ContextMenu: Default template for lists of menu items that can be shown on demand anywhere on the screen. Context menus copy their settings from this template, and the game wires its open animation and click bindings.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToolTipLabel: Default template for labels extended to display tool tips. Tooltip labels copy their settings from this template, and the game sets its display delay to half a second.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToolTipBox: Default template for the scrollable wrapper around a tooltip label that allows unfocused scrolling with a key-bind and the scroll wheel. Tooltip boxes copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ZeroButtonDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message with no button for the user to close them, expecting the application to close them. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.OneButtonDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message and prompt the user to press a single button. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template, and the game labels its button Okay bound to the confirm key.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TwoButtonDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message and prompt a choice between two options. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template, and the game labels the options Okay and Cancel.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ThreeButtonDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message and prompt a choice among three options. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template, and the game labels the options Yes, No and Cancel.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.OneButtonTextEntryDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message and prompt the user to edit text and press a single button. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TwoButtonTextEntryDialog: Default template for dialogs that show a message and prompt the user to edit text and choose between two options. Such dialogs copy their settings from this template, and the game labels the options Okay and Cancel.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TwoButtonPasswordEntryDialog: Default template for two-option text entry dialogs whose field masks the entered text. Password entry dialogs copy their settings from this template.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HollowWidget: Styles a hollow recessed frame drawn from the alternate box sprite region so a container shows an inset outline instead of a filled panel. Dialogs and toolboxes copy it onto their list and layout boxes, including the saved-game list, mods lists, settings tabs, tab-strip boxes, and many build, crew, paint, and resources toolbox panels.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MaskedSimpleBox: Adds an alpha nine-slice child mask to the plain [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SimpleBox]] so child content is clipped to rounded corners. The minimap, miniview, and the decal size picker popout build from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MaskedLayoutBox: Adds the rounded alpha child mask to a docked [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.LayoutBox]]. The new game config, career setup, and clear objects dialogs build boxes from it, and the vote window, comms toolbox, and the POI and planet doodad config windows copy its child mask onto themselves.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MaskedScrollBox: Adds the rounded alpha child mask to a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ScrollBox]] so scrolled content is clipped to the panel corners. Vanilla data uses it as the menu dropdown box and as the base for the tooltip box.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MaskedListBox: Adds the rounded alpha child mask to a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ListBox]]. The load and save game dialog's saved-game list and the paint toolbox layers list build from it, and vanilla data uses it as the drop-list list box.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MaskedTabBox: Adds the rounded alpha child mask to a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TabBox]]. Only the styling definition exists and no code or other data consumers were found.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BoxInnerShadow: Styles a non-interactive overlay that fills its parent and draws an inner shadow nine-slice, leaving input to pass through. The minimap and miniview add it as a child so their framed viewports get a recessed shadow along the inside edge.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SquareButton: Styles a compact square button using the un-rounded box sprite. Toolbox action buttons copy it, including build and paint rotate, flip, cut, copy, paste, delete and invert, plus the game speed steppers, eject and trashcan buttons, and formation buttons.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatButton: Styles a flat borderless button whose frame only appears on hover or press. It backs menu and toggle buttons and is copied onto the game menu button, ship command button, workshop preview, forfeit and new-ship buttons, and similar inline controls.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.OkayButton: Styles a standard button with green confirm text. Dialogs create their okay, submit, start, join, next and close buttons from it across the load and save, settings, feedback, news, mods, hire crew, and ship info dialogs among others.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.GoodButton: Styles a green affirmative button with a green-tinted frame and green text. Construct, ready, start, activate, do-trade and transfer buttons build from it, along with the title screen wishlist button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.BadButton: Styles a red cautionary button with a red-tinted frame and red text. Cancel, decline and deactivate buttons build from it, including cancel-all and cancel-ready in the build toolbox, the multiplayer cancel countdown, mod deactivate, FTL cancel jump, and mission decline.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.TitleBarButton: Styles a flat title-bar button that stays borderless normally and shows its frame only when highlighted or pressed. Vanilla data uses it as the base for [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.UndoButton]] and [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.RedoButton]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.VerticalSeparator: Styles a one-pixel-wide vertical divider line drawn from a thin sprite strip. Only the styling definition exists and no code or other data consumers were found.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuButton: Styles a large flat menu button using the glow font at size 20 with extra side padding. The multiplayer game setup screen builds its match results button from it, and it is the base for [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuIconButton]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuIconButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuButton]] with left-aligned text and a 48 pixel icon on the left. The title screen builds most of its main menu entries from it, and the lobby and game setup screens use it for their back, settings, mods, and direct connect buttons.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SelectedMainMenuButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuIconButton]] so the selected highlight frame is always shown. The lobby screen applies it to the online or LAN entry that matches the current screen to mark it as active.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuCategory: Combines [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuIconButton]] styling with dropdown menu behavior. The title screen builds its community and extras dropdown category button from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.MainMenuItem: Styles a taller 36 pixel menu entry with size 20 text and an icon. The title screen dropdown menus create their items from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.CodexItem: Styles a codex list entry as a [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ListItem]] with panel open and close sounds on selection. The codex dialog and its page window items build their entries from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToolButton: Styles a selectable tool button that combines flat button and image list item behavior with an all-around selected frame. Build, paint, resources, and crew toolboxes create their tool icons from it, along with the ship command selectable and the galaxy map FTL jump button.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.IconItem: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ToolButton]] with a filled normal-state frame so icons always sit in a visible cell. The texture picker, paint scheme icons, and the creative doodads toolbox build their entries from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.PopoutButton: Styles a button whose nine-slice has a downward popout tab and an extended right border. The part color picker, part popout toggle, and decal size picker buttons build from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatPopoutButton: Styles the flat variant of the popout tab button combining flat button and image list item behavior. The build and paint toolbox brush buttons and the ship gui popout button build from it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SwitchButton: Styles a tall toggle switch with a raised frame and a sliding indicator strip along the bottom border. The part switched build toggle button uses it for the plain switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.OffAlertSwitchButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SwitchButton]] with an alerting sprite for the off state. The part switched build toggle button uses it for the off-alert switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.OnAlertSwitchButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.SwitchButton]] with a mirrored alerting sprite for the on state. The part switched build toggle button uses it for the on-alert switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatSwitchButton: Styles the flat version of the sliding toggle switch. Build, resources, paint, and crew toolboxes build blueprint, mirror, supply, and target toggles from it, the ship gui builds its command switch, and the part switched toggle button uses it for the plain switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatOffAlertSwitchButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatSwitchButton]] with an alerting off-state sprite. The part switched toggle button uses it for the off-alert switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatOnAlertSwitchButton: Extends [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FlatSwitchButton]] with a mirrored alerting on-state sprite. The part switched toggle button uses it for the on-alert switch style.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.LeftTabButton: Restyles the tab selector button for tab columns stacked down the left edge rather than across the top. Pairs with [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.VerticalTabPageBox]] to build the left-hand tab strip of the settings dialog.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.VerticalTabPageBox: Styles the scrolling page body shown for each tab in a vertically stacked tab layout, and its tab-switch animation slides pages vertically instead of horizontally. The settings dialog pairs it with [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.LeftTabButton]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HorizontalExpanderButton: Styles an expander toggle whose selected state shows a sideways chevron, driving the collapsible custom-formations row in the fleet formations panel.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.VerticalExpanderButton: Styles an expander toggle with up and down chevrons and a centered icon for vertically collapsing sections. Only the styling definition exists and no game code currently instantiates it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.CategoryBox: Styles a borderless container for collapsible category groups such as the settings dialog sections, the multiplayer mode rules box, and the creative doodads toolbox. Receives an expand animation that scales the box open from zero height.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.FixedWindowBox: Provides the window frame used by the game's non-movable toolbox and popup windows including the build, resources, paint, crew, and comms toolboxes plus the FTL jump and multiplayer vote windows. Shares the standard look of [[Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.WindowBox]].
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressBarWhite: Styles a progress bar with a white fill, used for the countdown or capture bar shown by the PvP elimination game mode.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ThinProgressBarGood: Styles a slim horizontal bar with a green fill, used for the positive reputation progress bar in the career reputation tab.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ThinProgressBarBad: Styles a slim horizontal bar with a red fill, used for the negative reputation progress bar in the career reputation tab.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ThinProgressBarFame: Styles a slim horizontal bar with a fame-tinted fill, used for the fame progress bar in the career reputation tab.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressDotEmpty: Styles the unfilled milestone marker dot placed along the career reputation progress bars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressDotGood: Styles the green milestone marker dot for reached positive milestones on the career reputation bars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressDotBad: Styles the red milestone marker dot for negative milestones on the career reputation bars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ProgressDotFame: Styles the fame-colored milestone marker dot for the fame track in the career reputation tab.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.StatBar: Styles the progress bar behind each ship statistic readout, used by the ship stat bars in the build toolbox stats panel such as command points.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.IdealStatBar: Styles the thin green marker overlaid on a ship stat bar to indicate the ideal or target value, drawn by the build toolbox ship stat bars.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerMenuDown: Styles a three-line hamburger menu category whose dropdown opens downward, used for the options menus in the load/save, mods, ship library, roster, and role edit dialogs among others.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerMenuUp: Styles a hamburger menu category whose dropdown opens upward, used for the options menus anchored near the bottom of the build, paint, resources, and crew toolboxes.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerButtonDown: Styles a hamburger menu that adds a full button background and opens downward, used for the option menus in the creative battle helper, PvP and career config screens, and the ship info dialog.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerButtonUp: Styles a button-backed hamburger menu opening upward. Only the styling definition exists and no game code currently instantiates it.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerFlatButtonDown: Styles a hamburger menu with a flat button background opening downward, used for the option menus in the multiplayer player list, game setup screen, and color picker.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.HamburgerFlatButtonUp: Styles a hamburger menu with a flat button background opening upward, used for the menus on ship and part cards, the crew and comms trade toolboxes, and the crew and resource transfer window.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.UndoButton: Styles the undo icon button on toolbar title bars, used by the build, paint, resources, and crew toolboxes.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.RedoButton: Styles the redo icon button on toolbar title bars, used by the build, paint, resources, and crew toolboxes.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowUpLeft: Styles the up-left diagonal arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowUp: Styles the upward arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowUpRight: Styles the up-right diagonal arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowRight: Styles the rightward arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowDownRight: Styles the down-right diagonal arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowDown: Styles the downward arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowDownLeft: Styles the down-left diagonal arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.ArrowLeft: Styles the leftward arrow cell in the eight-way ship direction chooser.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.PopoutConnector: Styles the small connector graphic that visually links a popped-out panel back to its originating button, used by the build and paint color pickers, the formations box, the decal size picker, and part popout toggle buttons.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DragCandidateNineSlice: Styles the outline drawn around a valid drop target while a drag is in progress, shown on ship library folder items during drag and drop.
Cosmoteer.Gui.WidgetRules.DragHoverNineSlice: Styles the stronger highlight drawn on the drop target directly under the cursor, shown on ship library folder items when a dragged item hovers over them.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.T:: Stores rules for GUI elements specific to career mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.Comms: The icons, sounds, cursors and beam materials used by the comms tool, the hailing banners and the comm window.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.Missions: The icons, sounds and animations used by the mission log, the fame and reputation level banners and the mission notifications.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.DangerLevelColors: Color stops that tint danger tier labels, each entry pairing a tier with a color. Colors for tiers between two stops are interpolated in HSVA, and tiers above the last stop use its color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.TierValueMaximums: The largest ship value in credits that still counts as each tier, in ascending order. A ship's estimated tier is the position of the first entry its value fits into, and anything above the last entry becomes one tier higher than the list length.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeGuiRule.TierValueCombineOverhead: The per-ship value overhead removed when several ships are summed into one fleet tier. A fleet of N ships of tier T is valued as N times its tier maximum minus this overhead, plus the overhead once.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeMapRule.T:: Stores rules for map elements specific to career mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeMapRule.FriendliesPresentSprite: The badge drawn on a galaxy map node that holds friendly ships. It is skipped for the node the player is currently in, and its size is given in galaxy map world units before the camera scale is applied.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeMapRule.FriendliesPresentSpriteOffset: Offset of the badge from the node's center, in galaxy map world units. It rotates with the camera and scales with the zoom, so the badge keeps its place beside the node.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.T:: Stores rules for the main career mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Icon: The small career mode icon shown beside the mode name in the multiplayer game browser and at the top of the multiplayer game setup screen.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.LargeIcon: The large career mode icon shown on the single player new game screen where the player picks a game mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Gui: Career specific interface rules, covering the comms window, the mission log and HUD, the danger level color ramp and the fleet tier value tables.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Map: Galaxy map extras drawn only in career mode. It currently holds just the marker used for nodes where the player has ships parked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.StarterShips: The ships the player can cycle through on the single player new game screen. The player's remembered pick is stored as an index into this list, so inserting or reordering entries changes which ship an existing profile preselects.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.MapSizes: The galaxy sizes offered in the new game drop list, each naming the galaxy generator that builds the map. There is no default flag, so the multiplayer setup screen preselects the first entry.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CombatDifficultyLevels: The combat difficulty levels offered in the new game drop lists, in display order. Exactly one entry should set [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyRules.IsDefault]], because the game looks the default up by that flag when a save has no stored difficulty and throws if no entry carries it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.EconDifficultyLevels: The economy difficulty levels offered in the new game drop lists, in display order. Exactly one entry should set [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRules.IsDefault]], because the game looks the default up by that flag when a save has no stored difficulty and throws if no entry carries it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CrewScarcityLevels: The crew scarcity levels offered in the new game drop lists, in display order. Exactly one entry should set [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.IsDefault]], because the game looks the default up by that flag when a save has no stored level and throws if no entry carries it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Techs: The whole tech tree. Every `ID` and `OtherIDs` entry across the list must be unique or loading throws, and at load time a prerequisite that points at a tech which some other tech lists in its `UpgradedFrom` is rewritten to require those upgrade techs instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.SectorTypes: The kinds of star system a galaxy node can be, each with its own system generator and trade routes. IDs must be unique or loading throws, and a node with no explicit sector type falls back to the first entry in the list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.TradeShips: The pool of AI trade ships that fly between stations and gates, keyed by an id that saved trade traffic refers back to.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Exploration: Fog of war and breadcrumb trail settings for the in-system view.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Wanted: Settings for the wanted system, covering how long a faction keeps hunting the player and how its police ships are spawned.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.Dialogue: Settings for comms dialogue, surrender negotiation, truces and the money they cost or pay out.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.MissionMetatypes: The mission metatypes available in career mode, keyed by id. A mission stores only its metatype id and looks the rules back up here.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.MissionCategories: The categories that group entries in the mission log. List order is the display order, since a category's sort value is simply its index in this list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.SystemVisitMissions: The template for the automatic "visit this system" mission that career mode creates for every map node except the one the player starts in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.MaxPlayers: The number of player slots reserved for humans. Indices 0 up to this value minus one count as human players, and the multiplayer setup screen offers lobbies from 2 up to this many. Vanilla uses 4.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.AllowedShipClasses: The ship classes a design must belong to for career mode to consider it legal, which also filters the hulls offered by the new ship button. Vanilla allows only `cosmoteer.terran`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.AIStationAvoidanceDistance: How far beyond a space station's bounding circle, in tiles, AI ships steer around it. The same distance is used as a plain radius around a stasis space station. Vanilla uses 3000.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.StationOperationalEnemyCheckDistance: The radius in tiles around a shut down space station that must be free of enemy ships and enemy stasis spawners before the station switches to operating. A station that is not operating keeps all of its weapons suppressed and cannot be hailed for trade or construction help.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.ReputationLossPerValueDamageMilitary: Reputation lost per point of ship value the player destroys on a faction's military ships. The loss is scaled by the economy difficulty's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRules.ReputationRewardFactor]] and accumulates as a fraction until it reaches whole points. Vanilla uses 1/10000.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.ReputationLossPerValueDamageCivilian: The same per value rate as [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.ReputationLossPerValueDamageMilitary]], applied when the damaged ship is civilian. Vanilla charges 4/10000, four times the military rate.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.SalvagingDisabledMoneyRewardFactor: Multiplies mission money rewards when the game was started with salvaging disabled, compensating for the lost salvage income. Vanilla doubles them.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.NonJunkShipCategorySets: Sets of part categories that decide when a battered AI ship turns into junk. If for any single set the ship's blueprint contained parts in those categories but no working ones are left, the hulk is handed to the junk player and its crew is reassigned to nobody. Vanilla uses reactors, command parts, and weapons together with thrusters.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.NpcSpawnedResourceFractions: Per resource, the fraction of a full storage that non player ships spawned with the initial galaxy start with. A fresh roll from the range is made for each storage on the ship. Vanilla gives new NPC ships 25% to 75% of their hyperium.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.FameTitles: The player's fame ranks, listed in ascending fame order. The first entry is the rank the player starts at, and the game walks the list forward while the player's fame still meets the next entry's threshold.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.ReputationTitles: The per faction reputation ranks, listed in ascending reputation order. The first entry is the fallback used below every threshold.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CustomMarkerDoodad: The doodad spawned when the player drops a custom marker with the button next to the minimap. It has to name a POI doodad, since the game casts the looked up rules to that type without checking.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CustomMarkerIcon: The sprite for the custom marker tool button placed just above the minimap.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.T:: Stores rules for a particular difficulty level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.ID: The identifier this level is stored under in save games and in the multiplayer input that changes difficulty mid game. Loading a save whose stored id no longer matches any entry throws, so renaming an id breaks existing saves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.NameKey: Localization key for the level's name as it appears in the combat difficulty drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.TipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown when hovering this level in the combat difficulty drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.IsDefault: Marks this level as the preselected one in the new game screens and the one restored when a save has no stored combat difficulty. Exactly one entry in [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CombatDifficultyLevels]] should set it, since the lookup throws when none does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.DamageVsEnemies: Multiplies all damage a human player deals to a non player ship. It is not applied when the target has already become junk. Vanilla ranges from 70% on very hard to 140% on easy.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.DamageFromEnemies: Multiplies all damage dealt to a human player's ships by anything that is not a human player. Vanilla ranges from 70% on easy to 140% on very hard.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.IsPlayerInvulnerable: Makes every ship belonging to a human player immune to damage. Vanilla uses it for the "no death" level, which also marks itself [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyRules.DisabledInIronmanMode]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.ResourceDrainVsEnemies: Multiplies the amount of stored resources that player weapons drain out of enemy ships, the counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyRules.DamageVsEnemies]] for drain effects.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.ResourceDrainFromEnemies: Multiplies the amount of stored resources that enemy weapons drain out of the player's ships.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.DisabledInIronmanMode: Hides this level from the difficulty drop lists while ironman mode is enabled, forcing a switch to the first level that allows it. Vanilla marks the "no death" level this way.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.StatusFactorsVsEnemies: Has no effect.
