The table would scale the chance and strength of each status the player applies to an enemy, but the only code that reads it is `GetStatusFactors`, which nothing in the game calls. Its sibling damage multiplier [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyRules.DamageVsEnemies]] does work.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.StatusFactorsFromEnemies: Has no effect. The table would scale the chance and strength of each status an enemy applies to the player, but the only code that reads it is `GetStatusFactors`, which nothing in the game calls. See [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyRules.StatusFactorsVsEnemies]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.EnemyCombatNoBuildRadius: Radius in tiles around a ship inside which a recently firing enemy blocks construction, and the radius checked around the target spot before a brand new ship may be started. The check only runs in the `InstantCredits` and `InstantResources` construction modes, so with vanilla rules it is reached only after the player disables salvaging or crew construction. Vanilla uses 800, or 0 on the "no death" level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CombatDifficultyR.EnemyCombatNoBuildDuration: Seconds after an enemy last fired a weapon during which it still counts as blocking construction. The same value doubles as how long a failed construction check is cached before it is retested. Vanilla uses 5 seconds.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.T:: Stores rules related to the GUI for managing the ship's comms.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.ToolIcon: The icon on the comms button in the ship HUD's tool bar, next to the crew and resources buttons. Clicking it opens the comms toolbox.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailIcon: The icon on the "Hail" button of each ship row in the comms toolbox, shown for ships the player can call. Ships that are already hailing the player get accept and decline buttons instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.AcceptHailIcon: The icon on the "Accept" button of a comms toolbox row for a ship that is currently hailing the player. Accepting skips the outgoing hail and opens the comm window directly.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.DeclineHailIcon: The icon on the small decline button next to the accept button of an incoming hail. Clicking it drops the hail and plays [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.HailFailedSound]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailingIcon: The icon on the floating banner shown near the top of the screen while a call is being placed and while an AI ship is hailing the player. The banner pulses in opacity until the call resolves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.AIHailingIcon: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. It was meant to be the banner icon for an incoming AI hail, but both branches of the check that picks the icon use [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.HailingIcon]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailingFailedIcon: The icon on the banner shown when a called ship does not answer. The banner fades out between 1.5 and 2.5 seconds after it appears.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailingSound: Plays when the player places a call and when an AI ship starts hailing the player. For a player-placed call the duration of its first sound also decides how long the hailing banner stays up before the answer resolves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailAnsweredSound: Plays when the called ship answers and the comm window opens.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailFailedSound: Plays when a called ship refuses to answer and when the player declines an incoming hail from the comms toolbox.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenSound: Plays at the start of the "truce broken" screen animation, which fires when the player breaks a truce and loses fame for it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.CursorValid: The mouse cursor shown while the comms tool is active and a callable ship is under the cursor.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.CursorInvalid: The cursor intended for the comms tool when no callable ship is under the cursor. The game never shows it, because the input handler returns early when there is no valid target, so the cursor check always picks [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.CursorValid]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.RadioUnderlayUntargetedMaterial: The material of the radio beam drawn from the selected ship toward the mouse while the comms tool is active and no ship is targeted. The beam ends in a circle twice the selected ship's bounding radius.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.RadioUnderlayTargetedMaterial: The material of the radio beam drawn from the calling ship to the ship the player is about to call.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailUnderlayUntargetedMaterial: The material of the radio beam drawn from each ship hailing the player back to the player ship that would answer, while that hailer is not under the cursor.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailUnderlayInCommsMaterial: The material of the radio beam drawn between two ships that already have a comm window open with each other.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailUnderlayTargetedMaterial: The material used in place of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.HailUnderlayUntargetedMaterial]] for the hailing ship the player is currently pointing at.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HailUnderlayDecliningMaterial: The material used in place of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.HailUnderlayTargetedMaterial]] while the mouse is over that hailer's decline button, to signal that clicking will drop the call.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.MissionsTabIcon: The icon of the missions tab in the comm window. The tab only appears if the called ship's AI is willing to offer missions to the caller.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HireTabIcon: The icon of the crew hiring tab in the comm window. The tab only appears if the called ship's AI is willing to sell crew to the caller.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TradeTabIcon: The icon of the resource trading tab in the comm window. The tab only appears if the called ship's AI is willing to trade with the caller.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TechsTabIcon: The icon of the tech purchase tab in the comm window. The tab only appears if the called ship's AI is willing to sell techs to the caller.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.DialogueTabIcon: The icon of the dialogue tab in the comm window. The tab only appears if the called ship's AI has dialogue for the caller.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.DefaultDialogueLineIcon: The icon shown next to a dialogue line and on its reply buttons when the dialogue itself supplies no override icon. Its sprite size also fixes the size of the icon box in the dialogue tab.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.AcceptSurrenderIcon: The icon on the reply button that accepts an AI ship's offer to surrender in exchange for a payout.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.RejectSurrenderIcon: The icon on the reply button that turns down a surrender offer, whether the AI or the player made it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.OfferSurrenderIcon: The icon on the reply button the player uses to surrender to an AI ship or to pay off a bounty that ship's faction holds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.HoldGuiOnAICallDuration: Seconds the hailing banner stays on screen after an AI ship starts hailing the player. Vanilla uses 3.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenTitleColorAnim: Color keyframes animating the large "Truce Broken" headline, each entry a time in seconds paired with a color. Alpha components above 255 produce a bloom flash.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenInfoColorAnim: Color keyframes animating the smaller explanation line under the "Truce Broken" headline, each entry a time in seconds paired with a color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenFameAnimIn: Color keyframes fading in the fame loss counter below the truce broken text. It starts after [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRules.TruceBrokenDelayBeforeFameDuration]] has elapsed.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenFameAnimOut: Color keyframes fading the fame loss counter back out once the count down has finished and the hold delay has elapsed.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenFameTickDuration: Seconds the fame loss counter takes to count from 0 down to the full amount of fame lost.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenDelayBeforeFameDuration: Seconds between the "Truce Broken" text appearing and the fame loss counter appearing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.TruceBrokenHoldAnimDelayOut: Seconds the finished fame loss counter is held on screen before its fade out animation plays.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.LoopCommsWaveEmptySound: The looping sound played while the comms tool is active and pointed at empty space rather than a callable ship. It stops while a call is already in progress.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.LoopCommsWaveTargettingSound: The looping sound played while the comms tool is locked onto a callable ship. It replaces the empty wave loop and also stops while a call is in progress.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Comms.CommsGuiRul.CommsWaveFalloffDuration: Seconds a comms wave loop takes to fade from full volume to silence once it stops applying. Volume drops by the frame delta divided by this value each frame.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.T:: Stores rules for a particular crew scarcity level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.ID: The identifier this level is stored under in save games and in the multiplayer input that changes crew scarcity mid game. Loading a save whose stored id no longer matches any entry throws, so renaming an id breaks existing saves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.NameKey: Localization key for the level's name as it appears in the crew scarcity drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.TipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown when hovering this level in the crew scarcity drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.IsDefault: Marks this level as the preselected one in the new game screens and the one restored when a save has no stored crew scarcity. Exactly one entry in [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.CrewScarcityLevels]] should set it, since the lookup throws when none does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.CrewFamePrereqFameRange: The fame span the crew cap is spread over. A crew count at the bottom of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.CrewFamePrereqCountRange]] requires the minimum fame and one at the top requires the maximum, interpolating linearly in between. All vanilla levels run from 0 to the tier table's maximum fame.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.CrewFamePrereqFameRoundToMultiple: Rounds the interpolated fame requirement to a multiple of this before it is matched against the fame titles, which keeps the crew cap stepping in tidy increments. Vanilla rounds to 5.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CrewScarcityRules.CrewFamePrereqCountRange: Total crew the player may have at the lowest and the highest fame. The maximum is a hard ceiling, since asking for more crew than this reports that it can never be hired. Vanilla runs 24 to 1500 on standard and 2000 to 2000 on max, which removes the limit entirely.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DangerLevelColorR.T:: Stores rules for how a danger level's color should be determined.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DangerLevelColorR.Tier: The danger tier this stop of the color ramp is pinned to. Entries have to be listed in ascending tier order, since the game takes the first entry whose tier is at least the tier being colored. Vanilla pins only tiers 1 and 18.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DangerLevelColorR.Color: The color used at this stop. Tiers between two stops are blended in HSVA space, tiers below the first stop take its color outright, and tiers above the last stop take the last color. Vanilla runs green at tier 1 to red at tier 18.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.T:: Stores rules related to the "dialogue" system.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.SurrenderAreaCheckRadius: Radius in world units around the AI ship in which ships are gathered for a surrender check. Their combined firepower decides whether a surrender is offered and at what price, and the most valuable enemy ship inside it speaks for its team. Vanilla uses 1500, which the UI displays as 1.5 km.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.AISurrenderDuration: How long the truce and the protection agreement last after an AI ship surrenders to the player. Vanilla uses `Infinity` so the truce only ends when the player breaks it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerSurrenderDuration: How long the truce lasts after the player surrenders to a factionless AI team. It also ends early if the player leaves the area, see [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerSurrenderCancelDistance]]. Vanilla uses 1200, meaning 20 minutes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerSurrenderCancelDistance: Distance in world units the player's ship may move from the spot where it surrendered before the truce is cancelled. Vanilla uses 3000, which the UI displays as 3 km.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.AIHailDuration: How long an AI ship stays listed as hailing the player in the comms toolbox before the hail expires. Vanilla uses 10 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.SurrenderValidCheckBufferMult: Largest relative difference, as a 0..1 fraction, allowed between the surrender price shown in the dialogue and the price recomputed when the surrender is confirmed. Anything beyond it makes the game drop the surrender silently. Vanilla uses 5%.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.SurrenderPayoutRoundToMultiple: The final surrender payout is rounded to the nearest multiple of this many credits. Vanilla uses 100.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.LastFireTimeToBeConsideredAttacking: Meant to be the number of seconds since the player last fired a weapon for the player to still count as attacking, which would stop an AI from offering to surrender. The check adds this value to the current time instead of subtracting it, so with the vanilla value of 5, or any value at or above 0, it never triggers.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.SurrenderFirepowerWeightExponent: Exponent applied to each side's total firepower in the strength score that decides whether a surrender is offered. Values below 1 flatten firepower differences. Vanilla uses 0.6.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.SurrenderShipCostWeightExponent: Exponent applied to the ship's blueprint cost in the same strength score, which is then scaled by the ship's remaining value fraction. Vanilla uses 0.4.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerSurrenderBaseCost: Flat credits added to the price the player pays to surrender, on top of the damage the player did to the AI's team. It is scaled by the current fame title's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.FameLevelMultiplier]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerWantedPayoffCost: Extra credits added to the surrender price when the player is wanted by the AI ship's faction. It is scaled by the current fame title's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.FameLevelMultiplier]] and the whole price is then multiplied by that faction's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRules.WantedPayoffMultiple]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.FameLostOnTruceBreak: Base fame lost when the player attacks a ship that had surrendered to them. It is scaled by the current fame title's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.FameLevelMultiplier]] and capped at the player's remaining fame.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.AIInvincibilityOnSurrenderDuration: How long a surrendered AI ship is immune to damage, giving it a moment to disengage. Vanilla uses 2 seconds.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.T:: Stores rules for a particular difficulty level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.ID: The identifier this level is stored under in save games and in the multiplayer input that changes difficulty mid game. Loading a save whose stored id no longer matches any entry throws, so renaming an id breaks existing saves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.NameKey: Localization key for the level's name as it appears in the economy difficulty drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.TipKey: Localization key for the tooltip shown when hovering this level in the economy difficulty drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.IsDefault: Marks this level as the preselected one in the new game screens and the one restored when a save has no stored economy difficulty. Exactly one entry in [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.CareerModeRules.EconDifficultyLevels]] should set it, since the lookup throws when none does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.StartingMoney: Credits the player begins the game with. Unless construction is free, the blueprint cost of the chosen starter ship and of the techs it needs is subtracted from this, and the new game screen refuses ships that cost more than this amount.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.StartingFame: Fame the player begins the game with, which in turn sets the starting fame title and the initial crew cap. Every vanilla level starts at 0.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.EnemyResourceDropRateFactor: Multiplies the chance that a destroyed part on a non player ship drops a resource nugget. Vanilla ranges from 50% on the slow economy to 200% on the fast one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.SelfResourceDropRateFactor: Multiplies the chance that a destroyed part on the player's own ships drops a resource nugget. The factor is blended back toward 1 as the part's salvage fraction rises, so deliberately salvaged parts are unaffected.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.MoneyRewardFactor: Multiplies the credits paid out by mission money rewards, before the salvaging and reputation title multipliers are applied.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.FameRewardFactor: Multiplies the fame paid out by mission fame rewards and the fame value credited for mission target ships.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.ReputationRewardFactor: Multiplies reputation gained from mission rewards and, despite the name, also the reputation lost from damaging a faction's ships. A generous setting therefore makes reputation swing faster in both directions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.ResourceSaleRefund: Fraction of a resource's base price the player receives when selling it, before the buyer's reputation title factor. All vanilla levels refund 50%.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.ConstructionMode: How ships are built and repaired at this difficulty. `InstantFree` also unlocks every part and door, skipping the tech tree entirely. The in-game options for disabling salvaging or crew construction override this with `InstantCredits` and `InstantResources` respectively.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRul.DisabledInIronmanMode: Hides this level from the difficulty drop lists while ironman mode is enabled, forcing a switch to the first level that allows it. Vanilla marks the free build economy this way.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.T:: Stores rules for the spawning of encounter triggers and the handling of encounters
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.MinTimeBetweenEncounters: The seconds that must have passed since the last encounter before entering a trigger area can fire another one. Vanilla waits 500 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.TimeBeforeForcedRegenerate: The seconds after the last trigger placement before the whole trigger field is discarded and generated again, so trigger areas the player never walked into eventually move. Vanilla regenerates every 2000 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.TriggerRadius: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. A trigger area's radius comes from whatever spawner creates it, and vanilla only references this field from its own commented-out trigger spawner to space triggers apart.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.EncounterTriggersGenerator: The simulation generator that places the invisible trigger areas a player ship has to enter to set off an encounter. No spawner type in the shipped game actually creates encounter triggers and vanilla's own trigger spawner is commented out, so the trigger field stays empty and encounters never fire.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.PossibleEncounters: The pool of encounters a trigger can draw from, weighted by each entry's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.EncounterRules.RandomWeight]] and filtered by its conditions. Vanilla lists only the ambush encounter.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.T:: Stores rules for an encounter that is spawned by a trigger
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.ID: The identifier for this encounter. It is what the game records when the encounter fires, so [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.EncounterRules.MinOtherTriggersBeforeReTrigger]] can tell how long ago it last ran.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RandomWeight: The relative weight of this encounter on the roulette wheel among all currently eligible encounters. 0 keeps it out of the draw.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.Conditions: Spawn conditions the sector must satisfy for this encounter to be eligible, using the same fields as a simulation spawner such as `MinParentFieldTier` and `RequiredFame`. They are evaluated at the trigger area's center.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.MinOtherTriggersBeforeReTrigger: How many other encounters must fire before this one becomes eligible again. It is counted against the total number of encounters triggered in the sector since this one last ran, so 0 allows it back immediately.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RequiredReputation: The minimum reputation the player must have with [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.EncounterRules.RequiredReputationFaction]] for this encounter to be eligible. It is only tested when that faction is set, so on its own it does nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RequiredReputationFaction: The faction whose reputation is checked against [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.EncounterRules.RequiredReputation]]. Leaving it unset skips the reputation check entirely.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RandomSightRadiusRatio: A multiple of the triggering ship's sight radius, rolled between Min and Max, that contributes to how far away the encounter spawns. It is summed with the radar and flat-distance terms, and defaults to contributing nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RandomRadarRadiusRatio: A multiple of the triggering ship's radar radius, rolled between Min and Max, that contributes to how far away the encounter spawns. Vanilla's ambush uses 0.95 so the attackers appear right at the edge of radar range.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.RandomAddedDistanceFromPlayer: A flat distance in tiles, rolled between Min and Max, added on top of the sight and radar terms. The encounter is placed at the total distance from the triggering ship, along the direction from that ship toward the trigger area's center.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Encounter.Encount.EncounterGenerator: The simulation generator run at the computed spawn position to actually create the encounter, typically a ship spawner with an attached mission. Vanilla's ambush spawns a bounty fleet ordered to charge the player.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.T:: Stores rules related to the exploration system.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.SectorSize: Edge length in tiles of one fog of war cell. A cell is revealed as a whole as soon as any player radar circle touches it, so smaller values give finer grained but more expensive fog. Vanilla uses 512.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.UnexploredRadius: Radius in tiles of the circle of fog placed around the system center at the start of a game. Everything outside the circle counts as already explored, and the covered square of cells sizes the fog texture. Vanilla fogs 60 sectors, that is 30720 tiles.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.UnexploredTextureSizeFactor: How many texture pixels are allocated per fog cell along each axis. The game writes one flat color across every pixel of a cell, so raising this adds no detail to the fog and only costs texture memory. Vanilla uses 1.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.UnexploredMaterial: The material the fog quad is drawn with, including its shader, tint and blend mode. The fog texture is bound to it and stores full alpha for unexplored cells and zero alpha for revealed ones.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbPoints: Maximum number of trail points kept per player ship. Once the cap is reached the oldest point is dropped for each new one, so together with [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbPointDistance]] this sets how far back a trail reaches. Vanilla keeps 600.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbPointDistance: Minimum distance in tiles a ship must move from its last trail point before a new one is recorded. Vanilla uses 50.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbTrailBeginColor: Color at the newest end of the trail, next to the ship. The gradient runs from [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbTrailEndColor]] at the oldest point up to this color, so vanilla fades the trail in from fully transparent to half opaque grey.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbTrailEndColor: Color at the oldest end of the trail, applied to the first point still stored rather than to the segment nearest the ship. Vanilla makes it fully transparent so the tail dissolves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ExplorationRules.BreadcrumbMaterial: The material the trail line segments are drawn with. Vanilla only overrides its blend mode to add-alpha-blend.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.T:: Stores rules for the fame required to earn a specific title.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.Fame: The player fame at which this title takes over. The list is walked in order until a threshold is not reached yet, so entries must be sorted ascending and the first one is the starting title. The value is also the milestone position on the fame bar in the reputation log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.NameKey: Localization key of the title's name. It appears as the milestone label on the fame bar and, uppercased, in the fame level up banner.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.WantedPoliceTier: The builtin ship tier police ships are drawn from while the player is wanted. It is used as an exact tier rather than an upper bound.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.IsVictory: When true, reaching this title ends the run. The victory dialog is shown once the fame level up animation finishes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.FameTitleRules.FameLevelMultiplier: Scales the fame-priced numbers that apply at this title, namely [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.FameLostOnTruceBreak]], [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerSurrenderBaseCost]] and [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.DialogueRules.PlayerWantedPayoffCost]]. Vanilla ramps it from 1 at the lowest title to 15 at the highest.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.T:: Assigns difficulty tiers based on the strengths of the factions of each galaxy map node.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.Factions: The per-faction tier rules, applied in list order. Each entry sweeps every map node once, so a node influenced by several factions ends up with the combination of all their contributions.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.T:: Stores rules for how difficulty tiers should be chosen for a specific faction.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.FactionID: The faction whose influence on a map node drives that node's difficulty tier. Nodes where this faction has a strength of 0 are skipped entirely.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.TierRangeLow: The span the node's low difficulty tier is interpolated across, Min at the bottom of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTiersSpawner+FactionTiersRules.FactionStrengthRange]] and Max at the top.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.TierRangeHigh: The span the node's high difficulty tier is interpolated across, using the same faction strength fraction as [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTiersSpawner+FactionTiersRules.TierRangeLow]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.FactionStrengthRange: The faction strength values that map onto the two tier ranges, defaulting to 0..1. Strength is the influence the galaxy generator gave this faction on the node, and values outside the range extrapolate rather than clamp.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.FactionNodeTi.CombineMode: How the tiers this entry computes merge into a tier range another entry or spawner already put on the node. `Max` and `Min` take the larger or smaller of each end, `Sum` adds the two ranges together. Defaults to `Max`.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.T:: Assigns difficulty tiers to create a "path" of difficulty progression through the galaxy while attempting to modify existing tiers as little as possible.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.DesiredTierDeltas: The rules that shape the difficulty path, tried in list order at every node the walk visits. The walk starts at the node marked as the starting node by a `StartingNodePicker`, falling back to the node closest to the map origin.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.MinLowTier: The lowest low tier this spawner will hand out. A delta that would land below it is skipped, and the bottom of an assigned tier range is clamped up to it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.MaxLowTier: The highest low tier this spawner will hand out. A delta that would land above it is skipped. Vanilla keeps this a few tiers below the galaxy's maximum so the top tiers stay reserved for faction home systems.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.MaxHighTier: Caps the top of every tier range this spawner assigns, so [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNodeTiersSpawner+DesiredTierDeltaRules.HighTierSpread]] cannot push a node past the galaxy's intended ceiling.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.MinChangeableLowTier: The lowest pre-existing low tier a node may have and still be retiered by this spawner. Nodes below it are left alone and the difficulty walk cannot pass through them. A node with no tier range at all counts as -1, so even the default of 0 excludes untiered nodes and a spawner such as `FactionNodeTiers` has to run first.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.MaxChangeableLowTier: The highest pre-existing low tier a node may have and still be retiered by this spawner. Vanilla sets it equal to [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNodeTiersSpawner.MaxLowTier]] so faction home systems keep the tiers the faction spawner gave them.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.T:: Stores rules for a specific desired tier delta.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.SourceLowTierDelta: Added to the source node's current low tier to get the low tier this rule wants to place on a neighbouring node. Vanilla uses values from +3 down to -1 so the path mostly climbs but can double back.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.Priority: Ranks this rule against the others, lower being more important. It also selects which of the walk's queues the claimed node is appended to, so it doubles as an index and must be less than the number of entries in [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNodeTiersSpawner.DesiredTierDeltas]] or the generator throws. A node already claimed at a given priority is only re-claimed by a rule with a strictly lower number.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.HighTierSpread: How far above the desired low tier the claimed node's tier range extends, in tiers. 0 gives the node a single tier, and the top is clamped to [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNodeTiersSpawner.MaxHighTier]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.SourceLowTierRange: Limits this rule to source nodes whose current low tier falls inside the range, so different deltas can apply early and late in the progression. Defaults to everything from 0 upwards.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.ProgressionNo.PreferredAvailableConnections: How many onward unclaimed connections the chosen neighbour ideally has. Each candidate's free-connection count is capped at this number before comparing, so every candidate that reaches it ranks equally and the tie is settled by whichever node's original tier is closest to the desired one. The default of 0 caps every candidate to 0 and leaves the choice purely to tier distance.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomNodeTie.T:: Assigns random difficulty tiers to each galaxy map node.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomNodeTie.TierRangeLow: The span the low end of each map node's difficulty tier range is rolled from. Every node on the map gets an independent roll.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomNodeTie.TierRangeHigh: The span the high end of each map node's difficulty tier range is rolled from. It is rolled independently of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomNodeTiersSpawner.TierRangeLow]] and is not clamped against it, so overlapping spans can produce a node whose high tier is below its low tier.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.T:: Assigns random sector types to each galaxy map node.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.SectorTypes: The pool of sector types this spawner draws from, each with its own weight and tier limits. Every map node that does not already have a sector type assigned gets one rolled from this pool.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.T:: Stores info about a particular sector type that can be spawned.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.Type: The sector type assigned to the node when this entry is rolled.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.RandomWeight: The relative weight of this entry on the roulette wheel. An entry with weight 0.5 is picked half as often as one with weight 1.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.MinTier: The lowest node tier this sector type may appear at. A node qualifies when the top of its tier range reaches this value, so a node spanning tiers 4 to 6 still accepts a `MinTier` of 5. Nodes with no tier range assigned yet are rejected.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.RandomSectorT.MaxTier: The highest node tier this sector type may appear at. A node qualifies when the bottom of its tier range is at or below this value. Nodes with no tier range assigned yet are rejected.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.T:: Stores the rules for a particular type of MapNode sector.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.ID: The identifier this sector type is referenced by, for example from a `RandomSectorTypes` spawner entry or from a spawner's `OnlySectorTypes` and `ExcludeSectorTypes` conditions. Vanilla ships `basic`, `binary`, `electron`, `high_density_nebula` and `supernova`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.NameKey: The localization key for the sector type's display name, shown as the star system type in the galaxy map node tooltip. Vanilla uses keys like `SectorTypes/Supernova`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.SpawnFlags: Spawn flags added to the flag set handed to every spawner in a star system of this type, so generator entries can gate themselves with `RequireSpawnFlags` and `ProhibitSpawnFlags`. The career mode also adds `disable_nebulas` on top of these when the player turned nebulas off.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.SystemGenerator: The simulation generator that builds the contents of a star system of this type, run once when the sector is first entered.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.TradeRoutes: The trade route rules that drive the AI trade ships and station stockpiles in a star system of this type.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.ResourceDeliveryMissions: The resource delivery mission rules for stations in a star system of this type, controlling how many missions each station offers at once and how long they last.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.BackgroundStyles: Candidate background styles for a star system of this type, one picked at random per system. When unset, the game falls back to the global `DefaultInGameStyles`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.SectorTypeRul.EncounterRules: The encounter rules used while the player is in a star system of this type, driving which random encounters can trigger and how often.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.T:: Chooses the initial starting node based on a variety of criteria.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.AllowedFactions: Restricts starting-node candidates to map nodes controlled by one of the listed factions. Nodes with no controlling faction are always discarded when this is set. Vanilla lists only `fringe`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.MinTier: Discards candidate nodes whose tier range starts below this tier. Values of 0 or less disable the filter, and nodes that have no tier range assigned yet are discarded whenever it is active.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.MaxTier: Discards candidate nodes whose tier range ends above this tier. The default of `int.MaxValue` disables the filter, and nodes with no tier range assigned yet are discarded whenever it is active.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.MinConnections: Discards candidate nodes that have fewer than this many map connections to neighbouring nodes. Vanilla uses 2 so the player never starts in a dead end.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.MaxConnections: Discards candidate nodes that have more than this many map connections. The default of `int.MaxValue` disables the filter.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.CandidatesClosestToCenter: Keeps only this many candidates, the ones with the smallest distance from the galaxy origin. 0 disables the trim.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.CandidatesFarthestFromCenter: Keeps only this many candidates, the ones with the largest distance from the galaxy origin. Applied after [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodePickerSpawner.CandidatesClosestToCenter]], so setting both leaves the farthest ones from the already-trimmed set.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.CandidatesClosestToFactions: Keeps only `Count` candidates, the ones whose shortest map-graph hop distance to any node controlled by one of the listed factions is smallest. This trim runs last of all the candidate trims, after [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodePickerSpawner.CandidatesFarthestFromFactions]], regardless of the order the fields appear in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.CandidatesFarthestFromFactions: Keeps only `Count` candidates, the ones whose shortest map-graph hop distance to any node controlled by one of the listed factions is largest. Vanilla keeps the 5 nodes farthest from `imperium` and `io`, then narrows those to the 1 closest to `monolith` and `cabal`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.SetTierRangeTo: Overwrites the chosen starting node's tier range after it has been picked, so the first system can be forced to low difficulty no matter what the tier spawners produced. Vanilla sets `[1, 1 + TierSpread]`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Map.StartingNodeP.SetSectorTypeTo: Overwrites the chosen starting node's sector type after it has been picked. Vanilla forces `basic` so the first system is never a nebula or supernova.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionC.T:: Stores information about a category of missions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionC.ID: Identifies this category so that a `MissionMetatype`'s `CategoryID` can point at it. Categories are also sorted by their position in the `MissionCategories` list, so the order you declare them in is the order the headings appear in the mission log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionC.NameKey: Localization key for the heading text shown above the missions of this category in the mission log.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.T:: Stores meta information about a type of mission.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.NameKey: Localization key for the mission's title as shown in the mission log and HUD. The mission's own data is passed as formatting arguments, so the string may reference things like the target faction or ship name.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.DescriptionKey: Localization key for the longer description shown under the mission title. When absent the mission simply has no description text.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.CategoryID: The `MissionCategory` this mission is filed under in the mission log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.OverrideMissionCompletedKey: Localization key replacing the default `CareerMode/MissionCompleted` banner text shown when the mission is completed.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.AutoTrack: Whether the mission is automatically added to the tracked-mission list on the HUD when it is accepted. Tracking still only happens if the tracked list is below `MaxTrackedMissions` in the missions GUI rules.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionM.KeepInLog: Whether the mission stays in the mission log after it has been completed. By default a completed mission is removed from the log once its rewards have been given.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.T:: Spawns missions into the game simulation.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.Metatype: The `MissionMetatype` supplying this mission's name, description, log category and tracking behavior.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.Objectives: The objectives that must be completed to complete the mission, each created from one `ObjectiveSpawner`. If any objective spawner reports that it cannot find its targets the whole mission is abandoned and nothing is spawned.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.Rewards: The rewards handed to the player when the mission completes. Each spawner receives the mission's faction and the tier range computed from its objectives, so rewards can scale with mission difficulty.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.Faction: How the mission's owning faction is determined. `Specific` reads `SpecificFaction`, `OwnerOfTag` takes the owner of the object found by `FactionTag`, `SystemController` uses the faction controlling the star system, and `RandomByFactionStrength` picks randomly weighted by each faction's local strength.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.SpecificFaction: The faction the mission belongs to when `Faction` is `Specific`. Leaving it out in that case is a fatal rules error.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.FactionTag: Search for an already-spawned object whose owner becomes the mission's faction, used when `Faction` is `OwnerOfTag`. Objects belonging to factions that are enemies of the mission are excluded from the search.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.OkayIfFactionTagNotFound: Whether a `FactionTag` that matches nothing is tolerated. When false the missing tag is a fatal spawn error, when true the mission is spawned with no faction at all.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.SpawnAt: Which mission list receives the mission. `Player` puts it straight into the player's accepted missions, `SimGlobal` offers it at every station in the star system, `GameGlobal` at every station in the galaxy, and `Tag` offers it only from the ship found by `SpawnAtTag`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.SpawnAtTag: Search for the already-spawned ship that will offer this mission, used when `SpawnAt` is `Tag`. The found object must be a ship whose AI provides missions or a stasis ship spawner carrying a mission provider module, otherwise spawning fails.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.OkayIfSpawnAtTagNotFound: Whether a `SpawnAtTag` that matches nothing is tolerated. When false the missing tag is a fatal spawn error, when true the mission is silently dropped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.FamePrereq: Fame the player must have before the mission becomes available. `FamePrereqPerLowTier` and `FamePrereqPerHighTier` are added on top of this value. In the demo build the total is capped at 140.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.RequirePreviousMission: Whether this mission stays locked until the mission spawned immediately before it in the same spawn tree has been completed, which is how multi-step mission chains are built. Spawning fails if no earlier mission exists.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.FamePrereqPerLowTier: Extra fame prerequisite added according to the lowest tier among the mission's objectives. The tier is looked up directly, so the table needs an entry for every tier the objectives can produce or spawning throws.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionS.FamePrereqPerHighTier: Extra fame prerequisite added according to the highest tier among the mission's objectives. Like `FamePrereqPerLowTier`, a missing tier entry is a fatal lookup failure rather than a zero.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.T:: Stores rules related to the GUIs for displaying and managing missions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.LogIcon: The icon on the career HUD button that opens the log window and on that window's mission log tab.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationIcon: The icon on the reputation tab of the career log window. Also marks the fame bar inside that tab.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedIcon: The icon marking missions that are currently tracked. Shown next to tracked missions in the HUD list and on the untrack buttons in the mission log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedIcon: The icon on the track buttons of missions that are not currently tracked in the mission log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.NewMissionSound: Played together with the on-screen New Mission banner when the player receives a mission.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedSound: Played together with the on-screen Mission Complete banner when a mission is finished.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionFailedSound: Played together with the on-screen Mission Failed banner when a mission fails.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.FameLevelUpSound: Played together with the on-screen banner when the player's fame reaches a new level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.GoToMissionSound: Played when clicking a mission's location link in the missions panel or an objective, which jumps the view to the mission target.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelUpSound: Played together with the on-screen banner when reputation with a faction rises to a higher level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelDownSound: Played together with the on-screen banner when reputation with a faction drops to a lower level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.NewMissionColorAnim: Color keyframes for the New Mission headline shown at the top center of the screen. Each entry pairs a time in seconds from the start of the animation with the color the label tweens to, and the banner is removed after the last keyframe.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.NewMissionNameColorAnim: Color keyframes for the mission name line shown below the New Mission headline. Uses the same seconds-and-color keyframe format as [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.NewMissionColorAnim]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedColorAnimIn: Color keyframes that fade in the Mission Complete headline. The matching fade-out is [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.MissionCompletedColorAnimOut]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedNameColorAnimIn: Color keyframes that fade in the mission name line below the Mission Complete headline.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedFirstRewardAnimDelayIn: Seconds after the Mission Complete headline appears before the first reward line starts animating in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedAdditionalRewardAnimDela: Seconds between each further reward line starting to animate in after the first.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedRewardColorAnimIn: Color keyframes that fade in each reward line of the Mission Complete banner.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedRewardTickDuration: Seconds a reward line takes to count its displayed value up from zero to the full reward amount.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedDelayAfterLastReward: Seconds the completed banner holds after the last reward line has appeared before the fade-out animations begin.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedColorAnimOut: Color keyframes that fade out the Mission Complete headline once [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.MissionCompletedDelayAfterLastReward]] has elapsed.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedNameColorAnimOut: Color keyframes that fade out the mission name line of the Mission Complete banner.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedFirstRewardAnimDelayOut: Seconds into the fade-out phase before the first reward line starts fading out.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedAdditionalRewardAnimDela: Seconds between each further reward line starting to fade out after the first.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionCompletedRewardColorAnimOut: Color keyframes that fade out each reward line of the Mission Complete banner.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionFailedColorAnim: Color keyframes for the Mission Failed headline, covering both fade-in and fade-out in one sequence. Uses the same seconds-and-color keyframe format as [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.NewMissionColorAnim]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MissionFailedNameColorAnim: Color keyframes for the mission name line shown below the Mission Failed headline.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.FameLevelUpColorAnim: Color keyframes for the Fame Level Up headline shown when the player's fame reaches a new level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.FameLevelUpNameColorAnim: Color keyframes for the new fame title line shown below the Fame Level Up headline.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelUpColorAnim: Color keyframes for the Reputation Level Up headline shown when reputation with a faction rises to a higher level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.FameLevelUpCrewColorAnim: Color keyframes for the crew gained line of the fame banner. That line only appears when the new fame level raises the player's crew capacity.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.FameLevelUpCrewAnimDelayIn: Seconds after the Fame Level Up banner appears before the crew gained line starts animating.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelUpNameColorAnim: Color keyframes for the faction and title line shown below the Reputation Level Up headline.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelDownColorAnim: Color keyframes for the Reputation Level Down headline shown when reputation with a faction drops to a lower level.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.ReputationLevelDownNameColorAnim: Color keyframes for the faction and title line shown below the Reputation Level Down headline.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.MaxTrackedMissions: The most missions the player can have tracked at the same time. Trying to track more shows a dialog, and the value also caps the Show Nearby Missions choices in the gameplay settings.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionLandmarkIcon: The icon drawn over the HUD indicator of a ship or stasis landmark that is the target of a tracked mission. [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionLandmarkIcon]] is used instead when the mission is not tracked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionLandmarkIconOffset: Offset in GUI pixels from the center of the target's HUD indicator to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionLandmarkIcon]] is drawn. Negative Y moves the icon up.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionPOIIcon: The icon drawn over the HUD indicator of a point of interest that is the target of a tracked mission. [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionPOIIcon]] is used instead when the mission is not tracked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionPOIIconOffset: Offset in GUI pixels from the center of the point of interest's HUD indicator to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionPOIIcon]] is drawn. Negative Y moves the icon up.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionNodeIcon: The icon drawn on a galaxy map node that a tracked mission points to. [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionNodeIcon]] is used instead when the mission is not tracked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.TrackedMissionNodeIconOffset: Offset from the map node's center to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionNodeIcon]] is drawn, in galaxy map coordinates. The offset is multiplied by the same scale as the icon itself.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionLandmarkIcon: The icon drawn over the HUD indicator of a ship or stasis landmark that is the target of an untracked mission. Tracked missions use [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionLandmarkIcon]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionLandmarkIconOffset: Offset in GUI pixels from the center of the target's HUD indicator to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionLandmarkIcon]] is drawn. Negative Y moves the icon up.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionPOIIcon: The icon drawn over the HUD indicator of a point of interest that is the target of an untracked mission. Tracked missions use [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionPOIIcon]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionPOIIconOffset: Offset in GUI pixels from the center of the point of interest's HUD indicator to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionPOIIcon]] is drawn. Negative Y moves the icon up.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionNodeIcon: The icon drawn on a galaxy map node that an untracked mission points to. Tracked missions use [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.TrackedMissionNodeIcon]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Missions.UntrackedMissionNodeIconOffset: Offset from the map node's center to where [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.MissionsGuiRules.UntrackedMissionNodeIcon]] is drawn, in galaxy map coordinates. The offset is multiplied by the same scale as the icon itself.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.SubObjectives: The child objectives, which the player may complete in any order. If every child spawner declines to produce an objective the whole any-order objective is dropped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierCombineMode: How the danger tiers of the sub-objectives are folded into one tier. `Range` spans the lowest and highest child tier, `Max` takes the highest, `ValueSum` adds up the approximate ship values behind each child tier and converts the total back into a tier, and `None` reports no tier at all.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierOffset: Tiers added to (or with a negative value subtracted from) the combined tier. Has no effect while `TierCombineMode` is `None`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.NumRequiredToComplete: How many sub-objectives have to be completed for this objective to complete. Without it all of them are required, and with it the objective only fails once too few unfailed children remain to still reach the count.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.OverrideDisplayFormatKey: Localization key for a single mission log line that replaces the lines of all sub-objectives. It is looked up as plain text with no formatting arguments.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.EventCount: How many times the developer debug event must fire for the objective to complete, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time. The event is raised by the Shift + backtick + E debug hotkey, so this objective is only useful for testing mission plumbing.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetsTag: Search for the already-spawned ships that must be defeated. Every matching object becomes a target, and a match count of zero means the objective is skipped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCount: How many of the found ships must actually be defeated, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time and clamped to the number of ships found. Without it, and without `TargetCountFraction`, all found ships must be defeated.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCountFraction: How many of the found ships must be defeated, as a 0..1 fraction of the number found, rounded up. Ignored when `TargetCount` is present.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.MissionInvalidIfZeroTargets: Whether finding no matching ships aborts the entire mission. When false the objective is simply dropped and the rest of the mission still spawns.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetAreaTag: Search for a point-of-interest doodad marking the rough area the targets are in. The mission log points the player here while no target ship is visible on radar.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetLandmarkTag: Search for a landmark ship used as the fallback location marker when no point of interest is set or explored.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.AutoDiscoverTargetArea: Whether the point of interest found by `TargetAreaTag` is revealed on the map as soon as the mission is accepted, rather than the player having to explore it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierCombineMode: How the danger tiers of the individual target ships are folded into one tier for the objective. `None` makes the objective report no tier at all, which also removes it from the mission's tier range and from any tier-scaled reward tables.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierOffset: Tiers added to (or with a negative value subtracted from) the combined tier. Applied after `TierCombineMode`, and ignored when that mode is `None`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ListTargetsIndividually: Whether each target gets its own line in the mission log instead of one combined line with an x-of-y counter. A single target is always listed individually.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.OverrideDisplayFormatKey: Localization key replacing the default `Objectives/DefeatShips` text on the combined line. It receives named arguments including `target_ship`, `target_count`, `target_perc` and `target_faction`. Ignored when the targets are listed individually.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.AllowNpcKills: Whether a target killed by someone other than a human player still counts toward the objective. With it off the player has to land the kill themselves.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.AllowSurrender: Whether a target that surrenders counts as defeated. With it off the objective text becomes `Objectives/DestroyShips` and the game actively strips the surrender chance from the target ships' AI so they fight to the death.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.Amount: How many units of the resource must be delivered, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DeliveryLocationTag: Search for the already-spawned ship or station the resources have to be handed to.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.SuggestedCollectionAreaTag: Search for a point-of-interest doodad suggesting where the player can go to collect the resource. It is only a hint for the map marker, the player may source the resource anywhere.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ResourceType: The single resource the player must deliver. Either this or `RandomResourceTypes` is required, and when both are present this one wins and the list is ignored.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.RandomResourceTypes: A set of resources from which one is picked at random when the mission spawns. Ignored entirely if `ResourceType` is also given.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.POITags: Searches for the already-spawned point-of-interest doodads that must be discovered. Every match of every search is added as a target.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.LandmarkTags: Searches for the already-spawned landmark ships that must be discovered, counted together with the doodads found by `POITags`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DiscoverCount: How many of the found points of interest and landmarks must be discovered, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time and clamped to the number found. Without it, and without `DiscoverCountFraction`, all of them are required.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DiscoverCountFraction: How many must be discovered, as a 0..1 fraction of the number found, rounded up. Ignored when `DiscoverCount` is present.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ShowRealNames: Whether the mission log names each target instead of showing a single anonymous `Objectives/DiscoverUnknown` line with a counter. Targets sharing a name are grouped onto one line.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.GetTierFromTierField: Whether the objective takes its danger tier from the sector's tier field sampled at each target's location, spanning the lowest and highest sampled tier. Without it the objective reports no tier.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetsTag: Search for the already-spawned ships that the player must not surrender to. Every matching object becomes a target, and a match count of zero means the objective is skipped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCount: How many of those ships the player is allowed to surrender to before the objective fails, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time and clamped to the number of ships found. The name is misleading, the value lands in the objective's allowed-surrender count, so leaving it out means surrendering to even one target fails the objective.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCountFraction: The allowed surrender count as a 0..1 fraction of the number of ships found, rounded up. Ignored when `TargetCount` is present.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.MissionInvalidIfZeroTargets: Whether finding no matching ships aborts the entire mission. When false the objective is simply dropped and the rest of the mission still spawns.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierCombineMode: How the danger tiers of the target ships are folded into one tier for the objective. It defaults to `None` so this objective contributes no danger tier of its own, since it usually rides along with a defeat objective that already sets one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierOffset: Tiers added to (or with a negative value subtracted from) the combined tier. Has no effect while `TierCombineMode` is `None`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ListTargetsIndividually: Whether each target gets its own line in the mission log instead of one combined line. A single target is always listed individually.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DisplayTextDisabled: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it, presumably meant to suppress this objective's mission log line, which is what [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectives.ObjectiveSpawner.DisableDisplayLines]] on the shared objective spawner actually does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.OverrideDisplayFormatKey: Localization key replacing the default text on the combined line. It receives named arguments including `target_ship`, `target_surrender_count`, `target_surrender_perc` and `target_faction`.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.Fame: The total player fame that must be reached for the objective to complete. It is a threshold on the player's overall fame score rather than an amount earned during this mission, and the objective reports the mission's prerequisites as already satisfied once the player is at or above it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.Tier: A fixed danger tier reported by this objective, which feeds the mission's tier range and any tier-scaled reward tables. Without it the objective reports no tier.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DestinationShipTag: Search for the already-spawned ship the player must reach. The objective completes the moment that ship comes within sight range of a human player's team.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DestinationShipAreaTag: Search for a point-of-interest doodad marking the rough area of the destination, used as the mission log's map marker until the ship itself is visible.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.GetTierFromTierField: Whether the objective takes its danger tier from the sector's tier field sampled at the destination ship's location. Without it the objective reports no tier.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.InvertGoTo: Flips the objective into an escape objective, completing when every one of the player's significant ships is farther than `InvertGoToDistance` from the destination ship, or when that ship dies or leaves the system. Setting it without `InvertGoToDistance` is a fatal rules error.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.InvertGoToDistance: The distance in world units the player's ships must put between themselves and the destination ship for an inverted objective to complete. Vanilla's ambush encounter uses 4500.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.T:: The base class for classes that spawn mission objectives.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.Rewards: Rewards attached to this individual objective rather than to the mission as a whole, granted when the objective itself completes. The tier range passed to these spawners comes from this objective alone, and no faction is passed, so a `Reputation` reward here produces nothing unless it names its own `Faction`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DisableDisplayLines: Whether this objective is hidden from the mission log and HUD. The objective still runs and still has to be completed, it just contributes no text lines.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetsTag: Search for the already-spawned ships that must survive. Every matching object becomes a target, and a match count of zero means the objective is skipped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCount: How many of the found ships must still be alive at the end, rolled randomly from this range at spawn time and clamped to the number of ships found. Without it, and without `TargetCountFraction`, every found ship must survive.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetCountFraction: How many of the found ships must survive, as a 0..1 fraction of the number found, rounded up. Ignored when `TargetCount` is present.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.MissionInvalidIfZeroTargets: Whether finding no matching ships aborts the entire mission. When false the objective is simply dropped and the rest of the mission still spawns.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetAreaTag: Search for a point-of-interest doodad marking the rough area the protected ships are in. The mission log points the player here while no protected ship is visible on radar.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TargetLandmarkTag: Search for a landmark ship used as the fallback location marker when no point of interest is set or explored.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.AutoDiscoverTargetArea: Whether the point of interest found by `TargetAreaTag` is revealed on the map as soon as the mission is accepted, rather than the player having to explore it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierCombineMode: How the danger tiers of the protected ships are folded into one tier for the objective. It defaults to `None` so that friendly ships you escort do not inflate the mission's danger tier or its tier-scaled rewards.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierOffset: Tiers added to (or with a negative value subtracted from) the combined tier. Has no effect while `TierCombineMode` is `None`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ListTargetsIndividually: Whether each protected ship gets its own line in the mission log instead of one combined line with an x-of-y counter. A single target is always listed individually.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.DisplayTextDisabled: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it, presumably meant to suppress this objective's mission log line, which is what [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectives.ObjectiveSpawner.DisableDisplayLines]] on the shared objective spawner actually does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.OverrideDisplayFormatKey: Localization key replacing the default `Objectives/ProtectShips` text on the combined line. It receives named arguments including `target_ship`, `target_count`, `target_perc` and `target_faction`. Ignored when the targets are listed individually.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ContactShipTag: Search for the specific ship or station the player must contact to collect the mission's rewards. Leaving it out lets the player collect from any station in the star system the mission was spawned in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.ContactShipAreaTag: Search for a point-of-interest doodad marking the rough area of the contact ship, used as the mission log's map marker.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.SubObjectives: The child objectives, which must be completed in the order listed. Only the objectives up to and including the current one are shown in the mission log, so later steps stay hidden until the player gets there.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierCombineMode: How the danger tiers of the sub-objectives are folded into one tier. `Range` spans the lowest and highest child tier, `Max` takes the highest, `ValueSum` adds up the approximate ship values behind each child tier and converts the total back into a tier, and `None` reports no tier at all.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TierOffset: Tiers added to (or with a negative value subtracted from) the combined tier. Has no effect while `TierCombineMode` is `None`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.OverrideDisplayFormatKey: Localization key for a single mission log line that replaces the step-by-step lines of the sub-objectives. It is looked up as plain text with no formatting arguments.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.TimeLimit: How long the player has, in seconds, before the objective and its mission fail. A countdown line showing the remaining minutes and seconds is added to the mission log below the sub-objective lines.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Objectiv.StartOnCreation: Whether the clock starts the moment the mission is spawned rather than when the player accepts it. With it on the mission can expire out of the available list before it is ever taken.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..TextKey: Localization key for a line of text added to the mission's reward list. This reward gives the player nothing, it only annotates the mission with something like a story note or a hint at an off-book payoff.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..Fame: Base fame awarded, rolled randomly from this range when the mission spawns. Tier bonuses are added on top before rounding, and the payout is further scaled by the game's economic difficulty setting.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MaxFame: The player fame level this reward cannot push the player past, rolled randomly from this range. A player already at or above it receives nothing, which is how vanilla stops low-tier missions from carrying a player to high fame.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..FamePerLowTier: Fame added according to the lowest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..FamePerHighTier: Fame added according to the highest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..FamePerTierMultiplier: Scales the combined `FamePerLowTier` and `FamePerHighTier` bonus, rolled randomly from this range. It does not touch the flat `Fame` amount, and it is skipped entirely when the tier bonus came out as zero.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MaxFamePerLowTier: A fame ceiling chosen by the lowest danger tier among the mission's objectives. It only ever lowers the cap, the smaller of it and `MaxFame` wins.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MaxFamePerHighTier: A fame ceiling chosen by the highest danger tier among the mission's objectives. It only ever lowers the cap, the smallest of it, `MaxFamePerLowTier` and `MaxFame` wins.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..RoundToMultiple: Rounds the final fame award to the nearest multiple of this value. It applies to the award only, not to the `MaxFame` ceiling.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..Money: Base credits paid out, rolled randomly from this range when the mission spawns. Tier bonuses are added on top before rounding.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MoneyPerLowTier: Credits added according to the lowest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MoneyPerHighTier: Credits added according to the highest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..MoneyPerTierMultiplier: Scales the combined `MoneyPerLowTier` and `MoneyPerHighTier` bonus, rolled randomly from this range. It does not touch the flat `Money` amount, and it is skipped entirely when the tier bonus came out as zero.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..RoundToMultiple: Rounds the final payout to the nearest multiple of this value, so 500 keeps rewards at round numbers. Applied after the tier bonuses and multiplier.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..Faction: The faction whose reputation changes. Leaving it out falls back to the mission's own faction, and if the mission has none either the reward is dropped and nothing is given.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..Reputation: Base reputation granted with the faction, rolled randomly from this range when the mission spawns. Negative values are allowed and are shown in red in the reward list. The final amount is scaled by the game's economic difficulty setting.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..ReputationPerLowTier: Reputation added according to the lowest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..ReputationPerHighTier: Reputation added according to the highest danger tier among the mission's objectives, rolled randomly from the range in the matching row. A tier with no row simply adds nothing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..ReputationPerTierMultiplier: Scales the combined `ReputationPerLowTier` and `ReputationPerHighTier` bonus, rolled randomly from this range. It does not touch the flat `Reputation` amount, and it is skipped entirely when the tier bonus came out as zero. Vanilla uses values from 2 to 5 here.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..RoundToMultiple: Rounds the final reputation change to the nearest multiple of this value. Applied after the tier bonuses and multiplier.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.Missions.Rewards..T:: The base class for classes that spawn mission rewards.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.T:: Stores rules for the reputation required to earn a specific title.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.Reputation: The reputation with a faction at which this title takes over. The list is walked in order until a threshold is not reached yet, so entries must be sorted ascending and the first one acts as the floor. In the reputation log a negative threshold is displayed as one point below the next title's threshold instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.NameKey: Localization key of the title's name. It appears as the milestone label in the reputation log and, uppercased, in the reputation level up and level down banner.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.TipKey: Localization key of the tooltip shown on this title's milestone in the reputation log.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.MissionMoneyRewardFactor: Multiplies money rewards from missions given by a faction the player holds this title with. Applied on top of the economy difficulty's money reward factor.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.ResourceBuyCostFactor: Multiplies the price the player pays for resources bought from this faction. Above 1 makes buying more expensive.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.ResourceSellCostFactor: Multiplies the money the player receives for resources sold to this faction, on top of the economy difficulty's sale refund. Vanilla leaves it at 1 for every title.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.CrewBuyCostFactor: Multiplies the price of hiring crew from this faction.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.TechBuyCostFactor: Multiplies the price of techs bought from this faction.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.WantedDurationFactor: Multiplies [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.SearchingExpireTime]], so it controls how long this faction keeps searching for the player after losing track.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.WantedSearchRadiusFactor: Multiplies [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.SearchRadius]] for this faction's active search areas. Vanilla leaves it at 1 for every title.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.WantedPoliceCount: How many police ships this faction keeps spawned while it is hunting the player. Leaving it out means 0, so no police are sent.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ReputationTitleRu.WantedPayoffMultiple: Multiplies the whole price the player pays to surrender to a faction that has the player wanted. Leaving it out means 0, which makes the payoff free.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.T:: Stores rules for dynamically generating resource delivery missions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.Metatype: The mission metatype used for the delivery missions this sector type generates at its stations.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.TimeLimit: How long the player has to complete a delivery. It also sets the refresh rhythm, since each station starts its missions staggered across this span and gains a new one every `TimeLimit / SimultaneousMissionsPerStation`. Vanilla uses 30 minutes.
