Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.SimultaneousMissionsPerStation: How many delivery missions a station offers at the same time. Each one asks for a different resource, so [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryMissionRules.DeliveryTypes]] must list at least this many entries.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.RewardMoneyPerSellPrice: The reward money as a fraction of what the delivered resources would sell for at the destination. Vanilla uses 75%.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.RoundRewardMoneyToMultiple: The reward money is rounded to the nearest multiple of this many credits.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.DeliveryTypes: The resources a station may ask for, each with its own quantity range and weight. One entry is drawn at random per mission, re-drawing while the station already has a mission for that resource.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.T:: Stores delivery mission rules for a specific resource type.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.ResourceType: The resource the player has to deliver for this kind of mission.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.RandomWeight: The relative chance of this entry being drawn among the sibling delivery types. Only the ratio between the weights matters.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.Quantity: The range of units the mission asks for, before rounding by [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryMissionRules+DeliveryTypeRules.RoundQuantityToMultiple]]. Vanilla asks for 80 to 120 steel and 20 to 40 tristeel.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.ResourceDeliveryM.RoundQuantityToMultiple: The rolled quantity is rounded to the nearest multiple of this many units, so the mission asks for a round number.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.StarterShipRules.T:: Stores data about a ship that the player can choose to start the game with.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.StarterShipRules.Ship: The `.ship.png` loaded when the player picks this starter ship. Its design has to pass the career mode legality check, and unless construction is free its blueprint cost and required techs are deducted from the economy difficulty's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.EconDifficultyRules.StartingMoney]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.StarterShipRules.DescriptionKey: Localization key for the blurb shown beside the ship preview on the new game screen, between the ship's name and its cost summary.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.SystemVisitMissio.T:: Stores rules for system visitation missions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.SystemVisitMissio.Metatype: The mission metatype used for the automatically created "visit this system" missions, one per map node other than the one the player starts at.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.SystemVisitMissio.FamePrereqPerLowTier: The fame the player needs before a node's visit mission becomes available, keyed by the lower bound of that node's tier range. Written as `Tier` and `Fame` pairs.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.SystemVisitMissio.Rewards: The reward spawners rolled once for each node's visit mission, each given the node's tier range so higher tier systems can pay more. Spawners that produce nothing are skipped.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.T:: Stores rules for a single technology that can be purchased by the player.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.ID: The identifier this tech is referenced by, from another tech's [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.Prerequisites]] or [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.UpgradedFrom]], from save games, and from mission scripts. Every ID in the career mode tech list must be unique or loading fails.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.OtherIDs: Extra identifiers this tech also answers to, so an ID renamed in a later game version keeps resolving. They are registered in the tech lookup alongside [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.ID]] and must not collide with any other tech.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.Categories: Tags used to group techs for scripting. A mission script can ask whether the player has unlocked anything in a category, which vanilla uses for the `overclock` group.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.NameKey: The localization key for the tech's name in the trading window's tech list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.DescriptionKey: The localization key for the tech's description, rendered with XML formatting below the name in the tech list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.Icon: The icon shown next to the tech in the trading window's tech list. It is drawn greyed out while the tech's prerequisites are unmet.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.SecondaryIcon: An extra sprite layered on top of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.Icon]], used by the vanilla missile techs to overlay the warhead type on the launcher icon.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.PartsUnlocked: The parts that become buildable once the tech is bought. Any part listed by at least one tech starts the career locked, so a part no tech mentions is available from the start.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.DoorsUnlocked: The door types that become buildable once the tech is bought, working the same way as [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.PartsUnlocked]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.ToggleChoicesUnlocked: The part toggle settings that become selectable once the tech is bought, for example a single missile warhead type on the missile launcher. Any choice listed by a tech starts locked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.UpgradedFrom: Older techs this one replaces. Loading a save that has one of those older techs unlocked also unlocks this tech, and any other tech that listed the old ID as a prerequisite has it swapped for this one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.Cost: The price in credits to buy the tech at a station. The player's reputation title with the seller's faction multiplies it through `TechBuyCostFactor`, and free-build modes charge nothing. Vanilla ranges from 1000 for a small laser blaster to 20000 for nukes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.Prerequisites: The techs that must already be unlocked before this one can be bought. The requirement is transitive when the game totals up the techs a ship design needs.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.EditorGroup: The single build-menu group this tech is listed under in the trading window. Use it instead of [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.EditorGroups]] when the tech belongs in exactly one tab, which is what every vanilla tech does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.EditorGroups: The build-menu groups this tech is listed under in the trading window, one entry per tab it should appear in. Read only when [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules.EditorGroup]] is absent, and one of the two is required.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.0: The toggle ID, when the choice is written in the short two-element list form `[missile_type, 0]` instead of a group. Equivalent to [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules+ToggleChoice.ToggleID]].
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.1: The mode number, when the choice is written in the short two-element list form `[missile_type, 0]` instead of a group. Equivalent to [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRules+ToggleChoice.Mode]], and the list form cannot express a `PartID`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.T:: Stores data for a specific unlockable toggle choice.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.ToggleID: The part toggle this choice belongs to, matching a `PartToggleGuiRules` ID such as `missile_type`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.Mode: The mode number of the locked choice within that toggle. It is the choice's own `Mode` when the toggle declares one, otherwise its index in the toggle's `Choices` list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TechTree.TechRule.PartID: Restricts the lock to one part. Without it the choice is locked on every part that offers the toggle, and the game checks both the part-specific and the part-agnostic form when deciding whether a choice is available.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.AIHal.T:: Stores rules for AI "halt for comms" modules.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.AIHal.HaltForTrade: Whether the ship also stops for an in-progress trade rather than only for an open comms channel. With it on the ship stays put while it has pre-purchased resources pending, manual resource transfer jobs running, crew off ship, or unassigned crew aboard. Either way it does not halt if it is already within `DestinationReachedDistance` of where its current command was sending it.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.AITra.T:: Stores rules for AI trade ship modules.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Stati.T:: Stores rules for controlling what resources stations desire to buy or sell to trade ships.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Stati.ResourceType: The resource this stocking rule applies to. Only resources listed in `StationResourceTradeDeltas` are traded at all.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Stati.PercentOfTypedTiles: The share of the station's storage tiles that are dedicated to this resource that it wants filled, rolled between Min and Max on each trade. Vanilla asks for 80% to 90% across the board.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Stati.PercentOfUntypedTiles: The share of the station's untyped storage tiles it additionally wants filled with this resource, rolled between Min and Max on each trade. Negative values pull the target below what the station already holds, which makes it sell that resource to the trade ship rather than buy it. Vanilla spans -10% to 10% depending on how common the good is.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.T:: Stores rules related to the automated NPC trade routes between FTL gates and stations.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.MaxTradeShipsPerEndpoint: Multiplied by the number of trade endpoints in the system, meaning FTL gates plus operating space stations, and rounded up to get the cap on simultaneous trade ships. A system with fewer than two endpoints gets no trade ships at all. Vanilla uses 2.25.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.MaxSimultaneousTradeShipsPerStation: How many trade ships may dock at the same station at once. A ship that arrives at a full station immediately picks a different destination instead of waiting.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.TradeShipSpawnInterval: The delay between trade ship arrivals, rolled fresh after each spawn. It only counts down while the system is below the cap set by [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.TradeRoutesRules.MaxTradeShipsPerEndpoint]]. Vanilla waits 5 to 10 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.DestinationReachedDistance: How close, in tiles, a trade ship's center must get to its destination before it counts as arrived and starts trading. The `HaltForComms` AI module uses the same distance to decide the ship is already close enough to stop.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.DestinationReachedSpeed: How slowly a trade ship must be moving before it counts as arrived. The game compares the ship's squared velocity against this raw number without squaring it, so the effective cut-off is the square root. Vanilla's 0.25 therefore means half a tile per second.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.FtlRemoveDelay: How long after a trade ship starts its FTL jump-out animation at a gate before it is removed from the simulation. Vanilla ties it to the standard ship FTL effect duration so the ship vanishes as the effect ends.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.MinTradeShipSpawnDistFromEndpoints: How much room, in tiles, to leave clear of both endpoints when seeding trade ships along existing routes as a system is first generated. Ships that spawn later arrive through an FTL gate and ignore this. Vanilla keeps 1000 tiles.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.StationResourceTradeDeltas: The per-resource stocking targets stations trade toward. It also acts as the whitelist of tradeable goods, since only resource types listed here are ever moved between a station and a trade ship.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.T:: Stores rules controlling the probability that a tile spawns with a certain type of resources.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.ResourceType: The resource a storage tile is loaded with when this entry is drawn.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.RandomWeight: The relative weight of this entry on the roulette wheel used to fill each untyped storage tile. Vanilla runs from 3 for mine parts up to 40 for steel.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.RandomQuantity: The amount put in the tile as a fraction of the resource's maximum stack size, rolled between Min and Max. The low end is rounded up and the high end down before the roll.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.T:: Stores rules for a single trade ship that can spawn into the game.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.ShipID: The built-in ship design flown by this trade ship, named by its ship-library entry such as `Courier`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.Faction: The faction that owns the ship. Trade ships are only eligible in a system where their faction has some influence, and the spawned ship belongs to that faction's civilian player.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.TierRange: The node difficulty tiers this ship can appear at. One tier is rolled from the current map node's tier range and must fall inside this span for the ship to enter the pool.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.AI: The ship AI rules the trade ship runs, which for vanilla is `TradeShip` and drives the gate-to-station route logic.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.RandomWeight: The relative weight of this ship among all eligible trade ships of the same faction and tier. A weight of 0 removes it from the pool entirely.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.MultiThreadedSpawnDelay: How long the game waits while a physically spawned trade ship's design is loaded on a background thread. Saving is blocked for the duration, so keeping it short matters. Vanilla uses 1 second.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.StasisSpeed: How fast the ship travels, in tiles per second, while it is being simulated abstractly in stasis. It is also the velocity the ship is given the moment it materializes into the real simulation. Vanilla ranges from 25 for lumbering freighters to 88 for blockade runners.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.StasisTradeTime: How long a stasis trade ship sits at a station before its resources and crew are swapped in one instant transaction. Vanilla uses 20 seconds for crew shuttles and 40 to 100 seconds for freighters.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.AvoidableDoodadTags: The doodad spawner tags the ship steers around while moving in stasis, and which also disqualify a candidate spawn location. Vanilla lists `sun`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: The clearance kept around avoided doodads, in tiles. Only matters when [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.TradeShipRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]] is set. Vanilla keeps 100 tiles from suns.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.EmptyTileChance: The 0..1 chance that an untyped storage tile spawns empty instead of drawing from [[Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.TradeShipRules.ResourcesCarried]]. Tiles that already have a preferred resource type ignore this and always try to fill. Vanilla leaves 40% empty.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.TransferableCrew: The fraction of the ship's crew capacity it is willing to hand over at a station. The ship keeps at least the remaining fraction of its capacity aboard, so vanilla's 30% means a full ship gives away up to 30% of its berths' worth of crew. Crew only flows from the trade ship to the station, never back.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.RememberResourcesAndCrew: Whether the ship's stackable cargo and crew are snapshotted when it leaves the real simulation for stasis and restored when it comes back. With it false the ship reverts to a fresh loadout every time it materializes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.TradeRoutes.Trade.ResourcesCarried: The weighted pool of resources used to fill the ship's untyped storage tiles at spawn. Tiles with a preferred resource type only fill if that exact type appears in the pool.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.T:: Stores rules related to the "wanted" system.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.SearchRadius: Radius in tiles of the area police sweep around the player's last known position once they have lost sight of the player. It is scaled by the faction reputation title's `WantedSearchRadiusFactor`, and while the player is still being tracked directly the radius is 0. Vanilla uses 4000.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.AggroRadius: How far in tiles a police ship looks for a wanted search area to head for. Last known positions further away than this are ignored, so a police ship outside this range has nothing to hunt. Vanilla uses 4000.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.SearchingExpireTime: Seconds after the player was last seen before a faction gives up on that sighting and, once all of its sightings expire, despawns its police response. The faction's reputation title scales this through `WantedDurationFactor`. Vanilla uses 60 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.PoliceShipTags: Tags a builtin ship must carry to be picked as a police responder. Candidates are further filtered to the offended faction and to the tier range of the player's current fame title, and spawning throws if nothing matches. Vanilla asks for `combat`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.PoliceSpawnDistance: Distance in tiles from the player's last known position at which police warp in, rolled per ship in a random direction. Vanilla spawns them 2000 to 3000 tiles out.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.PoliceSpawnAvoidableDoodadTags: Tags of avoidable doodads that police must not warp on top of. Up to 100 spawn positions are rolled until one is clear, and the last roll is used regardless if none of them is. Vanilla avoids `sun`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.PoliceSpawnAvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra clearance in tiles added around each avoided doodad, and around AI avoided nebulas, when testing a candidate police spawn position. Vanilla uses 100.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.PoliceAIType: The ship AI given to spawned police ships, which is what makes them hunt wanted search areas. Vanilla uses `Police`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.MultiThreadedPoliceSpawnDelay: Seconds of preload time granted per police ship that is still spawning, so a wave of responders staggers in instead of stalling the game at once. Saving is blocked while a spawn is waiting. Vanilla uses 1 second.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Career.WantedRules.WantedAlertSound: The sound played the moment the wanted indicator appears on the HUD.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.T:: Stores rules for GUI elements specific to creative mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ShipLibraryIcon: The icon on the menu bar button that opens the ship library toolbox for spawning saved designs.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.DoodadsIcon: The icon on the menu bar button that opens the doodads toolbox for spawning asteroids and other scenery.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.EditNodesIcon: The icon on the galaxy map button for the tool that creates, renames and deletes star map nodes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.EditConnectionsIcon: The icon on the galaxy map button for the tool that draws and deletes connections between star map nodes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.SelectObjectsIcon: The icon on the menu bar button for the tool that selects and transforms objects already in the system.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.SelectObjectsCursor: The mouse cursor used while the select objects tool is active.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectSelectionOutlineSprite: The sprite whose material and vertex color draw the four edges of the drag selection box. Each edge takes the matching edge of the sprite's UV rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectSelectionFillSprite: The sprite that fills the inside of the drag selection box while the box is being dragged.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.SelectedObjectNineSlice: The frame drawn around every object that is already selected. It is drawn at the camera's world scale so it keeps a constant size on screen.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.TentativeSelectedObjectNineSlice: The frame drawn around objects that the current drag selection box would add once the mouse is released.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectGhostColor: Tints the translucent preview of an object drawn at its prospective new position, rotation or scale while a move, rotate or scale drag is in progress.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ShipsPresentSprite: The badge drawn on a galaxy map node that holds ships, unless it is the node the player is currently in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ShipsPresentSpriteOffset: Offsets `ShipsPresentSprite` from the node's center in map units. The offset rotates with the node and scales with the map zoom.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.OtherPlayerCursorSprite: The pointer drawn at every other player's mouse position, both in the system view and on the galaxy map, tinted with that player's color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.OtherPlayerCursorOffset: Offsets `OtherPlayerCursorSprite` from the other player's actual cursor position in pixels, so the sprite's tip rather than its corner lands on the point. It is multiplied by the global UI scale.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.DefaultNewNodeNameGenerator: Generates the name prefilled into the rename dialog that opens when a new galaxy map node is created. It is asked for a name of at most 30 characters.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.DefaultNewNodeConnectionDistance: The radius in map units searched around a new galaxy map node for existing nodes to auto connect it to. Nodes whose connection would cross an existing one are skipped, and the whole search is skipped when auto connecting is turned off.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.DefaultNewNodeConnectionLineColor: The color of the rubber band line drawn while dragging a new connection between galaxy map nodes, and of the preview lines to the nodes a new node would auto connect to.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.DeleteConnectionLine: The line style drawn over an existing galaxy map connection while the cursor hovers it, marking it as the one that would be deleted.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectMoverWidget: The drag handle that moves the selected object. One is created per selected transformable object.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectRotatorWidget: The drag handle that rotates the selected object. It is anchored above the object.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectScalerWidget: The drag handle that resizes the selected object. Four are created, one at each corner of the selection.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeGui.ObjectConfigWidget: The click handle that opens the selected object's configuration dialog.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.T:: Stores rules for the creative mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.Icon: The icon shown for Creative in the multiplayer game mode picker.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.LargeIcon: The larger icon shown for Creative on the single player new game screen.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.Gui: The GUI rules for the creative mode specific tools and overlays.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.StartingMoney: The money every player is given. Creative rewrites each player's balance to this figure on every network input tick, so spending never reduces it and the value acts as a permanent budget rather than a starting sum.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.MapSizes: The selectable galaxy sizes offered on the setup screen. The first entry is the one shown before the host picks anything.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.PlanetsGenerator: The simulation generator that populates a newly entered system with planets. It only runs when the host enabled planet generation, and it also snaps the camera out to maximum zoom.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.NebulasGenerator: The simulation generator that populates a newly entered system with nebulas. It only runs when the host enabled nebula generation.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.CreativeModeRul.FtlGatesGenerator: The simulation generator that populates a newly entered system with FTL gates. It only runs when the host enabled FTL gate generation.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.T:: Stores the base rules for adjustable widgets attached to commands.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.StateNoneSprite: The widget sprite drawn while the mouse is neither over the widget nor holding it. Its size also sets the widget's hit rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.StateOverSprite: The widget sprite drawn while the mouse hovers over it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.StateDownSprite: The widget sprite drawn while the mouse button is held on the widget.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.PixelOffset: Shifts the widget away from its anchor point, in pixels before the UI scale and the camera zoom are applied. The offset rotates with the widget and is scaled down in step with the sprite whenever `MaxWorldSize` or `MaxObjectRelativeSize` clamps it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.MaxWorldSize: Caps the widget's drawn size in world units, so the widget stops growing once the view is zoomed far enough out. Leave it at zero to disable the cap.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Creative.SOSWidgetRules.MaxObjectRelativeSize: Caps the widget's drawn size at this fraction of the shorter side of the selected object's bounding rectangle, so the handles never swamp a small object. Leave it at zero to disable the cap.

Cosmoteer.Modes.MapSize.T:: Stores information about a selectable map size.
Cosmoteer.Modes.MapSize.NameKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the map size drop list of the career and creative setup screens.
Cosmoteer.Modes.MapSize.TipKey: The localization key for the tooltip shown when hovering this entry in the map size list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.MapSize.MapGenerator: The galaxy generator run to build the star map when this size is picked. It is the only thing that actually differs between sizes, so the extent of the map lives in the generator, not here.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.T:: Stores information about a specific build area.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.Radius: The radius of a team's build circle in world units. Ships that drift outside it during the build phase are pushed back inside, and teammates' ships are spread around a circle of half this radius.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.SightRadius: The radius in world units of the vision the build area grants its own team, and only during the build phase. Vanilla makes it slightly larger than `Radius`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.TargetingAsteroidDistance: How far in world units from the build area center the practice asteroid is spawned. The direction around the build area is random.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.TargetingAsteroidRules: The doodad spawned once next to each build area to give players something to shoot at while testing their design.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.MinDistanceBuffer: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. Build and Battle lays its build areas out on a fixed ring, so it never runs the spacing check that Domination uses this for.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.AreaExpand: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. Build and Battle does not size its map from the areas it places the way Domination does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.Circle: The ring drawn around the build area in the world, tinted with the owning team's color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildAre.MinimapThicknessScale: Multiplies the minimap pixel scale used for the build area ring's thickness on the minimap, so a ring that is thin in the world stays readable at minimap size.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.T:: Stores rules for multiplayer Build and Battle mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Icon: The icon shown for Build and Battle in the multiplayer game mode picker.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.VictoryPointIcon: The empty victory point pip. One is drawn above the phase timer for each point of the host's victory point limit, and it is also the unfilled pip in the scoreboard's victory point column.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.VictoryPointWonIcon: Replaces `VictoryPointIcon` on a pip once the team has won that many rounds. The sprite is tinted with the team's color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.RefundIcon: The icon on the small button that sells a tech back during the same build phase it was bought in.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.StashIcon: The placeholder image filling the stash slot while no tech is stashed in it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.SendToStashIcon: The icon on the button that moves an offered tech into the stash so it can still be bought in a later round.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.BuildGameSpeed: Multiplies the host's build phase time limit to give the real length of a build phase. The simulation clock runs at normal speed while building, so 1 makes a build phase last exactly its configured time, while the battle phase is instead stretched by the host's game speed setting.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.CapturePointIncomeInterval: The seconds between capture point payouts during the battle phase. The same value divided by the current clock scale is shown in the label under the capture point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.BaseCountdownInterval: The spacing in seconds between countdown beeps while more than `FastCountdownStart` of the current phase remains. A beep fires whenever the whole seconds remaining is an exact multiple of this.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.FastCountdownStart: The seconds remaining in the phase at or below which beeps switch from `BaseCountdownInterval` spacing to `FastCountdownInterval` spacing.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.FastCountdownInterval: The spacing in seconds between countdown beeps once the remaining phase time has dropped to `FastCountdownStart`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.FastestCountdownStart: The seconds remaining in the phase at or below which the countdown beeps once every second, ignoring both intervals.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ShipRules: The ship class every player builds in. Its whole part list starts out locked apart from `PartsWhitelist`, and each player's starting hull is spawned from it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.AIRules: The ship AI given to the cloned combat ships when the host turns on AI controlled battles. The AI's origin is set to the capture point so the ships fight over the center of the map.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.RandomOfferingsPerRound: How many techs are offered each build phase from any category or from no category at all, on top of the per category counts in `TechOfferingsPerRound`. A category that cannot fill its quota hands its leftover slots to this pool.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ExtraFirstRoundOfferings: Added to `RandomOfferingsPerRound` during the first round only, so players get a wider choice to open with.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.TechOfferingsPerRound: Pairs of tech category and the number of techs from that category offered each build phase. Listing the same category twice is a load error, and a tech whose `Category` names a category missing from this list makes loading fail.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Techs: Every tech that can be offered during the game. Each entry's `ID` must be unique.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.PartsWhitelist: Parts of `ShipRules` that are never locked behind a tech, so they can be built from the first round on. Everything else in the ship class starts locked.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.CapturePointRules: The single capture point, which is always placed at the exact center of the map.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.BuildAreaRules: The per team build areas. One is created per team, spaced evenly around a circle 10000 world units from the map center.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.T:: Stores rules for a single technology that can be purchased by the player.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ID: The unique identifier for this tech. Other techs reference it through `Prerequisites`, and a duplicate ID is a load error.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.NameKey: The localization key for the tech name printed along the bottom of its offer button.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.DescriptionKey: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. The offer button shows only the name and the price, and there is no tooltip that would use a description.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Icon: The sprite on the tech's offer button, greyed out through the disabled icon shader while the button cannot be pressed. The button uses it without a null check even though the field is optional, so every tech should set one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.SecondaryIcon: An extra sprite drawn over `Icon` in the same rectangle at its natural size. Vanilla uses it to badge overclock techs on top of the part icon they modify.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Category: The tech categories this tech belongs to, deciding which per category slots of `TechOfferingsPerRound` may offer it. A tech with no category can only appear through a random offering, and naming a category that `TechOfferingsPerRound` does not list makes loading fail.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.PartsUnlocked: The parts added to the buyer's buildable set when the tech is purchased. A refund is refused while the player's ship still contains one of these parts and no other owned tech unlocks it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ResourcesUnlocked: The resources the buyer may start designating when the tech is purchased. A refund is refused while the ship still uses one of them and no other owned tech unlocks it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ToggleChoicesUnlocked: The part toggle settings the buyer may start selecting when the tech is purchased. A refund is refused while any part on the ship is still set to one of them and no other owned tech unlocks it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Cost: The base price of the tech in credits. Every further tech bought in the same round adds the host's additional unlock cost on top of this.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.FundsThresholdBeforeOffered: The tech stays out of the offer pool until the funds handed out through the current round reach this many credits. The comparison uses the sum of the host's per round funds up to and including the current round, not the player's actual balance.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Prerequisites: Techs the player must already own before this one can be offered. All of them are required, not just one.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.0: In the two element list shorthand `[toggle_id, mode]`, position 0 is the toggle ID. See `ToggleID`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.1: In the two element list shorthand `[toggle_id, mode]`, position 1 is the mode number. The shorthand cannot set `PartID`, so the choice covers every part with that toggle. See `Mode`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.T:: Stores data for a specific unlockable toggle choice.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.ToggleID: The part toggle this choice belongs to, matching a `ToggleID` in the game GUI's toggle list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.Mode: The mode number of the choice being unlocked. It matches a choice's `Mode` in the toggle's `Choices` list, defaulting to that choice's index when the choice does not set one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.BuildBat.PartID: Restricts the unlock to a single part type. When it is left out, the choice is locked and unlocked on every part that carries the toggle.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.T:: Stores information about a specific capture point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.Radius: The radius of the capture circle in world units. Any significant ship that can still take orders and overlaps the circle counts as occupying the point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.TimeToCapture: The seconds a single team needs inside the circle to take a neutral point from no progress to fully captured. Progress drains at the same rate when a different team moves in before the capture finishes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.TimeToUncapture: The seconds a rival team needs inside the circle to drag an already captured point back to neutral. The same rate refills progress once the owning team is alone in the circle again.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.IncomeRate: Multiplies the host's capture point income setting for the figure printed in the point's on-map label. The payout actually credited to the owning team uses the host setting unscaled, so any value other than 100% makes the label disagree with the money paid.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.MinDistanceBuffer: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. Build and Battle always places its one capture point at the map center, so the map generator spacing this feeds in Domination mode has nothing to do here.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.AreaExpand: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. Build and Battle does not size its map from capture point areas the way Domination does.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.Circle: The ring drawn at the capture radius in the world, tinted with the owning team's color and flashed through `TransitionColorMultiply` when ownership changes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.ProgressCircle: The band drawn inside the ring to show capture progress. Its outer radius is `Radius` times the current progress, and its inner radius animates over `ProgressCircleTransitionDuration`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.TextYOffset: How far below the capture ring the name and income label sits, on top of `Radius`. It is multiplied by the camera scale, so the gap widens as the view zooms out.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.TextFadeZoomRange: The two camera scales between which the capture point's label crossfades from fully transparent to fully opaque.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.MinimapThicknessScale: Multiplies the minimap pixel scale used for the ring's thickness on the minimap, so a ring that is thin in the world stays readable at minimap size.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.ProgressCircleTransitionDuration: The seconds the progress band takes to collapse or expand after the point reaches full capture or starts slipping away from it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.ColorTransitionDuration: The seconds the ring takes to fade from the previous owner's color to the new owner's color after the point changes hands.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.TransitionColorMultiply: Multiplied into the ring color during a change of ownership, peaking halfway through `ColorTransitionDuration` and returning to white at the end. Vanilla doubles the alpha so the ring flashes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.AlertSound: Plays for the owning team's players at the moment a fully captured point starts losing progress to a rival.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.ActivateSound: Plays for the capturing team's players the instant progress reaches full and the point becomes theirs.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.BuildBattle.CaptureP.DeactivateSound: Plays for the losing team's players the instant progress reaches zero and the point goes neutral.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.T:: Stores information about a specific capture point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.Radius: The radius of the capture point circle in world units. A ship must physically overlap this circle to occupy the point, and the same radius is passed to `RandomGenerators` as the area to fill with scenery.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.TimeToCapture: How long a team must sit alone in a neutral point to take it. The same rate runs backwards while a different team is the sole occupant, so a claim in progress is undone at the speed it was made.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.TimeToUncapture: How long an enemy team must sit in an already captured point to knock it back to neutral. Once the enemy leaves, the owner's hold recovers at the same rate.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.IncomeRate: Multiplies the host's chosen capture point income to give this point's payout per income tick. Vanilla uses 100%, 200% and 300% for the small, large and huge points.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.CaptureBonus: The one-off payout a team receives the moment it finishes capturing the point, as a multiple of the point's own income. Vanilla pays exactly one extra income tick.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.MinDistanceBuffer: The minimum clearance in world units the map generator keeps between this point and any other capture or spawn point. It is checked from both sides, so whichever of the two buffers is larger wins.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.AreaExpand: The area in square world units this capture point type contributes to the circle the map is generated inside. The generator adds it once per capture point type rather than once per placed point, so raising `CapturePointTypeCounts` does not make the map any bigger.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.RandomGenerators: The pool of simulation generators for the scenery inside the point, one of which is picked at random and run centered on the point with a radius of `Radius`. All points in one symmetric set share the same pick, so mirrored map halves stay identical.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.Circle: The ring drawn around the capture point in the world, tinted with the owning team's color. Its `Thickness` also pushes the drawn radius outward by half a thickness so the ring sits just outside the actual capture area.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.ProgressCircle: The renderer for the disc that fills in as a capture progresses. Its `InnerRadius` and `Thickness` are overwritten every frame from the current progress, so only the texture, color and quad count of this renderer matter.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.TextYOffset: The gap between the bottom of the capture point circle and its name and income label. It is scaled by the camera scale so the gap looks constant on screen rather than in world units.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.TextFadeZoomRange: The camera scale range over which the capture point's label fades in. Vanilla `[600, 300]` makes the label invisible when zoomed out to 600 and fully opaque at 300 or closer.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.MinimapThicknessScale: Multiplies the minimap pixel scale used for the capture point ring's thickness on the minimap, so a ring that is thin in the world stays readable at minimap size.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.ProgressCircleTransitionDuration: How long the progress disc takes to wipe in or out once capture progress arrives at or leaves full. The wipe runs from the moment progress last hit full.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.ColorTransitionDuration: How long the capture point ring takes to blend from the previous owner's color to the new owner's color after ownership changes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.TransitionColorMultiply: The color the ring is multiplied by at the peak of the pulse that runs alongside the ownership color transition. Vanilla's alpha of 510 pulses the ring to double opacity and back.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.NeutralIcon: The sprite for this point in the row of capture point icons next to the match timer, shown while no team owns it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.OwnedIcon: The sprite for this point in the row of capture point icons next to the match timer, shown once a team owns it and tinted with that team's color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.AlertSound: Plays for the owning team the moment an enemy starts pushing a fully held point back toward neutral.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.ActivateSound: Plays for a team the moment it finishes capturing the point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.CapturePo.DeactivateSound: Plays for the team that just lost the point when it drops back to neutral.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.T:: Stores the rules for generation a domination mode map.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.NameKey: The localization key for this map style's name in the host's map style drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.DescriptionKey: The localization key for the tooltip shown beside the map style in the lobby.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.Teams: The number of teams this map style is built for, which also sets the rotational symmetry of everything the generator places. A value of 2 additionally lets the generator pick a left-right mirrored layout at random instead of a rotated one.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.CapturePointTypeCounts: The total number of capture points of each type to place across the whole map, positionally matching `DominationModeRules/CapturePointTypes`. A count that is not a multiple of `Teams` has its remainder replaced by exactly one extra point placed alone at the map center, so `[2, 1, 0]` on a two-team map means one small point per team plus a single large point in the middle.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.StartingCapturePointTypeCountsPerTeam: How many capture points of each type each team already owns at match start, positionally matching `DominationModeRules/CapturePointTypes`. Lone points at the map center are never pre-owned, so only points placed in symmetric sets can be counted here.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.DoodadTypeCounts: The doodads scattered symmetrically over the generated map, on top of whatever the asteroid and nebula generators add. Every doodad in one symmetric group is generated from the same random seed, so mirrored halves of the map look identical.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.T:: Stores rules for multiplayer domination mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.Icon: The sprite identifying domination mode in the multiplayer game list and in the lobby's mode header.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.IncomeInterval: How often every team is paid its accumulated basic and capture point income. The capture point label and the income readout divide it by the current game speed so they show real seconds.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.SpawnSeparationRadiusFactor: Inflates each ship's bounding circle by this factor while a newly spawned ship is pushed clear of existing ships. Values above 1 leave visible space between hulls instead of parking them edge to edge.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.JunkDamageFractionPerTick: The fraction of a part's max health destroyed each time decay damage hits a part of a derelict ship. Ships whose rules set `ImmuneToEnvDamage` are skipped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.JunkDamageChancePerTick: The chance per physics tick that any one part of a derelict ship is hit by decay damage. Vanilla writes it as a per-second figure divided by `PhysicsUpdatesPerSecond`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.PerimeterDistance: The clearance in world units left between the outermost capture or spawn point circle and the perimeter of death. Domination has no perimeter distance drop list in the lobby, so this fixed value is used for every match instead of `PvpModeRules/PerimeterDistances`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.MapStyles: The map layouts offered in the host's lobby drop list, in declaration order. The host's choice is stored as an index, so inserting an entry in the middle changes what saved rulesets select.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.CapturePointTypes: The capture point types a map style may place. `CapturePointTypeCounts` and `StartingCapturePointTypeCountsPerTeam` index into this list by position.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.Dominatio.SpawnPointType: The single spawn point definition used for every team's spawn area.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.DoodadTyp.T:: How many doodads of one type a domination map places, and the conditions that have to hold for them to appear.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.DoodadTyp.DoodadID: The doodad type to scatter over the map. Its `SpawnRadius` is what the generator keeps clear of other objects, so a doodad with a small spawn radius may end up crowding capture points. Also accepted as element 0 of the positional `[id, count, conditions]` form vanilla uses.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.DoodadTyp.Count: How many of this doodad to place across the whole map. The count is rounded down to a multiple of the map style's `Teams` so every team gets the same share, and the remainder is dropped rather than placed at the center. Also accepted as element 1 of the positional form.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.DoodadTyp.Conditions: Conditions checked once per doodad just before it is created, with the doodad skipped if they fail. Domination only supplies the map's spawn flags, so `RequireSpawnFlags` and `ProhibitSpawnFlags` are the useful ones and the career-only checks such as sector type and node tier never reject anything. Vanilla prohibits `disable_asteroids` so asteroid doodads vanish when the host turns asteroid spawning off. Also accepted as element 2 of the positional form.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.T:: Stores information about a specific spawn point.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.Radius: The radius of the spawn area in world units. New ships appear at its center, and any enemy ship overlapping the circle takes damage.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.SightRadius: The radius of the vision the spawn point grants its own team, in world units, independent of any ship being present. Vanilla makes it twice `Radius`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.EnemyDamageFractionPerTick: The fraction of a part's max health destroyed each time an enemy ship inside the spawn area is hit. Unlike the perimeter and junk damage, this ignores `ImmuneToEnvDamage`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.EnemyDamageChancePerTick: The chance per physics tick that any one part of an enemy ship inside the spawn area is hit. The hits play `PvpModeRules/PerimeterDamageMediaEffects`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.MinDistanceBuffer: The minimum clearance in world units the map generator keeps between this spawn point and any capture point. It is checked from both sides, so whichever of the two buffers is larger wins.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.AreaExpand: The area in square world units one team's spawn point contributes to the circle the map is generated inside. It is multiplied by the map style's team count, so more teams give a proportionally larger map.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.Circle: The ring drawn around the spawn area in the world, tinted with the owning team's color.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Domination.SpawnPoin.MinimapThicknessScale: Multiplies the minimap pixel scale used for the spawn area ring's thickness on the minimap, so a ring that is thin in the world stays readable at minimap size.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.Eliminat.T:: Stores rules for multiplayer elimination mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.Eliminat.Icon: The sprite identifying elimination mode in the multiplayer game list and in the lobby's mode header.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.Eliminat.VictoryConditions: The destruction goal choices offered in the host's lobby drop list. Exactly one entry must set `IsDefault` or the lobby throws.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.Eliminat.FullHealthColor: The color of a team's strength bar while that team still has all of its starting fleet value.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.Eliminat.ZeroHealthColor: The color of a team's strength bar once its remaining fleet value reaches zero. The bar blends between this and `FullHealthColor` in HSVA, so a hue difference sweeps through the intervening hues rather than desaturating.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.VictoryC.T:: An option that the host can choose that determines how a game is won.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.VictoryC.DestructionGoal: The fraction of a team's starting fleet value that must be destroyed before that team counts as knocked out, from 0 to 1. It also marks the empty portion of the team strength bar, and a value of 0 turns the check off entirely so no team is ever eliminated by damage.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.VictoryC.NameFmtKey: The localization key for this option's label in the lobby drop list. It is formatted with `DestructionGoal` already multiplied by 100, so the format string supplies the percent sign itself.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Elimination.VictoryC.IsDefault: Marks this the option preselected when the lobby opens. Exactly one entry in `VictoryConditions` must set it or the lobby throws.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.FleetDistance.T:: An option that the host can choose that controls the distance between each team's fleet.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.FleetDistance.Distance: How far in world units from the map center each team's fleet starts.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.FleetDistance.NameFmtKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the fleet distance drop list. It is formatted with one argument, `Distance` in world units.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.FleetDistance.IsDefault: Marks the entry preselected when the host opens the lobby. Exactly one entry in the list must set it, since the game takes the first match and throws when there is none.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.OfficialRuleset.T:: Stores an official ruleset for a game mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.OfficialRuleset.NameKey: The localization key for the ruleset's name in the lobby's ruleset drop list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.OfficialRuleset.ShortNameKey: The localization key for a compact name, shown beside the match in the multiplayer game browser where the full name would not fit.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.OfficialRuleset.IsDefault: Marks the ruleset applied when the host opens the lobby. Unlike the other option lists this one tolerates having no default, in which case the lobby starts on the built-in fallback values.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PerimeterDistance.T:: An option that the host can choose to adjust the "perimeter of death".
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PerimeterDistance.Radius: The starting radius of the perimeter of death in world units. Modes with a shrinking perimeter scale this down as the phase runs out.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PerimeterDistance.NameFmtKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the perimeter drop list. It is formatted with one argument, `Radius` in world units.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PerimeterDistance.IsDefault: Marks the entry preselected when the host opens the lobby. Exactly one entry in the list must set it, since the game takes the first match and throws when there is none.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.T:: Stores rules for multiplayer arena mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.Icon: The sprite identifying arena mode in the multiplayer game list and in the lobby's mode header.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.ValuePerPoint: How many credits of ship value are worth one arena point. A ship enters the match carrying its total physical value divided by this, rounded up, and that pool is what attackers earn as they chew through it.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.RollingDamageTime: The window of recent damage remembered per attacker on each ship. When a ship finally dies, the leftover points are split between players in proportion to the damage they did inside this window, so a finishing blow alone does not take the whole kill.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.RespawnDelay: How long after a player loses all their ships before they respawn automatically.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.ManualRespawnCooldown: The minimum time after a player's last spawn before the manual respawn button becomes usable again.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.NotRespawningPenaltyFractionPerSecond: The fraction of a player's current score drained per second while they sit dead and refuse to respawn. The drain only touches players with a positive score, so it cannot push anyone below zero on its own.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.NotRespawningPenaltyDelay: The grace period on top of `RespawnDelay` before the score drain starts, in seconds. It is declared as a plain number rather than a `Time` unlike every other duration here, so time-style values are not accepted.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.RespawnSelfDestructDuration: How long an abandoned ship takes to self destruct once its owner despawns with no points left on that ship. Ships that still hold points are left floating as abandoned wrecks instead.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.MinRespawnDistanceFromCenter: The radius from the map center at which the search for a respawn position starts, in world units. It grows by `RespawnCheckDistanceIncrement` each time a full circle of candidate angles is rejected.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.MinRespawnDistanceFromOthers: The clearance kept from other living ships when placing a respawning fleet, in world units. The fleet's own bounding radius is added on top, so this is a gap between hulls rather than between centers.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.RespawnCheckAngleIncrement: The angular step between candidate respawn positions tested around the current search radius. Smaller values try more spots per ring at the cost of more work per respawn.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.RespawnCheckDistanceIncrement: How far the respawn search radius grows in world units after every candidate angle at the current radius has been rejected.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.JunkDamageFractionPerTick: The fraction of a part's max health destroyed each time decay damage hits a part of a derelict or abandoned ship. Ships whose rules set `ImmuneToEnvDamage` are skipped.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.JunkDamageChancePerTick: The chance per physics tick that any one part of a derelict or abandoned ship is hit by decay damage. Vanilla sets both this and the fraction to 1 so abandoned hulls are shredded almost immediately.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Arena.Are.EnemyDefeatedSound: Plays for the local player when they are credited with finishing off an enemy ship, alongside the enemy defeated banner.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.T:: The base class for PvP pointmatch-style mode rules.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.MinGoalPoints: The lowest score the host may set as the target to win, enforced by the goal points number box in the lobby.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.MaxGoalPoints: The highest score the host may set as the target to win, enforced by the goal points number box in the lobby.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.DefaultGoalPoints: The score the goal points box starts at when the lobby opens.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.ShipSpawnInvulnerabilityDuration: How long a freshly respawned ship cannot be damaged. It is applied only on respawn, not to the fleet a player starts the match with.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.PointsTickUpSound: The looping sound played while the score readout counts upward. The duration of its first sound also decides how fast the readout counts, capped at half a second per change.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Pointmatch.Pointmatc.PointsTickDownSound: The looping sound played while the score readout counts downward, with its first sound's duration setting the count speed the same way `PointsTickUpSound` does.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpMapType.T:: An option that the host can choose that controls the density of asteroids.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpMapType.Generator: The simulation generator run when this entry is picked, used for both the asteroid density and the nebula type lists. Vanilla gives the None entries a generator with an empty spawner list.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpMapType.NameKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the drop list. Unlike the other PvP option types this is used as a plain key, not as a format string.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpMapType.IsDefault: Marks the entry preselected when the host opens the lobby. Exactly one entry in the list must set it, since the game takes the first match and throws when there is none.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.T:: The base class for PvP mode rules.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.MapGenerator: The galaxy generator run once at match start to build the map the battle takes place on. The generated node closest to the origin becomes the sector everyone plays in, and vanilla points this at an otherwise empty galaxy so a PvP match is a single sector.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.AllowedShipClasses: The set of ship classes a design must belong to before it counts as legal for this mode. A design of any other class is rejected, alongside the `RequiredPartCategories` and blueprint validity checks.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.RequiredPartCategories: The part categories a design must have at least one part from, all of them. Missing even a single listed category makes the design illegal for the mode, and vanilla requires only `command`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.Teams: The team-count choices offered in the host's lobby drop list. A `TeamCount` of 0 means free for all, where every player becomes their own team, and exactly one entry must set `IsDefault` or the lobby throws.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.TimeLimits: The match-length choices offered in the host's lobby drop list. Exactly one entry must set `IsDefault`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.AsteroidDensities: The asteroid-field choices offered in the host's lobby drop list. The chosen entry's `Generator` is run at match start over the whole play area, out to the perimeter radius.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.NebulasTypes: The nebula choices offered in the host's lobby drop list. The chosen entry's `Generator` is run at match start over the whole play area, exactly like `AsteroidDensities`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.FleetDistances: The starting-separation choices offered in the host's lobby drop list, in world units. With two teams each fleet is placed this far from the map center, and with more teams the value is treated as an edge-to-edge gap and converted into a circumradius.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterDistances: The choices offered in the host's lobby drop list for the breathing room between the outermost starting object and the perimeter of death, in world units. A chosen `Radius` of 0 disables the perimeter entirely.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterDamageFractionPerTick: The fraction of a part's max health destroyed each time the perimeter of death hits it, before the distance term is added. Only parts whose own center lies outside the current perimeter are eligible.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterDamageFractionPerTickPerDistanc: Extra damage fraction added per world unit that the ship's center sits beyond the perimeter, on top of `PerimeterDamageFractionPerTick`. The distance is measured once per ship, so every eligible part on that ship takes the same amount.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterDamageChancePerTick: The chance per physics tick that any one part outside the perimeter is hit. Vanilla writes it as a per-second figure divided by `PhysicsUpdatesPerSecond`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterDamageMediaEffects: The effects played at each part the perimeter of death damages. Domination mode reuses this same list for the damage enemy ships take inside a spawn point, despite the name.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterCircle: The ring drawn at the perimeter of death, rendered only when the perimeter is not fully on screen. Its `UVRect` width is recomputed at match start from the circumference and `Thickness` so the texture repeats evenly all the way round.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.PerimeterCircleThicknessZoomExponent: The exponent applied to the camera's world scale before it multiplies the perimeter ring's thickness. 0 keeps the ring a constant width in world units and 1 makes it scale fully with zoom, and vanilla uses .4 for something in between.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.GameEndSound: The sound played once when the match ends.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.SpawnPatterns: The starting formation offsets for one player's fleet, indexed by ship count minus one, so the first entry is used for a single ship, the second for two ships and so on. Each offset is scaled by `DistBetweenShipsInPattern` plus twice the largest ship's bounding radius, so the values are relative rather than absolute positions.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.DistBetweenShipsInPattern: The base spacing multiplied into the `SpawnPatterns` offsets, in world units. Twice the largest ship's bounding radius is added to it first, so the gap grows with fleet size.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.DistBetweenPlayersOnTeam: The vertical gap left between the formations of two players on the same team when their fleets are stacked at match start, in world units. Build Battle mode uses this value in place of `DistBetweenShipsInPattern` when it lays out a team.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.ShipSaleRefund: The fraction of a ship's or part's cost paid back when it is sold. Vanilla refunds 75%.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.NebulaSizeFactor: Multiplies the size of the nebula triangle grid used to render and simulate nebulas in PvP matches. Vanilla shrinks it to 0.2 of the default so nebulas have finer detail on a small map.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.ForfeitIcon: The sprite on the forfeit button in the in-game HUD.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.PvpModeRules.OfficialRulesets: The preset lobby configurations offered at the top of the rulesets drop list, above any custom rulesets the player has saved. Each entry's `Options` group supplies values by the same setting names the lobby widgets use.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Ruleset.T:: Stores a ruleset for a game mode.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Ruleset.Options: The lobby settings this ruleset presets, keyed by each mode config option's sync name. Drop lists take the index of the wanted entry, checkboxes take 0 or 1, and number boxes take the number itself. Options left out keep their built-in default.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Teams.T:: An option that the host can choose to select the number of teams.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Teams.TeamCount: How many teams the match is split into. Zero means free for all, where every player becomes their own team and the scoreboard hides team grouping.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Teams.NameFmtKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the teams drop list. It is formatted with one argument, `TeamCount`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.Teams.IsDefault: Marks the entry preselected when the host opens the lobby. Exactly one entry in the list must set it, since the game takes the first match and throws when there is none.

Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.TimeLimit.T:: An option that the host can choose to give the game a time limit.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.TimeLimit.Seconds: The length of the timed phase in seconds. A value of zero or less means no time limit at all.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.TimeLimit.NameFmtKey: The localization key for this entry's label in the time limit drop list. It is formatted with one argument, `Seconds` divided by 60, so the vanilla strings print minutes.
Cosmoteer.Modes.Pvp.TimeLimit.IsDefault: Marks the entry preselected when the host opens the lobby. Exactly one entry in the list must set it, since the game takes the first match and throws when there is none.

Cosmoteer.Modes.StatusFactors.0: Has no effect, like the rest of this type. In the list shorthand, position 0 is `Chance`. A one element list leaves `Value` at zero instead of at its usual default of 1, while writing a bare number instead of a list or group copies that number into both fields.
Cosmoteer.Modes.StatusFactors.1: Has no effect, like the rest of this type. In the two element list shorthand `[chance, value]`, position 1 is `Value`.
Cosmoteer.Modes.StatusFactors.T:: Scales both how often a status lands and how much of it lands. Written as one number to scale both, or as a `[chance, value]` pair.
Cosmoteer.Modes.StatusFactors.Chance: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. It was meant to scale how often a status such as fire takes hold between the player and the enemies at a given career combat difficulty, but nothing in the game ever asks for the factors.
Cosmoteer.Modes.StatusFactors.Value: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. It was meant to scale the strength of an applied status, alongside `Chance`.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFileTrackRules.T:: Stores rules for a music track that simply reads from a single audio file.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFileTrackRules.File: Path to the audio file this track streams. The game registers the `music` extension as Ogg Vorbis, so tracks point at `.music` (Ogg) files. The filename also serves as the track's default name in the music debugger when no [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DebugName|DebugName]] is given.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules.T:: Stores rules for a music track that plays a finite state machine of sub-tracks.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules.IntroTracks: Candidate starting states for the state machine, one of which is chosen at random when the track begins. Required. The constructor iterates it with no null check, so an FSM track without this key crashes on load. Each state's own [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules+FsmState#NextTracks|NextTracks]] chains into the rest of the machine, falling back to [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules#DefaultNextTracks|DefaultNextTracks]].
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules.FirstBootIntroTracks: Alternate set of starting states used only on the game's very first boot. When unset the machine starts from [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules#IntroTracks|IntroTracks]] as usual.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules.DefaultNextTracks: Fallback set of next states used whenever the current state's own [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules+FsmState#NextTracks|NextTracks]] is unset. If this is also unset the machine has nowhere to go and the track ends.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules/FsmSt.T:: A single track in the state machine.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules/FsmSt.CueCondition: Python expression evaluated against the music parameters that gates whether this state is eligible to be chosen. When it returns false the state is skipped during selection. With no condition the state is always eligible.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules/FsmSt.MaxConsecutivePlays: Cap on how many times in a row this same state may be selected. Once it has played back-to-back this many times it is excluded from the next random pick, forcing variety. The default is effectively unlimited.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules/FsmSt.NextTracks: Candidate states the machine may move to when this state's track finishes, one chosen at random among those whose [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules+FsmState#CueCondition|CueCondition]] and [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules+FsmState#MaxConsecutivePlays|MaxConsecutivePlays]] allow it. When unset the machine falls back to the track's [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules#DefaultNextTracks|DefaultNextTracks]].

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicLayersTrackRules.T:: Stores rules for a music track that combines multiple sub-layers.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicLayersTrackRules.Layers: Sub-tracks mixed together and played simultaneously, their samples summed. Required. The track sizes its layer array from this collection with no null check, so a layers track without this key crashes on load. Combine with per-layer [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolume|DynamicVolume]] or [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#ZoomVolumes|ZoomVolumes]] to fade individual layers in and out over the same passage.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.T:: Stores rules related to the game music.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.RootTrack: Top-level track of the whole music system, rendered continuously by the game. Every other track hangs off it as a sub-track. If its [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicCondition|DynamicCondition]] or [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolume|DynamicVolume]] is left unset, the game supplies `True` and `1` respectively.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.BufferTime: Amount of audio, in seconds, buffered ahead when streaming the music. Fed into the streaming sound configuration. Larger values guard against playback hitches at the cost of latency when the music changes.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.MenuZoom: Zoom value supplied to every track's [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#ZoomVolumes|ZoomVolumes]] curve when the game is not in a simulation, such as in menus. In-game the real camera scale is used instead.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.ChannelCount: Number of audio channels the music is rendered at (for example 2 for stereo). Propagated to every track and used together with [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules#Frequency|Frequency]] to convert between samples and playback time.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules.Frequency: Sample rate in Hz at which the music is rendered (for example 44100). Determines how sample counts map to seconds, driving every time-based feature such as [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#TimeVolumes|TimeVolumes]] and the fade-out timings.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicSequenceTrackRules.T:: Stores rules for a music track that plays a series of sub-tracks in sequence.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicSequenceTrackRules.Tracks: Sub-tracks played one after another in the listed order, advancing to the next as each finishes. Required. The track reads its length with no null check, so a sequence track without this key crashes on load, and a written-but-empty list throws for having no sub-tracks.

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicSilenceTrackRules.T:: Stores rules for a music track that is simply a specific length of silence.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicSilenceTrackRules.Length: Duration in seconds of the silence this track produces. Useful as a timed gap between sub-tracks in a [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicSequenceTrackRules|Sequence]] or as a state in an [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicFsmTrackRules|FSM]].

Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.T:: The base class for rules for a single music track.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.DebugName: Name shown for this track in the in-game music debugger. When absent the track shows a generic default based on its kind (`FSM`, `Sequence`, `Layers`, `Silence`, or the source filename for a file track).
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.Loop: How many additional times the track replays after its first pass through. `0` plays it once, `2` plays it three times total, and any negative value loops forever.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.TimeVolumes: Volume envelope keyed on elapsed playback time. Each pair is `[seconds, volume]` where volume is a multiplier applied to the samples. The game interpolates linearly between points, holds the first point's volume before it and the last point's volume after it.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.ZoomVolumes: Volume envelope keyed on camera zoom, letting a track fade in or out as the player zooms. Each pair is `[zoom, volume]`. Interpolation happens in log2 space of the zoom value, so the curve is even across zoom octaves. The zoom fed in is the game camera scale, or [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules#MenuZoom|MenuZoom]] while in menus. See [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#ZoomVolumeVelocityUp|ZoomVolumeVelocityUp]] for how fast it responds.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.ZoomVolumeVelocityUp: Rate per second at which the track's zoom volume rises toward its target when the target increases. `1` reaches the target over one second. Set both this and [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#ZoomVolumeVelocityDown|ZoomVolumeVelocityDown]] at once with the `ZoomVolumeVelocity` alias.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.ZoomVolumeVelocityDown: Rate per second at which the track's zoom volume falls toward its target when the target decreases. `1` reaches the target over one second. The `ZoomVolumeVelocity` alias sets this and [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#ZoomVolumeVelocityUp|ZoomVolumeVelocityUp]] together.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.DynamicCondition: Python expression evaluated every buffer against the music parameters (game state such as zoom, battle, paused). When it returns false the track is silenced. Combined multiplicatively with [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolume|DynamicVolume]]. On the [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules#RootTrack|RootTrack]] it defaults to `True` when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.DynamicVolume: Python expression returning a volume multiplier evaluated every buffer against the music parameters. Applied on top of [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicCondition|DynamicCondition]]. On the [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicRules#RootTrack|RootTrack]] it defaults to `1` when left unset. Its approach speed is governed by [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolumeVelocityUp|DynamicVolumeVelocityUp]].
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.DynamicVolumeVelocityUp: Rate per second at which the dynamic volume rises toward its target when the target increases. `1` reaches the target over one second. The `DynamicVolumeVelocity` alias sets this and [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolumeVelocityDown|DynamicVolumeVelocityDown]] together.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.DynamicVolumeVelocityDown: Rate per second at which the dynamic volume falls toward its target when the target decreases. `1` reaches the target over one second. The `DynamicVolumeVelocity` alias also sets [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#DynamicVolumeVelocityUp|DynamicVolumeVelocityUp]].
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.FadeOutAfter: Seconds of playback after which the track begins fading out, gated by [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutCondition|FadeOutCondition]]. [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutDuration|FadeOutDuration]] must also be set or the game throws when the fade would start.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.FadeOutDuration: Length in seconds of the fade to silence once a fade-out is triggered by [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutAfter|FadeOutAfter]] or [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutOnSimPop|FadeOutOnSimPop]]. Required whenever a fade can occur.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.SilenceAfterFadeOut: Seconds of silence appended after the fade completes before the track counts as finished. Defaults to zero.
