Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.FadeOutCondition: Python expression that gates the [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutAfter|FadeOutAfter]] fade. Once the elapsed time is reached the fade only starts if this returns true. With no condition the fade starts as soon as the time elapses.
Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules.FadeOutOnSimPop: When true the track fades out whenever the active simulation root changes, for example when the player leaves a battle or simulation. Uses [[Cosmoteer.Music.MusicTrackRules#FadeOutDuration|FadeOutDuration]] for the fade length.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaActiveEffectRule.T:: The base class for nebula effects that are actively applied to objects within the nebula.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaBuffRules.T:: S Stores rules and acts as an IBuffProvider for a buff provided by a nebula.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaBuffRules.BuffType: The buff applied to every part of a ship while it is inside the nebula. See `BuffAmount` for the strength.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaBuffRules.BuffAmount: The buff value provided at full nebula strength, scaled linearly by how deeply the ship is immersed in the nebula (0 at the outer feather edge, 1 well inside). Vanilla uses fractions such as `90%` for a bonus and `-40%` for a penalty.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageCrewEffect.T:: Stores rules for a nebula active effect that damages crew within the nebula.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageCrewEffect.DamageChancePerCrewPerTick: The probability per physics tick that a single crew member in space inside the nebula takes a hit, multiplied by the nebula strength at that crew member's location. Values of 0 or less disable the effect entirely.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageCrewEffect.DamagePerCrewPerTick: The hit points removed from a crew member each time the `DamageChancePerCrewPerTick` roll succeeds. The damage is clamped so health never drops below `MinHealthRemaining`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageCrewEffect.MinHealthRemaining: The health floor this effect will not damage a crew member below. Leave at 0 to let the nebula kill crew outright.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageCrewEffect.OnDamageMediaEffects: The one-shot media effects played at the crew member's location whenever this effect actually removes health.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageShipsEffec.T:: Stores rules for a nebula active effect that damages ships within the nebula.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageShipsEffec.DamageChancePerPartPerTick: The expected number of parts damaged per physics tick expressed per part on the ship, multiplied by the ship's nebula strength. A ship with 200 parts and a value of 0.001 loses health on about 0.2 parts per tick. Values of 0 or less disable the effect entirely.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageShipsEffec.DamageFractionPerPartPerTick: The fraction of a part's MaxHealth removed each time that part is picked for damage. It is also passed to `OnDamageMediaEffects` as the effect Intensity.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageShipsEffec.MinHealthRemaining: The health floor this effect will not damage a part below. Leave at 0 to let the nebula destroy parts outright.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaDamageShipsEffec.OnDamageMediaEffects: The one-shot media effects played on each part that gets damaged. The effect Intensity is set to `DamageFractionPerPartPerTick`.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaLightningStrikes.T:: Stores rules for a nebula active effect that strikes ships with random bolts of lightning.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaLightningStrikes.LightningChancePerTilePerTick: The number of strike attempts per physics tick per tile of the ship's bounding rectangle, multiplied by the ship's nebula strength. Each attempt picks a random tile in that rectangle and does nothing if no part occupies it, so the actual strike rate works out to roughly one per ship part. Values of 0 or less disable the effect entirely.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaLightningStrikes.OriginDistanceFromShip: The random distance in tiles, measured outward from the ship's bounding radius, at which a bolt originates. The strike is cancelled if the chosen origin lies outside the nebula or if any ship overlaps a circle of radius `OriginDistanceFromShip` Min around it.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaLightningStrikes.HitEffects: The hit effects applied where the bolt's ray cast first connects, which may be a shield or a different ship than the one that attracted the strike.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaLightningStrikes.MediaEffects: The one-shot media effects played at the impact point, with SourceLocation set to the bolt origin so a beam can be drawn between the two.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.T:: Stores rules that apply to all nebula types.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.DefaultTriangleSize: The side length in tiles of one cell of the equilateral-triangle grid the nebula map is stored on. Vanilla uses 2000. The value is scaled at runtime by the sim mode's nebula size factor.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.RegionSize: The size in triangle cells, as [columns, rows], of one nebula render batch. Larger regions mean fewer draw calls but more geometry rebuilt whenever a single triangle changes.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.MaxPathfindIterations: The cap on A-star nodes expanded per contiguous nebula group when routing a ship around nebulas. Raising it lets ships find their way around larger obstructions at the cost of more CPU per path request.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.MaxStasisPathfindsPerTick: The number of nebula path searches stasis spawners may perform per tick across the whole simulation. Extra requests reuse the previous cached result until the next tick.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.MinToolTipZoom: The minimum camera scale at which the nebula tooltip is shown under the mouse. This uses the same scale as `Camera/MinScale` and `Camera/MaxScale` in cosmoteer.rules, where larger numbers mean further zoomed out, so vanilla's 500 only shows the tooltip at strategic zoom levels.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.StasisIgnoredNebulaTypes: The nebula types stasis spawners treat as passable when picking spawn locations and routes. Types listed here are ignored even if they set `DefaultAvoidDistance`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaRules.NebulaTypes: Every nebula type in the game. Each entry is a full NebulaTypeRules definition, in vanilla pulled in from a separate file per type.

Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.T:: Stores the rules for a particular type of nebula.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.ID: The identifier other rules use to refer to this nebula type, for example `NebulaType` on a Nebula spawner, `NebulaID` on a nebula doodad, or an entry in NebulaRules `StasisIgnoredNebulaTypes`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.ToolTipKey: The localization key for the tooltip shown when the mouse hovers over this nebula in the world, and also for the nebula icon on the ship info card. Without it no world tooltip appears at all, regardless of NebulaRules `MinToolTipZoom`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.HudIcon: The icon shown on a ship's info card while the ship is inside this nebula. Setting it is what creates the card entry at all, so a nebula without it shows no status icon even if it has a `HudTextKey`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.HudHiddenIcon: The variant of `HudIcon` shown while the ship is hidden from sight. The check is on the ship being hidden at all, not on this nebula being the one hiding it, so a ship hidden by one nebula also swaps the icon of any other nebula it is in. Falls back to `HudIcon` when unset.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.HudTextKey: The localization key for the text drawn under the nebula icon on the ship info card. It is formatted with one argument, the nebula strength at that ship as a percentage from 0 to 100.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DefaultLogicalFeather: The distance in tiles over which nebula strength ramps from 0 outside the nebula to 1 inside it. Everything gameplay related scales with that strength, including buffs, sight and radar factors, damping and active effects. See `DefaultVisualFeather` for the purely cosmetic edge softness.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DefaultVisualFeather: The [min, max] width in tiles of the soft rendered edge of the nebula. The mesh carries both widths per vertex and the shader blends between them using `DefaultVisualFeatherOverZoom`, so the nebula edge gets softer as the camera zooms out.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DefaultVisualFeatherOverZoom: The [zoomed in, zoomed out] camera scale range over which the drawn edge interpolates from `DefaultVisualFeather` Min to its Max. It uses the same scale as `Camera/MinScale` and `Camera/MaxScale` in cosmoteer.rules, and vanilla's [100, 4000] spans from mid zoom to fully zoomed out.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DefaultVisualFeatherOverZoomExponent: The exponent applied to the normalized camera scale before interpolating across `DefaultVisualFeatherOverZoom`. Values below 1, such as vanilla's 0.5, reach the wide feather earlier while zooming out.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.SharpCurveEdges: The number of line segments used to round off a fully convex 120 degree corner of the nebula outline. Higher values give smoother blobs at the cost of more triangles.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DullCurveEdges: The number of line segments used to round off the shallower 30 degree corners of the nebula outline. See `SharpCurveEdges` for the fully convex case.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.SightRangeFactor: The multiplier on a ship's visual sight range at full nebula strength. The applied factor is interpolated from 1 at the nebula edge to this value deep inside, and factors from overlapping nebulas multiply together.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.RadarRangeFactor: The multiplier on a ship's radar range at full nebula strength, interpolated from 1 at the nebula edge the same way as `SightRangeFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.HidesToOutsideObserversThreshold: The nebula strength from 0 to 1 at or above which a ship or crew member becomes invisible to observers that are not inside the same contiguous patch of this nebula. Leave unset to never hide anything. The vanilla cloudy nebula uses 0%, so merely touching the feathered edge is enough.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.HidesRadarToOutsideObserversThreshold: The nebula strength from 0 to 1 at or above which a ship's radar signature is hidden from observers outside the same contiguous patch. See `HidesToOutsideObserversThreshold` for visual hiding.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.LinearDampingFactor: The multiplier on a ship's linear drag at full nebula strength, interpolated from 1 at the nebula edge. Values below 1 make ships coast further, values above 1 make the nebula feel viscous.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.AngularDampingFactor: The multiplier on a ship's rotational drag at full nebula strength, interpolated from 1 at the nebula edge the same way as `LinearDampingFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.ActiveEffects: The effects run every physics tick on ships and crew inside this nebula, such as `LightningStrikes`, `DamageShips` and `DamageCrew`. Each entry picks its kind through a `Type` field.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.Buffs: The whole-ship buffs granted while a ship is inside this nebula. Each entry names a BuffType and an amount that is scaled by the ship's nebula strength.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.ProhibitFtlJumpInThreshold: The nebula strength from 0 to 1 at or above which a ship sitting in this nebula prevents other ships from FTL jumping in to it. Leave unset to allow jumps in at any strength.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.ProhibitFtlJumpOutThreshold: The nebula strength from 0 to 1 at or above which a ship in this nebula is barred from making an FTL jump out. Leave unset to allow jumps out at any strength.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DefaultAvoidDistance: The clearance in tiles that ship and stasis pathfinding keeps from this nebula. Setting it at all is what makes the nebula an obstacle for pathfinding, and it also replaces `DefaultLogicalFeather` when the game measures how far inside the nebula a point is for avoidance purposes.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.AIShouldAvoid: Whether AI ships treat this nebula as a region to stay out of when choosing where to move, in addition to the pathfinding clearance from `DefaultAvoidDistance`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.PathfindTravelCost: The multiplier on the cost of routing a path through this nebula, where 1 is the same as open space. Any value above 1 also flags the resulting path as having avoided nebulas. Vanilla ion storms use 100*100 to make routes go around them at almost any length.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.LodBias: Scales the value fed to the nebula shaders as the percent-scale constant, which drives their level-of-detail blending. Values below 1, such as vanilla electron's 0.9, delay the switch to coarser detail as the camera zooms out.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.MaterialLow: The material used for the bottom nebula layer, drawn behind ships, when fancy nebulas are enabled. See `SimpleMaterialLow` for the low-graphics fallback.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DiffuseMaterialLow: The material used to render the bottom layer into the diffuse lighting target. Only drawn when fancy nebulas are enabled and the sim has a diffuse target.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.NormalsMaterialLow: The material used to render the bottom layer into the normals target so the nebula can catch dynamic lighting. Only drawn when fancy nebulas are enabled and the sim has a normals target.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.SimpleMaterialLow: The single-pass material used for the bottom layer when the fancy nebulas setting is off. Vanilla derives it from `MaterialLow` and only swaps the shader.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.MaterialMiddle: The material used for the middle nebula layer, which draws between the low and high layers. Leaving all of the middle materials unset skips the layer entirely.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DiffuseMaterialMiddle: The diffuse-target pass for the middle layer. See `DiffuseMaterialLow`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.NormalsMaterialMiddle: The normals-target pass for the middle layer. See `NormalsMaterialLow`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.SimpleMaterialMiddle: The fallback material for the middle layer when the fancy nebulas setting is off.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.MaterialHigh: The material used for the top nebula layer, drawn in front of ships. Vanilla gives it a partly transparent color so ships stay readable through it.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.DiffuseMaterialHigh: The diffuse-target pass for the top layer. See `DiffuseMaterialLow`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.NormalsMaterialHigh: The normals-target pass for the top layer. See `NormalsMaterialLow`.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.SimpleMaterialHigh: The fallback material for the top layer when the fancy nebulas setting is off.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.MaterialMinimap: The material used to draw this nebula on the minimap. Unset means the nebula does not appear on the minimap at all. Vanilla just points it at one of the other materials.
Cosmoteer.Nebulas.NebulaTypeRules.AmbientMediaEffects: The continuous media effects played at the center of the view while the camera sits inside an explored part of this nebula, for example ambient sound. Their Intensity parameter tracks the nebula strength at that point and they end when it reaches 0.

Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.T:: Global settings for the loose resource nuggets that drift in space and are collected by crew, covering how fast they are flung out and how quickly they slow down.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.LinearDamping: Viscous linear drag applied to loose resource nuggets. Each tick a nugget loses `velocity * LinearDamping * dt`, and the same coefficient feeds the nugget's drag solver so it coasts to a stop. Pairs with [[AngularDamping]] for spin.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.AngularDamping: Viscous rotational drag applied to loose resource nuggets, damping their spin the same way [[LinearDamping]] damps linear motion.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.DropLinearVelocity: Speed range for the random launch velocity given to a nugget when it is dropped. A magnitude is picked from this range and applied in a random direction. Paired with [[DropAngularVelocity]] for spin.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.DropAngularVelocity: Spin range for the random angular velocity given to a nugget when it is dropped with randomized motion. When a nugget is placed without random velocity, the spin is zero instead.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.SelectionRadius: Radius in world units of the circular area around a nugget used for mouse picking and spatial indexing. The click circle is scaled by the camera's zoom.
Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.Rarities: Per-rarity rendering rules keyed by resource rarity ID. Each resource's [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules|Rarity]] looks up its entry here to decide fog-dot display, draw order, and dot sprite. See [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules|ResourceRarityRules]].

Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules.T:: Presentation settings for one nugget rarity tier, mainly the dot drawn for it in fogged space and the order it sorts into.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules.UseFogDot: Whether scanned nuggets of this rarity are shown as a fog-of-war map dot when off-screen. When false, nuggets of this rarity are never batched into the dot renderer. [[FogDotSprite]] supplies the dot image.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules.BucketOrder: Offset added to the render bucket of nuggets of this rarity, controlling their draw order relative to other nuggets. Higher values draw later (on top).
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules.FogDotSprite: Sprite drawn for the fog-of-war map dot representing a scanned nugget of this rarity. Its size sets the dot's on-screen footprint. Only used when [[UseFogDot]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRarityRules.FogDotSizeExponent: Exponent applied to the camera's zoom when scaling the fog dot, as `pow(worldScale, FogDotSizeExponent)`. Lower values make the dot shrink less as the player zooms out, keeping distant nuggets visible.

Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.T:: One resource type such as `power`, `bullets` or `hyperium`, with its icon, buy and sell prices, stack sizes and the situations that drop it.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.ID: The unique identifier other rules use to refer to this resource, for example in part costs or [[Cosmoteer.Data.Rules.FtlFuelResource]]. Loading fails if two resources share the same ID.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NameKey: Localization key of the resource's display name, shown in the resources toolbox, tooltips and transfer windows.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.PluralNameKey: Localization key of the name used when referring to more than one unit of the resource. Falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NameKey]] when omitted.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.DescriptionKey: Localization key of the descriptive text shown in the resource's tooltips, for example on toolbox buttons and nuggets.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.BuyPrice: The money cost to buy one unit of the resource. Also serves as the per-unit value when totaling ship costs and refunds, and as the sell refund when [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.SellPrice]] is not set.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.SellPrice: The money refunded when selling one unit of the resource. Defaults to [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.BuyPrice]] when omitted.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.Icon: The sprite representing the resource in UI lists, buttons and transfer windows. It is also registered as a text image named `resource.<ID>` so the resource can be shown inline in text.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.IconButtonVerticalOffset: Vertical offset, in pixels, applied to the position of [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.Icon]] inside the resource's button in the resources toolbox.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.Overlay: The sprite drawn over storage tiles assigned to this resource in the resource management overlay, and at the cursor while assigning a tile's resource type.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.QuantityDisplayDivisor: Divides quantities and capacities of the resource before they are displayed in the UI. Vanilla batteries use `1000` so that internal charge units display as whole batteries.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.QuantityDisplayFormat: The .NET numeric format string used to render displayed quantities after dividing by [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.QuantityDisplayDivisor]]. The default `n0` shows whole numbers with digit grouping.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.MaxPerNugget: The quantity of the resource in a full nugget, and the most a single crew member can carry at once. Also spans the quantity range that [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprites]] is mapped over.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.CarrySpeed: Multiplies a crew member's move speed while carrying this resource. Values below 1 slow the carrier down.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.MaxStackSize: How many units a single storage stack can hold. Any value above 0 makes the resource stackable and storable in resource grids, which also requires [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.FlexGridPriorityKey]] to be set.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.ReturnToStorage: Whether leftover carried amounts are returned to the ship's storage instead of simply discarded, and whether stored amounts count toward the ship's resource refund. Resources with this enabled must define [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprites]].
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.LoseExcessOnDelivery: Destroys whatever part of a crew delivery the destination could not accept, instead of leaving the excess in the crew member's hands.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.FlexGridPriorityKey: Identifier under which crew role priorities for fetching this resource into flex resource storage are stored. Required for stackable resources (see [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.MaxStackSize]]).
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.FlexGridDefaultPriority: The default crew job priority for fetching this resource into flex resource storage, used when a crew role has no explicit priority set under [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.FlexGridPriorityKey]].
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.DropRates: The `0..1` chances that this resource drops as nuggets when its containing part or storage is destroyed or salvaged or its carrier is killed, plus the fraction of the build cost charged when repairing. Each rate has a `Player…` variant that overrides it for player-built parts.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.StackSprites: The sprites drawn on a storage tile holding this resource. The sprite advances to the next entry for every [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.ResourcesPerStackSprite]] units in the stack.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.ResourcesPerStackSprite: How many units of the resource each successive entry of [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.StackSprites]] represents. With the default of 1 the stack sprite changes with every unit added.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.StackReceiveMediaEffects: Effects played when this resource is delivered into a stack, for example into storage or a construction or repair site.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.StackPickupMediaEffects: Effects played when a crew member picks this resource up from a stack.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetPickupMediaEffects: Effects played when a nugget of this resource is collected in space.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.DeathHitEffects: Hit effects performed when a storage stack of this resource is destroyed. Their strength scales with how full the stack was relative to [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.MaxStackSize]].
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.DeathMediaEffects: Effects played when a storage stack of this resource is destroyed. Their strength scales with how full the stack was, like [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.DeathHitEffects]].
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.HitResponse: Defines the response to the resource's containing part being hit.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.Rarity: The rarity category of the resource's nuggets, which must match an entry in [[Cosmoteer.Resources.NuggetRules.Rarities]]. It controls how the nuggets are rendered as dots on the map and in fog of war. Defaults to `Common`.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprite: A single sprite used for this resource's nuggets and for the resource while carried by crew. Shorthand for [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprites]] with one entry.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprites: The sprites used for this resource's nuggets and for the resource while carried by crew. The sprite is picked by the quantity relative to [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.MaxPerNugget]], so later entries represent larger amounts. Required when [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.ReturnToStorage]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NestedNuggetSprites: Nested form of [[Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules.NuggetSprites]]. The outer list splits the `1..MaxPerNugget` quantity range into bands and each inner list subdivides its band further.

Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.T:: Makes stored resources react when their part is hit, playing effects and optionally being lost, at a chance that scales with the damage dealt.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.HitEffects: The hit effects to perform, if any.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.MediaEffects: The media effects to play, if any.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.Chance: The default base chance to respond to a hit.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.ChancePerNDamage: The chance added per NDamage in a hit.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.NDamage: The quantity of damage in a hit that adds a response chance of ChancePerNDamage.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.RequireDirectHit: Whether triggering a response requires a specified HitArea that includes the resource's location.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.RemoveOnResponse: Whether the responding resources should be removed on a successful response.

Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.T:: Overrides the reaction chance for one damage type, so a resource can cook off readily from fire but shrug off a bullet.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.Chance: When set, overrides the default Chance value.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.ChancePerNDamage: When set, overrides the default ChancePerNDamage value.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/HitRes.NDamage: When set, overrides the default NDamage value.

Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.T:: The chance that a resource falls out as a collectable nugget in each situation, with a separate figure for player-owned ships.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PartDestroyed: Chance from 0 to 1 that a nugget of this resource drops when a part holding it is destroyed by damage, for non-player-owned ships. The actual drop chance is interpolated between this and [[PartSalvaged]] by how much of the part was salvaged rather than destroyed. [[PlayerPartDestroyed]] overrides it for the local player.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerPartDestroyed: Overrides [[PartDestroyed]] when the destroyed part belongs to a player-owned ship. Falls back to [[PartDestroyed]] when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PartSalvaged: Drop chance from 0 to 1 for a fully salvaged part, for non-player ships. The effective chance is interpolated between [[PartDestroyed]] and this value by the salvage fraction, so a cleanly salvaged part uses this rate. [[PlayerPartSalvaged]] overrides it for the player.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerPartSalvaged: Overrides [[PartSalvaged]] when the salvaged part belongs to a player-owned ship. Falls back to [[PartSalvaged]] when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.StorageDestroyed: Chance from 0 to 1 that a nugget drops when a storage part holding this resource is destroyed, for non-player ships. Interpolated toward [[StorageSalvaged]] by salvage fraction. Also used as the fallback for [[CrewKilled]]. [[PlayerStorageDestroyed]] overrides it for the player.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerStorageDestroyed: Overrides [[StorageDestroyed]] when the destroyed storage belongs to a player-owned ship. Falls back to [[StorageDestroyed]] when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.StorageSalvaged: Drop chance from 0 to 1 for a fully salvaged storage part, for non-player ships. The effective chance is interpolated between [[StorageDestroyed]] and this value by salvage fraction. [[PlayerStorageSalvaged]] overrides it for the player.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerStorageSalvaged: Overrides [[StorageSalvaged]] when the salvaged storage belongs to a player-owned ship. Falls back to [[StorageSalvaged]] when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.CrewKilled: Chance from 0 to 1 that a nugget drops when a crew member carrying this resource is killed, for non-player ships. When unset, [[StorageDestroyed]] is used instead. [[PlayerCrewKilled]] overrides it for the player. Salvage fraction does not affect crew drops.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerCrewKilled: Overrides [[CrewKilled]] when the killed crew belongs to a player-owned ship. Falls back through [[CrewKilled]], then [[PlayerStorageDestroyed]], then [[StorageDestroyed]] when left unset.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PartRepairCost: Fraction of a part's build cost, per unit of damage, charged in this resource to repair the part, for non-player ships. Repair cost is `ceil(buildCost * damageFraction * PartRepairCost)`, capped so it never exceeds the resources that would be recoverable by deconstructing. [[PlayerPartRepairCost]] overrides it for the player.
Cosmoteer.Resources.ResourceRules/Nugget.PlayerPartRepairCost: Overrides [[PartRepairCost]] when repairing a player-owned ship's part. Falls back to [[PartRepairCost]] when left unset.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AICommsModuleRules.T:: Decides what an AI ship offers the player over comms. Write one of the concrete modules, which cover trade, missions, part techs, crew for hire and surrender talk.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.T:: Per-ship overrides handed to a ship's AI when it spawns, such as its patrol radius and origin, its fleet leader and its willingness to surrender.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolRadius: Overrides the AreaPatrol strategy and stasis modules' `DefaultPatrolRadius` for this one ship. Radius in world units of the circle around [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]] in which patrol destinations are rolled.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.MinPatrolRadius: Radius in world units of an inner keep-out circle around [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]]. A rolled patrol destination is discarded when the straight line to it would cut through that inner circle, unless the ship is already inside it. Leaving it unset means no inner circle is enforced.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin: World location the ship treats as its home point. It centers the patrol circle, it is the point the AggroEnemies module falls back to when it retreats, and it is the reference for [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.TargetAcquireRangeFromOrigin]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.TargetUnacquireRangeFromOrigin]]. Falls back to the location at which the ship first appeared.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.TargetAcquireRangeFromOrigin: Distance in world units from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]] within which the AggroEnemies module engages freely. Outside it the ship only keeps fighting if it has not already begun retreating, and normal aggression is restored only once it is back inside the circle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.TargetUnacquireRangeFromOrigin: Hard leash distance in world units from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]]. Past it the AggroEnemies module always heads back to the origin, keeping its target in the firing arc if it still has one. Leaving it unset means the ship is never leashed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.StasisSpeed: Overrides the stasis modules' `DefaultStasisSpeed` for this one ship. Speed in world units per second at which the stasis spawner drifts toward its destination. The kick of velocity a ship is given as it leaves stasis still uses the rules value, not this one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.ChanceToConsiderSurrenderingToPlayer: Overrides the Dialogue comms module's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialogueModuleRules.DefaultChanceToConsiderSurrenderingToPlayer]] for this one ship. A 0..1 probability that is rolled once, the first time the ship ticks. Career mode mission objectives set it to 0 on ships that must not be able to surrender.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.FleetLeader: Object id of the ship or stasis spawner this ship follows. The FollowFleetLeader strategy and stasis modules do nothing while it is unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolAroundWorldOrigin: Forces [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]] to the world origin (0, 0). It is applied after the rest of the parameters are read, so it overrides any [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolOrigin]] given alongside it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIStasisModuleRules.T:: Drives a ship cheaply while it sits outside live simulation range. Write one of the concrete modules, which patrol, follow a fleet leader, search wanted areas or leave the sector.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIStrategyModuleRules.T:: Sets what a live AI ship is trying to do. Write one of the concrete modules, which attack, flee, patrol, hold position, self repair or leave the sector.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AITacticsModuleRules.T:: Chooses the range and hull angle an AI ship attacks a target from. Write one of the concrete modules.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AITargetingModuleRule.T:: Picks which enemy part an AI ship's weapons aim at. Write one of the concrete modules.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AICrewPr.T:: Lets the player hire crew off this AI ship, setting how many are for sale and what each one costs.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AICrewPr.CrewForHireFraction: Fraction of the ship's total bed capacity that is offered to the player for hire. The crew put on offer are taken from the ship's assigned crew in ascending order of their role's assignment priority, with roleless crew first.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AICrewPr.CrewHireCostPerCrewRatio: Table of ratio and cost pairs that prices a single hire against the buying player's crew count divided by their current fame based crew cap. Costs are interpolated linearly between entries, and any ratio past the last entry pays the last entry's cost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AICrewPr.CrewHireCostRoundToMultiple: The hire price is rounded to a multiple of this after the faction reputation discount has been applied. Use 1 for no rounding.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.T:: Lets the AI ship hail others and haggle over surrender, setting how readily it offers, demands or accepts one and what the payout is.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.DefaultChanceToConsiderSurrenderingToPla: Probability from 0 to 1 that the ship is willing to surrender to the player at all, rolled once on the ship's first tick from a generator seeded with its unique id. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.ChanceToConsiderSurrenderingToPlayer]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.ChanceToConsiderAcceptingSurrenderFromPl: Probability from 0 to 1, rolled once per ship, that the ship is willing to accept a surrender from the player. A player who is wanted by the ship's faction can always buy off the bounty regardless.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.ChanceToConsiderOfferingSurrender: Probability from 0 to 1 that a ship which already passed [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialogueModuleRules.DefaultChanceToConsiderSurrenderingToPlayer]] will hail the player on its own to offer its surrender. Ships that fail this roll still surrender if the player opens comms with them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.ChanceToConsiderDemandingSurrender: Probability from 0 to 1 that a ship which already passed [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialogueModuleRules.ChanceToConsiderAcceptingSurrenderFromPlayer]] will hail the player to demand that the player surrenders. Only the dialogue leader of a nearby group does the hailing, and it silences the demand for the rest of the group.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.ValueRatioDifferenceRangeToSurrender: Range from which each ship rolls its personal strength ratio threshold once. A surrender is only on the table when the surrendering side's weighted strength divided by the other side's is at or below that threshold, so lower values mean the ship must be more thoroughly outmatched before it gives up. Strength here combines nearby allied firepower, blueprint cost and remaining health.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.PlayerSurrenderPayoutMultiple: Fraction of the damage value the player has done to the surrounding enemy ships that the player pays to surrender. The career mode base surrender cost, and any wanted payoff and reputation multiplier, are added on top.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIDialog.AISurrenderPayoutMultiple: Fraction of the AI ship's current physical value that it pays the player when it surrenders. It stands in for the loot the player gives up by not destroying the ship.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AIMissio.T:: Lets the AI ship hand out missions to the player.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITechPr.T:: Lets the AI ship sell part techs to the player.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITradeM.T:: Lets the AI ship trade with others, and says whether it also refills oxygen or helps with construction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITradeM.AllowHumanTrade: Whether the ship opens its trade tab to a human player's ship. Ships preparing to FTL jump and space stations that are not operating refuse regardless.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITradeM.AllowNpcTrade: Whether the ship trades with other AI ships. Enemies are always refused, whichever of the two flags applies.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITradeM.HelpWithConstruction: Whether the ship lends its crew to construction and repair work on a non-enemy caller's ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.CommsModules.AITradeM.AllowO2Refill: Whether crew belonging to a non-enemy player may refill their oxygen at this ship's airlocks.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.T:: One named ship AI personality such as `Police` or `TradeShip`, assembled from strategy, tactics, targeting, comms and stasis modules.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.NameKey: Localization key for the AI's display name, shown in the creative mode "Set AI" menu, the creative mode battle helper and the multiplayer game setup AI drop list. Entries without a key fall back to the `Misc/Unknown` string.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.UpdateInterval: Random range, in seconds, between AI ticks. A fresh value is drawn from the range after every tick, and each tick re-runs the strategy, tactics and targeting modules once. Stasis modules are not driven by this value, they run on the simulation's global stasis update interval.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.IsAvailableInCreativeMode: Whether this AI appears in the creative mode "Set AI" menu and in the battle helper's AI list.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.IsCreativeModeDefault: Whether the creative mode battle helper preselects this AI. The first AI in the rules with this set is the one that is picked.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.IsAvailableInMultiplayer: Whether this AI appears in the multiplayer game setup screen's AI drop list.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.IsMultiplayerDefault: Whether this AI is the preselected entry of the multiplayer game setup AI drop list.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.StrategyModules: The modules that issue the ship's high level commands, such as patrolling, attacking, fleeing or repairing, once per AI tick. They are evaluated from the last entry to the first and the first module that reports it acted stops the rest, so entries later in the list have higher priority.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.TacticsModules: The modules that adjust the ship's current attack command, its approach angle in one pass and its attack radius and rotation in a second pass. Each pass runs from the last entry to the first and stops at the first module that reports it acted.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.TargetingModules: The modules that assign targets to individual weapons. They are evaluated from the last entry to the first, each removing the weapons it handled from the pool, until no untargeted weapon is left.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.CommsModules: The modules that decide whether the ship answers hails and whether it trades, provides crew, missions, techs or dialogue. Each question is put to the modules from the last entry to the first and the first non-null answer wins, while the per-tick update runs on all of them in list order.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.StasisModules: The modules that move and manage the ship while it is in stasis, that is while it is simulated cheaply as an off screen spawner. Like [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.ShipAIRules.StrategyModules]] they are evaluated from the last entry to the first and stop at the first module that acted.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.T:: Keeps a stasis ship circling its spawn location or the world origin at the given radius and speed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.DefaultPatrolRadius: Radius in world units of the circle around the spawner's patrol origin inside which random stasis destinations are rolled. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolRadius]], and paired with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.MinPatrolRadius]] as an inner keep-out circle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.DefaultStasisSpeed: Speed in world units per second at which the stasis spawner drifts toward its patrol destination. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.StasisSpeed]], except for the kick of velocity the ship is given when it leaves stasis, which always uses this value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun` or `station`, that the spawner will neither pick as a destination nor drift through. Leaving it unset disables doodad avoidance, nebulas flagged as AI-avoidable are still routed around either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasisAreaPatrolModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla AIs use 100.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.T:: Deletes the stasis spawner as soon as it is created, so the ship never appears.
Sends a ship out of the sector while it is still in stasis, travelling at the given stasis speed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.DefaultStasisSpeed: Speed in world units per second at which the stasis spawner drifts toward the nearest FTL gate. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.StasisSpeed]], except for the kick of velocity the ship is given when it leaves stasis, which always uses this value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun` or `station`, that the spawner steers around on its way to the gate. Leaving it unset disables doodad avoidance, nebulas flagged as AI-avoidable are still routed around either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasisExitSectorModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla AIs use 100.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.IsActivated: Whether the module is live from the start. While false it does nothing and hands control to the next stasis module, and it is switched on when a ship whose ExitSector strategy module is already active enters stasis. Vanilla `ai_police.rules` sets it so that idle police leave the sector.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.T:: Keeps a stasis ship trailing its fleet leader at the given stasis speed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.DefaultStasisSpeed: Speed in world units per second at which the stasis spawner drifts toward its fleet leader. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.StasisSpeed]]. The module does nothing at all while [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.FleetLeader]] is unset or points at something that no longer exists.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun` or `station`, that the spawner steers around while following its leader. Leaving it unset disables doodad avoidance, nebulas flagged as AI-avoidable are still routed around either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasisFollowFleetLeaderModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.T:: Holds the missions a stasis ship carries, so they exist before the ship is ever fully simulated.
Sends a stasis ship prowling through nearby wanted areas.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.DefaultStasisSpeed: Speed in world units per second at which the stasis spawner drifts toward a random point inside the nearest wanted search area. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.StasisSpeed]]. Vanilla police use 100 here, faster than the 75 of their other stasis modules.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun`, that the spawner will neither pick as a search destination nor drift through. Leaving it unset disables doodad avoidance, nebulas flagged as AI-avoidable are still routed around either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasi.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StasisModules.AIStasisWantedSearchModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla police use 100 around suns.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.T:: Makes the ship pick a nearby enemy and attack, weighing candidates by firepower, distance and whether an ally is already on them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.TargetSwitchThresholdFactor: Multiplies the score of the ship's current target while candidates are compared, so a different enemy has to beat the current one by this factor before the AI switches. 1 means switch as soon as anything scores higher, vanilla combat AIs use 6.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.TargetDistanceFactorExponent: Exponent applied to the reciprocal of the edge to edge distance to a candidate before that distance factor is multiplied by the candidate's firepower rating. Values above 1 make the AI favour close enemies more strongly, vanilla combat AIs use 1.5.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.AlreadyTargetedByAllyFactor: Multiplies the score of candidates that another ship of the same player is already attacking. Values below 1 spread a fleet's attention over several enemies, vanilla combat AIs use 0.7.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.TargetFirepowerCacheTime: How long, in seconds, a candidate ship's computed total firepower is reused before it is recalculated. Larger values cost less CPU but make the AI slower to notice that a target has lost its weapons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.AcquireAggroWithinRadar: Searches for targets out to the ship's radar blip radius instead of its sight radius. Enemies still have to be within radar of the ship's own player to be considered.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.ReleaseAggroWithinRadar: Keeps an already acquired target in the running as long as it stays within radar radius, even after it drops out of sight. It also switches acquisition to radar radius from the moment the ship's physical value drops, that is as soon as it starts taking damage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.RotateOnly: Attacks by rotating in place, issuing a rotate only attack command with collision avoidance switched off. It also disables the origin leash checks driven by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.TargetAcquireRangeFromOrigin]], as well as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAggroEnemiesModuleRules.GotoLastKnownTargetLocation]], which is what turret style ships like defense platforms want.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.GotoLastKnownTargetLocation: Sends the ship to the spot where its target was last seen after it loses track of it. Ignored when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAggroEnemiesModuleRules.RotateOnly]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun` or `station`, whose areas the AI treats as no-go zones. Enemies sitting inside such an area are never picked as targets and the chase after a lost target is called off. Leaving it unset disables doodad avoidance, nebulas flagged as AI-avoidable are still avoided either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAgg.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAggroEnemiesModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Has no effect unless that field is set.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAre.T:: Makes the ship patrol a circle around its spawn location or the world origin.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAre.DefaultPatrolRadius: Radius in world units of the circle around the ship's origin inside which random patrol destinations are rolled. Overridden per ship by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.AIParameters.PatrolRadius]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAre.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun` or `station`, whose areas a patrol destination must not fall inside. A destination that lands in one is simply dropped for that tick.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAre.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIAreaPatrolModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla combat AIs use 100.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIDel.T:: Deletes the ship the moment its AI first runs.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIExi.T:: Sends the ship to an FTL gate to leave the sector as soon as it can.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIExi.IsActivated: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it, because the strategy module is always built with its parameterless constructor and so never sees the rules object. The module is instead switched on at runtime when the ship surrenders, or when the ship leaves stasis with an activated stasis ExitSector module. Vanilla `ai_police.rules` sets it and is affected by this.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.T:: Makes the ship run once enemies come within `FleeStartRange`, optionally recalling its crew and jumping away after a delay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.FleeStartRange: Distance in world units at which a significant enemy makes a ship that is not yet fleeing start to run. The effective range is capped by the ship's own radar radius, so a value larger than that has no further effect.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.FleeStopRange: The same trigger distance, but used while the ship is already fleeing, which gives the behaviour hysteresis. Set it larger than [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFleeFromEnemiesModuleRules.FleeStartRange]] to keep the ship running after it has broken contact. It is capped by the ship's radar radius as well.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.FleeDistance: How far in world units each flee move command sends the ship away from its pursuers. The direction is the sum of the unit vectors pointing away from every enemy in range, and because that sum is not renormalized the actual travel distance grows with the number of pursuers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.RecallCrew: Cancels off-ship resource transfer and salvage jobs the moment fleeing starts, and holds back the flee move until every crew member is back aboard.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFle.FtlAfter: Random delay range, in seconds, measured from the start of the flee, after which the ship makes a local FTL jump to a reachable landmark rather than just flying away. The timer is cleared as soon as the ship stops fleeing, and leaving the field unset means the ship never jumps.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIFol.T:: Makes the ship stay with the fleet leader named in its AI parameters.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIHol.T:: Keeps the ship parked where it spawned, optionally holding its spawn rotation too.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIHol.HoldRotation: Also pins the ship to the facing it had when it first took up position, instead of only pinning its location. When false the ship holds its spot but is free to turn, which lets the tactics modules aim it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.T:: Makes a damaged ship stop and repair or rebuild itself before carrying on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.RepairChecksPerTick: Number of randomly drawn damaged or destroyed objects the ship tries to repair each AI tick. Higher values close the damage faster at more CPU cost, vanilla trade ships use 1 and stations use 10.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.RepairDamaged: Includes damaged but still standing parts among the repair candidates.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.RebuildDestroyed: Includes destroyed parts and doors among the candidates, so they are rebuilt from scratch.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.AllowPartialRepair: Lets the ship queue a repair on a damaged part it cannot fully pay for, as long as it holds at least some of one of the required resources. Only has an effect in the crew and resources construction mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.AllowPartialRebuild: The same allowance as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISelfRepairModuleRules.AllowPartialRepair]], but for rebuilding destroyed parts and doors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun`, whose areas suppress repairing. While the ship sits inside one of these areas the module does nothing and hands control to the next strategy module.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISel.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AISelfRepairModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla trade ships use 100 around suns.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIWan.T:: Sends the ship searching through nearby wanted areas.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIWan.AvoidableDoodadTags: Ids of doodad spawners, such as `sun`, whose areas the ship will not fly to when it picks a random point inside the nearest wanted search area. A point that lands in one produces no move command that tick.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIWan.AvoidableDoodadBuffer: Extra distance in world units added to the radius of every doodad matched by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.StrategyModules.AIWantedSearchModuleRules.AvoidableDoodadTags]]. Vanilla police use 100 around suns.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefa.T:: Holds an attacking ship at its default weapon range and picks the hull angle that brings the most guns to bear.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefa.AttackRotationSwitchThresholdFactor: Multiplies the estimated firepower of the rotation the ship is currently holding while the candidates are compared, so a different rotation has to beat the current one by this factor before the ship turns. Vanilla combat AIs use 1.25.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefa.AttackRotationsToCheck: Number of candidate rotations evaluated, spread evenly around the full circle starting from the current attack rotation. Vanilla combat AIs use 8, which gives 45 degree steps.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefa.RotateOnly: Picks only the best rotation and never touches the attack radius, which is what immobile ships such as defense platforms want. It also suppresses the saved attack radius from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefaultAttackRadiusAndRotationModuleRules.UseSavedAboveHealth]], while the saved rotation is still honoured.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIDefa.UseSavedAboveHealth: Health fraction, meaning current physical value divided by blueprint cost, above which the ship uses the attack radius and rotation saved on its blueprint instead of recomputing them. Below the threshold, or when the field is left unset, the ship always recomputes. Vanilla combat AIs use 50%.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIRand.T:: Keeps shifting an attacking ship's approach angle so it circles its target, and can coordinate flanking with allies.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIRand.AttackAngleChangeInterval: Random range, in seconds, between re-rolls of the world relative angle from which the ship approaches its target. Vanilla combat AIs re-roll every 5 to 10 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIRand.AttackAngleChangeDelta: Random range of offsets added to the base approach angle at every re-roll. The base angle is the direction from the target to this ship, or the direction away from where allied attackers already sit when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIRandomAttackAngleModuleRules.CoordinateFlanking]] is on. The default spread is a full -180 to 180 degrees, vanilla combat AIs narrow it to -30 to 30 degrees.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TacticsModules.AIRand.CoordinateFlanking: Bases the approach angle on where the same player's other ships attacking the same target are already approaching from, and heads for the opposite side. This is what makes a fleet spread out around its target instead of bunching up.

Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TargetingModules.AIVa.T:: Aims the ship's weapons at whichever enemy part is worth the most, allowing for how much armor a shot must punch through.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TargetingModules.AIVa.TargetChecksPerUpdate: Number of randomly drawn parts of the target ship that are scored each AI tick, on top of the part already being shot at. Only parts with a positive [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AIValueFactor]] are scored, and if none of them qualifies a random one of the remaining parts is picked instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TargetingModules.AIVa.TargetSwitchThresholdFactor: Multiplies the score of the part currently being shot at while candidates are compared, so a different part has to beat it by this factor before the weapons retarget. Vanilla combat AIs use 2.
Cosmoteer.Ships.AI.TargetingModules.AIVa.TargetValueFactorPerPenetrationDist: Base of an exponential falloff applied per tile of ship between the shooter and the part. A part's value is multiplied by this raised to the distance in tiles from the first hull hit along the line of fire to the part's centre, so the vanilla 0.75 makes deeply buried parts much less attractive.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.T:: Sends a named signal out through the part network in build mode, so matching value overlays on connected parts light up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.Signal: ID of the signal to send.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.SignalThroughNode: ID of the blueprint-available component to spread the network signal through.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.T:: Draws a number over the part in build mode when a matching signal arrives through the part network, reading the number from another component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.BorderColor: Color of the border drawn as four segments around the part's rect when the overlay is active. If both this and [[#FillColor]] are unset, no highlight box is drawn (only the value text).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.FillColor: Color of the solid quad that fills the part's rect when the overlay is active. Combines with [[#BorderColor]] for a filled-and-outlined highlight.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.ValueSource: ID of the component (an `IComponentValueProvider`) on this part whose numeric value is read and displayed. Its value is multiplied by [[#ValueScale]] then formatted with [[#FormatKey]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.FormatKey: Localization key passed to the string formatter along with the scaled value to produce the displayed text, letting the number be labeled and unit-formatted.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.ValueScale: Multiplier applied to [[#ValueSource]]'s raw value before it is formatted and shown, for converting internal units into display units.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.ValidSignals: The collection of signal IDs that can activate the value overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.AllowUpstreamSignals: Whether signals upstream from the SignalThroughNode subnetwork are valid.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.AllowDownstreamSignals: Whether signals downstream from (visible to) the SignalThroughNode subnetwork are valid.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.SignalThroughNode: ID of the blueprint-available component to receive the network signal from.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.BlueprintNetw.DrawOnHover: Whether this value overlay should be drawn regardless of signal when the part is hovered in build mode.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.ExternalBluep.T:: The blend sprites that draw the outer hull wall around a ship in build mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.ExternalBluep.AmbiguousSprites: Blend sprites that draw the outer edge of a ship's blueprint where its parts meet open space. Each entry's situation code is expanded into unambiguous per-neighbor sprites covering all 256 edge configurations. Every configuration must be covered or building the wall throws, since undefined codes are not allowed here.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Base.T:: How the line joining two connected network ports is drawn in build mode, including its color when the link is broken or unroutable. A port names one by id in `Overlay/RouteLine`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Base.ColorFactor: Base tint multiplied into the route line's color. Defaults to white (no tint).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Base.DisconnectedColorFactor: Extra tint multiplied into the line color when its route endpoint is not connected. Applied only when set, on top of [[#ColorFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Base.UnroutableColorFactor: Extra tint multiplied into the line color when the route cannot be reached from the selected part. Applied only when set, on top of [[#ColorFactor]] and any disconnected tint.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Base.RenderToSeparateTexture: When true the lines are first drawn to an offscreen mipmapped render target and then composited once over the scene, avoiding double-blending where semi-transparent lines overlap and giving smoother downscaling. When false they draw straight to the screen.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.T:: Draws a curved arc around the part in build mode at the given radius and sweep, used to show things like shield coverage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.Radius: Outer radius of the arc band in tiles, measured from the part's center. The [[#Sprite]] fills inward from this radius by the sprite's own height, so the band thickness equals the sprite height.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.Arc: Total angular width of the arc, centered on the part's facing direction. The band spans from minus half this angle to plus half.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.Sprite: Sprite drawn along the curved band. Its texture is stretched across the whole arc and its height sets the band's radial thickness.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.SpriteSegments: Number of flat quad segments the arc is tessellated into. Higher values make the curve smoother at more vertex cost. The two end segments fade their outer edges to transparent.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.VisibilityToggle: ID of a component whose blueprint toggle state gates whether the arc is drawn. When set, the arc only shows while that toggle is on. The component must support `IBlueprintComponentToggle`. When omitted the arc is always visible.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.T:: Draws a build-mode sprite that blends into neighbouring parts, choosing the sprite from a situation code saying which sides must have a match.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.Location: Offset in tiles of the sprite from the part's center, before the part's build rotation and flip are applied. Combines with each sprite's own [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite]] offset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.AmbiguousSprites: Blend sprites keyed by neighbor situation code, chosen at draw time from which of the eight surrounding cells this part blends with. Although marked optional here, the deserializer requires it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.BlendsWithCategories: Part categories this sprite is allowed to blend against. A neighboring cell only counts as present if its part belongs to one of these categories. When omitted, the sprite blends with any neighboring part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.BlendCheckRectType: Which rect of a neighboring part is tested when deciding whether that cell is occupied. `Normal` uses the part's logical footprint, `Physical` uses its collision footprint.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.AllowUndefinedBlendSprites: When true, neighbor configurations with no matching sprite draw nothing instead of throwing. When false, every one of the 256 configurations must be covered by [[#AmbiguousSprites]] or building fails.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.RequireExternalWallsToBlend: When true, a neighboring part only counts for blending if it has a blueprint external wall facing this cell. Lets the sprite blend along solid hull edges only rather than across every adjacent part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.CellOffset: Shifts, in whole cells, the grid position at which neighbor occupancy is sampled when computing the situation code. Used to align blending for sprites that sit off the part's origin cell.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.T:: Draws one flat sprite for the part in build mode. The sprite's own fields such as `File` and `Size` are written directly on this component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.ShowOnlyInToggleMode: Restricts the sprite to a single build-mode toggle state. It pairs a toggle ID with a mode value, and the sprite draws only while that toggle sits in that mode. When omitted the sprite always draws.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.T:: Draws a build-mode sprite that blends with its neighbours, picking the variant from the on or off state of the toggles in `SituationToggles`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.Location: Offset in tiles of the sprite from the part's origin, transformed by the part's placement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.SituationToggles: Ordered list of toggle component IDs whose on/off states form the situation code. Each toggle contributes one bit, so the code length equals the list length and the shown sprite depends on the combined toggle states. Although marked optional here, the deserializer requires it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.AmbiguousSprites: Blend sprites keyed by situation code, expanded to cover the toggle-state combinations. Every combination of the [[#SituationToggles]] bits must be covered unless [[#AllowUndefinedBlendSprites]] is set. Although marked optional here, the deserializer requires it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Blue.AllowUndefinedBlendSprites: Accepted for this component but has no effect in the current game code. The generator takes this flag and never reads it, so the toggled variant still throws when [[#AmbiguousSprites]] does not cover every combination of toggle states.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.Graphics.Part.T:: Draws a network route as one straight line with a cap at each end, with the line's sprite and thickness fields written inline.
Draws a network route as a line split lengthwise, so a two-way link shows both halves and a one-way link only one.

Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffModifier.T:: Pulls the current strength of one buff on the part in as the modifier, leaving the value untouched when the part has no such buff.
Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffModifier.BuffType: The ID of the BuffType that the modifier uses.

Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffRemapModifier.T:: Maps a buff's strength from `RemapFrom` onto `RemapTo` before applying it, so a buff running 0 to 1 can drive any output range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffRemapModifier.RemapFrom: Input range of the buff's amount that gets mapped. A buff value at RemapFrom.Min maps to RemapTo.Min and one at RemapFrom.Max maps to RemapTo.Max, linearly in between.
Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffRemapModifier.RemapTo: Output range the buff amount is mapped onto. The mapped result becomes the modifier value that ModificationMode then combines with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.BuffRemapModifier.Clamp: When true the buff amount is clamped to RemapFrom before mapping, so values outside the input range produce RemapTo.Min or RemapTo.Max rather than extrapolating past them. When false the mapping is unclamped.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.T:: One named buff that parts hand out to their neighbours, fixing how several sources combine, the range it spans and the icon shown in build mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.CombineMode: How the raw values of multiple providers buffing the same receiver are merged into one number, before [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Exponent]], [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Multiplier]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.BaseValue]] are applied. Defaults to `Max`. Vanilla engine-room thrust takes the strongest single buff with `Max` while factory and railgun buffs stack with `Add`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.BaseValue: Amount added to the buff value as the final step of the math, after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Exponent]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Multiplier]]. The full pipeline is `combined ^ Exponent * Multiplier + BaseValue`, clamped between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.MinValue]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.MaxValue]]. It only applies while at least one provider is buffing the receiver, an unbuffed receiver has no buff value at all, which is why vanilla multiplier-style buffs like `Engine` set `BaseValue = 100%` so a provider's contribution reads as a bonus on top of the normal 1.0.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.MinValue: Lower clamp on the final buff value, applied after all other math. A receiving part can raise this floor further through [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MinBuffValues]], the larger of the two bounds wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.MaxValue: Upper clamp on the final buff value, applied after all other math. A receiving part can lower this ceiling further through [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxBuffValues]], the smaller of the two bounds wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Exponent: Power the combined provider value is raised to, before [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Multiplier]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.BaseValue]]. With [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.CombineMode]] `Add`, values below 1 give diminishing returns per provider. The vanilla `RailgunShot` buff uses 0.8 so each additional accelerator adds less damage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Multiplier: Scale applied to the combined provider value after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Exponent]] and before [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.BaseValue]] is added.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.Icon: Sprite drawn centered over each affected part when the build UI shows this buff's connections, for example over the receivers of a selected provider or over a part receiving the buff. The sprite's own Size is in tiles. Only one buff icon is shown per part, see [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconPriority]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextFormatKey: Localization key formatted with the buff's display number to draw a text label at affected parts in the build overlay. When omitted no text is shown. Vanilla buffs use `BuildBox/BuffPercentageFmt`, which renders as `+{0:0}%`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextMultiply: Scale applied to the buff value for the overlay label, the displayed number is `value * IconTextMultiply + IconTextAdd`. Vanilla percentage buffs use 100 together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextAdd]] `-100`, turning a 1.25 buff value into a displayed 25.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextAdd: Offset added to the buff value after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextMultiply]] to produce the number shown in the overlay label. Affects only the displayed text, not the buff itself.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconPriority: Sort priority when a part is covered by several buff overlays. Buffs with higher priority get their icon and label drawn first, and since each part shows at most one buff icon they win the spot. The vanilla `RocketThrust` buff uses 1 to override the engine-room buff icon on rocket thrusters.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.ShowIconTextForZeroValue: Whether the overlay label is drawn when the displayed number (after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextMultiply]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.IconTextAdd]]) equals 0. Vanilla percentage buffs set this to false so an unchanged value shows no `+0%` label.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.RectBorderColor: Border color of the highlight rectangle drawn over the connected provider parts when the build overlay shows this buff. Used together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.RectFillColor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.RectFillColor: Fill color of the highlight rectangle drawn over the connected provider parts when the build overlay shows this buff. When set, the fill and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Buffs.BuffType.RectBorderColor]] pair is also registered as a part-highlight style under the buff's ID, which shades a provider's area of effect in the blueprint overlay.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.AttackCommandRu.T:: Tuning and on-screen presentation for the attack order, which drives a ship into weapons range of a target and keeps it firing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.AttackCommandRu.FocusWidget: The widget drawn halfway between the attacking ship and its target that focuses the camera on both of them when clicked. It only appears while the ship is selected and this is its displayed command, and it hides itself when the camera is already focused on exactly those two objects or when the player has turned off the midpoint focus widget in the camera settings.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.T:: Movement, collision avoidance and sound settings shared by every ship order, and written directly for `DirectControl`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.IssueSound: The interface sound played when the player issues a command of this kind. When several commands are given at once only the first one in the batch plays its sound.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.ReplaceSound: The interface sound played when a command of this kind replaces an existing command rather than being newly enqueued. `IssueSound` is played instead when this is left out.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.ThrusterSRFFactors: Weights the thruster solver applies to the forward axis, the sideways axis and the torque axis while the ship is still flying toward its destination. The X and Y components are measured relative to the ship's flight direction, and raising a component makes the solver spend more thrust satisfying that axis. Vanilla direct control uses `[1, 2, 100]` to prioritise rotation far above translation, while RTS commands use `[1, 2, 1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.ThrusterSRFStrafeFactors: The same axis weights as `ThrusterSRFFactors`, used once the ship is close enough to be adjusting its position and rotation in place. It is also the weighting used for every maximum-acceleration and deceleration query, for holding still while waiting for crew, and for ships that currently have no command.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidRadiusBuffer: Extra radius in tiles added to the ship's bounding circle when it searches for objects it might run into. Larger values make ships start steering around obstacles from farther away.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidSlowdownAroundRadiusFactor: Multiplies the radius of the obstacle being avoided when the intermediate steering point is pushed outward past that obstacle. Higher values make the ship swing wider around whatever it is dodging.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidSlowdownAroundRadiusAngleRange: Angular range over which the ship blends between aiming at the far edge of its clear arc and aiming at the point right next to the obstacle. The angle measured is between the direction to the real destination and the direction to the avoidance point, so the bigger the detour the closer in the ship aims, which slows it down.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidModeVelocityFactorThreshold: Multiplies the ship's current speed to get an obstacle radius in tiles. While a ship is still flying toward its destination, obstacles smaller than that are dodged toward whichever side of the clear arc is closest to the current flight direction, and larger ones toward whichever side needs the shorter sideways detour.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidanceMergeSpeedThreshold: Largest difference in velocity, in tiles per second, that two neighbouring obstacles may have and still be merged into a single blob that the ship steers around as one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.RepulseRadiusBufferMult: Multiplies the ship's bounding radius to get the circle inside which other objects push it away. The push ramps from nothing at the edge of that inflated circle up to full strength at actual contact and is split between the two objects according to their masses.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidInsignificantMassFactor: Fraction of the ship's own mass below which another ship is too light to bother avoiding. During normal path avoidance it only excuses junk, enemies and insignificant ships, but during the close-range repulsion pass it applies to every ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.AvoidableDoodadTags: The doodad spawner tags, vanilla uses just `sun`, that ships steer around and route their nebula paths around. The copy on the FtlGateJump rules is also what the game consults when placing ships arriving from an FTL jump.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.IgnoreCollisionTimeThreshold: Longest predicted time to collision, in seconds, that still counts as worth avoiding. Collisions predicted farther in the future than this are ignored entirely.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.WeaponOutOfCoverageColorFactor: Color multiplier applied to the weapon coverage overlay for weapons that cannot cover the target from the position being previewed. Vanilla halves both brightness and alpha.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseCommandRule.WeaponCoverageFadeInDuration: Seconds over which the weapon and shield coverage overlay fades in after the player starts dragging a command into place.
