Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.T:: Settings shared by the orders that trail another ship, covering how close the follower sits and the handles, circles and lines drawn for the order.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MaxFollowRadiusFactor: Caps how far the ship may be told to sit from its target, as a multiple of the larger of the two ships' bounding radii and measured between their bounding circles rather than between their centers. The cap applies every time the follow distance is set, including the default distance chosen when the command is created and any distance the player drags out.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MatchVelocityFactor: Fraction of the target's velocity that the follower adds to its own desired velocity so it keeps station instead of chasing from behind. A value of 1 matches the target exactly, and it is only applied while the ship actually has a follow distance and is not being diverted by collision avoidance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.AvoidanceLookaheadTime: Seconds of the ship's current velocity projected ahead of it to build a probe destination for collision avoidance once it is already holding station. The probe is only used when it lands farther away than the real follow destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RightClickAdjustPixelThreshold: Screen distance in pixels, scaled by the global UI scale, that the mouse must travel while the command button is held before the follow distance and angle start being adjusted.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RightClickSetsAngleThreshold: Controls how far around the target the cursor must be dragged before a fixed follow angle is locked in rather than cleared. The authored angle is divided by the current follow distance in tiles and then multiplied by the camera zoom, so the effective threshold shrinks the farther away the ship is following from. A value of 0 means any drag at all sets an angle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.Circle: The circle drawn around the target ship while this command is displayed. It is drawn once per target regardless of how many ships are following that target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.CircleAddedRadius: Tiles added to the target ship's bounding radius, scaled by the target's own sprite scale, to get the radius of `Circle`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.CircleDuration: Seconds over which `Circle` fades in and shrinks to its final size after the command is given. Clicks on the target only start passing through to its individual parts once this time has elapsed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.CircleShrinkFromFactor: Radius multiplier that `Circle` starts at, shrinking to 1 over `CircleDuration`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RadiusAngleCircle: The arc drawn around the target, from the target's own facing to the chosen follow angle, showing where in the target's frame of reference the ship will sit. It is only drawn while the command has a target-relative follow angle set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RadiusAngleLines: The line style used for the two radial lines drawn from the target's center out to the ends of the `RadiusAngleCircle` arc.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MovePathLine: The line drawn from the previous command's endpoint to this command's follow destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MovePathLineCamScaleExponent: Exponent applied to the camera scale to get the thickness scale of `MovePathLine`, so that the line does not thin out linearly as the player zooms. The result is floored at the camera scale times `MinMovePathLineSize`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MinMovePathLineSize: Floor on the `MovePathLine` thickness scale, expressed as a fraction of the camera scale. When a formation follower draws the lead ship's queued destinations the same expression is combined with a minimum instead of a maximum, so there it acts as a ceiling.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.TargetPathLine: The line drawn from the follow destination to the target ship's center. Unlike `MovePathLine` it is drawn at the command's full color without the distance and angle fade.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.TargetPathLineCamScaleExponent: Exponent applied to the camera scale to get the thickness scale of `TargetPathLine`, floored at the camera scale times `MinTargetPathLineSize`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MinTargetPathLineSize: Floor on the `TargetPathLine` thickness scale, expressed as a fraction of the camera scale.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RotationTargetLine: The line drawn from the follow destination to the separate rotation target a command can be given. It is always drawn in the current player color rather than in the command's own color.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.GhostColorFactor: Color multiplier for the translucent ship ghost drawn at the follow destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.GhostBlinkColorFactor: Color multiplier the destination ghost blends toward on each blink right after the command is given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.BlinkInterval: Length in seconds of one full blink cycle of the destination ghost, split evenly between `GhostColorFactor` and `GhostBlinkColorFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.BlinkCount: Number of blink cycles the destination ghost performs after the command is given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.FadeMinDistance: Distance in tiles between the previous command's endpoint and this destination at which the ghost and the move path line begin to appear. Below it they are invisible unless the rotation difference keeps them visible.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.FadeMaxDistance: Distance in tiles at which the ghost and the move path line reach full opacity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.FadeMinAngle: Difference between the ship's current rotation and the commanded rotation at which the ghost and the move path line begin to appear. Whichever of the distance fade and the angle fade gives the higher opacity wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.FadeMaxAngle: Rotation difference at which the ghost and the move path line reach full opacity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.MoverWidget: The widget dragged to change the follow distance and the follow angle at once. It sits on the follow destination and points at the target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.RotatorWidget: The widget dragged to change the rotation the ship holds while following. It sits one ship bounding radius from the follow destination, in the direction the destination ghost faces.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.DeleterWidget: The widget clicked to delete this command. It sits diagonally off the follow destination by one ship bounding radius plus one tile and stays aligned with the camera.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.BaseFollowComma.DistIcon: The icon shown on the ship card beside the remaining distance to the follow destination.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.T:: Holds one settings block per ship order, so this is where move, attack, follow, salvage and FTL orders are all tuned.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.Move: Rules for the move command. They also govern a ship that has no command at all and a ship running only auto-fired thrusters, both of which read their thruster and avoidance settings from here.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.Attack: Rules for the attack command, which follows its target at a weapons range chosen from the ship's own weapons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.Follow: Rules for the follow command, which also backs the ad hoc formations created when several ships are moved together.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.Salvage: Rules for the salvage command, which flies to a wreck and queues salvage jobs on its parts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.DirectControl: Rules used while the player flies a ship manually. Only the base command fields apply, and vanilla overrides just `ThrusterSRFFactors` to weight rotation far above translation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.FtlGateJump: Rules for jumping out through an FTL gate. The game also reads `AvoidableDoodadTags` and `DestinationSeparationRadiusFactor` from this group when placing ships arriving from any FTL jump.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.FtlLocalJump: Rules for jumping to another point within the same sector.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandRules.WeaponTarget: Rules for the overlays and the sound used by explicitly assigned weapon targets. These are not a ship command, they just live in the same group.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.T:: One draggable handle on an issued order, such as the grip that sets its distance or rotation, with a sprite for each mouse state.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.StateNoneSprite: The sprite drawn while the cursor is not over the widget. Its `Size` is in pixels and gets multiplied by the camera's pixel-to-world scale and the global UI scale before the two size caps below are applied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.StateOverSprite: The sprite drawn while the cursor is over the widget but no mouse button is held on it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.StateDownSprite: The sprite drawn while the mouse button is held down on the widget.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.PixelOffset: Offset in pixels from the widget's anchor point, rotated along with the widget and scaled by the same pixel-to-world and UI scale as the sprite. Whenever `MaxWorldSize` or `MaxShipRelativeSize` shrinks the sprite, the offset shrinks by the same ratio so the widget keeps its relative placement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.MaxWorldSize: Upper bound on the drawn size of the widget in world tiles, applied per axis. Leaving it at zero turns the cap off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.CommandWidgetRu.MaxShipRelativeSize: Upper bound on the drawn size of the widget as a fraction of the commanded ship's bounding diameter, applied per axis. Leaving it at zero turns the cap off.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.T:: Tuning for the follow order, mainly how far behind the target a ship sits for ships, stations and junk.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.DefaultDistRadiusFactor: Gap between the bounding circles of the two ships that a new follow command starts with, as a multiple of the larger of their two bounding radii. It is used for any target that is neither a space station nor junk.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.JunkDistRadiusFactor: Gap used instead of `DefaultDistRadiusFactor` when the target is junk, as a multiple of the following ship's own bounding radius rather than the larger of the two.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.StationFollowDistRadiusFactor: Gap used instead of `DefaultDistRadiusFactor` when the target is a space station, as a multiple of the larger of the two bounding radii. Vanilla keeps it small so ships park close to stations.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.AdHocFormationRadiusFactor: How close two selected ships must be to be swept into the same ad hoc formation. They are grouped when the gap between their bounding circles is no wider than this multiple of the larger of their two radii.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.FinalCircle: The circle drawn at each of the lead ship's queued destinations when a formation follower is showing where the formation is ultimately headed. It is only drawn while the lead ship is selected.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.FinalCircleDuration: Seconds over which `FinalCircle` grows and fades away, measured from the time the lead ship's own command was given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FollowCommandRu.FinalCircleGrowFactor: Radius multiplier `FinalCircle` grows to over `FinalCircleDuration`, starting from the following ship's bounding radius.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.T:: Tuning for the order that sends a ship through an FTL gate to another sector, including the course line drawn to it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.FtlReadinessIcon: The icon shown on the ship card, with the FTL drive charge as a percentage, once the ship has reached the gate and is preparing to jump. Before that the ordinary follow distance icon from `DistIcon` is shown instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.DefaultDistRadiusFactor: Distance between the bounding circles of the ship and the gate that a new gate jump command starts with, as a multiple of the larger of the two radii. The starting distance is additionally clamped to the ship's current distance from the gate so that issuing the command never makes the ship back away.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.DestinationSeparationRadiusFactor: Multiplies the bounding radius of every arriving ship and of every ship already present when jump-in positions are spread apart so that arrivals do not land on top of anything. The game reads it from these rules for all FTL arrivals, not only gate jumps.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.CommandColor: Base color for this command's path lines, destination ghost, target circle and widgets.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.CourseLine: The line drawn from the ship out in the galaxy-map direction of the gate's destination node while the ship is in position and preparing to jump. It always extends 100 units scaled by the camera rather than reaching any actual point.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.CourseLinePulseInterval: Seconds per pulse cycle of the course line, which oscillates between plain white and `CourseLinePulseColorFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.CourseLinePulseColorFactor: The color the course line pulses toward on each cycle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlGateJumpComm.CourseLineUOffsetSpeed: Rate at which the course line's texture scrolls along the line. It is multiplied by elapsed time and by the camera scale, so the apparent scroll speed on screen stays constant across zoom levels.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.T:: Tuning for the short in-system FTL jump, including the delays between spooling up, vanishing and arriving.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.FtlReadinessIcon: The icon shown on the ship card with the FTL drive charge as a percentage. It reads 100% for the whole time the jump sequence is running.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.PreJumpDelay: Seconds the ship waits after its drive reports ready before the jump sequence actually begins. The command and the destination are re-checked when the delay ends, so a target that disappears in the meantime cancels the jump.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.ShipRemoveDelay: Seconds between the jump-out animation starting and the ship being taken out of the sector.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.ShipTransitDelay: Seconds the ship spends in transit after leaving the sector, before it is placed at its destination and the jump-in animation plays.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.DestinationDistance: Tiles beyond the destination object's bounding circle at which the ship arrives. It comes out on the side it jumped from and is then nudged to the nearest free spot large enough for the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.CommandColor: Color this command reports along with its destination to the ship destination overlay. The course line uses white pulsed with `CourseLinePulseColorFactor` instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.CourseLine: The line drawn from the ship to its jump destination for as long as the destination is valid.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.CourseLinePulseInterval: Seconds per pulse cycle of the course line, which oscillates between plain white and `CourseLinePulseColorFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.CourseLinePulseColorFactor: The color the course line pulses toward on each cycle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.FtlLocalJumpCom.CourseLineUOffsetSpeed: Rate at which the course line's texture scrolls along the line. It is multiplied by elapsed time and by the camera scale, so the apparent scroll speed on screen stays constant across zoom levels.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.T:: Tuning for the move order, covering how close counts as arrived and the ghost, circle and path line drawn while the order stands.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.SeparationRadiusFactor: Multiplies each ship's bounding radius when a batch of move commands issued together is spread out so the destinations do not overlap. Larger values leave wider gaps between the ships of a fleet at its destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.SatisfiedDistanceAsRadiusFraction: How close to its destination the ship must get, as a fraction of its own bounding radius, before the command counts as satisfied and the next queued command starts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.RightClickAdjustPixelThreshold: Screen distance in pixels, scaled by the global UI scale, that the mouse must travel while the command button is held before the destination rotation starts following the cursor. Creative mode reuses this same value as the drag threshold for rotating placed objects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.Circle: The circle that pulses out at the destination when a move command is given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.CircleDuration: Seconds the destination pulse lasts, over which `Circle` grows and fades away completely.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.CircleGrowFactor: Radius multiplier the destination pulse grows to over `CircleDuration`, starting from the commanded ship's bounding radius.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.PathLine: The line drawn from the previous command's endpoint to this destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.PathLineCamScaleExponent: Exponent applied to the camera scale to get the thickness scale of `PathLine`, so the line does not thin out linearly as the player zooms. The result is floored at the camera scale times `MinPathLineSize`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.MinPathLineSize: Floor on the `PathLine` thickness scale, expressed as a fraction of the camera scale.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.RotationTargetLine: The line drawn from the destination to the separate rotation target a move command can be given. It is always drawn in the current player color.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.GhostColorFactor: Color multiplier for the translucent ship ghost drawn at the destination.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.GhostBlinkColorFactor: Color multiplier the destination ghost blends toward on each blink right after the command is given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.BlinkInterval: Length in seconds of one full blink cycle of the destination ghost, split evenly between `GhostColorFactor` and `GhostBlinkColorFactor`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.BlinkCount: Number of blink cycles the destination ghost performs after the command is given.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.FadeMinDistance: Distance in tiles between the previous command's endpoint and this destination at which the ghost and the path line begin to appear. Below it they are invisible unless the rotation difference keeps them visible.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.FadeMaxDistance: Distance in tiles at which the ghost and the path line reach full opacity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.FadeMinAngle: Difference between the ship's current rotation and the commanded rotation at which the ghost and the path line begin to appear. Whichever of the distance fade and the angle fade gives the higher opacity wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.FadeMaxAngle: Rotation difference at which the ghost and the path line reach full opacity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.MoverWidget: The widget dragged to move this command's destination. It sits on the destination itself and is never rotated.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.RotatorWidget: The widget dragged to change the rotation the ship holds at the destination. It sits one ship bounding radius from the destination, in the direction the destination ghost faces.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.DeleterWidget: The widget clicked to delete this command. It sits diagonally off the destination by one ship bounding radius plus one tile and stays aligned with the camera.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.MoveDistIcon: The icon shown on the ship card beside the remaining distance to the destination for an ordinary move.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.MoveCommandRule.StrafeDistIcon: The icon used instead of `MoveDistIcon` when the move was issued with a forced destination rotation, which is how strafing moves are given.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.SalvageCommandR.T:: Tuning for the salvage order, which trails a wreck and cancels itself once every salvage job is done.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.SalvageCommandR.DistRadiusFactor: Gap between the bounding circles of the salvaging ship and its target that a new salvage command starts with, as a multiple of the salvaging ship's own bounding radius.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.SalvageCommandR.QueueSalvageDistanceAsRadiusFraction: How close the ship must get to its station-keeping spot, as a fraction of its own bounding radius, before salvage jobs are queued for the target's parts. The jobs are queued only once per command.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.SalvageCommandR.CommandColor: Base color for this command's path lines, destination ghost, target circle and widgets.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.T:: The reticle, box and line drawn when the player hand-picks a target for a weapon.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.IssueSound: The interface sound played once when the player assigns a batch of explicit weapon targets.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetNineSlice: The box drawn around a part that has been explicitly targeted. Weapons can override it with their own `OverrideTargetNineSlice`, and only this default box is tinted with the player's enemy color.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetCircle: The circle drawn around a whole ship that has been explicitly targeted. Weapons can override it with their own `OverrideTargetCircle`, and only this default circle is tinted with the player's enemy color.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TentativeTargetNineSlice: The box drawn around a part the player is about to target, used by the weapon targeting mode, the miniview and the part targeter buttons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TentativeTargetCircle: The circle drawn around a whole ship the player is about to target from a part targeter button, used unless that button's rules supply an `OverrideTentativeTargetCircle`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetLine: The line drawn from the weapon to its explicit target, and from one target to the next when a weapon has several. Weapons can override it with their own `OverrideTargetLine`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetLineFadeOutDuration: Seconds over which the target line fades away after the target was assigned, so the boxes and circles stay while the connecting lines disappear.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetNineSliceShrinkDuration: Seconds over which the box around a newly targeted part fades in and shrinks down onto the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetNineSliceShrinkFromInflate: Tiles by which the box around a newly targeted part is inflated on every side at the start of its shrink animation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetCircleShrinkDuration: Seconds over which the circle around a newly targeted ship shrinks down onto the ship. Unlike the part box, this circle does not fade in.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.TargetCircleShrinkFromInflate: Tiles added to the radius of the circle around a newly targeted ship at the start of its shrink animation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Commands.WeaponTargetRul.ReticleSprite: The reticle drawn on top of every explicit target, kept aligned with the camera. Weapons can override it with their own `OverrideReticleSprite`, and only this default reticle is tinted with the player's enemy color.

Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules.T:: One tab of roof decals in the paint tool, naming the folders its decal images are loaded from.
Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules.Folders: Folders scanned for this group's decal `*.png` images, which are loaded into the shared roof decals atlas. A folder may contain a `whitelist.txt` listing the filenames to include, otherwise every PNG is taken. When the same decal name appears in multiple folders the folder later in the list wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules.NameKey: Localization key for the group's display name, shown as the tooltip on its button in the paint toolbox.
Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules.Icon: Sprite used as the group's button image in the decal picker.
Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules.IconTextKey: Localization key for optional text drawn on the group's button, layered over the [[#Icon]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.T:: One door type buildable on a ship, with its resource cost, its open and closed sprites for each orientation and where it sits in the build menu.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.NameKey: The door's display name, shown as the title of its build tooltip and in the controls settings when listing door hotkeys.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.IconNameKey: Label shown on the door's button in the build palette. Falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.NameKey]] when omitted.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.ID: Game-wide unique ID of the door. Must be in the form `author_name.door_name`, loading fails otherwise. The vanilla door is `cosmoteer.door`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.OtherIDs: Alternate IDs this door also answers to. Each one is registered as a full lookup alias, so saved ships and references that use an old ID still resolve to this door. The vanilla door lists its pre-rename ID `door`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.Resources: Resource type and quantity pairs defining what the door costs to build. Their combined buy price is the door's money cost, and crew deliver exactly these resources during construction and haul them away again during deconstruction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.IsBuildable: If false, the door is hidden from the build palette, gets no editor hotkey, and door blueprints of this type are never valid to construct.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.Layer: The ship render layer the door's open and closed sprites are drawn on, which also decides the sprite atlas they are packed into. Must be a layer declared in the ship's `RenderLayers`. Vanilla uses the `doors` layer.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.StencilLayer: The ship render layer the door's stencil sprite is drawn on. Vanilla uses the `walls_stencil` layer, the stencil pass of the exterior walls.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.DescriptionKey: Descriptive text shown in the door's build tooltip, below the name and cost line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.DefaultEditorHotkey: The default key binding that selects this door for placement in the ship editor, rebindable by the player. Only registered when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.IsBuildable]] is true. The vanilla door uses `[X]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.EditorIcon: The icon shown on the door's button in the build palette.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalOpenSprite: Sprite shown for a horizontally-oriented door while at least one crew member is holding it open. Its animation restarts whenever the door opens, picking up at the position matching how far the closing animation had progressed, so vanilla uses the door-opening frames with `ClampAnimation` for a smooth swing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.VerticalOpenSprite: Sprite shown for a vertically-oriented door while at least one crew member is holding it open. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalOpenSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalClosedSprite: Sprite shown for a horizontally-oriented door while no crew member is holding it open, which is also the door's resting state. Its animation restarts whenever the last crew member releases the door, so vanilla plays the opening frames in reverse here as a closing animation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.VerticalClosedSprite: Sprite shown for a vertically-oriented door while no crew member is holding it open. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalClosedSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalStencilSprite: Sprite a horizontally-oriented door constantly renders on [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.StencilLayer]] while it exists and is not under construction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.VerticalStencilSprite: Sprite a vertically-oriented door constantly renders on [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.StencilLayer]] while it exists and is not under construction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalBlueprintSprite: Sprite representing a horizontally-oriented door in blueprint mode and over destroyed doors awaiting repair. Drawn with the ship's blueprint materials, using the invalid material when the door blueprint cannot be built.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.VerticalBlueprintSprite: Sprite representing a vertically-oriented door in blueprint mode and over destroyed doors awaiting repair. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalBlueprintSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.HorizontalDoorSize: Width and height, in tiles, of the highlight rectangle the build tools draw centered on a horizontally-oriented door, for hover highlights, the removal X, and repair markers. The vanilla door uses `[1, .5]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.VerticalDoorSize: Width and height, in tiles, of the highlight rectangle the build tools draw centered on a vertically-oriented door. The vanilla door uses `[.5, 1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.ConstructionFinishedMediaEffects: One-shot effects played at the door's location when its construction completes, meaning the last required resource has been delivered. The vanilla door plays a construction sound here.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.DeconstructionFinishedMediaEffects: One-shot effects played at the door's location when its deconstruction completes, meaning the last stored resource has been carried away.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.FractionalNonPlayerRefund: The fraction (0..1) of the door's cost refunded in Career mode when selling a door the player did not build, for example on a bought or captured ship, floored to whole credits. Doors built by the player refund their full cost. Defaults to 0.25 in code, and vanilla sets it to `25%` explicitly.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.EditorGroups: The build-palette group tabs this door's button appears under, with one button per listed group. Grouped door buttons use the large button size and can be marked as favorites. Without any group the door lands in the ungrouped palette section with a small button.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.EditorGroup: Single-group shorthand for [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Doors.DoorRules.EditorGroups]]. Only read when `EditorGroups` is absent.

Cosmoteer.Ships.EffectScaleModifier.T:: Feeds the effect's own intensity into the value, raised to `Exponent`, so the value scales with how strong the hit or media effect is.
Cosmoteer.Ships.EffectScaleModifier.Exponent: The effect scale is raised to this power to produce the modifier value, which ModificationMode then combines with the running value. At the default of 1 the modifier value is the effect scale itself.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.BuiltInFormat.T:: A fleet formation that ships with the game rather than being built by the player, listed with its name key and button icon. Write one of the concrete formation types.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.BuiltInFormat.NameKey: Localization key for the formation's display name shown in the UI.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.BuiltInFormat.Icon: Sprite drawn on the formation's button in the fleet formation UI.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.CustomFormati.T:: One lettered slot in the player's custom formation list, giving the letter on the button and the slot's full name.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.CustomFormati.LetterKey: Localization key for the slot's single-letter label used to identify the slot in a custom formation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.CustomFormati.NameKey: Localization key for the slot's full display name.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.LineFormation.T:: Lines the fleet up with the slowest ship at the centre, and can angle the two wings back to make a wedge or a claw.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.LineFormation.RadiusFactor: Spacing factor between consecutive ships in the line. The gap between two neighbors is the sum of their bounding radii plus RadiusFactor times the larger radius, so higher values spread the line out.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.LineFormation.LeftWingAngle: Heading offset of the left wing relative to the lead ship's flight direction. Ships placed on the left wing (every second follower) trail the lead at this angle. Defaults to pointing up relative to the lead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Formations.LineFormation.RightWingAngle: Heading offset of the right wing relative to the lead ship's flight direction. Ships placed on the right wing (every other follower) trail the lead at this angle. Defaults to pointing down relative to the lead.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.T:: A number that buffs and statuses can bend at runtime. Write it as a plain number, or as a group with `BaseValue` plus `Modifiers` or the inline `BuffType` and `StatusType` shorthands.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.BaseValue: The unmodified starting value, before any modifiers. When the whole modifiable value is written as a bare number rather than a group, that number becomes BaseValue with no modifiers. Modifiers are applied on top of it and the result is clamped to MinValue..MaxValue.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.Modifiers: The list of modifiers applied to BaseValue, in order, each transforming the running value. If this list is present, the inline BuffType, StatusType, and EffectScaleExponent shortcuts below are ignored. If it is absent, those shortcuts are collected into an equivalent modifier list instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.MinValue: Lower clamp on the final modified value, applied after all modifiers run. Defaults to the type's minimum. Also serves as the default lower bound for the inline Buff, Status, and EffectScale modifiers when their own min is unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.MaxValue: Upper clamp on the final modified value, applied after all modifiers run. Defaults to the type's maximum. Also serves as the default upper bound for the inline Buff, Status, and EffectScale modifiers when their own max is unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.BuffType: Inline shorthand for a single buff modifier. When set (and no explicit Modifiers list is given), a BuffModifier for this buff is added, letting the value respond to a ship buff without writing out a full Modifiers entry.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.BuffMode: How the inline BuffType modifier combines its buff amount with the running value. Defaults to `Replace`. Only read when BuffType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.BuffMinValue: Lower clamp applied by the inline BuffType modifier. Defaults to MinValue. Only read when BuffType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.BuffMaxValue: Upper clamp applied by the inline BuffType modifier. Defaults to MaxValue. Only read when BuffType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.StatusType: Inline shorthand for a single status modifier. When set (and no explicit Modifiers list is given), a StatusModifier for this status is added, letting the value respond to a ship status without writing out a full Modifiers entry.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.StatusMode: How the inline StatusType modifier combines its status amount with the running value. Defaults to `Replace`. Only read when StatusType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.StatusMinValue: Lower clamp applied by the inline StatusType modifier. Defaults to MinValue. Only read when StatusType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.StatusMaxValue: Upper clamp applied by the inline StatusType modifier. Defaults to MaxValue. Only read when StatusType is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.EffectScaleExponent: Inline shorthand for an effect-scale modifier. When set (and no explicit Modifiers list is given), an EffectScaleModifier is added that raises the effect scale to this exponent and combines it into the value, so the number scales with a hit or media effect's intensity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ModifiableValue.EffectScaleMode: How the inline EffectScaleExponent modifier combines the scaled effect value with the running value. Defaults to `Multiply`. Only read when EffectScaleExponent is set.

Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueModifier.T:: Looks up a modifier by name from whatever is evaluating the value. Nothing in the game supplies named values, so it leaves the value unchanged.
Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueModifier.ValueID: The named value looked up in the modification data. Its current value becomes the modifier value, which ModificationMode then combines with the running value. If the named value is not present, the modifier leaves the value unchanged.

Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueRemapModifier.T:: Maps a named value from `RemapFrom` onto `RemapTo` before applying it. Nothing in the game supplies named values, so it leaves the value unchanged.
Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueRemapModifier.RemapFrom: Input range of the named value that gets mapped. A value at RemapFrom.Min maps to RemapTo.Min and one at RemapFrom.Max maps to RemapTo.Max, linearly in between.
Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueRemapModifier.RemapTo: Output range the named value is mapped onto. The mapped result becomes the modifier value that ModificationMode then combines with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.NamedValueRemapModifier.Clamp: When true the named value is clamped to RemapFrom before mapping, so values outside the input range produce RemapTo.Min or RemapTo.Max rather than extrapolating past them. When false the mapping is unclamped.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.T:: Settings shared by the edge ports that join two neighbouring parts into one network, including which port types may connect and how the link is drawn in build mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.BlueprintOperationalToggle: The ID of the blueprint component to use for the blueprint port's operational checks, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.BlueprintConnectionMode: The mode used to determine the validity of a connection between two blueprint ports.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.Overlay: Visual options controlling how the port is drawn in the ship's network overlay. Its sub-fields (OverlayIcon, ConnectedEdgeIcon, RouteLine, DrawRouteHub, RouteDrawMode, IconDrawMode, HighlightPartOnPrimaryConnection, PartHighlightColor, SpreadHighlightThroughNetwork) are read directly into the port's own group rather than under a nested `Overlay` key. Purely cosmetic, none of it affects routing or connection validity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.RouteEndpoint: The IPartNetworkRegistrable component ID that inbound routes should connect to. If null, inbound routes will not be created.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.RouteSource: The IPartNetworkRegistrable component ID that outbound routes should connect from. If null, outbound routes will not be created.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.BlueprintRouteEndpoint: The IPartNetworkRegistrable component ID that inbound blueprint routes should connect to. If null, inbound blueprint routes will not be created.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.BlueprintRouteSource: The IPartNetworkRegistrable component ID that outbound blueprint routes should connect from. If null, outbound blueprint routes will not be created.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.Types: The port types that the port fulfills, and, if CompatibleTypes is unset, the port types that the port accepts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.CompatibleTypes: The port types that the port will accept connections with.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.BasePartNetwork.IncompatibleTypes: The port types that the port will refuse connections with, even if they are otherwise compatible.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkBasi.T:: A plain junction in a part's network wiring that carries routes through and does nothing else.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkBasi.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the node exists as a real component on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When true the node participates in the live part network as a routing hop. When false the node has no physical presence.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkBasi.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether the node exists in blueprint mode, backing `HasBlueprintComponent`, so routes can be drawn through it while the ship is still a blueprint. Independent of IncludeInPhysical.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkFilt.T:: Narrows a part-network search to components carrying one of the listed categories. Its `Categories` and `AllowUncategorized` fields are written directly on the searching component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkFilt.Categories: The network categories that components must match one or more of to be considered valid. If this is null, all categories will be allowed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkFilt.AllowUncategorized: Whether components with no network categories will be included.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkNode.T:: Stands in for another network component on the same part, so routes can point at this id while the real component named by `ComponentID` does the work.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.T:: How a network port looks in build mode: its icon, its route line, whether a hub is drawn and whether connected parts light up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.OverlayIcon: The ID of the custom overlay icon drawn to represent the port.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.ConnectedEdgeIcon: The ID of the additional icon to draw on the port's edge when connected, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.RouteLine: The ID of the custom overlay route line drawn for the port's routes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.DrawRouteHub: Whether this port wants its component to draw a 'route hub' sprite. A hub will be drawn if this is true for any connected ports.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.RouteDrawMode: The mode determining when route lines should be drawn for the port.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.IconDrawMode: The mode determining when the icon should be drawn for the port
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.HighlightPartOnPrimaryConnection: Whether the port's part will be highlighted when connected to a port on a part being placed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.PartHighlightColor: The color of the highlight drawn when HighlightPartOnPrimaryConnection is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.SpreadHighlightThroughNetwork: The ID of a network node provider component that the highlight should spread from to all parts in its network, if any.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.T:: One edge port that connects to a matching port on the neighbouring part, sitting at `Location` and facing `Direction`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkPort.Direction: The orthogonal direction that the port connects in.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.T:: A storage on the part that takes a resource in and hands it off to sinks elsewhere in the part network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.Mode: Strategy for spreading a pushed batch of resources across the subnetwork's sinks. Passed straight to the subnetwork's PushResources call, so it decides which target storages fill first when the input distributes into multiple destinations. See the MultiResourceStorageMode values for each ordering rule.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.T:: A storage on the part that fills itself from resource sources elsewhere in the part network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.Mode: Strategy for pulling resources out of the subnetwork's sources. Passed straight to the subnetwork's PullResources call, so it decides which source storages drain first when the output draws from multiple providers. See the MultiResourceStorageMode values for each ordering rule.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.T:: Opens an existing resource storage on the part to the network so other parts can draw from it or push into it, with optional reserved and maximum levels.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.ResourceType: The resource the store trades on the part network. Exposed as the store's sink and source ResourceType, so it only provides and receives this one resource type through the network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.ResourceStorage: The backing resource storage that the store will use to provide and receive resources.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.ReservedResourceLevel: The amount of resources in the ResourceStorage that are unavailable to the store. Represents a percentage of max capacity if ResourceLevelsAreFractions is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.MaxResourceLevel: The resource level in the ResourceStorage that the store is able to deposit up to. Represents a percentage of max capacity if ResourceLevelsAreFractions is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.ResourceLevelsAreFractions: Whether the resource level values are a fraction of the ResourceStorage's capacity, or an absolute value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.AllowProviding: Whether the store can fulfill requests for its resource from the part-network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.AllowReceiving: Whether the store can receive resources pushed through the part-network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkReso.Categories: The network categories of the storage.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.0: List-form index 0. When a route is written as a 3-element list `[Start, End, Cost]` instead of a named group, this is the origin component, equivalent to Start.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.1: List-form index 1. The destination component in the `[Start, End, Cost]` list form, equivalent to End.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.2: List-form index 2. The path cost in the `[Start, End, Cost]` list form, equivalent to Cost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.T:: One directed hop from a component on the part to another, with a cost that steers which path the network prefers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.Start: The ID of the route's origin component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.End: The ID of the route's destination component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.Cost: The path cost of traversing the route.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.T:: Wires the network components on a single part together, saying which of them can reach which.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.RouteGenerators: The set of route generators the router uses to define its internal routes. Each generator (`Simple`, `Bidirectional`, or `Omni`, chosen by its `Type`) yields a collection of directed routes between the router's own port components, and the router concatenates all of them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the router exists on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When false the router has no physical component and its routes only exist in blueprint mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.IncludeInBlueprints: When the router's blueprint component is created. `None` (alias `false`) never creates it, `Normal` (alias `true`) creates it for regular blueprint updates, and `All` also includes it in lightweight blueprint validity checks. Backs `HasBlueprintComponent` and `IncludeInLightweightBlueprintUpdates`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.T:: Declares routes as `A B Cost` triples and builds the hop in both directions from each one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.Routes: List of `[A, B, Cost]` entries. Each entry is expanded at load into two directed routes, A to B and B to A, both with the given path cost, so a single line defines a two-way connection between the two components.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.T:: Supplies the hops inside a router. Write `Simple` for one-way hops, `Bidirectional` for pairs, or `Omni` to link every listed component to every other.
Links every component in `ComponentIDs` to every other one, in both directions, at the same cost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.ComponentIDs: The set of components to fully interconnect. At load, a directed route is generated between every ordered pair of these components (both directions for each pair), so all listed components can route to each other.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.Cost: The path cost applied to every route the generator produces between the ComponentIDs.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.T:: Lists the router's hops one at a time, each with its own start, end and cost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkRout.Routes: Explicit list of individual directed routes, each with its own Start, End, and Cost. Unlike the bidirectional and omni generators, entries are used as-is with no automatic reverse or pairwise expansion.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.T:: Combines every matching toggle reachable through the part network into one on or off state for this part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.Mode: How the on/off states of the toggles received from the subnetwork are combined into this receiver's single toggle state. `All` on, `Any` on, exactly `One` on, or `None` on (all off). Fed to the subnetwork's toggle-mode handle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.Invert: Flips the combined result, so the receiver reads as on precisely when the Mode condition is not met.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the component exists on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When false it has no physical presence and exists only in blueprint mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether the component's blueprint variant is created, backing `HasBlueprintComponent`, so it works while the ship is a blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.T:: Publishes a toggle from another component on this part to the network, so receivers elsewhere can read it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.ToggleSource: The ID of the IPartComponentToggle that this exposes to the network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.Categories: The network categories of the toggle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the component exists on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When false it has no physical presence and exists only in blueprint mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTogg.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether the component's blueprint variant is created, backing `HasBlueprintComponent`, so it works while the ship is a blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTrig.T:: Fires whenever any matching trigger reachable through the part network fires.
Publishes a trigger from another component on this part to the network, so receivers elsewhere fire with it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTrig.TriggerSource: Reference to the component trigger this exposes on the part network, so the trigger's firing propagates to network trigger receivers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkTrig.Categories: Network categories tagging this trigger, used by receiver NetworkFilters to decide whether to listen to it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.T:: Combines every matching value reachable through the part network into one number for this part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.Mode: The combination mode for the retrieved values.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the component exists on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When false it has no physical presence and exists only in blueprint mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether the component's blueprint variant is created, backing `HasBlueprintComponent`, so it works while the ship is a blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.T:: Publishes a number from another component on this part to the network, so receivers elsewhere can read it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.ValueSource: The ID of the IPartComponentValue that this exposes to the network.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.Categories: The network categories of the value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the component exists on the built ship, backing `HasPhysicalComponent`. When false it has no physical presence and exists only in blueprint mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Networks.PartNetworkValu.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether the component's blueprint variant is created, backing `HasBlueprintComponent`, so it works while the ship is a blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.T:: One roof decal by id, size in tiles, rotation and flips. In rules it is the replacement half of `RoofDecalUpgrades`, which rewrites decals saved by older versions.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.ID: Identifies which roof decal image this instance paints, resolving against the decals loaded by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules]]. The deserializer requires it despite the optional signature.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.Location: Top-left cell of the decal on the ship's roof grid. Defaults to the origin.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.Rot0Size: Decal footprint in tiles measured at rotation 0, before [[#Rotation]] is applied. The drawn size comes from combining this with the decal's own base size. Defaults to zero, which falls back to the decal's natural size.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.Rotation: Number of 90-degree clockwise quarter-turns applied to the decal, 0 through 3.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.Invert: Inverts the decal's alpha so opaque areas become transparent and vice versa, turning it into a negative or cutout.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Paint.Decal.FlipY: Convenience input for a vertical flip. At load time it is normalized into a horizontal [[#FlipX]] plus a 180-degree [[#Rotation]] and is not stored as its own value.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.T:: Shared setup for the components that hand out a buff, above all which `BuffType` is given and how strong it is. A modder writes one of the concrete providers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BuffAmount: The strength of the buff delivered to each receiver, defaulting to 1. Each receiver gets this amount multiplied by the provider shape's distance falloff factor and by the value of the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuffProviderRules.BuffMultiplier]] component, and the values of all providers are then combined according to the buff type's CombineMode. Being modifiable, it can itself be scaled by buffs on the providing part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BuffMultiplier: A value component on the same part whose current value multiplies the provided buff amount, with the buff updating live whenever that value changes. The vanilla chaingun points this at its ramp-up accumulator so its buff scales with spin-up, and overclock kits use a toggle-driven 0-or-1 value to switch a buff on and off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BlueprintBuffMultiplier: The value reference for the buff value multiplier for the BlueprintPartBuffProvider.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.ShowBuffRange: Highlights every cell of the buff's area in the build-mode blueprint overlay. The highlight colors come from the `PartHighlights` entry in the game GUI rules whose ID matches the buff type's ID. No vanilla part enables it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BlueprintsOnly: Skips creating the runtime component, so the provider exists only on ship blueprints and never buffs the live ship. Vanilla uses it for display-only providers such as the chaingun magazine's connection indicators, which exist purely to draw build-mode overlays.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BlueprintOverlayToggle: A toggle component on the same part that gates this provider's build-mode overlay, so its buffed parts are only highlighted while the toggle is on. Has no effect on the actual buff. The vanilla railgun launcher points its normal and overclocked chain providers at its overclock mode toggle so only the active one draws its overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.InvertBlueprintOverlayToggle: Reverses [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuffProviderRules.BlueprintOverlayToggle]] so the provider's build-mode overlay is drawn only while the toggle is off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.BuffType: The type of buff this provider gives, referenced by its key in the buffs map (`Data/buffs/buffs.rules` in vanilla). Only parts that list the type in their [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ReceivableBuffs]] register as receivers for it. Although marked optional, the value is always read and loading fails without it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.BasePartBuff.ChainsFromBuffType: Declares that this provider passes on a buff of the given type that its own part receives, letting the build-mode overlay walk chains of providers when highlighting buffed parts and computing displayed buff totals. The type must be listed in the part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ReceivableBuffs]] or loading fails. Only the build-mode GUI reads it, as used by the vanilla railgun accelerators and rocket thruster parts that relay buffs down a line.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuff.T:: Buffs every part covering a rectangle of cells measured from this part's own position.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuff.BuffArea: The buffed rectangle as `[x, y, width, height]` in part-local tile coordinates, rotated and flipped with the part into ship space. Parts whose physical footprint intersects it receive the buff. The vanilla chaingun magazine uses `[-1, 0, 1, 1]` to target just the single tile beside it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuff.BuffsSelf: Lets the provider buff its own part in addition to other parts in the area. Off by default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuff.Criterias: Filters that a part in the area must additionally match to receive the buff. Each entry can require part IDs or categories, exclusions, and a specific rotation, flip, or position relative to the provider, and matching any single entry is enough. When absent, every part in the area is buffed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuff.Criteria: A single filter used instead of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartAreaBuffProviderRules.Criterias]] when one entry suffices. Only read when Criterias is absent.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffTogg.T:: Switches on while the buff this part receives falls between `MinBuffValue` and `MaxBuffValue`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffTogg.MinBuffValue: The lowest combined buff value, inclusive, at which the toggle turns on. A part that is not receiving the buff at all keeps the toggle off regardless of this bound.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffTogg.MaxBuffValue: The highest combined buff value, inclusive, at which the toggle turns on. Together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffToggleRules.MinBuffValue]] this forms the window the part's current buff value must fall into.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffTogg.Invert: Reverses the toggle so it is on while the part is not buffed or its buff value falls outside the window.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffTogg.BuffType: The buff type watched on the owning part. The toggle is on while the part's combined value for this buff lies within [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffToggleRules.MinBuffValue]] to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffToggleRules.MaxBuffValue]]. Vanilla thrusters watch the `EnginePowerDistribution` buff to switch off their own battery consumer while an engine room supplies them. Although marked optional, the value is always read and loading fails without it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffable.T:: Provides a number that the part's buffs and statuses can modify, which is how a buffed part changes what it does.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffable.Value: The base value this component reports to components that reference it, defaulting to 1. Being modifiable, it can carry buff and status modifiers, and referencing components see the modified result update live as the part's buffs and statuses change. Vanilla thrusters wrap values like their maximum activation in a `BuffableValue` so overclock buffs can scale what other components read.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartBuffable.IncludeInBlueprints: Creates a blueprint counterpart of the component so build-mode logic can read the value as well. Off by default.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.T:: Buffs the parts inside a circle around this part, with `Falloff` weakening the buff toward the edge.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.BuffRadius: The radius, in tiles, of the circle within which the buff applies. Parts whose physical footprint intersects the circle receive the buff. No vanilla part uses a CircleBuffProvider.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.BuffCenter: The center of the buff circle, defaulting to the center of the part's own footprint. The value is used as-is in ship coordinates and is not offset or rotated with the part, so leaving it unset is almost always what you want.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.BuffsSelf: Lets the provider buff its own part in addition to other parts in range. Off by default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.Falloff: An exponent that weakens the buff with distance from the circle's center, measured to the nearest edge of the receiver's footprint. The buff amount is multiplied by `(1 - distance / BuffRadius)` raised to this power. At 0, the default, all parts in the circle get full strength.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.Criterias: Filters that a part in the circle must additionally match to receive the buff. Each entry can require part IDs or categories, exclusions, and a specific rotation, flip, or position relative to the provider, and matching any single entry is enough. When absent, every part in the circle is buffed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBu.Criteria: A single filter used instead of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartCircleBuffProviderRules.Criterias]] when one entry suffices. Only read when Criterias is absent.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.T:: Spreads its buff outward from receiver to receiver, reaching parts up to `ChainLengthLimit` links away.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.BuffRegion: The part-relative region in which the buff spreads, applied first around this part and then again around every part already receiving the buff, so the buff flood-fills outward through chains of receivers. A part is buffed when its footprint lies in the region of the provider or of any part already in the chain, subject to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuffProviderRules.FloodFillLimitRegion]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuffProviderRules.ChainLengthLimit]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.FloodFillLimitRegion: The region around the initial source provider that this provider can flood-fill to. Infinite if null.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.ChainLengthLimit: The maximum number of parts aside from the source that can be chained through to provide a buff, including the receiver.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.BuffsSelf: Lets the provider buff its own part in addition to the parts reached by the flood fill. Off by default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.Criterias: Filters that a candidate part must additionally match to receive the buff, always evaluated against the original providing part rather than the part being chained through. Each entry can require part IDs or categories, exclusions, and a specific rotation, flip, or position relative to the provider, and matching any single entry is enough. When absent, every reachable part is buffed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuf.Criteria: A single filter used instead of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartFloodBuffProviderRules.Criterias]] when one entry suffices. Only read when Criterias is absent.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.T:: Buffs every part within `GridDistance` cells, counted along the grid rather than as a straight-line distance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.GridDistance: The maximum distance, in tiles, between the nearest edges of this part's footprint and a receiving part's footprint for the buff to apply. Orthogonally adjacent parts are at distance 1. Vanilla factories use 1 so only directly adjacent parts get their `Factory` buff.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.AllowDiagonals: Measures the distance as the larger of the horizontal and vertical gaps instead of their sum, so diagonally adjacent parts count as distance 1 and the buff range becomes a square instead of a diamond.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.BuffsSelf: Lets the provider buff its own part in addition to other parts in range. Off by default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.Falloff: An exponent that weakens the buff with distance. The buff amount is multiplied by `(1 - (distance - 1) / GridDistance)` raised to this power, so parts at distance 1 get full strength and farther parts progressively less. At 0, the default, all parts in range get full strength.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.Criterias: Filters that a part in range must additionally match to receive the buff. Each entry can require part IDs or categories, exclusions, and a specific rotation, flip, or position relative to the provider, and matching any single entry is enough. When absent, every part in range is buffed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuff.Criteria: A single filter used instead of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartGridBuffProviderRules.Criterias]] when one entry suffices. Only read when Criterias is absent.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.PartSelfBuff.T:: Buffs only the part it sits on, which is how a part boosts itself.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.WholeShipBuf.T:: Buffs every part on the ship at once.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Buffs.WholeShipBuf.BuffsSelf: Lets the provider buff its own part in addition to every other part on the ship. Off by default.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartCompo.T:: Shared setup for components that can be pinned to another component and move with it, such as a muzzle riding a turret. A modder writes one of the concrete types.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartCompo.Location: The component's position, in tiles in the part's un-rotated rules space, with `[0, 0]` at the part's top-left corner. With [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartComponentRules.ChainedTo]] set it instead becomes an offset from the chained component, rotated by that component's rotation, so the component follows the chained one as it moves and turns.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartCompo.Rotation: The component's facing, in degrees. With [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartComponentRules.ChainedTo]] set it is added on top of the chained component's rotation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartCompo.ChainedTo: Another chainable component on the same part that this component's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartComponentRules.Location]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.ChainablePartComponentRules.Rotation]] are measured relative to. Chains may be several links long, and position and rotation updates propagate down them, which is how vanilla weapons keep muzzles and emitters attached to their rotating turret.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.T:: Shared setup for custom part hit shapes, including the damage and status resistances they carry. A modder writes the circle or the polygon version.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.Density: The physics density of the collider's material, falling back to the part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Density]] when unset. It is used both for the physics fixture and for the collider's contribution to ship mass, which is its area times this density.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.IsHigh: Whether this collider counts as a high collider rather than a low one for collision filtering, so beams and projectiles that pass over low parts still strike it. Selects which collision categories the fixture is placed in.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.DamageResistances: Per-damage-type resistances used in place of the part's own [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DamageResistances]] for hits that struck this collider. Each range interpolates from Min to Max as the part's damage fraction goes from 0 to 1, and status effects can then modify the result.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.StatusResistances: The collider's base resistances to status types, interpolated by the current DamageFraction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.BaseColl.InitialPenetrationResistance: The penetration resistance drained from a penetrating shot that enters the part through this collider, used in place of the part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InitialPenetrationResistance]]. Interpolated from Min to Max by the part's damage fraction.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.CircleCo.T:: Gives the part a round hit shape that fire is tested against instead of the part rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.CircleCo.Radius: The radius of the circular collider, in tiles, centered on the component's location. The circle's area times the collider's density gives the mass the collider adds to the ship.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.PolygonC.T:: Gives the part a hit shape built from listed corner points, for wedges and other non-rectangular parts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Colliders.PolygonC.Vertices: The corner points of the polygon, in tiles relative to the component's own location, rotating with the component and mirrored when the part is flipped. The enclosed area times the collider's density gives the mass the collider adds to the ship.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Commands.CommandCo.T:: Adds its `CommandPoints` to what the ship's control rooms must supply, so too many heavy parts leave the ship uncontrollable.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Commands.CommandCo.CommandPoints: The number of command points this component uses while operational. When operational consumers use more points than `CommandProvider` components supply, the ship can no longer receive or execute commands.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Commands.CommandPr.T:: Supplies `CommandPoints` to the ship, which is what makes a part a control room.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Commands.CommandPr.CommandPoints: The number of command points this component supplies to the ship while operational. A ship can receive and execute commands only while the total provided points are above zero and at least the points used by operational `CommandConsumer` components, which is how losing every control room leaves a ship uncontrollable.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Commands.CommandTo.T:: On while the ship has enough command points to be controlled.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Construction.SoftR.T:: Sets whether crew clearing a status such as fire must finish that work before the part's other repairs or share the effort with them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Construction.SoftR.RepairType: How crew repair work is applied to this soft repair. `Blocking` repairs consume the crew's repair work budget first and halt health repair and all `Simultaneous` repairs until finished, which is how vanilla fire must be extinguished before a part heals. `Simultaneous` repairs receive the full work budget alongside normal health repair without consuming any of it, as the vanilla scorched, heat, and shield overload statuses do.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.T:: Lets crew step outside the ship and back in, and is where ejected crew are thrown from.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.EnterExitPoint: The point, in tiles relative to the unrotated part's upper-left corner, where crew leave and enter the ship and where ejected resource nuggets spawn. The cell containing it also decides which contiguous crew path network the airlock serves. The vanilla airlock uses `[.5, .5]`, the center of its single tile.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.NuggetEjectVelocity: The speed, in tiles per second, given to ejected resource nuggets, rolled at random between Min and Max for each nugget and added on top of the ship's own velocity at the eject point. The vanilla airlock uses `[1.5, 2.5]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.NuggetEjectDirection: The direction ejected resource nuggets fly, as an angular range relative to the airlock component's world direction, rolled at random for each nugget. The vanilla airlock uses `[-100d, -80d]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.NuggetEjectDoorOpenDuration: Seconds the airlock's crew-proximity door is held open whenever a resource nugget is ejected. The vanilla airlock uses 0.65.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.UITileRect: The rectangle, in tiles relative to the unrotated part's upper-left corner, drawn as this airlock's overlay tile in the resource-management view, where the airlock acts as a drop target for ejecting resources. Falls back to the part's physical rect when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.EntryToggle: Has no effect. The game deserializes the reference but no code ever reads it, so an airlock's entry side cannot be gated by a toggle component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.ExitToggle: Has no effect. The game deserializes the reference but no code ever reads it, so an airlock's exit side cannot be gated by a toggle component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.CrewLeaveEffects: One-shot media effects played when a crew member exits the ship through this airlock and becomes a space-walking crew.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.CrewEnterEffects: One-shot media effects played when a space-walking crew member arrives at [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.AirlockRules.EnterExitPoint]] and enters the ship through this airlock.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewDestinati.T:: On while a crew member heading for this part comes within `Distance` of it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewDestinati.Distance: The range, in tiles, at which a space-walking crew heading for a destination on this part flips the toggle on, measured from the crew to its destination point. Vanilla airlocks and factory roof doors use it to swing their outer door open as EVA crew approach. The toggle is also held open briefly when crew enter or exit and when nuggets are ejected or collected.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewLocationR.T:: Marks the spot where a single crew member stands and which way they face while manning the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewLocationR.EnforceRotation: Whether a crew standing at this location also has their rendered facing overridden by the location's rotation, which is how gunners face along their weapon. When false only the position is enforced and the crew keeps their own facing.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRul.T:: Supplies the ship with crew members and gives them a rectangle to idle in, which is what a crew quarters does.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRul.Crew: The number of crew this part houses. It becomes the part's crew capacity and the assignment capacity of this source, and a part may have at most one CrewSource component. The vanilla small crew quarters houses 2.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRul.IdleRect: The rectangle, in part rules coordinates, where this part's assigned crew stand while idling at home. Each idle crew picks a random point inside it. When unset, the part's physical rect shrunk by 0.25 tiles on each side is used.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRul.ColorSRange: The saturation band, as 0..1 fractions, that the assigned role's color is remapped into for this component's color, which sprites with `GetColorFrom` pointed at the source display. The role color's own saturation interpolates within the band. Vanilla crew quarters use `[0, 0.25]` for a desaturated role tint on their bunks.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRul.ColorVRange: The brightness band, as 0..1 fractions, that the assigned role's color is remapped into for this component's color. The counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.CrewSourceRules.ColorSRange]] for the color's value channel, `[0.5, 0.75]` in vanilla crew quarters.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.T:: Sets how many crew must man the part before it works, how urgent that job is and where they stand.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.Crew:
The number of crew that operate this part. The component itself acts as a toggle that reads on
while at least this many crew have arrived, which is how `IsOperational`-style
[[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules]] chains gate a weapon on its operators.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.DefaultPriority:
The base priority with which crew work this job, used whenever the player has not set a custom
priority for it in the crew management UI. Higher values win crew over lower ones.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.OverridePriorityPart:
Stores and looks up the player-set crew priority under another part's identity instead of this
part's own. Keeps priorities saved in old ships working after a part is renamed or split.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.OverridePriorityKey:
Stores and looks up the player-set crew priority under another component's id instead of this
component's own. Several crew components can share one key so they appear as a single priority
entry, and vanilla uses it to keep old saves working after a component was renamed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.OverridePriorityName:
Stores and looks up the player-set crew priority under an arbitrary label instead of a component
id. The free-form spelling of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.OverridePriorityKey]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.PrerequisitesBeforeCrewing:
Toggles that must all be on for the part to request operators at all. While any is off for longer
than [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.PrerequisitesUnmetAbandonDelay]], the job asks for
zero crew and the current operators walk away. Vanilla weapons list their power and scorched
toggles here, so an unpowered turret does not hold crew.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.HighPriorityPrerequisites:
Toggles that must all be on for the operators to hold their station against other work. While any
is off for longer than [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.PrerequisitesUnmetAbandonDelay]],
the job's effective priority drops by 10000, so any other job (a delivery run, another part) pulls
the operators away, and they only return when nothing else needs them. The vanilla missile
launcher points this at a `ToggleProxy` whose target each missile mode supplies, so crew stand
down when the selected mode has no ammo. A proxy with no connected target reads as off, so every
toggled component set must declare the proxied component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.CrewDestinations:
The points, in part rules coordinates, an operator walks to and stands at. Each assigned crew
picks one destination, so there should be at least [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Crew.PartCrewRules.Crew]]
entries.
