Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycl.ModeRange: The inclusive Min and Max mode numbers the cycle moves through. Stepping past an end wraps around to the other end unless [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycleRules.Clamp]] is set. Defaults to `[0, 1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycl.StartingMode: The mode the component starts in when the part is first created. Defaults to the Min of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycleRules.ModeRange]]. The current mode persists in saves.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycl.Clamp: Stops the cycle at the ends of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeCycleRules.ModeRange]] instead of wrapping around, so incrementing at Max and decrementing at Min do nothing.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeProx.T:: Stands in for a mode component in another part, reporting `ModeWhenNotConnected` when there is nothing to connect to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeProx.ModeWhenNotConnected: The mode this proxy reports while it is not connected to a proxied mode component, defaulting to 0. Connecting or disconnecting raises a mode change whenever it alters the reported value.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTogg.T:: On while the mode component it watches sits on one of the modes listed in `OnModes`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTogg.Mode: A mode component on the same part whose integer mode is watched. The toggle is on while that mode is one of the values listed in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeToggleRules.OnMode]] or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeToggleRules.OnModes]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTogg.Invert: Reverses the result, so the toggle is on while the watched mode is not one of the listed values.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTogg.OnMode: A single mode value that switches the toggle on. Merged with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeToggleRules.OnModes]] into one set, so both can be given together.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTogg.OnModes: The mode values that switch the toggle on. Merged with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeToggleRules.OnMode]] into one set.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTrig.T:: Fires whenever the mode component it watches moves into one of `TriggerInModes`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTrig.Mode: A mode component on the same part that is watched. The trigger fires each time its mode changes, as long as this component is operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartModeTrig.TriggerInModes: The mode values that fire the trigger, checked against the new mode after each change. When unset, every mode change fires.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.T:: Combines several toggles into one that is on when all, any, exactly one or none of them are on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.Toggles: The toggle components whose states are combined according to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules.Mode]]. Each entry can be written as just the component's name, or as a group with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules+ToggleRules.Toggle]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules+ToggleRules.Invert]] fields. The vanilla small crew quarters combines its two door toggles with `Toggles = [LeftDoorToggle, RightDoorToggle]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.ViaBuffs: Additionally includes toggle components from other parts connected through the buff system. The group names the `ComponentID` (or `ComponentIDs`) to pick up in each connected part, with either `IncomingBuffTypes` selecting parts that buff this part or `OutgoingBuffProviders` selecting parts buffed by this part's own buff provider components.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.Mode: How the sub-toggle states combine into this toggle's state. `All` is on when every listed toggle is on, `Any` when at least one is, `One` when exactly one is, and `None` when none are. With no toggles at all, `All` and `None` are on while `Any` and `One` are off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.Invert: Flips the combined result after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules.Mode]] is applied.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.T:: One entry in a multi toggle, naming the toggle to read and whether to invert it first.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.Toggle: The toggle component this entry reads, referenced by its component ID, or as a group with `ID` and an optional `ToggleID` selecting a named toggle within that component. The whole entry can also be written as just the component name, in which case it is read directly as this reference.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTog.Invert: Flips this entry's state before it is combined by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiToggleRules.Mode]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTri.T:: Fires whenever any of the triggers it lists fires.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTri.Triggers: The source triggers merged into this one. A firing of any of them re-fires this trigger with the same event value, as long as this component is operational. Each entry can be written as just the component name, or as a group with `ID` and an optional `TriggerID`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiTri.ViaBuffs: Additionally relays firings from trigger components in other parts connected through the buff system. The group names the `ComponentID` (or `ComponentIDs`) to pick up in each connected part, with either `IncomingBuffTypes` selecting parts that buff this part or `OutgoingBuffProviders` selecting parts buffed by this part's own buff provider components.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiVal.T:: Combines several value components into one number by adding, multiplying or taking the smallest, largest or average.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartMultiVal.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether a blueprint version of this component is also created for ship blueprints. `None` creates none, `Normal` includes it in regular blueprint updates, and `All` additionally includes it in lightweight blueprint validity checks. `false` and `true` are accepted as aliases for `None` and `Normal`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartPolledVa.T:: Reads another component's value every tick and announces changes, for sources that never report changes themselves.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartPolledVa.ValueSource: The value component polled once per fixed simulation tick while the component is operational, with its value republished to listeners on change. This lets components that need change notifications read lazily evaluated values such as timers. Written either as a bare component ID or as a group with `ID` and an optional `ValueID`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartPolledVa.DefaultValue: The value reported before the first poll and restored whenever the component becomes non-operational. The vanilla tractor beam uses 0 so its overload charge progress reads zero while the overload toggle is off.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartSmoothed.T:: Follows another component's value gradually, moving no more than `MaxDelta` per second toward it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartSmoothed.ValueSource: The value component this component's own value chases over time. Written either as a bare component ID or as a group with `ID` and an optional `ValueID` naming a specific sub-value. If the smoothed value ever becomes NaN it snaps directly to the source value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartSmoothed.MaxDelta: The maximum rate, in value units per second, at which the smoothed value moves toward the source value. Accepts buff modifiers. The vanilla small thruster smooths its normalized activation for overclock heat output with `MaxDelta = 1 / (&../Overclock_ThrusterHeatProducer/Interval)`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartSmoothed.StartValue: The value the component starts at when added to its part. When unset it starts at the source's current value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartSmoothed.Deterministic: Whether the value advances on fixed simulation ticks, keeping it consistent across the deterministic simulation. When false it advances once per rendered frame instead, which is only safe for purely visual values.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticMo.T:: A fixed mode number that other components can read.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticMo.Mode: The fixed integer mode value this component reports to other components, such as a ModeToggle or ModeTrigger.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticTo.T:: A toggle stuck permanently on or off, handy as a constant input to other components.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticTo.ToggleOn: The fixed on or off state this component reports to other components. The vanilla overclock base part uses an always-on StaticToggle as its default `IsOperational` component, and the resonance beam turret uses an always-off one as its `OverclockModeToggle`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticVa.T:: A fixed number that other components can read, most often a tuning constant.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStaticVa.Value: The constant value the component provides to other components. Vanilla parts define tiny `Zero` and `One` StaticValue components as fixed inputs for value selectors, as the small thruster's overclock state selector does.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.T:: Counts time upward while the part runs, stopping at `Max` and restartable from a trigger.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.Max: The maximum elapsed time, in seconds, that the stopwatch can accumulate. The elapsed time is clamped to this cap every update and holds there until reset. The elapsed time is also the value this component reports to other components.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.TimeScaleMultiplier: Multiplier on how fast the stopwatch advances relative to real time. Each fixed update adds the update interval times this multiplier to the elapsed time. The stopwatch only counts while the part is operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.StartValue: The elapsed time, in seconds, that the stopwatch begins at and returns to whenever it is reset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.ResetOnOperational: Resets the elapsed time to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatchRules.StartValue]] whenever the part becomes operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.ResetOnNotOperational: Resets the elapsed time to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatchRules.StartValue]] whenever the part stops being operational. Without either reset option the elapsed time simply pauses while non-operational and persists in saves.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatc.ResetTrigger: A trigger component on the same part that resets the elapsed time to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartStopwatchRules.StartValue]] each time it fires.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.T:: On while a value from another component sits between `MinAmount` and `MaxAmount`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.ValueFrom: A value component on the same part whose current value is watched. The toggle is on while that value lies between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThresholdToggleRules.MinAmount]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThresholdToggleRules.MaxAmount]] inclusive. Also accepted under the alias `AmountFrom`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.MinAmount: The lower bound, inclusive, of the on range. Defaults to unbounded. Being modifiable, buffs and statuses can move the bound, and the toggle re-evaluates when they change. The vanilla chaingun's IsShellFullyOpen toggle sets `MinAmount = 100%` on its shell-opening tween value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.MaxAmount: The upper bound, inclusive, of the on range. Defaults to unbounded. The vanilla chaingun's IsShellFullyClosed toggle sets `MaxAmount = 0%` on the same tween value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.Invert: Reverses the result, so the toggle is on while the value lies outside the range instead of inside it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.T:: Fires when a value from another component moves into the band between `MinAmount` and `MaxAmount`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.AmountFrom: A value component on the same part whose current value is watched. The trigger fires at the moment the value enters the range between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThresholdTriggerRules.MinAmount]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThresholdTriggerRules.MaxAmount]], and not again until the value has left the range and re-entered it. Vanilla thrusters watch their thrust level this way to fire burst effects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.MinAmount: The lower bound, inclusive, of the value range that satisfies the trigger. Defaults to no lower bound. The vanilla medium thruster uses `MinAmount = .5` so its `BurstTrigger` fires when thrust output reaches half strength.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.MaxAmount: The upper bound, inclusive, of the value range that satisfies the trigger. Defaults to no upper bound.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartThreshol.Invert: Reverses the condition, so the trigger fires when the watched value leaves the Min to Max range instead of entering it.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.T:: Scores the tiles along a straight line out from the part and stops where a blocking part or shield gets in the way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.Line: The tile line this component scores. Walking outward from the line's start, each tile contributes its score from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.BaseTileScoreValueRules.PartIDTileScores]], [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.BaseTileScoreValueRules.PartCategoryTileScores]] or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.BaseTileScoreValueRules.EmptyTileScore]], stopping at the first blocking tile. The running total becomes the component's value. The vanilla radiator scores a 120-tile line to compute its heat dissipation rate.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.BlockingPartIDs: Parts that terminate the line. When a tile is occupied by one of these parts, scoring stops at that tile and it contributes nothing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.BlockingPartCategories: Part categories that terminate the line, matched against the occupying part's type categories. Checked after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.BlockingPartIDs]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.ZeroScoreTilesBlock: Whether a tile whose score works out to 0 also terminates the line, in addition to the explicit blocking-part checks.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.EmptyTilesBlock: Whether a tile with no part terminates the line. When false, empty tiles contribute [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.BaseTileScoreValueRules.EmptyTileScore]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.Falloff: An exponent that fades tile scores with distance along the line. Each tile's score is multiplied by `((MaxTiles - distance) / MaxTiles) ^ Falloff`, so 0 disables the falloff and 1 fades linearly to zero at the line's full length. The same curve scales occlusion effects by hit distance and fades out the blueprint overlay line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.OcclusionCheckInterval: The time interval between each line occlusion check and subsequent application of effects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.OccludedByShields: Whether other ships' shield arcs occlude the line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.OcclusionHitEffects: The hit effects applied to other ships intersecting a line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.OcclusionContinuousMediaEffects: The media effects played when other ships intersect a line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.EffectScaleFactor: The component providing the value that the occluded score is multiplied by to calculate the effect scale.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.MediaIntensity: The value passed to media effects as intensity. Defaults to the effect scale if null.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.CustomShapeMediaEffects: Continuous media effects played while the component is operational and at least one tile is scored. The effects receive the scored stretch of the line as a custom shape and the number of scored tiles as their intensity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.CustomShapeValueSource: A value component on the same part whose value is reported when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.CustomShapeMediaEffects]] sample a random point with an associated value. Defaults to 1 when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.BlueprintMaterial: The material the line is drawn with in blueprint mode. The overlay quad covers the scored tiles, ends at the first blocking tile, and fades out along its length according to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.Falloff]]. No line is drawn when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.BlueprintLineWidthScale: A multiplier on the width of the blueprint overlay line, where 1 draws it a full tile wide. The vanilla radiator uses 0.1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.ValueTextFormatKey: A localization key whose text is drawn at the line's starting tile in blueprint mode. Format argument `{0}` receives the line score multiplied by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.TextValueScaleFactor]] and `{1}` receives the secondary value derived from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.FractionalTextValueBasis]]. No text is drawn when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.TextValueScaleFactor: A multiplier applied to the line score before it is passed as format argument `{0}` to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.ValueTextFormatKey]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.FractionalTextValueBasis: If not null, the line score as a fraction of this value is passed as a secondary text value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.FractionalTextValueScaleFactor: The value that the secondary text value is scaled by.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.T:: One line to score, given as a starting cell, a direction and how many tiles it reaches.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.Location: The tile the line starts at, in the part's unrotated rules coordinate space. Transformed with the part's rotation and flip to find the ship cell the line is walked from.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.Direction: The part-relative orthogonal direction the line extends in, transformed by the part's rotation and flip. The vanilla radiator points its dissipation line `Up`, away from the panel.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.MaxTiles: The number of tiles walked and scored along the line, which is also the full length used by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLineScoreValueRules.Falloff]]. The default of 0 scores nothing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileLine.MaxOcclusionDistance: The maximum length, in tiles from the line's start, of the occlusion raycast against other ships. The ray actually cast covers the currently scored tiles capped at this distance. A value of 0 or less disables occlusion checking for the line. The vanilla radiator caps its 120-tile line at 10.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileScor.T:: Scores the parts filling a region of tiles around the part and provides the total as a value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileScor.Region: The region that will be included in the calculations.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileScor.Falloff: An exponent that weakens tile scores with distance from the part. Each tile's score is multiplied by one minus its distance fraction across [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileScoreValueRules.Region]], raised to this power, so tiles near the region's edge contribute less. At 0, the default, every tile counts at full score.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTileScor.IncludeSelf: Counts the tiles covered by the owning part itself. By default those tiles are skipped, with the part's footprint judged by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.BaseTileScoreValueRules.PartRectType]]. The component's reported value is the sum of all counted tile scores.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.T:: Fires when `Duration` runs out, able to restart itself for a steady repeating tick.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.Duration: The countdown length in seconds. When a running timer's remaining time reaches zero it fires its trigger, and as a toggle provider the component reads on once expired. The component also acts as a value provider reporting the remaining time as a fraction of this duration, and exposes whether it is counting down under the toggle ID `IsRunning`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.AutoStart: Starts the countdown automatically the first time the component becomes operational, unless the timer has already run before.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.Repeats: Restarts the countdown immediately after each expiry, so the timer keeps firing its trigger every [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.Duration]] seconds instead of stopping after the first one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.StartTrigger: A trigger that starts the countdown. An already expired timer is first reset to the full [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.Duration]], while a stopped timer resumes with its remaining time. Has no effect while the timer is already running.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.StopTrigger: A trigger that pauses the countdown, preserving the remaining time. A later start via [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.StartTrigger]] resumes from that remaining time.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.ResetTrigger: A trigger that sets the remaining time back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.DurationAfterResetTrigger]], or the full [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.Duration]] if that is unset. Does not start or stop the countdown by itself.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.DurationAfterResetTrigger: The remaining time, in seconds, the timer is set to when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.ResetTrigger]] fires. Falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.Duration]] when unset. The vanilla overclock reset timer uses 0 so a reset expires it instantly.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.TriggerWhenStarted: Fires the timer's trigger immediately whenever the countdown is started, in addition to firing when it expires.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.StartExpired: Puts the timer into the already expired state, with zero remaining time, when it first becomes operational. Its toggle therefore reads on before the timer has ever been started. The vanilla `base_part_overclock.rules` combines this with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRules.StartTrigger]] to gate re-enabling overclock behind a cooldown.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTimerRul.InvertToggle: Inverts the timer's toggle output, so it reads on while time remains instead of once the countdown has expired.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTogglePr.T:: Stands in for a toggle component in another part, reporting `IsOnWhenNotConnected` when there is nothing to connect to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTogglePr.IsOnWhenNotConnected:
The toggle state this proxy reports while no target component is connected (default `false`).
Disconnected covers a `PartLocation` cell with no matching part, and equally a `ComponentID`
that no active component carries. The vanilla missile launcher relies on that: its
`MissilesPrereqProxy` targets a `MissilesPrereq` component that each `ToggledComponents`
missile mode must supply, so a mode that forgets it reads permanently off and the launcher's
crew stand down.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTr.T:: Fires whenever the toggle it watches switches on, off, or either way.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTr.Toggle: A toggle component on the same part that is watched. The trigger fires whenever that toggle changes state, filtered by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTriggerRules.TriggerWhenOn]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTriggerRules.TriggerWhenOff]], and only while this component is operational unless [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTriggerRules.AllowOperationalBypass]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTr.TriggerWhenOn: Whether the trigger fires when the watched toggle switches on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTr.TriggerWhenOff: Whether the trigger fires when the watched toggle switches off. With both this and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTriggerRules.TriggerWhenOn]] true, the trigger fires on every change.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleTr.AllowOperationalBypass: Whether the component can trigger without being operational, as long as it has no operational toggle, or the toggle is already true.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.T:: Provides one of two values depending on whether a toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.Toggle: The ID of the toggle component whose state selects the output. While the toggle is on the output is the value of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleValueSelectorRules.ToggleOnValue]], while off it is [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleValueSelectorRules.ToggleOffValue]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.BlueprintToggle: The toggle to use in place of Toggle for blueprints, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.ToggleOffValue: The ID of the value component whose value is output while the toggle is off. The vanilla small thruster selects between `Zero` and `One` StaticValue components this way to report its overclock state.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.ToggleOnValue: The ID of the value component whose value is output while the toggle is on. Changes of the selected component's value pass through immediately.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.IncludeInPhysical: Whether the component is created on physical in-game ships. Set to false together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleValueSelectorRules.IncludeInBlueprints]] to make a blueprint-only selector.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleVa.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether a blueprint version of the component is also created for ship blueprints. The blueprint version uses [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleValueSelectorRules.BlueprintToggle]] in place of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggleValueSelectorRules.Toggle]] when that is set.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledC.T:: Adds or removes the components nested inside it depending on a toggle, which is how a part swaps whole behaviors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledC.Toggle:
The toggle that controls whether this set's `Components` exist on the part. They are added the
moment the toggle turns on and removed when it turns off, so the part behaves as if they were
never written while inactive. Invert the reading with
[[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledComponentsRules.Invert]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledC.Invert:
Inverts [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledComponentsRules.Toggle]], so the components
exist while that toggle is off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartToggledC.IncludeInBlueprints:
Whether the sub-components are included when rendering the ship's blueprints: never (`False`),
always (`True`), or following the toggle's current state (`Dynamic`, the vanilla missile
launcher's choice so only the selected mode's visuals appear).

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.T:: Slides and turns between a start and an end pose as the value it watches moves across its range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ValueFrom: A value component on the same part whose current value drives the interpolation, with 0 giving the Start transform and 1 the End transform. The vanilla chaingun drives its `TurretSlider` from a `ValueTween` to slide the turret while changing shells.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.StartLocation: The location offset, in tiles, applied at value 0. Offsets are relative to the component's normal location and rotate with the component. Components chained to this one follow the interpolated transform. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.EndLocation: The location offset, in tiles, applied at value 1. The component's actual offset is interpolated between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformLerpRules.StartLocation]] and this as the value goes from 0 to 1. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.StartRotation: The rotation offset, in degrees, added to the component's normal rotation at value 0. While the part is not operational the component reverts to its uninterpolated transform.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.EndRotation: The rotation offset, in degrees, added at value 1. The actual offset is interpolated between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformLerpRules.StartRotation]] and this as the value goes from 0 to 1.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.T:: Chases another component's position and rotation at a limited speed, and can be sent back to rest by a toggle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.MatchTransformOf: The component on the same part whose transform this component continuously tracks while operational. Each simulation tick the component's own location and rotation move toward the target's, but only along the axes for which [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchLocationSpeed]] or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchRotationSpeed]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.MatchLocationSpeed: The speed, in tiles per second, at which the component's location moves toward the location of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchTransformOf]]. When unset, the location is not matched at all and stays at the component's own rules-defined position.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.MatchRotationSpeed: The speed, in degrees per second, at which the component's rotation turns toward the rotation of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchTransformOf]]. When unset, the rotation is not matched. The vanilla chaingun's `AimingTurretSlider` uses 100 degrees per second to follow its turret.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ResetTransformWhen: A toggle component on the same part. While its toggle is on, this component moves back toward its own rules-defined transform instead of tracking [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchTransformOf]], using [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.ResetLocationSpeed]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.ResetRotationSpeed]]. The chaingun resets its aiming slider whenever its shell is not fully open.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.InvertResetTransformWhen: Inverts the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.ResetTransformWhen]] test, so the transform resets back to its rules-defined position while that toggle is off instead of on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ResetLocationSpeed: The speed, in tiles per second, used while the location is resetting back to its rules-defined position. Falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchLocationSpeed]] when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ResetRotationSpeed: The speed, in degrees per second, used while the rotation is resetting back to its rules-defined direction. Falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.MatchRotationSpeed]] when unset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ClampLocationToRect: A rules-relative rectangle the component's location is clamped into every tick, limiting how far it can follow the matched component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ClampLocationToCircle: A rules-relative circle the component's location is clamped into every tick. Applied after [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransformMatchRules.ClampLocationToRect]] when both are set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ClampRotationToArc: An arc the component's rotation is constrained to while turning toward its target. The chaingun clamps its aiming slider to the turret's firing arc.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ToggleOnLocationThreshold: The distance, in tiles, within which the component's location counts as having caught up with its target. The component is itself a toggle provider that reads on only when both location and rotation are within their thresholds, and always off while resetting. Defaults to 0, requiring an exact match.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.ToggleOnRotationThreshold: The angular distance, in degrees, within which the component's rotation counts as having caught up with its target for the component's own toggle output. The chaingun turns its slider into an is-aimed toggle with a 2 degree threshold.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.InterpolateLocation: Smooths the matched location by interpolating between fixed simulation ticks on every rendered frame. Without it the location only jumps at the fixed tick rate.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTransfor.InterpolateRotation: Smooths the matched rotation by interpolating between fixed simulation ticks on every rendered frame. Without it the rotation only jumps at the fixed tick rate.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggerP.T:: Stands in for a trigger component in another part, passing its firing along to this part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggerP.TriggerID: The ID of a named trigger within the proxied component. When unset, the component's default trigger is relayed.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggere.T:: Switches on when one trigger fires and off when another does.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggere.OnTrigger: The trigger component that switches the toggle on, written as a component name or as a group with `ID` and an optional `TriggerID`. When [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggeredToggleRules.OffTrigger]] resolves to the same trigger, each firing flips the toggle instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggere.OffTrigger: The trigger component that switches the toggle off. The toggle also switches off whenever this component becomes non-operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartTriggere.StartsOn: The toggle state taken when the component is added to its part. The current state is saved and loaded with the ship afterwards.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.T:: Builds a value up while its toggle is on and lets it drain away again, the way heat gathers and cools.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AccumulatingToggle: The IPartComponentToggle that determines the operational state of the accumulator.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.BaseValue: The value the accumulator starts at and moves towards when toggle off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AccumulationRate: The rate at which the value accumulates when toggled on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.DissipationRate: The rate at which the value moves towards BaseValue when toggled off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.NonOperationalBehaviour: The accumulator's behaviour while it is non-operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.MinValue: The lowest value that the accumulator can reach.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.MaxValue: The highest value that the accumulator can reach.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.T:: One trigger that changes the accumulated value, with the amount, the operation and the states in which it may apply.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.Trigger: The IPartComponentTrigger that triggers this accumulation instance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.Value: The value to use for accumulating, dissipating, or setting on being triggered.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.Operation: Whether this trigger acts as accumulation, dissipation, or directly sets the value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AllowWhenOn: Whether this trigger activates when the accumulator is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AllowWhenOff: Whether this trigger activates when the accumulator is off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AllowWhenOperational: Whether this trigger activates when the accumulator is operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueAcc.AllowWhenNonOperational: Whether this trigger activates when the accumulator is non-operational.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueCha.T:: Fires when a watched value moves and provides the size of that change as its own value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueCha.ValueSource: The watched value component. Whenever its value changes the trigger fires, and this component's own value becomes the change delta, new value minus old. Written either as a bare component ID or as a group with `ID` and an optional `ValueID`, and changes are only observed while the component is operational.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueCha.TriggerOnIncrease: Whether increases of the source value fire the trigger. A filtered-out change neither fires nor updates the exposed delta value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueCha.TriggerOnDecrease: Whether decreases of the source value fire the trigger.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.T:: Remaps a value from an input range onto an output range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.InputValue: The ID of the value component whose value is remapped. The output is recomputed whenever the input changes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.InputRange: The input span mapped from. The input's position between the range's Min and Max yields the interpolation fraction. Defaults to 0 to 1, and both ends accept buff modifiers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.OutputRange: The output span mapped onto. The interpolation fraction from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLerpRules.InputRange]] picks the output linearly between the range's Min and Max. Defaults to 0 to 1, both ends accept buff modifiers, and Min may be larger than Max to reverse the mapping, as the vanilla tractor beam does with `OutputRange = [10, 1]` to fade its overload charging effects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.ClampInput: Clamps the interpolation fraction to 0..1, so inputs outside [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLerpRules.InputRange]] pin to its ends. Set to false to extrapolate the fraction beyond the range instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLer.ClampOutput: Clamps the result to stay within [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLerpRules.OutputRange]]. Set to false to allow extrapolated results outside it, which only matters when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueLerpRules.ClampInput]] is also false.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.T:: Divides, subtracts, raises to a power or takes the modulo of two values and provides the result.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.Operator: The math operation applied to the two inputs. `Divide` outputs [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOperationRules.ValueOne]] divided by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOperationRules.ValueTwo]], `Power` raises ValueOne to the power of ValueTwo, `Modulo` outputs the remainder of dividing ValueOne by ValueTwo, and `Subtract` outputs ValueOne minus ValueTwo.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.ValueOne: The value component providing the first input. Written either as a bare component ID or as a group with `ID` and an optional `ValueID` naming a specific sub-value of that component. The result is recomputed whenever either input changes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.ValueTwo: The value component providing the second input, in the same form as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOperationRules.ValueOne]]. The vanilla small thruster divides its thruster activation by a `BuffableValue` holding the maximum activation to get a normalized 0..1 activation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.MinValue: The lower bound the operation's result is clamped to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.MaxValue: The upper bound the operation's result is clamped to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.NaNFallbackValue: The value substituted when the operation produces NaN, such as dividing zero by zero. Defaults to 0. The fallback is still clamped between [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOperationRules.MinValue]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOperationRules.MaxValue]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueOpe.IncludeInBlueprints: Whether a blueprint version of this component is also created for ship blueprints. `None` creates none, `Normal` includes it in regular blueprint updates, and `All` additionally includes it in lightweight blueprint validity checks. `false` and `true` are accepted as aliases for `None` and `Normal`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValuePro.T:: Stands in for a value component in another part, reporting `ValueWhenNotConnected` when there is nothing to connect to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValuePro.ValueWhenNotConnected: The value the proxy reports while it is not connected to a value component on another part. Defaults to 0.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.T:: Eases its value between `OffValue` and `OnValue` whenever a toggle flips, over the tween duration given for that direction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.IsOnToggle: The ID of the toggle component that drives the tween. While the toggle is on the value moves linearly toward [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OnValue]], while off it moves toward [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OffValue]]. The tween only advances while the component is operational, and without a toggle the value never changes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.OffValue: The value the tween moves toward while the toggle is off. Defaults to 0.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.OnValue: The value the tween moves toward while the toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.StartingValue: The value the component starts at when the part is newly created. When unset it starts at [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OnValue]] or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OffValue]] depending on the toggle's initial state.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.OnTweenDuration: How long, in seconds, the value takes to move all the way from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OffValue]] to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OnValue]] after the toggle turns on. The vanilla `base_part_overclock.rules` tweens its overclock state on over 1 second and back off over 0.1 seconds.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTwe.OffTweenDuration: How long, in seconds, the value takes to move all the way from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OnValue]] back to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.PartValueTweenRules.OffValue]] after the toggle turns off.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.T:: The block every proxy component writes to say which component it stands in for and which neighboring part holds it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.PartLocation:
The cell, in this part's rules coordinates, whose occupying part is proxied. Rotation and flip
of the placed part are applied, and the proxy reconnects automatically as parts are built or
destroyed on that cell. When omitted, the proxy targets a component of its own part instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.ProxyToggle:
A toggle of this part that gates the proxy connection. While it is off the proxy disconnects
entirely, as if the target did not exist. Invert the reading with
[[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.InvertProxyToggle]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.InvertProxyToggle:
Inverts [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.ProxyToggle]], so the proxy connects while
that toggle is off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules.ProxyableComponents:
The candidate targets, checked in order against the proxied part. The first entry whose
`PartCriteria` matches (or that has none) wins, and its `ComponentID` names the component to
mirror. The flat `ComponentID = …` spelling on the proxy is the one-entry shorthand for this
list.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules/P.T:: One candidate a proxy may connect to, a component id plus optional criteria the other part has to meet.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules/P.PartCriteria:
A filter the candidate part must match (part id, categories, ownership relative to this part)
before this entry's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules+ProxyableComponent.ComponentID]]
is proxied. An entry without criteria matches any part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ProxyRules/P.ComponentID:
The id of the component to mirror in the targeted part. The connection is live: if the
component does not exist yet (a `ToggledComponents` mode that is switched off, a part still
under construction), the proxy waits and connects the moment a component with this id
appears, and disconnects again when it is removed.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ShipConstruc.T:: On while the ship has building work queued, optionally ignoring plain repairs.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.ShipConstruc.IgnoreRepairs: Excludes queued repairs, so the toggle is on only while the ship has non-repair construction operations queued. The vanilla overclock base part sets this true and pairs the toggle with a ToggleTrigger that fires when construction ends.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.T:: Replaces the part with a different part when triggered, carrying health and resources across if asked.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.Trigger: The trigger that performs the swap. When it fires, the current part is removed from the ship and replaced by a freshly created [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPartSwapRules.NewPartID]] part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.NewPartID: The part that replaces this one when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPartSwapRules.Trigger]] fires. The ID must exist in the ship's part list or the game raises an error at swap time.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.NewPartLocation: The tile location of the replacement part in the old part's unrotated rules coordinate space. Together with the new part's size it is transformed through the old part's location, rotation and flip to place the new part on the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.NewPartRotation: The rotation of the new part in 90 degree steps, added on top of the old part's rotation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.NewPartFlip: Whether the new part is mirrored relative to the old part, so a flipped old part produces an unflipped replacement and vice versa.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.InheritHealthFraction: Multiplies the new part's spawn health by the old part's current health fraction, on top of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPartSwapRules.NewPartHealthFraction]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.NewPartHealthFraction: The fraction of maximum health the replacement part spawns with. Defaults to 1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.CrewAction: What happens to crew inside the old part when it is removed. `None` takes no action, `Delete` removes them without effects, `Kill` kills them with effects, `Reset` sends them back to their quarters or deletes them if they have none, `Eject` converts them to crew floating in space, and `EjectWithKillChance` ejects them with a chance of killing each one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.TriggeredPar.InheritResources: Transfers the resources stored in the old part's storages into the new part's storages of matching resource types, capped at their capacity. Any surplus is lost.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.UIToggleMode.T:: Forces a player-facing toggle into `TargetMode` on one trigger and hands control back on another.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.UIToggleMode.TargetUIToggle: The ID of the PartUIToggle to override.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.UIToggleMode.TargetMode: The mode to set the TargetUIToggle to when overridden.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.UIToggleMode.OverrideTrigger: The ID of the component that will trigger the override.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Logic.UIToggleMode.ResetTrigger: The ID of the component that will end the override, returning the toggle to its previous value.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalChainab.T:: Shared setup for chainable components that only run while their operational toggle is on. A modder writes one of the concrete types.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalChainab.OperationalToggle: A toggle component on the same part that gates whether this component operates. The component is operational only while the part is active and the toggle reads on. When unset, the component operates whenever the part is active. Behaves exactly like [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartComponentRules.OperationalToggle]], on a component that can also be chained.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalChainab.InvertOperationalToggle: Reverses the reading of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalChainablePartComponentRules.OperationalToggle]], so the component operates while the toggle is off and shuts down while it is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalChainab.DisableWhenDeconstructing: Makes the component non-operational while its part is queued for deconstruction. It resumes operating if the deconstruction order is cancelled.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartCom.T:: Shared setup for components that only run while their operational toggle is on. A modder writes one of the concrete types.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartCom.OperationalToggle: A toggle component on the same part that gates whether this component operates. The component is operational only while the part is active and the toggle reads on. When unset, the component operates whenever the part is active. Vanilla parts typically point this at an `IsOperational` toggle chain combining power, crew, and mode conditions.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartCom.InvertOperationalToggle: Reverses the reading of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartComponentRules.OperationalToggle]], so the component operates while the toggle is off and shuts down while it is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.OperationalPartCom.DisableWhenDeconstructing: Makes the component non-operational while its part is queued for deconstruction. It resumes operating if the deconstruction order is cancelled.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.PartOverl.T:: Shared setup for the overlays drawn over a part while it or its ship is selected. A modder writes `WeaponTargetOverlay`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.PartOverl.RenderWhenPartSelected: Whether this overlay draws while its own part is individually selected.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.PartOverl.RenderWhenShipSelected: Whether this overlay draws while its whole ship is selected. When individual parts are selected instead, only the overlays of those parts draw.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTar.T:: Draws a marker on the weapon's current target and a line running out to it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTar.Weapon: The weapon component on the same part whose current target this overlay marks. Must be a turret weapon.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTar.TargetSprite: A sprite drawn centered on the weapon's current target while the overlay renders. Its base size, in tiles, comes from the sprite's own `Size`, scaled with the camera zoom according to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTargetOverlayRules.CameraScaleExponent]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTar.CameraScaleExponent: The exponent applied to the camera's zoom scale when sizing [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTargetOverlayRules.TargetSprite]]. At 0, the default, the sprite keeps a constant world-space size, while 1 makes it grow as the camera zooms out so it keeps a roughly constant on-screen size.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Overlays.WeaponTar.TargetLineColor: The color of a straight line drawn from the weapon to its target's center, rendered in the underlay pass beneath the target sprite. Defaults to fully transparent, which disables the line, so drawing it requires an alpha above 0.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.T:: Everything a part actually does lives in one of these components, written under the part's `Components` group.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.OnlyWithRotation: Restricts the component to one part rotation (0 to 3 quarter turns). At any other rotation the component is simply not created, which also applies to its blueprint and destroyed-part forms. Combine several rotation-locked components to give a part different behavior or graphics per orientation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.OnlyWithFlip: Restricts the component to one horizontal-flip state of the part, so it only exists when the part's flip matches. The vanilla tri-steel factory declares a `FloorSprite` with `OnlyWithFlip = false` and a mirrored `FloorSpriteFlipped` with `OnlyWithFlip = true`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.IncludeWhenUnderConstruction: Whether the component is also created while the part is an unfinished construction site. Off by default, though collider and death-effect components force it on in code. Vanilla `base_part_terran.rules` enables it, with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.IncludeWhenNotUnderConstruction]] set to false, for its construction scaffolding sprites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.IncludeWhenNotUnderConstruction: Whether the component is created on the finished part. Setting this to false while enabling [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.IncludeWhenUnderConstruction]] makes a construction-site-only component, such as the vanilla scaffolding and construction progress sprites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartComponentRules.BlueprintSortOrder: Specifies the ordering of DrawBlueprintData@) relative to other components on the part. Declaration order is used to break ties.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.T:: One buildable part, covering its size, health, build cost, walls, crew and the components that give it behavior.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.NameKey: The part's name, displayed when it is selected or hovered over.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IconNameKey: The part name as it shows up in the ship editor's menus.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.JobsNameKey: The part's display name in the crew jobs UI (the role edit window). When omitted, [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.NameKey]] is shown instead. Vanilla crew quarters use it to show a generic job name like "General".
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ID: Game-wide unique ID of the part. Must start with the author's name.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.OtherIDs: Alternate part identifiers this part also answers to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FlipWhenLoadingIDs: Part IDs that trigger flipping when the ship is loaded.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DontStackInEditorGroups: Editor tabs in which this part's sub-parts (see [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.EditorParentParts]]) are not collapsed into one stacked palette button. In the listed groups the part gets a plain button of its own. Vanilla armor uses this to appear un-stacked in the Structure tab.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.EditorParentParts: The IDs of parts that will contain this part as a 'sub-part' within the ship editor.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DefaultEditorHotkey: The default key binding that selects this part for placement in the ship editor. Listing more than one key makes a key combination, e.g. `[PlatformCmdCtrl, B]`, while most parts use a single key like `[Z]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.EditorReplacementPartID: The part automatically placed into each vacated cell when this part is deleted or built over in the ship editor. Inherited as `corridor` from `base_part.rules`. Setting it to `""` leaves the cells empty, which vanilla armor wedges do.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DescriptionKey: Descriptive text shown in the part's tooltip, below the name and cost line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Resources: Resource name and cost pairs defining what the part costs to build.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsBuildable: If false, the part cannot be built.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FractionalCostToRepair: How much of the build cost, at most, is spent to repair the part to full health.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Size: The width and height of the part, in tiles.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.PhysicalRect: The sub-rectangle of the part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Size]] footprint that is physically solid, as `[x, y, width, height]` in tiles from the part's un-rotated top-left. Only these cells collide, carry mass and hull walls, and connect to neighboring parts. The remaining cells are non-solid overhang, which vanilla weapons and thrusters use for barrels and nozzles, e.g. the medium cannon's `[0, 1, 2, 1]`. Must lie within the part's size rect.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SaveRect: Shifts the part's origin in saved ship files: the location written to and read from saves is offset by this rect's top-left instead of using the part's own top-left. Keeps previously saved ships loading correctly when a part's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Size]] or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.PhysicalRect]] changes. Vanilla weapons and thrusters typically set `SaveRect = &PhysicalRect`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AllowedContiguity: The edges of the part that count as structural connections to neighboring parts when the game determines ship contiguity. A connection exists only if both parts allow the shared edge, and directions are in the part's un-rotated orientation. Wedge parts restrict this so their empty diagonal side does not connect, e.g. vanilla `armor_wedge` uses `[Right, Bottom]`. Any value other than `Sides` also makes the part incompatible with the editor's brush tools unless [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ForceBrushCompatibility]] says otherwise.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.GenerateRectCollider: Whether the part gets an automatic rectangular collider spanning its [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.RectColliderRectType]] rect, which also provides its physics cells and mass. Set to false for parts with a custom `PolygonCollider` component, as vanilla wedge and triangle parts do.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.RectColliderRectType: Which rect the automatic collider spans. `Normal` covers the full [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Size]] footprint, `Physical` only the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.PhysicalRect]]. Ignored when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.GenerateRectCollider]] is false.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BoundingRectType: Which rect contributes the part's corner points to the ship's overall bounding circle. `Normal` uses the full [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Size]] footprint, `Physical` uses the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.PhysicalRect]]. Vanilla thrusters use `Physical` so their non-solid nozzle overhang does not inflate the ship's bounds.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.PartNetworkOverlayMidpoint: The point where the blueprint resource-network overlay's route lines converge on this part, in tiles from the part's top-left corner. When omitted, the center of the part's rect is used.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CellOccupancyFactor: The value by which to multiply the calculated collider occupancy value of cells within the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SelectionPriority: Determines selection ordering when parts overlap.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SelectionTypeID: Part ID used to group parts together for selection.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SelectionTypeByRotation: If true, double-clicking the part in-game only selects parts of the same type facing the same direction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SelectionTypeRotations: Rotation offsets treated as equivalent when double-click selecting parts of the same type with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SelectionTypeByRotation]]. Two parts match if any pair of listed offsets brings their rotations to the same value modulo 4. Vanilla's 2-way small thruster uses `[0, 3]` so both orientations of the same placement select together.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IgnoreRotationForMirroredSelection: If true, mirror selection in the ship editor matches the mirrored counterpart by part type and occupied cells only, ignoring rotation and flip. Set on rotationally symmetric parts like armor, corridors and storages, whose mirrored copy may be stored with a different rotation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Density: How much one tile of the part weighs, in tons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxHealth: How much damage the part can endure before being destroyed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.HealthType: The part's health category. See the HealthTypes reference.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionWork: Total crew-seconds of work needed to build the part. When omitted, it is derived from health as the ship's `DefaultConstructionWorkPerHealth` times [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxHealth]], which in vanilla works out to one second per corridor tile.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionSwapDelay: Seconds to wait after construction reaches 100% before the under-construction placeholder is swapped for the finished part. Vanilla Terran parts use `0.2`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.WorkPerRepairedHealth: Crew-seconds of work needed to restore one point of health when repairing the part. When omitted, the ship's `DefaultWorkPerRepairedHealth` is used.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SalvageProgressMediaEffects: Continuous visual and sound effects played at the part while it is being salvaged, with intensity rising as salvage progresses.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SalvageProgressMediaEffectsTimeout: Seconds after the last salvage progress before [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SalvageProgressMediaEffects]] stop playing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionProgressMediaEffects: Continuous visual and sound effects played at the part while it is being constructed, with intensity rising as construction progresses.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionProgressMediaEffectsTimeout: Seconds after the last construction progress before [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionProgressMediaEffects]] stop playing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionFinishedMediaEffects: One-shot effects played when construction of the part completes, just before the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ConstructionSwapDelay]] swap to the finished part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExplosiveDamageAbsorption: The fraction (`0..1`) of an explosion's remaining damage this part can absorb, soaking the blast and shielding parts behind it. The range interpolates from the first value at full health to the second when nearly destroyed. Inherited as `50%` from `base_part.rules`, and vanilla armor uses `100%`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DamageResistances: Per damage type, the fraction of incoming damage removed before it is applied: the part takes `damage * (1 - resistance)`, so `50%` halves the damage and negative values amplify it. Each range interpolates from the first value at full health to the second when nearly destroyed, and unlisted damage types have zero resistance. Vanilla armor uses `explosive = 50%` and `thermal = -25%`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.StatusResistances: The part's base resistances to status types, interpolated by the current DamageFraction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPart: Part that underlies this part and spawns in its place when it is destroyed, one instance covering the whole footprint. The underlying part's resources and cost are deducted from this part's, so it only pays the difference. Also readable as `CreatePartWhenDestroyed`. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPartPerTile]] for the per-tile variant and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CreateUnderlyingWhenDestroyed]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPartPerTile: Per-tile variant of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPart]]: one copy of the referenced part per physical tile spawns when this part is destroyed, and its cost per tile is deducted from this part's cost. Also readable as `CreatePartPerTileWhenDestroyed`. Inherited as `structure` from `base_part.rules`, so destroyed vanilla parts leave structure behind.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CreateUnderlyingWhenDestroyed: If false, the underlying part (see [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPart]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPartPerTile]]) only appears when this part is removed by salvage, not when it is destroyed in combat.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.TempConstructionPartPerTile: Part temporarily placed on each physical tile as scaffolding while this part is under construction, removed when the finished part is swapped in. Vanilla structure wedges use a full `structure` tile per cell.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CreatePartPerTileWhenGrabbed: Part placed on each physical tile when this part is grabbed (picked up or moved) in the ship editor. Inherited as `corridor` from `base_part.rules`, and vanilla armor sets `""` so grabbing it leaves nothing behind.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DestroyedPartHealthFraction: The fraction of its max health the spawned underlying part starts with when this part is destroyed in combat, with salvage progress pulling the value toward full. Inherited as `50%` from `base_part.rules`. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.UnderlyingPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewKillChanceWhenDestroyed: Chance (`0..1`) that each crew member inside the part is killed when the part is destroyed. Survivors are ejected into space at [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewThrowSpeedWhenDestroyed]]. Inherited as `25%` from `base_part.rules`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewThrowSpeedWhenDestroyed: Speed added in a random direction to surviving crew ejected into space when the part is destroyed. Inherited as `10` from `base_part.rules`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InitialPenetrationResistance: How much of a penetrating projectile's remaining penetration budget is consumed when it first breaches the part through a wall. The range interpolates from the first value at full health to the second when nearly destroyed. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ContinuingPenetrationResistance]] for travel after the breach. Vanilla armor uses `7` versus the base part's `1`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ContinuingPenetrationResistance: How much of a penetrating projectile's remaining penetration budget is consumed while it continues through the part after the initial breach. The range interpolates from the first value at full health to the second when nearly destroyed. Usually lower than [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InitialPenetrationResistance]], e.g. `.5` versus `1` in `base_part.rules`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewSpeedFactor: The speed at which crew move within the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewCongestedSpeedFactor: The speed at which crew move within the part while passing other crew.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.CrewMinimumSpeedFactor: The minimum values to multiply crew speed by within the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FireDamageFactor: Has no effect. The game stores the value but no code ever reads it, so it does not scale the damage fire deals to the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsCrewSalvageable: Whether crew can salvage the part by walking up to it. If false, the part can only be salvaged with salvage weapons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.HasNonContiguousPathing: Set to true if some tiles of the part cannot be walked across by crew in a given direction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlockedTravelCells: Cells of the part, counted from its un-rotated top-left, that crew can never stand on or walk through. Usually paired with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.HasNonContiguousPathing]] so the remaining cells form separate walkable islands. Vanilla large weapons use it to keep crew out of the mechanism.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlockedTravelCellDirections: Per-cell directional travel blocks. Each `Key` is a cell of the part (un-rotated, from the top-left) and each `Value` lists the directions crew may not move while in that cell, so unlike [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlockedTravelCells]] the other directions stay open. Directions rotate and flip with the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ForceManhattanPathInPart: If true, crew heading to a specific spot inside the part must path all the way to that exact cell instead of stopping at the first reachable cell of the part. Vanilla pairs it with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlockedTravelCells]] on large weapons to funnel crew along a fixed interior route.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ProhibitRects: Rectangular keep-out zones the part projects, each a category plus an `[x, y, width, height]` rect in tiles from the part's un-rotated top-left, typically extending outside its footprint. Parts listing the category in their [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ProhibitedBy]] cannot be placed or built inside the zone. The zones rotate and flip with the part, and the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Prohibits]] shorthands generate entries here.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ProhibitedBy: The prohibit categories this part respects: it cannot be placed or built where another part projects a keep-out zone (see [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ProhibitRects]]) of a listed category. This is a hard placement block, not a warning. Inherited as `[default]` from `base_part.rules`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ContiguityOriginPriority: When a ship breaks into disconnected pieces, the piece containing the highest-priority part is kept as the surviving origin ship, with ties broken by largest total area. Vanilla control rooms set 1 to 3 by size so the piece holding the best control room stays the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsExternal: If false, the part must have either no doors to anything else or only doors with legal placement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsRotateable: Whether the part can be rotated during placement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsFlippable: Whether the part can be flipped during placement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsWalled: If false, the part can only have doors to parts that are themselves not walled.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsSelfDestructible: Whether the ship's self-destruct command destroys this part. Vanilla armor sets it to false, so plating survives a self-destruct.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.IsLowPriorityDeconstruction: If true, crew only deconstruct this part when no other construction, repair or normal deconstruction job needs doing. Vanilla airlocks set it so they are removed last.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ForceBrushCompatibility: Overrides whether the part can be drawn with the editor's line, rectangle and fill brush tools. When omitted, a part qualifies automatically if it is 1x1, has [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AllowedContiguity]] `Sides`, and its [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AllowedDoorLocations]] is unset or empty.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AllowedDoorLocations: Cells just outside the part, in un-rotated coordinates from its top-left, that doors to this part may connect to. For example a 1x1 airlock lists `[0, 1]`, the cell directly below it. Omitting the field allows doors on every side-adjacent cell, while an empty list `[]` forbids doors entirely, as vanilla armor and structure do.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxDoors: The maximum number of doors that may border the part, enforced both when placing doors manually and by the automatic door generator. The default means no limit.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.GeneratorRequiresDoor: If true, the procedural ship generator only places the part where at least one door can be created for it, so generated crew-operated parts are never sealed off. Inherited as true from `base_part.rules`, with armor and structure turning it off.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AutoDoorMaxPathLength: Radius, in walkable interior cells, within which the automatic door generator will not add another door near an existing one on this part. Inherited as `6` from `base_part.rules`. `0` lets auto-doors be placed as densely as possible.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.NoAutoDoors: Excludes the part from automatic door creation, both as a source and as a target, and also suppresses the door-access warning. Doors can still be placed manually.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.DoorAccessWarningLevel: How the ship editor warns when crew have no walkable path from this part to the ship exterior. `Strong` shows the full no-access warning, `Weak` a softer variant, and `None` skips the check. Purely a warning, it never blocks building.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWalls: The sides of the part that count as solid hull. A wall sprite renders against each listed side from the neighboring cell whenever that cell is empty space or an open side of another part (see [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWalls]]). Directions are in the part's un-rotated orientation and rotate and flip with it. Inherited as `[All]` from `base_part.rules`, so a part that says nothing is walled on every side.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlueprintExternalWalls: The blueprint-view counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWalls]]. When omitted, the blueprint uses `ExternalWalls`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWallsByCell: Per-cell override of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWalls]] for multi-cell parts. Each `Key` is a cell of the part (`[0, 0]` is the top-left cell) and each `Value` lists the sides of that cell that count as solid hull, with `[]` meaning no walls there. Cells without an entry keep the whole-part `ExternalWalls` value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlueprintExternalWallsByCell: The blueprint-view counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWallsByCell]]. When omitted, the blueprint uses `ExternalWallsByCell`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWalls: The sides of the part's cells that are visually open, so a wall may render inside this part's own cell along them. A wall appears on a listed side only when the neighbor on that side declares the shared edge solid via its [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWalls]]. Inherited as `[None]` from `base_part.rules` (fully enclosed room). Angled armor lists its open wedge sides here, and open-platform structure uses `[All]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlueprintInternalWalls: The blueprint-view counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWalls]]. When omitted, the blueprint uses `InternalWalls`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWallsByCell: Per-cell override of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWalls]] for multi-cell parts, in the same `Key`/`Value` form as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ExternalWallsByCell]]. Cells without an entry keep the whole-part `InternalWalls` value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.BlueprintInternalWallsByCell: The blueprint-view counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.InternalWallsByCell]]. When omitted, the blueprint uses `InternalWallsByCell`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.VirtualInternalCells: Pairs of `ExternalCell`/`InternalCell` (in un-rotated cells relative to the part) that make the wall renderers treat [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.VirtualInternalCell.InternalCell]] as solid walled hull interior when evaluated from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.VirtualInternalCell.ExternalCell]], so exterior hull walls wrap correctly around a sloped part's diagonal face. Vanilla wedge armor and structure use it to merge visually with their diagonal neighbor. Ignored while the part is under construction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.TypeCategories: Part-category identifiers used to classify the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.RequiresCategories: Part categories of which the ship must contain at least one part, otherwise this part is flagged invalid in the ship editor and blueprint. Provider parts list the dependent categories in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AffectsValidityOfCategories]] so the flag updates promptly.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AffectsValidityOfCategories: Part categories whose members get their validity re-checked whenever this part is added or removed. Set on parts that other parts depend on through [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.RequiresCategories]], so their invalid markers update immediately.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SignificanceToggle: ID of the IPartComponentToggle that determines whether this part should be considered for determining ship 'significance'.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.EditorIcon: The icon that represents the part on build-palette buttons and in other UI such as the parts card and the jobs window. This is a UI image only, not the in-world sprite.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.JobsIcon: Sprite shown for the part's job assignments.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FlipHRotate: The rotation mapping applied when the part is flipped horizontally.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FlipVRotate: The rotation mapping applied when the part is flipped vertically.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.AIValueFactor: How much the AI wants to destroy this part on ships it considers enemies.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.ReceivableBuffs: The buff types this part can receive from buff-providing parts, with received values clamped by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MinBuffValues]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxBuffValues]]. Vanilla thrusters list `Engine` and related buffs, and an empty list `[]` disables buff reception.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MinBuffValues: Per-buff minimum values this part clamps received buffs to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.MaxBuffValues: Per-buff maximum values this part clamps received buffs to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Stats: Stat lines shown in the part's stats tooltip. Each entry maps a stat ID to the number (or numbers) substituted into that stat's localized format string, so units and meaning come from the stat definition, not from this field. Lines render in the order the stats are declared game-wide, and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.StatsByCategory]] can group further lines under headings.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Features: Feature tags listed under the "Features" header of the part's stats tooltip. Each ID resolves to a localized label from the game-wide part-feature list, falling back to the raw ID string.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.StatsByCategory: Groups of stat lines rendered under their own named heading in the part's stats tooltip, after the top-level [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Stats]]. Each entry holds a `NameKey`, a `Stats` map and optional `Features`, which vanilla uses for example to show one block per firing mode of the cannon deck.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.StatsNotesKey: Footnote text appended at the very bottom of the part's stats tooltip, after all [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.Stats]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.StatsByCategory]] lines.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.SecondaryToolTip: An extra tooltip panel with its own title, description, stats and features, shown next to the main part tooltip when the player has secondary tooltips enabled in the settings. Vanilla's cannon deck uses it for a second stats block.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.FractionalNonPlayerRefund: The fraction of the part's cost refunded when a non-player ship sells or refunds it in Career mode. The player always gets the full cost back. Inherited as 25% from `base_part.rules`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.PartRules.EditorGroups: The names of the ship-editor tabs the part appears in.
