While the toggle is on, those effects are applied in addition to the normal ones.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.Duration: Seconds the beam stays on after each trigger. Triggering again while emitting extends the emission back up to this duration, so a repeatedly fired beam becomes continuous. At 0, the default, the beam is instantaneous and applies its hit effects once per shot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.HitInterval: Seconds between successive applications of the beam's hit effects while a continuous beam is emitting. Only meaningful when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.Duration]] is greater than 0.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.KeepLengthWhenHitNothing: Keeps the beam at its previous length when it stops hitting anything, instead of instantly extending to full range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ResourceUsageScaleOverRange: Multiplier on the emitter's resource usage, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam's current length goes from 0 to full range. Defaults to a constant 1. [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.InvertRangeScaling]] reverses the direction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.HitEffectsScaleOverRange: Multiplier on the scale of all hit effects, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam's current length goes from 0 to full range. The vanilla ion beam uses `[1, 80%]` to deal reduced damage at long range. Defaults to a constant 1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ValueOverRange: Multiplier on the value this emitter reports to other components (for example through a `MultiValue`), interpolated from Min to Max as the beam's current length goes from 0 to full range. Defaults to a constant 1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.MediaEffectsScaleOverRange: Multiplier on the intensity of the beam's media effects, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam's current length goes from 0 to full range. Defaults to a constant 1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ResourceUsageScaleOverRampUp: Multiplier on the emitter's resource usage, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam ramps up over [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.RampUpTime]]. Defaults to `[0, 1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.HitEffectsScaleOverRampUp: Multiplier on the scale of all hit effects, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam ramps up over [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.RampUpTime]]. Defaults to `[0, 1]`, so damage fades in during ramp-up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ValueOverRampUp: Multiplier on the value this emitter reports to other components, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam ramps up over [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.RampUpTime]]. Defaults to `[0, 1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.MediaEffectsScaleOverRampUp: Multiplier on the intensity of the beam's media effects, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam ramps up over [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.RampUpTime]]. Defaults to `[0, 1]`, so the visuals fade in during ramp-up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.InvertRangeScaling: Reverses the interpolation of the four OverRange scaling fields, so their Min applies at full beam length and their Max at zero length.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.EffectsScaleFactor: A value component on the same part whose current value is used as the beam's effect scale, feeding every modifiable with an `EffectScaleExponent` such as hit damage, spread, and media effect intensity. The vanilla ion beam prism points this at its stored ion energy so beam power tracks accumulated energy.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ValueScaleFactor: A value component on the same part whose current value multiplies the value this emitter reports to other components, together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ValueOverRange]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ValueOverRampUp]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.UpdateScaleFactorsPerEmit: When true, [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.EffectsScaleFactor]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ValueScaleFactor]] are sampled only at the moment the beam emits. When false, the default, they are re-read every tick while a continuous beam is firing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.RampUpTime: Seconds for the beam to ramp up to full strength after it starts firing. While ramping, the four OverRampUp scaling fields interpolate from their Min to their Max. At 0, the default, the beam is always at full ramp-up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.RequireHitForRampUp: Makes ramp-up count only time spent actually hitting something. The ramp starts at the first hit and drains back down over the same time span once the beam stops hitting, as used by the vanilla tractor beam.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.InitHitLengthResetDelay: Seconds after the beam loses its hit during which its initial hit length is remembered and the emission is kept alive, letting the beam re-acquire the target. While remembered, [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.StretchRange]] continues to apply.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.BeamMediaEffects: The media effects that render the beam itself, played continuously while a continuous beam is on or as a one-shot for instantaneous beams. Their beam length parameter follows the beam's actual length plus [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.BeamMediaEffectsLengthOffset]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.BeamMediaEffectsOffset: The offset, in tiles relative to the anchoring component, at which [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.BeamMediaEffects]] are attached. The vanilla manipulator beam uses this to start the visual at its muzzle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.BeamMediaEffectsIntensity: Multiplier on the intensity of the beam, start, and end media effects, on top of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.MediaEffectsScaleOverRange]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.MediaEffectsScaleOverRampUp]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.AttachBeamMediaEffectsTo: A component on the same part that the beam media effects anchor to instead of the emitter itself. The vanilla ion beam prism attaches them to its interpolated turret so the visual follows the turret's rendered rotation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ColorRed: The red channel of a tint applied to all of the beam's media effects. Channels left unset default to 1, and setting any of the four channels enables the custom tint. Being modifiable, it can be driven by buffs, as the vanilla resonance beam does with its thermal buffs.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ColorGreen: The green channel of the beam's media effect tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ColorRed]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ColorBlue: The blue channel of the beam's media effect tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ColorRed]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ColorAlpha: The alpha channel of the beam's media effect tint. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.ColorRed]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.BeamMediaEffectsLengthOffset: A distance, in tiles, added to the beam's actual length when setting the visual beam length. Negative values shorten the visual, as the vanilla manipulator beam does to compensate for its muzzle offset.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.Spread: A random angular deviation added to the beam's aim direction, rolled between Min and Max each time the beam updates. Angles are written with a `d` suffix for degrees, for example `[-1.5d, 1.5d]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.PelletSpread: An extra angular deviation applied per pellet when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.Pellets]] emits more than one, rolled between Min and Max for each pellet. With [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.EvenPelletSpread]] the pellets are spaced across the range instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.EvenPelletSpread: Spaces the pellets evenly across the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitterRules.PelletSpread]] range instead of rolling each pellet's angle at random.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.StartMediaEffects: One-shot media effects played when a continuous beam starts emitting, such as the vanilla tractor beam's start sound.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.EndMediaEffects: One-shot media effects played when a continuous beam stops emitting.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.T:: What the beam does to one kind of thing it strikes, with a second set of effects for when the emitter's conditional toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ConditionalHitEffects: Hit effects performed only when the ConditionalEffectToggle is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamEmitte.ConditionalMediaEffects: Media effects played only when the ConditionalEffectToggle is true.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.T:: Turns the length of a beam into a value, which is how a beam reacts to how far away it hit.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.Emitter: The beam-emitting component on the same part whose current beam length this regulator measures. A `BeamEmitterProxy` also qualifies, which the vanilla tractor beam uses so all of its mode-specific regulators read the same emitter.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.BeamLengthRange: The span of beam lengths, in tiles, that is mapped onto [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegulatorRules.OutputValueRange]]. The beam's current length is located within this span and the output interpolates accordingly, clamping at both ends. Min and Max are modifiable, so buffs can shift them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.RelativeToInitHitLength: Measures the beam length relative to the length at which the beam first hit its current target, so the output tracks how far the target has drifted since being caught. While the beam is not hitting anything the output is 0. The vanilla tractor beam's hold mode combines this with a symmetric `[-Range, Range]` length span to pull or push the target back toward its capture distance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.OutputValueRange: The value span this component reports to other components, interpolated from Min to Max as the beam length moves across [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegulatorRules.BeamLengthRange]]. A beam length of 0 always yields an output of 0. Min and Max are modifiable, and the vanilla tractor beam maps pull mode to `[.1, 1]` and push mode to `[-1, -.1]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BeamRegula.AutoClearTargetOf: A weapon component on the same part whose confirmed explicit target is cleared automatically when the beam loses contact, meaning its initial-hit length drops back to zero. No vanilla part uses this.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.T:: Fires the bullet described in `Bullet`, with spread and pellet counts for shotgun-style shots.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.Bullet: The bullet this emitter spawns each shot. Its [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.BulletRules.Range]] also serves as the weapon's maximum and ideal attack range for the ship AI.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.TargetLeadPrediction: Leads the target when aiming, using the bullet's speed (the average of Min and Max for ranged speeds), the target's motion, and the firing ship's own velocity. When false the emitter aims straight at the target's center, as the vanilla missile launchers do since their missiles steer themselves.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.Spread: A random angular deviation added to the shot's direction, rolled between Min and Max once per shot and shared by all pellets of that shot. Angles are written with a `d` suffix for degrees.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.EvenSpread: Replaces the random spread roll with an interpolation from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmitterRules.Spread]] Min to Max across the shots of a burst, so the burst sweeps evenly across the spread range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.AntiPhasingRaycastDistance: The distance, in tiles, behind the muzzle from which a raycast is cast forward to the spawn point to detect part colliders overlapping the emitter. When one is hit, the bullet spawns at the hit point instead, preventing shots from phasing through objects pressed against the weapon. Vanilla cannons use 1.5 to 2.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.AntiPhasingRaycastIgnoreLowCollisions: Makes the anti-phasing raycast test only high part colliders instead of operational part colliders, so parts with only low colliders no longer catch the spawn point.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.PelletSpread: An extra angular deviation rolled between Min and Max for each pellet when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.Pellets]] emits more than one, applied on top of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmitterRules.Spread]]. With a single pellet, or when unset, no per-pellet deviation is applied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.EvenPelletSpread: Spaces the pellets evenly across the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmitterRules.PelletSpread]] range instead of rolling each pellet's angle at random.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmit.TriggerValueIsShotOffsetTime: Whether the emitter fakes an emission time offset using the value from the FireTrigger.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.DirectCont.T:: On while the player is firing the named weapon in direct control.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.DirectCont.Weapon: A weapon component on the same part that scopes this toggle to that specific weapon. When set, the toggle is on only while that weapon itself is under the player's direct control. When unset, the toggle is on whenever the ship is in direct control mode at all.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.DirectCont.RequireWeaponBindingPressed: Additionally requires the weapon's fire binding to be held down for the toggle to be on. Only meaningful when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.DirectControlToggleRules.Weapon]] is set. The vanilla chaingun's `IsInDCMode` toggle sets both.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterPro.T:: Stands in for an emitter in another part or at another spot, so targeting and effects can follow a turret.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.T:: Shared setup for the things a weapon fires, covering the fire trigger, burst pattern and resource cost. A modder writes `BulletEmitter` or `BeamEmitter`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.FireTrigger: The trigger component whose triggering makes this emitter fire. Written either as just the component's ID or as a group naming the component and a specific trigger within it. The vanilla chaingun's bullet emitter fires from its `FixedWeaponShooter` trigger.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.GetTargetFrom: The weapon component on the same part that supplies this emitter's fire target, ship target, permission to fire, and direct control state. The vanilla chaingun's bullet emitter reads these from its `Turret` component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.FireDelay: Seconds between the fire trigger and the actual emission, counted down tick by tick. Triggers arriving while a delayed shot is still pending are ignored, and the delay is also included when predicting aim lead. At 0, the default, the shot is emitted immediately.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.DynamicDelayPredictor: A time-providing component on the same part whose current time is added to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.FireDelay]] in the delay used for aim lead prediction. It does not change the actual emission countdown. The vanilla railgun launcher points this at its `Projectile` component so aiming accounts for the projectile's travel time through the railgun before launch.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourceUsage: The resource costs of firing, as a list of entries that each drain a storage component on the same part per shot. The older flat [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceStorage]] form adds one entry to this list.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.Recoil: The strength of the backward impulse applied to the ship at the emitter's location each time it fires. The vanilla chaingun uses 10, tripled while overclocked.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.Burst: The number of shots fired per trigger, rolled between Min and Max. Follow-up shots are spaced by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.BurstDelay]] and the burst ends early if resources run out. Defaults to a single shot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.BurstDelay: Seconds between the shots of a burst. At 0, the default, all shots of the burst are emitted in the same tick.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.Pellets: The number of bullets or beams emitted per shot, rolled between Min and Max. Each pellet can get its own angular deviation through the emitter's PelletSpread field, such as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.BulletEmitterRules.PelletSpread]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.UseResourcePerShotInBurst: Deducts resources on every shot of a burst instead of only once on the burst's final shot. Resource availability is checked before every shot either way. The vanilla overclocked chaingun enables this.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourceScaleFactor: A value component on the same part whose current value multiplies every ResourcesUsed amount, with the result rounded up. The vanilla ion beam prism scales its resource usage by its stored ion energy.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.RevealsShip: Whether firing marks the ship as having fired its weapons, which temporarily reveals the ship through fog of war for [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.WeaponFireRevealDuration]]. The vanilla manipulator beam sets this false so it can fire without revealing the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourceStorage: The single-storage form of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceUsage]]. When set, it is converted into one resource usage entry together with the sibling [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourcesUsed]] and [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.MinResourcesUsed]] fields.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourcesUsed: The amount drained from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceStorage]] per shot in the single-storage form, scaled by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceScaleFactor]] and rounded up. Only read when ResourceStorage is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.MinResourcesUsed: The minimum amount that must be ready in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceStorage]] for the emitter to fire, checked instead of the scaled ResourcesUsed amount. The amount actually deducted is unchanged. Vanilla beam weapons set 1 so they can keep firing from a nearly empty battery.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.T:: One resource an emitter spends per shot, naming the storage and the amount taken.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourceStorage: The resource storage component on the same part that this entry drains when the emitter fires.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.ResourcesUsed: The amount drained from the storage per shot, scaled by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.ResourceScaleFactor]] and rounded up. Defaults to 1. With [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules.UseResourcePerShotInBurst]] off it is only deducted once per burst, on the final shot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRul.MinResourcesUsed: The minimum amount that must be ready in the storage for the emitter to fire, checked instead of the scaled [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.EmitterRules+ResourceUsageRules.ResourcesUsed]] amount. The amount actually deducted is unchanged. Vanilla beam weapons set 1 so they can keep firing from a nearly empty battery.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.T:: A weapon that cannot turn and fires only at targets inside the arc it already faces.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.TargetingArc: The angular width, centered on the weapon's facing, of the sector in which the weapon searches for enemy parts to auto-fire at, accounting for aim lead against each candidate ship. When unset the weapon only checks a single ray along its exact firing line. The vanilla railgun launcher uses `90d`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.TargetingRange: The radius, in tiles, of the target search sector used with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeaponRules.TargetingArc]]. When unset it falls back to the targeting emitter's current range times [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultTargetingRangeFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.AutoTarget: How the weapon acquires targets automatically. Fixed weapons require the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAutoTargetRules.TargetType]] to be `ShipParts` and honor the optional [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAutoTargetRules.Toggle]], a toggle component that enables firing at anything in the weapon's sights. While that toggle is off the weapon only fires at its explicitly assigned target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.AllowFireInFogOfWar: Lets the weapon auto-fire at parts hidden by fog of war. When false, the default, a part in the weapon's sights only counts as a valid auto-fire target while its position is inside the team's sensor vision.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.ChainFireToggleComponent: A toggle component looked up on allied parts caught in the weapon's line of fire. When such a part's toggle is on, the weapon treats the allied part as something to fire at, chaining its shot into it. The vanilla ion beam emitter and prism both name `IonBeamChainToggle` here so emitters keep firing into a prism that is set to relay the beam.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.TargetSearchInterval: Seconds between full enemy-in-sights searches while deciding whether to auto-fire. Defaults to 1, with cheaper cached checks between searches and a random initial phase per weapon so searches spread across ticks.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.AutoExplicitTargetPartsFilter: A filter tested against the part hit by the weapon's targeting ray. A part that passes is automatically made the weapon's confirmed explicit target. The vanilla ion beam emitter uses a friendly-prism filter so it locks onto a prism placed in its firing line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeapo.CoverageLine: The line visual drawn along the weapon's firing path when the game shows its coverage, reaching out to the weapon's range and clipped where friendly parts block the line of fire. Used by the vanilla chaingun, railgun launcher, and ion beam parts.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.T:: Rocks back and forth by `Angle` every `Interval` while operational, sweeping whatever is chained to it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.Angle: The angular amplitude of the oscillation, written with a `d` suffix for degrees. The component's rotation follows a cosine wave that deviates up to this angle to either side of its rest rotation. The vanilla small mining laser wobbles its beam emitters by a third of a degree.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.Interval: Seconds for one full back-and-forth cycle of the oscillation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.Interpolate: Updates the rotation every rendered frame using the real-time clock, giving a smooth swing. When false, the default, the rotation updates once per simulation tick using deterministic logical time. Gameplay logic must not depend on an interpolating oscillator, since the real-time clock is not deterministic across players.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.ResetWhenOperational: Restarts the oscillation whenever the component becomes operational, beginning centered on the rest rotation. When false the swing resumes from the phase it had when it last stopped. The vanilla small mining laser resets so its wobble always starts from center.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.Oscillator.ResetWhenNonOperational: Snaps the oscillation back to its starting phase when the component becomes non-operational, parking the rotation at the full [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.OscillatorRules.Angle]] deflection. When false the rotation freezes wherever the swing happened to be.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggle.T:: Hands the weapon one of two emitters depending on a toggle, which is how a part switches ammunition.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggle.Toggle: The toggle component on the same part whose state selects which of the two emitters this component exposes to whatever is chained to it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggle.ToggleOffEmitter: The emitter exposed while [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggleEmitterSelectorRules.Toggle]] is off. Range, aim, and spawn queries go through whichever emitter is currently exposed, and trigger events are forwarded only from that emitter. The vanilla laser blasters expose their normal bullet emitter here.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggle.ToggleOnEmitter: The emitter exposed while [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.PartToggleEmitterSelectorRules.Toggle]] is on. The vanilla laser blasters switch to their overclocked beam emitter through this slot when their overclock toggle turns on.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.T:: Accelerates along the part from a start offset to an end offset and triggers on arrival, as a railgun stage does.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.XStartOffset: The X offset, in tiles from the component's rules location, of the point where the moving projectile marker starts when the component becomes operational. Defaults to 0.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.YStartOffset: The Y offset, in tiles from the component's rules location, of the projectile marker's start point. The vanilla railgun launcher uses a base of 3 multiplied by its Railgun buff, so the run gets longer as more accelerators are chained behind it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.XEndOffset: The X offset, in tiles from the component's rules location, of the point where the projectile marker's run ends. Defaults to 0.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.YEndOffset: The Y offset, in tiles from the component's rules location, of the projectile marker's end point. On reaching it the component fires its trigger, which the vanilla railgun launcher uses to emit the actual bullet. The vanilla launcher uses -4, placing the end at its muzzle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.SpeedStart: The marker's speed, in tiles per second, at the start of its run. Speed is interpolated linearly toward [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunProjectileRules.SpeedEnd]] by the fraction of distance covered, and that fraction is also reported as the component's value to other components.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.SpeedEnd: The marker's speed, in tiles per second, at the end of its run. The vanilla railgun launcher sets this to its bullet's speed so the emitted bullet continues seamlessly.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.RailgunPro.Interpolate: Smooths the component's rendered location between fixed simulation steps, so visuals chained to it move without stutter. Vanilla warns to use this only for interpolating graphics, since hooking game logic to an interpolated component causes multiplayer desyncs. The vanilla launcher's recoil logic runs on a separate non-interpolated copy of the component.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.T:: A weapon on a turret that rotates at `RotateSpeed` to bear on its target before firing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.FiringArc: Total width, in degrees, of the arc the turret can rotate through, centered on its mount direction. `360d` lets it spin all the way around.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.TargetingRange: Maximum distance, in tiles, at which the turret searches for new targets. Defaults to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.ValidRange]] if that is set, otherwise to the targeting emitter's range multiplied by the ship's [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultTargetingRangeFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.TargetingArc: Width, in degrees, of the arc within which the turret searches for new targets. Defaults to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.ValidArc]] if that is set, otherwise to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.FiringArc]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.ValidRange: Maximum distance, in tiles, at which an acquired target remains valid to keep and fire at. Defaults to the targeting emitter's current range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.ValidArc: Width, in degrees, of the arc within which an acquired target remains valid to keep and fire at. Defaults to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.FiringArc]], and missile launchers widen it to `360d` beyond their launch arc.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.RotateSpeed: Degrees per second the turret rotates toward its desired aim direction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.ReturnToCenter: With nothing to aim at, the turret rotates back to its centered rest direction. When false it stays at whatever rotation it last had, as on the manipulator beam.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.FireThresholdAngle: Maximum angular distance, in degrees, between the turret's current facing and the aim direction for it to be willing to fire. Vanilla turrets use small values like `1d`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AllowFireWithBlockedLOS: Skips all line-of-sight checks, letting the turret target and fire even when the path to the target is obstructed. Missile launchers enable it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AllowFireInFogOfWar: Lets the turret keep targets that are outside its team's sight. When false a target hidden in fog of war is invalid.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.BlueprintArcSprite: Sprite for the firing-arc indicator fanned out in front of the part while it is being placed in build mode. The fan spans [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.ValidArc]] if set, otherwise [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.FiringArc]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.BlueprintArcRadius: Radius, in tiles, of the build-mode arc indicator drawn with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.BlueprintArcSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.BlueprintArcSpriteSegments: Number of quad segments the build-mode arc indicator is subdivided into. Vanilla turrets use 64.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.CoverageSectorArc: Renderer for the coverage sector shown when the weapon's coverage is displayed during commands. The sector spans [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.ValidArc]] (or [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.FiringArc]]) and extends to the weapon's standard range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.TargetSearchesPerSecond: How many times per second the turret runs a search for a new target. Defaults to 2, and the flak cannon raises it to 8.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.InstantSearchesAfterTargetLost: Number of search passes run immediately when the turret loses its target, instead of waiting for the next scheduled search. The chaingun uses 5.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.TargetChecksPerSearch: How many candidate targets each search validates before giving up. The manipulator beam checks 10 per search.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.HoldTargetWhileFiring: Seconds the turret's rotation stays frozen after the weapon toggles on, so it does not swing away while firing. The timer is refreshed for as long as the weapon stays toggled on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.HoldTargetAfterCancel: Seconds the turret holds its current rotation after losing its target instead of immediately swinging elsewhere. Laser blasters tie it to their emitter's `FireDelay`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AllowRotationToggle: The component ID of a toggle component. While that toggle is off the turret may not rotate, either freezing in place or returning to center depending on [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.ResetRotationIfNotAllowed]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.ResetRotationIfNotAllowed: When rotation is disallowed by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.AllowRotationToggle]], the turret rotates back to its centered direction instead of freezing at its current rotation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.TargetPathThickness: Thickness, in tiles, of the line-of-sight ray used when checking whether the path to the target is blocked. Point defense sets it to match its bullet's size so shots need a wide enough clear corridor.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AutoTargets: Ordered list of automatic targeting behaviors the turret tries, first entry first, until one yields a target. Each entry can be gated by its own [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAutoTargetRules.Toggle]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AutoTargetCrewSafetyDist: When auto-targeting crew in space, a candidate is skipped if any allied crew member is within this distance, in tiles, of it. Vanilla anti-crew weapons use 8.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.PreventOverlappingTargets: Prevents two turrets that both set this flag from auto-targeting the same object at once. The manipulator beam uses it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AimIncludesEmitterOffset: Compensates the aim direction for the emitter's offset from the turret's pivot so the shot itself lines up with the target. The chaingun disables it and simply points the turret at the target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeap.AllowAimAtProhibitedTarget: Lets the turret acquire and track targets that [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.ProhibitTargetPartsFilter]] prohibits, without treating them as something to fire at. The ion beam prism enables this.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.T:: One automatic targeting rule for a weapon, saying what it may pick out and shoot at on its own.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.TargetType: The kind of object this auto-target entry searches for. `ShipParts` targets individual parts of ships, `ShipCenters` targets a ship's center as a whole (used by the vanilla tractor beam), `Bullets` targets projectiles matching [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAutoTargetRules.BulletTargetCategories]], `Crew` targets crew floating in space, `Salvage` targets parts marked for salvage, `CollectNuggets` targets nuggets queued for collection, and `MoveCrew` targets space crew traveling to a destination. Turret weapons try the entries of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.AutoTargets]] in order, so earlier entries take priority, while a fixed weapon's single [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.FixedWeaponRules.AutoTarget]] accepts only `ShipParts` and refuses to load any other type.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.BulletTargetCategories: The bullet category labels this entry can target, matched against each targetable projectile's [[Cosmoteer.Bullets.Targeting.BulletTargetableRules.TargetCategory]]. Only used when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAutoTargetRules.TargetType]] is `Bullets`, and when left unset the entry matches no bullets at all. The vanilla point defense turret lists `[missile, mine, bullet]`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.Toggle: A toggle component on the same part that enables this entry only while the toggle is on. A target acquired through this entry is dropped as soon as the toggle turns off. The vanilla point defense turret gates its bullet entry on its defend toggle and its ship-parts entry on its attack toggle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.Overridable: Lets earlier, higher-priority entries in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.TurretWeaponRules.AutoTargets]] keep searching while the weapon holds a target acquired through this entry, replacing the target when one of them finds a match. When false the weapon keeps this entry's target until it becomes invalid. The vanilla point defense turret marks its ship-parts entry overridable so intercepting bullets always takes priority.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponAuto.EnableInDirectControlMode: Keeps this entry acquiring targets while the player is directly controlling the weapon. By default auto-targeting pauses under direct control. The vanilla missile launchers set this so their missiles still pick their own targets while the launcher is player-controlled.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.T:: Shared setup for weapons, covering fire interval, what may be targeted and whether the player can take direct control. A modder writes `FixedWeapon` or `TurretWeapon`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.FireInterval: Seconds between shots. A newly built weapon starts fully unloaded and must wait one full interval before its first shot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.FirePermissionToggle: The component ID of a toggle component that gates firing. While that toggle is off the weapon holds fire even when it wants to shoot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.TargetingEmitter: The component ID of the emitter whose range and aim prediction drive this weapon's targeting checks. When neither this nor [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.Emitter]] is set, the weapon assumes infinite range and aims straight at the target's center.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ResourceCheckEmitters: The component IDs of emitters whose resource supply gates firing. The weapon holds fire unless at least one listed emitter has the resources it needs to shoot, or every one of them when [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.ResourceCheckRequiresAllEmitters]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ResourceCheckRequiresAllEmitters: Requires every emitter in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.ResourceCheckEmitters]] to have its resources before the weapon fires, instead of just one of them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AIFirepowerRating: The weapon's contribution to its ship's total firepower score, which the AI uses to judge how threatening a ship is. Vanilla weapons point this at the part's damage-per-second stat.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AddAIFirepowerRatingsWhenTargetedByPartC: Part categories of other weapons on the same ship whose firepower rating is added to this weapon's own rating while they are targeting this part. The ion prism lists `[ion_beam_emitter, ion_beam_prism]` so the beams feeding it count toward its rating.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.CanBeGivenExplicitTarget: Whether the player can give this weapon explicit targets. When false the weapon is skipped by all target-assignment input and never receives ship-wide targets.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AllowShipWideExplicitTargets: Whether the weapon picks up ship-wide explicit targets given by right-clicking enemy parts with no specific weapon selected. Ignored unless [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.CanBeGivenExplicitTarget]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AllowShipWideExplicitTargetsToggle: The component ID of a toggle component. When set, the weapon only accepts ship-wide explicit targets while that toggle is on, as with the flak cannon's fire-preference toggle.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ShowExplicitTarget: Whether the weapon's explicit targets are drawn in the world with a reticle and target line.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ShowTargetButtons: Whether the target buttons for this weapon appear in the part's UI card. Ignored unless [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.CanBeGivenExplicitTarget]] is true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AllowDirectControl: Whether the weapon can be aimed and fired in direct control mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AllowDirectControlToggle: The component ID of a toggle component. When set, direct control only drives this weapon while that toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.DefaultDirectControlBinding: The zero-based index of the direct control fire button that fires this weapon. Turreted weapons default to 0 and fixed weapons to 1, while vanilla assigns 2 to the tractor beam and 3 to the mine launcher.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.CanSalvage: Counts the weapon as a salvaging weapon, like the mining laser. A ship with an operational salvaging weapon can be ordered to salvage parts that are not crew-salvageable.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IsDefensiveOnly: Marks the weapon as purely defensive, like point defense. It is excluded from firepower estimation and does not count when the game checks whether a crippled ship still has significant weapons.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IncludeInFirepowerEstimation: Whether the weapon counts toward firepower estimation, which attack commands use to position the ship so its weapons bear on the target and the AI uses for its total firepower score. Also controls whether the weapon's coverage area is drawn while giving commands.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.EstimateFirepowerToggle: The component ID of a toggle component. When set, the weapon only counts toward firepower estimation while that toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AutoFireToggle: The component ID of the toggle that enables autonomous fire. The weapon only wants to fire on its own while that toggle is on.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AlwaysShowCoverage: Draws the weapon's coverage area while giving commands even when the weapon is excluded from firepower estimation. Used by the mining laser and the flak cannon.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IgnoreFriendlyShipLowLOSChecks: Lets the weapon's line-of-sight rays pass through the low colliders of ships it cannot damage, so it can shoot over low parts of friendly ships like the deck cannon does. Also accepted under the older name `IgnoreSourceShipLowLOSChecks`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IgnoreFriendlyShipHighLOSChecks: Lets the weapon's line-of-sight rays pass through even the high colliders of ships it cannot damage, so friendly ships never block its fire. The manipulator beam enables this together with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.IgnoreFriendlyShipLowLOSChecks]]. Also accepted under the older name `IgnoreSourceShipHighLOSChecks`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IgnoreFriendlyStructureLOSChecks: Lets the weapon's line-of-sight rays pass through structure cells of ships it cannot damage, so friendly structure does not block fire.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.IgnoreJunkLOSChecks: Junk debris never blocks this weapon's line of sight, even junk whose [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.JunkBlocksWeaponLOS]] setting says it should.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.AllowEnemyStructureAutoTargeting: Lets auto-targeting pick structure cells on enemy ships. When false, enemy structure is only targeted once the ship has no operational parts left. FixedWeapon flips this default to true.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ProhibitTargetPartsFilter: Filter for parts the weapon refuses to target. The ion beam emitter uses it to avoid force-firing on friendly ion prisms.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ProhibitShipRelativePointTargets: Refuses explicit targets that are points pinned relative to a ship rather than actual parts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SuppressShipWideExplicitTargetsWhenTarge: While the weapon's current target matches this filter, it stops accepting ship-wide explicit targets, so whole-ship attack orders do not override a special assignment such as a friendly ion prism.
While the weapon is targeting a ship-relative point, it stops accepting ship-wide explicit targets.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SuppressDirectControlWhenTargetingPartsF: While the weapon's current target matches this filter, direct control ignores the weapon so manual fire does not override the assignment.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SuppressDirectControlWhenTargetingShipRe: While the weapon is targeting a ship-relative point, direct control ignores it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SuppressFirepowerEstimationWhenTargeting: Excludes the weapon from firepower estimation while its current target matches this filter, for example an ion beam aimed into a friendly prism.
Excludes the weapon from firepower estimation while it is targeting a ship-relative point. The ion prism uses this so the same prism is not counted for both its turret mode and its fixed mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SuppressFirepowerEstimationWhenNotTarget: Excludes the weapon from firepower estimation unless it is targeting a ship-relative point. The counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.SuppressFirepowerEstimationWhenTargetingShipRelativePoints]] used by a part's chained or fixed mode.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SaveSelfTargetPartCategories: Part categories for which a target on the weapon's own ship is saved with the ship design and restored on load. Ion beams and prisms use it to keep beam-into-prism setups intact.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.SaveShipRelativeTargets: Saves the weapon's ship-relative point targets with the ship design so they are restored on load.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ToggleOnMode: The condition under which this weapon counts as on when other components read it as a toggle source. Defaults to `WantsAndReadyToFire`, meaning the weapon both wants to fire and is reloaded with resources and permission to shoot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.OverrideTargetNineSlice: Replaces the standard rectangle drawn around this weapon's explicit targets in the targeting overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.OverrideTargetCircle: Replaces the standard circle drawn around this weapon's explicit targets in the targeting overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.OverrideTargetLine: Replaces the standard line drawn from the weapon to its explicit target, and between queued targets, in the targeting overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.OverrideReticleSprite: Replaces the standard reticle sprite drawn on this weapon's explicit targets in the targeting overlay.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.Emitter: Shorthand that registers one emitter as both the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.TargetingEmitter]], when that is not set explicitly, and an entry in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.ResourceCheckEmitters]]. Most vanilla weapons set only this field.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRule.ResourceCheckEmitter: Shorthand that adds one more emitter to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Parts.Weapons.WeaponRules.ResourceCheckEmitters]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.T:: One sprite in a blend set, matched by a situation code where `0`, `1` and `*` say which neighbouring sides must be empty, filled or either.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.SituationCode: Eight-character pattern describing which of the eight surrounding neighbor slots this sprite blends against. Each character is `0` (no neighbor), `1` (neighbor present) or `*` (either, expanded into both cases). Must be exactly 8 characters or generation throws. A single ambiguous code expands into every matching 8-bit neighbor configuration.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.MinDamageFraction: Lower bound of the damage range this sprite covers, from 0 (undamaged) to 1 (destroyed). The part's damage fraction is remapped across [[#MinDamageFraction]] to [[#MaxDamageFraction]] before selecting which entry of [[#DamageLevels]] to show.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.MaxDamageFraction: Upper bound of the damage range this sprite covers. When the part's damage exceeds this value the sprite is not drawn at all, letting a different blend sprite take over at higher damage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.AllowRotation: When true the sprite is also emitted for the three 90-degree rotations of its situation code, rotating both the neighbor bit pattern and the sprite's UVs. Set false for sprites that must not be reused rotated, such as directional or text decals.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.AtlasSprite: Single sprite for this situation, with no damage or random variation. One of `AtlasSprite`, [[#RandomAtlasSprite]], [[#DamageLevels]] or [[#RandomDamageLevels]] must be defined.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.RandomAtlasSprite: List of interchangeable sprites, one picked at random per part instance, with no damage variation. Use to break up visual repetition across identical tiles.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.DamageLevels: Sprites ordered from least to most damaged. The part's remapped damage fraction indexes into the list, so later entries show as the part takes more damage. No random variation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousBlend.RandomDamageLevels: Combines both axes: the outer list is random variants (one chosen per instance) and each inner list is that variant's damage-level sprites indexed by damage fraction.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.T:: One sprite set in a toggled blend group, matched by a situation code read over the component's toggles rather than over neighbouring tiles.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.SituationCode: Pattern of `0`, `1` and `*` characters describing which neighboring toggled slots this sprite blends against, one character per slot. `*` is a wildcard expanded into both a `0` and a `1` case. Every possible code of the layer's length must end up covered across all sprites or generation throws.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.DamageLevelSprites: Sprites ordered from least to most damaged for this situation. The remapped damage fraction indexes into the list. Although marked optional here, the deserializer requires it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.MinDamageFraction: Lower bound of the damage range this sprite covers, from 0 to 1. Damage is remapped across [[#MinDamageFraction]] to [[#MaxDamageFraction]] before indexing [[#DamageLevelSprites]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.MaxDamageFraction: Upper bound of the damage range this sprite covers. Beyond it the sprite is not shown, deferring to another sprite defined for higher damage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AmbiguousToggl.AllowRotation: When true the sprite is also generated for every rotation of its situation code (each bit-wrap of the code), reusing the artwork rotated. Set false when the sprite is directional and must not appear rotated.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.T:: One image drawn on a ship, naming the file, its size and offset in tiles, plus any animation frames and normal maps that go with it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.File: Single image file for a one-frame sprite. Mutually exclusive with [[#AnimationFiles]]: the deserializer reads `File` first and only falls back to `AnimationFiles` when `File` is absent. Its pixels are baked into the ship's shared texture atlas.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.AnimationFiles: List of image files laid out into a horizontal animation sequence, one file per frame, played in order. Every frame must be exactly the same pixel size or atlas generation throws. Use [[#File]] instead for a static single-frame sprite. [[#NormalsAnimationFiles]] supplies the matching normal maps.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.NormalsFile: Normal map paired with [[#File]] for lit rendering. Must be exactly the same pixel size as the base sprite. When omitted, a flat neutral normal map is generated automatically from the base sprite's alpha.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.NormalsAnimationFiles: Normal maps paired frame-for-frame with [[#AnimationFiles]]. The count must exactly equal the number of sprite frames or loading throws. Each must match its base frame's pixel size.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.Size: Width and height of the sprite quad in tiles. The quad is centered on the sprite's ship location, then shifted by [[#Offset]]. Defaults to `1, 1` when a file is present and `0, 0` otherwise.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.Offset: Shifts the drawn sprite away from its centered position, in tiles. [[#RotSpeed]] rotation still pivots around the original unshifted center rather than the shifted quad center.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.Z: Height (depth) value, scaled by the ship's world scale. Higher values render above lower ones within the same layer and drive parallax and lighting height.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.VertexColor: Tint multiplied into every pixel of the sprite. Defaults to white (no tint) when a file is present, or transparent white when there is no file.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.UVRotation: Rotates the texture in 90-degree clockwise steps. The value is a whole number of quarter turns and is combined with any rotation the renderer applies.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.MirrorU: Mirrors the texture horizontally (flips the U axis).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.MirrorV: Mirrors the texture vertically (flips the V axis).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.AnimationInterval: Time between animation frames. Only has an effect when the sprite has more than one frame. Defaults to one second.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.AnimationStartTime: When a newly spawned sprite's animation begins. `Zero` anchors it to time 0, `MinValue` far in the past (effectively already looping), `WhenSpawned` at the moment of spawn, and `Random` at a random offset within one full loop so identical sprites do not animate in lockstep. `Default` resolves to `WhenSpawned`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.ClampAnimation: When true the animation holds on its final frame instead of looping back to the start.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.RotSpeed: Angular speed at which the sprite spins continuously around its center. Pivots around the unshifted center even when [[#Offset]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.SampleMode: Has no effect here. AtlasSprite's deserializer never reads this value. Texture sampling is controlled by the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]] of the containing render layer instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.MipLevels: Has no effect here. AtlasSprite's deserializer never reads this value. Mip generation is controlled by the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]] of the containing render layer instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.FixTransparentColors: Has no effect here. AtlasSprite's deserializer never reads this value. Transparent-color fixing is controlled by the [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]] of the containing render layer instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasSprite.PreMultiplyByAlpha: Has no effect. The game contains no field of this name anywhere in its code, so the value is read from the rules and discarded. Alpha premultiplication is controlled by `MultiplyByAlpha` on [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.T:: Packing settings for the texture atlas a group of ship sprites is baked into, such as mip levels, compression and sampling.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.SampleMode: Texture filtering for the generated atlas. `Point` gives crisp nearest-neighbor sampling, `Linear` smooths between texels. When omitted, the game's default sample mode is used.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.ColorKey: Every pixel that exactly matches this color is replaced with fully transparent black before the atlas is built. Skipped when left at the default (transparent black), so a color key of `0, 0, 0, 0` means no keying.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.MultiplyByAlpha: Premultiplies each pixel's red, green and blue channels by its alpha. Enables premultiplied-alpha blending and produces cleaner mipmaps, since mipmap generation then treats the texture as premultiplied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.FixTransparentColors: Replaces the color of every fully transparent pixel with the average of its opaque neighbors. Prevents dark or wrong-colored halos bleeding in around sprite edges under `Linear` sampling.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.MipLevels: Number of mipmap levels to generate for the atlas. A value of `1` disables mipmaps. Also determines the padding each source sprite is rounded up to (a multiple of `2^(MipLevels-1)` pixels). When omitted, the graphics default mip count is used.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTexturePa.Compression: GPU compression applied to the finished atlas. When anything other than `None`, the texture is first padded to a multiple of 4 pixels and then block-compressed. `NoAlpha`, `AlphaCutout` and `FullAlpha` trade alpha fidelity for size, and `NormalMap` uses a normal-map-specific scheme.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Roles.RoleRules.T:: The colors the game picks from when the player creates a crew role.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Roles.RoleRules.DefaultRoleColor: Color given to the built-in default crew role that every ship starts with.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Roles.RoleRules.NewRoleColor: Color assigned to a freshly created crew role when the player adds one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Roles.RoleRules.RoleColorSRange: Saturation range the role color picker is limited to, keeping player-chosen role colors within a usable saturation band.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Roles.RoleRules.RoleColorVRange: Value (brightness) range the role color picker is limited to, keeping player-chosen role colors within a usable brightness band.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledBuffModifier.T:: Scales a buff's strength away from `Basis`, then raises it to `Exponent` before applying it, which sharpens or softens how hard the buff bites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledBuffModifier.Scale: Multiplier applied to the buff amount's distance from Basis. The scaled value is `(buff - Basis) * Scale + Basis`, so the buff amount is stretched or compressed around the Basis pivot.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledBuffModifier.Exponent: Power the scaled buff value is raised to before ModificationMode combines it with the running value. At the default of 1 no power curve is applied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledBuffModifier.Basis: Pivot point the scaling is measured from. The buff amount is scaled toward or away from this value rather than from zero. Defaults to 0.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledEffectScaleModifie.T:: Scales the effect intensity away from `Basis`, then raises it to `Exponent` before applying it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledEffectScaleModifie.Scale: Multiplier applied to the effect scale's distance from Basis. The scaled value is `(effectScale - Basis) * Scale + Basis`, then raised to the inherited Exponent before ModificationMode combines it with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledEffectScaleModifie.Basis: The value that Scale will scale the EffectScale towards.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledStatusExponentModi.T:: Scales a status value away from `Basis`, then raises it to `Exponent` before applying it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledStatusExponentModi.Scale: Multiplier applied to the status value's distance from Basis. The scaled value `(statusValue - Basis) * Scale + Basis` is added to BaseStatusValue, converted per ValueType, and raised to the inherited Exponent before ModificationMode combines it with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ScaledStatusExponentModi.Basis: Pivot point the status value is scaled toward or away from, rather than from zero. Defaults to 0.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.T:: How a ship's build-mode blueprint is drawn, covering its materials, its sprite atlas settings and the outer wall sprites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.AtlasTextureParams: Texture-generation settings for the combined blueprint sprite atlas shared by all blueprint part sprites. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.Material: Material used to draw blueprint part sprites where the part's placement is valid.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.InvalidMaterial: Material used to draw blueprint part sprites where placement is invalid, typically tinting them red. Chosen instead of [[#Material]] whenever the part cannot be legally placed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.ExternalWalls: Blend-sprite rules for drawing the outer hull edge of the ship's blueprint. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Blueprints.ExternalBlueprintWallRules]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipBlueprintRules.DrawProhibitedZoneCategories: Set of prohibit-category IDs whose prohibited zones are drawn in build mode. A part's prohibited zone is only shown if its category is in this set.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFile.T:: Points at a saved `.ship.png` design on disk, written as a plain path wherever a rules file names a ready-made ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFile.FilePath: The path of the saved ship file.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.T:: The look and timing of a ship's FTL jump, from the crop-in animation through the light-speed streak to the jump sounds.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.TotalDuration: Total length of the FTL warp animation. Internal progress runs from 0 to 1 over this time when jumping out and back from 1 to 0 when jumping in. Every phase timing below ([[CropTime]], [[WarpEffectIn]], [[WarpEffectOut]]) is measured in seconds against progress multiplied by this duration.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropTime: Time window (in elapsed jump seconds) over which the crop line, the leading edge that wipes the ship into and out of warp, sweeps across the ship's bounding rect from one side to the other. Also drives the position of the [[CropSprite]] along that sweep.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropSprite: Sprite drawn at the moving crop edge as the ship wipes into warp. Its position tracks the [[CropTime]] sweep, its size comes from [[CropSizeFactor]] modulated by the pulse fields, and its alpha ramps in via [[CropZeroAlphaSize]] and [[CropFullAlphaSize]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropSizeFactor: Base width and height multipliers for the [[CropSprite]], applied against the ship's convex hull width along and across the jump direction. The pulse fields [[CropWidthPulse]] and [[CropHeightPulse]] are added on top each frame.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropPulseInterval: Interval of the sine wave (sampled over clock time) that pulses the [[CropSprite]]. The single wave value scales the width, height and alpha pulse amounts each frame.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropAlphaPulse: Amount the [[CropSprite]] alpha oscillates by, driven by the [[CropPulseInterval]] wave. Added to the sprite's base vertex alpha each frame.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropWidthPulse: Amount the [[CropSprite]] width oscillates by, driven by the [[CropPulseInterval]] wave. Added to the X component of [[CropSizeFactor]] each frame. Height counterpart is [[CropHeightPulse]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropHeightPulse: Amount the [[CropSprite]] height oscillates by, driven by the [[CropPulseInterval]] wave. Added to the Y component of [[CropSizeFactor]] each frame. Width counterpart is [[CropWidthPulse]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropZeroAlphaSize: Apparent crop size (0..1, peaking at the middle of the sweep and falling to 0 at each end) at or below which the [[CropSprite]] is fully transparent. Alpha ramps up from here to [[CropFullAlphaSize]], so the sprite fades out as it reaches the edges of the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.CropFullAlphaSize: Apparent crop size (0..1) at or above which the [[CropSprite]] reaches full opacity. Together with [[CropZeroAlphaSize]] it defines the size window over which the crop sprite fades between transparent and opaque as it sweeps.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.WarpEffectIn: Time window (in elapsed jump seconds) over which the warp ghost drawn with [[WarpEffectShader]] fades in at the start of a jump. Its alpha interpolates from 0 to 1 across this range. The fade-out counterpart is [[WarpEffectOut]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.WarpEffectOut: Time window (in elapsed jump seconds) over which the warp ghost fades back out toward the end of a jump. Its alpha interpolates from 1 down to 0 across this range. The fade-in counterpart is [[WarpEffectIn]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.WarpEffectShader: Shader that draws the warping ship ghost during a jump, distorting the captured background. Fed the FTL background capture and [[WarpEffectTexture]], with alpha driven by [[WarpEffectIn]] and [[WarpEffectOut]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.WarpEffectTexture: Texture bound to the [[WarpEffectShader]] as the warp distortion source when rendering the warping ship ghost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.LightSpeedEffectShader: Shader that draws the light-speed streak ghost over the ship during a jump, tinted by [[LightSpeedEffectColor]] and composited with [[LightSpeedEffectBlendMode]]. Its overall alpha fades as the jump progresses.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.LightSpeedEffectColor: Tint applied to the light-speed streak ghost drawn by [[LightSpeedEffectShader]]. Its alpha is additionally scaled down by the square of jump progress, so the streak is strongest at the start of the effect and fades to nothing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.LightSpeedEffectBlendMode: Blend mode used to composite the light-speed streak ghost onto the scene when drawing it with [[LightSpeedEffectShader]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.JumpOutMediaEffects: Media effects (particles, sounds) spawned at the ship's location when it jumps out to FTL, after the [[JumpOutDelay]]. Counterpart is [[JumpInMediaEffects]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.JumpOutDelay: Randomized delay before the jump-out animation and [[JumpOutMediaEffects]] begin. A value is picked uniformly from this range each time a ship jumps out.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.JumpInMediaEffects: Media effects (particles, sounds) spawned at the ship's location when it arrives from FTL, after the [[JumpInDelay]]. Counterpart is [[JumpOutMediaEffects]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipFtlEffectRules.JumpInDelay: Randomized delay before the jump-in animation and [[JumpInMediaEffects]] begin. A value is picked uniformly from this range each time a ship arrives from FTL.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.T:: How the rebuild overlay on a destroyed ship is drawn, including the repair indicator sprites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.Material: Material used to draw the redprint (destroyed-part outline) sprites shown where parts are missing or awaiting rebuild.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.RepairIndicatorAtlasTextureParams: Texture-generation settings for the atlas holding the repair indicator sprites. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.IndicatorsMaterial: Material used to draw the repair indicator sprites over parts.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.RepairIndicatorSprite: Sprite shown over a part that is queued or flagged for repair but not yet actively being repaired.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRedprintRules.RepairingIndicatorSprite: Sprite shown over the part currently being repaired.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.T:: One drawing layer for ship sprites, fixing when in the frame it is drawn and which materials light, stencil and ghost it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.UniqueBucket: Sort key ordering this layer against the other layers in the same [[#RenderStage]]. Layers are drawn low-to-high by this value, so a larger bucket draws on top. Must be unique among layers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.RenderStage: Coarse pass in which the layer is drawn, fixing its order relative to crew and the other passes. Within a stage the fine order comes from [[#UniqueBucket]]. `Crew` interleaves with crew rendering and `Indicators` is the on-ship indicator overlay pass.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.AtlasTextureParams: Texture-generation settings for this layer's sprite atlas, controlling sampling, mipmaps, color keying and compression. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.Material: Material used to draw the layer's sprites to the screen. When omitted the layer contributes only to the auxiliary render targets below and is not drawn directly.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.StencilMaterial: Material used to render the layer into the stencil render target, when that target exists. Feeds masking used by later passes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.DiffuseMaterial: Material used to render the layer into the diffuse render target, when that target exists. Supplies the diffuse-color input for deferred lighting.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.NormalsMaterial: Material used to render the layer into the normals render target, when that target exists. Supplies surface normals for lighting.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.LightMaterial: Material used to render the layer into the light buffer, when it exists. Lets the layer emit light in the fancy-lighting pipeline.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.GhostMaterial: Material used to draw a ghost copy of the layer, such as the translucent placement preview shown while building.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.DrawForLocalPlayerOnly: When true the layer is drawn only for ships viewable by the local player, hiding it on enemy or unrevealed ships.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.DrawWithFancyLightingOnly: When true the layer is drawn only while the Fancy Lighting graphics setting is enabled, and skipped otherwise.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.IsRoof: Marks this as a roof layer. It is drawn with the current roof opacity so it fades out when the ship interior is revealed, and is skipped entirely when roof opacity is zero.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.IsIndicators: Marks this as an on-ship indicators layer. It is drawn only when the Show On-Ship Indicators setting is on, the GUI is active and indicators are not suppressed for the current view.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.Inflate: Expands every sprite quad outward by this many tiles on all sides when the layer's geometry is built. Used to hide seams or give an outline margin.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRenderLayerRules.HasNormals: When true, normal-map atlases are generated and loaded for this layer, enabling normal-mapped lighting. When false, only the base color atlas is built.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.T:: The roofs drawn over interior tiles, covering their fade in and out, the base textures and the decal groups the paint tool offers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofFadeInDuration: Seconds over which roof opacity moves back to full when the interior view is dismissed. Drives how fast roofs fade in.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofFadeOutDuration: Seconds over which roof opacity fades to zero when the ship interior is revealed. Paired with [[#RoofFadeInDuration]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofTexturesFolders: Folders scanned for `*.png` roof base textures, each keyed by its filename without extension. When the same filename appears in more than one folder, the folder later in the list wins.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DefaultRoofTexture: ID of the roof texture applied when a ship has none set. Resolves against the textures loaded from [[#RoofTexturesFolders]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofTextureSizePerTile: Size, in texture units per ship tile, at which the roof base texture is tiled. Sets the UV scale so the texture repeats consistently regardless of ship size.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DecalsShader: Shader used to draw roof decals.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofDecalGroups: Groups of decal image folders loaded into the roof decals atlas. Each group's folders are scanned for `*.png` decals, optionally filtered by a `whitelist.txt`, and the groups organize decals in the paint UI. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.DecalGroupRules]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofDecalDefaultSizes: Overrides the default placement size, in tiles, for specific decals. When a decal is absent here its size is derived from its image dimensions divided by [[#DecalSizePerTile]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.RoofDecalUpgrades: Remaps old decal IDs (`Old`) to replacement decals (`New`) when loading saved ships, so renamed or removed decals still resolve.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DecalsAtlasParams: Texture-generation settings for the combined roof decals atlas. See [[Cosmoteer.Ships.Rendering.AtlasTextureParams]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DecalSizePerTile: Pixel dimensions of one tile's worth of decal texture. Every decal image's dimensions must be exact multiples of this or atlas building throws, and the quotient is the decal's size in tiles.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.BaseColorSRange: Allowed saturation range for the roof base color. Colors the player picks are clamped into this range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.BaseColorVRange: Allowed value (brightness) range for the roof base color, clamping player-picked colors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.BaseTextureARange: Allowed alpha range for the roof base color, limiting how transparent or opaque the roof texture can be made.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DecalsSRange: Allowed saturation range for decal colors. Clamps colors chosen in the decal color picker.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DecalsVRange: Allowed value (brightness) range for decal colors, used by the decal color picker and by the metadata clamp when loading a ship. Note that `PaintUpdateInfo.SetRoofDecalColor` mistakenly clamps brightness against [[#DecalsSRange]] instead of this range, so this range is not applied on that particular path.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DefaultBaseColor: Roof base color a ship starts with before the player repaints it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRoofRules.DefaultDecalsColors: Default color of each decal layer, one entry per layer, applied to new ships.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.T:: One kind of hull such as the terran ship or an asteroid, listing every part and door it can be built from plus all its flight, construction and combat tuning.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ID: The unique identifier of this ship type, which must be in the form `author_name.ship_name`. Ship saves and game modes reference the ship type through this ID.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.OtherIDs: Additional IDs that resolve to this same ship type. Lets a renamed ship type keep loading saves and references that still use an old ID.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ShipScale: Multiplies the world-space size of the ship's tiles, scaling part sprites and physical sizes. Also caps how many crew can work the same construction, repair, or salvage job at the whole-number part of this value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.NameKey: Localization key for the ship type's display name, shown for example when choosing a ship class for a new ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Parts: Every part type that can exist on ships of this type. Each part's ID must be unique within the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Doors: The door types available on ships of this type. Each door's ID must be unique within the ship.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultDoorID: The door type used when doors are auto-created or when assigning a type to doors from a legacy ship save. Must match an entry in [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Doors]], or be empty for ships without doors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ExternalWalls: Sprite rules for the exterior walls drawn automatically around the outside of the ship's interior.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ExternalRoofWalls: Sprite rules for the exterior walls drawn on the ship's roof layer, using the same format as [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ExternalWalls]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxBorders: The rectangle of tile coordinates parts may be built within. The build tools reject parts outside it, imported PNG blueprints are checked against its size, and recentering centers the blueprint inside it. Vanilla allows -60 to 60 on both axes.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxAbsLinearVelocity: Hard cap on the ship's linear speed. The physics engine clamps the ship body's velocity to this magnitude. Vanilla ships use `Infinity`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxAbsAngularVelocity: Hard cap on the ship's rotation speed, applied to the physics body's angular velocity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.RenderLayers: The render layers ship sprites can draw into, keyed by layer ID. Each layer's sprites are packed into texture atlases, and layers are drawn in sorted order within their render stage.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Blueprints: Rules for rendering the ship's blueprint view, including the blueprint materials, atlas parameters, and blueprint external walls.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Redprints: Rules for rendering redprints, the red overlay used for invalid blueprint parts, including its material and the repair indicator sprites.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LinearDrag: The drag solver applied to the ship body's linear velocity, slowing the ship when it is not thrusting. Omitting it gives the ship no linear drag. Vanilla uses an `Exponential` solver.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AngularDrag: The drag solver applied to the ship body's angular velocity, slowing its rotation. Omitting it gives the ship no angular drag. Vanilla uses a `Viscous` solver.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Restitution: Bounciness of the ship's collision fixtures. 0 makes collisions absorb all bounce, higher values make the ship rebound off other objects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.RotationalInertiaFactor: Multiplier on the rotational inertia computed from the ship's mass distribution. Higher values make the ship slower to rotate.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ThrusterUpdateInterval: Seconds between recalculations of the ship's thruster activations, drawn at random from this range so ships don't all update on the same tick. Ignored while the ship's speed is inside [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ThrusterUpdateIntervalOverrideSpeedRange]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ThrusterUpdateIntervalOverrideSpeedRange: Speed range within which thruster activations are recalculated every physics tick instead of waiting for [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ThrusterUpdateInterval]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ThrusterSolverIterations: Number of iterations the thrust solver runs when translating a desired acceleration into individual thruster activation levels. More iterations track the desired acceleration more closely at more CPU cost.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxLinearMagicAcceleration: Maximum linear acceleration applied directly to the ship's body to make up for whatever its thrusters cannot deliver. Lets a ship move without adequate thrusters. Omitted or 0 disables the effect.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxAngularMagicAcceleration: Maximum angular acceleration applied directly to the ship's body to make up for whatever its thrusters cannot deliver, like [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxLinearMagicAcceleration]] but for rotation. Omitted or 0 disables the effect.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.UncommandedThrusterShutdownDelay: Seconds after the last movement command before the ship's thrusters shut down and stop updating.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxRampUpTimeForDeceleration: Seconds of thruster ramp-up the deceleration planner is willing to rely on. When predicting braking thrust, a thruster's usable activation is capped so reaching that level takes no longer than this.
