Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.TargetReachedDistanceSizeRatio: Multiple of the ship's bounding diameter within which the autopilot considers its destination reached and switches to fine position adjustment.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.TargetResetDistanceSizeRatio: Multiple of the ship's bounding diameter beyond which the autopilot abandons fine adjustment and resumes a normal approach. Acts as the hysteresis counterpart to [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.TargetReachedDistanceSizeRatio]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AdjustRotationVelocity: Speed the ship must slow to before the autopilot starts rotating it toward the commanded final facing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.VelocityCalculateFactor: Gain that converts the remaining distance to the destination, after subtracting the predicted stopping distance, into desired acceleration. Higher values make the autopilot approach more aggressively.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.TooCloseVelocityOverrideStrength: Multiplier on the push-away velocity used when the ship gets too close to another ship or obstacle. Vanilla's large value makes the override dominate normal movement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AngularVelocityCalculateFactor: Gain that converts the remaining rotation offset, after subtracting the predicted stopping angle, into desired angular acceleration. The rotational counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.VelocityCalculateFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.RetroVelocityCalculateFactor: Gain applied against the ship's current velocity when computing desired acceleration. Acts as the damping term that cancels residual drift.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.RetroAngularVelocityCalculateFactor: Gain applied against the ship's current angular velocity when computing desired angular acceleration. The rotational counterpart of [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.RetroVelocityCalculateFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AngleSatisfiedThreshold: Range of remaining rotation offset, in degrees, used to scale forward thrust while the ship still needs to turn. At or below the minimum the ship thrusts at full power, at or above the maximum it holds thrust until the rotation catches up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.HorizontalSatisfiedThreshold: Range of sideways velocity, measured as a fraction of the remaining forward distance, used to scale forward thrust while cruising. At or below the minimum the ship thrusts fully forward, at or above the maximum it diverts thrust into lateral correction instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DecelerationDistanceDtRange: Bounds, in seconds, on the timestep used by the iterative stopping-distance prediction. The actual step is the current speed times [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DecelerationDistanceDtSpeedRatio]] clamped into this range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DecelerationDistanceDtSpeedRatio: Multiplied with the ship's current speed to pick the timestep of the stopping-distance prediction, clamped into [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DecelerationDistanceDtRange]]. Larger values give a coarser but cheaper prediction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ForwardThrustRatioHistoryCount: Number of recent thrust updates over which the ship averages its forward thrust ratio. The average feeds arrival-time matching with other ships flying in formation.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ArrivalTimeOptimisticBuffer: Seconds subtracted from other ships' predicted arrival times when matching arrival times, so the ship assumes its companions arrive slightly sooner than predicted.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ArrivalTimeRampDown: Controls how quickly forward thrust may drop when slowing to match arrival times with other ships. Each update the allowed thrust ratio can fall by the update interval divided by this value, so larger values give a more gradual ramp down.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.OrbitModeRadiusFactor: Multiplier on a follow command's follow radius used to decide when the ship is close enough to switch into orbiting and fine adjustment around its target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxPartSearchIterations: Cap on pathfinding iterations when searching outward for nearby parts or cells, for example when crew search from an airlock or when looking for resource destinations.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.SupplierSearchInterval: Has no effect. The game requires and stores the value but no code ever reads it, so it does not control any supplier search timing.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.SelfDestructForce: Impulse applied to the ship at every cell bordering a self-destructing part, pushing the surrounding structure away from the destroyed part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.BaseSightRadius: Sight radius, in tiles beyond the ship's bounding radius, that every ship of this type has even without sensor parts. Sensor parts with a larger radius take precedence, and nebulas scale the result.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.BaseRadarRadius: Radar radius, in tiles beyond the ship's bounding radius, available without sensor parts. Sensor parts with a larger radius take precedence, and nebulas scale the result.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MinCommsRadius: Minimum communication radius, in tiles beyond the ship's bounding radius. The effective comms radius is the larger of this and the ship's sight radius.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.WeaponActivationEnemyCheckRadius: Distance beyond the ship's bounding radius scanned for visible enemy ships. Whether an enemy is inside drives weapon activation and gates behavior that requires safety, such as automatic crew exit.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultTargetingRangeFactor: Multiplies a weapon's emitter range to get its default auto-targeting acquisition range when the weapon does not define its own TargetingRange.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MapJumpFuelCostPerMass: Distance-independent term of the galaxy-map FTL jump fuel cost, charged per unit of ship mass. The total cost also scales with the ship's FTL jump efficiency.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MapJumpFuelCostPerMassDistance: Fuel charged per unit of ship mass per unit of galaxy-map distance jumped. Vanilla is tuned to 1 fuel per 100 mass to jump 10 light-years at 100% efficiency.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MapJumpDistanceExponent: Exponent applied to the map jump distance before it is multiplied by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MapJumpFuelCostPerMassDistance]]. 1 makes fuel cost linear in distance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LocalJumpFuelCostPerMass: Distance-independent term of the in-system FTL jump fuel cost, charged per unit of ship mass. The total cost also scales with the ship's FTL jump efficiency.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LocalJumpFuelCostPerMassDistance: Fuel charged per unit of ship mass per tile of in-system jump distance. Vanilla is tuned to 1 fuel per 100 mass to jump 25000 tiles at 100% efficiency.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LocalJumpDistanceExponent: Exponent applied to the in-system jump distance before it is multiplied by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LocalJumpFuelCostPerMassDistance]]. 1 makes fuel cost linear in distance.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.LocalJumpMinDistance: Minimum distance, measured from the ship's bounding circle to the destination, required to start an in-system FTL jump. Closer destinations are rejected.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ImmuneToEnvDamage: Exempts the ship from environmental damage sources such as damaging nebulas, lightning strikes, and out-of-bounds damage in PvP arenas.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AlwaysVisibleInNebulas: Prevents nebulas from hiding this ship from other players' sight.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.IsAsteroid: Marks this ship type as an asteroid. Crew can salvage asteroids from manipulator-beam distance instead of standing adjacent, and creative mode's clear-objects tool counts them as asteroids rather than ships.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.JunkBlocksWeaponLOS: Whether junk chunks of this ship type block weapon line-of-sight checks and homing projectile target acquisition. Weapons with `IgnoreJunkLOSChecks` shoot through regardless.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.Roofs: Rules for rendering ship roofs, including fade in and out durations, roof texture and decal parameters, and the default roof colors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.FtlEffects: The visual and sound effect played when the ship makes an FTL jump, including the flash sprite, warp distortion, light-speed streak, and the jump-in and jump-out sounds.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultCollectNuggetPriority: Default crew priority of the collect-loose-resources job. Shown in the crew priority UI under the part named by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateCollectNuggetJobWithPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateCollectNuggetJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the collect-nuggets job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultCollectNuggetPriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultEjectNuggetPriority: Default crew priority of the eject-resources job, used when crew carry unwanted resources to an airlock and jettison them.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateEjectNuggetJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the eject-nuggets job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultEjectNuggetPriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultSalvagePriority: Default crew priority of salvage jobs. Shown in the crew priority UI under the part named by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateSalvageJobWithPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultConstructPriority: Default crew priority of part construction jobs. Shown in the crew priority UI under the part named by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateConstructJobWithPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultDeconstructPriority: Default crew priority of part deconstruction jobs. Shown in the crew priority UI under the part named by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateDeconstructJobWithPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultRepairPriority: Default crew priority of part repair jobs. Shown in the crew priority UI under the part named by [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateRepairJobWithPart]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateSalvageJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the salvage job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultSalvagePriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateConstructJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the construct job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultConstructPriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateDeconstructJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the deconstruct job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultDeconstructPriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.AssociateRepairJobWithPart: The part whose crew-priority entry hosts the repair job. The job appears under this part's priorities with [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultRepairPriority]] as its default.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultConstructionWorkPerHealth: Crew work required to construct a part, per point of its max health, for parts that do not define their own `ConstructionWork`. Vanilla is tuned so a corridor tile takes about one second.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.DefaultWorkPerRepairedHealth: Crew work required per point of health repaired, for parts that do not define their own `WorkPerRepairedHealth`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ConstructionResourceSearchesPerTick: How many pending construction jobs may search for source resources each simulation tick. Throttles the cost of construction searches on busy ships.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ConstructionNuggetSinkSearchesPerTick: How many searches for places to deposit leftover construction nuggets run each simulation tick, like [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.ConstructionResourceSearchesPerTick]] but for the nugget sink side.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.MaxCrewExitShipSpeed: Maximum ship speed at which crew are still allowed to automatically exit the ship, for example to work exterior jobs.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.OverrideConstructionMode: Forces this construction mode for ships of this type, overriding the construction mode the game mode would otherwise use.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.SalvagingDisabledSuppressesResourceDrops: Suppresses resource nugget drops from this ship's destroyed parts while the game mode has salvaging disabled.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.WeaponFireRevealDuration: Seconds after the ship last fires a weapon during which it counts as temporarily revealed, even if it would otherwise be hidden from other players.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.CategoryLimits: Per part-category limits on how many parts a ship may have. The build tools refuse to place parts beyond a category's `Max`. Warning messages use the nouns from [[Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.CategoryNouns]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.CategoryNouns: Singular and plural localization keys naming each part category, used in messages such as build-limit warnings. Categories without an entry fall back to the raw category ID.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules.VitalCategories: Part categories the ship should always contain. When a blueprint has no part in one of these categories, the build UI shows a missing-parts warning using that entry's `WarningKey`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryLimit.T:: Caps how many parts of one category a ship may carry, and can demand a minimum as well.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryLimit.Category: The part category this limit applies to. Its [[Min]] and [[Max]] bound how many parts of this category a ship may or must have.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryLimit.Min: Minimum number of parts in this [[Category]] that a ship must contain to count as complete. A blueprint reports having its minimum categories only when every category limit is met. Default 0 imposes no minimum.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryLimit.Max: Maximum number of parts in this [[Category]] a ship may contain. The build tool blocks placing more than this many. The default (int max) means unlimited.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryNounDa.T:: The singular and plural words used for a part category in messages, such as one reactor and three reactors.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryNounDa.Category: The part category whose display noun is defined here. When the UI needs a word for this category it looks up the matching entry for its [[SingularKey]] and [[PluralKey]], falling back to the raw category ID if none matches.
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryNounDa.SingularKey: Localization key for the singular noun of this [[Category]] (for example "reactor"). Returned by the game's singular-noun lookup for the category. Plural form is [[PluralKey]].
Cosmoteer.Ships.ShipRules/CategoryNounDa.PluralKey: Localization key for the plural noun of this [[Category]] (for example "reactors"). Returned by the game's plural-noun lookup for the category. Singular form is [[SingularKey]].

Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusExponentModifier.T:: Raises a status value to `Exponent` before applying it.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusExponentModifier.Exponent: Power applied to the status value. BaseStatusValue plus the status's value is converted per ValueType, raised to this exponent, and the result is combined with the running value by ModificationMode.

Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusModifier.T:: Pulls the current value of one status on the part in as the modifier, leaving the value alone when the part does not carry that status.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusModifier.ValueType: How the status value is interpreted before use. `Raw` uses the value as-is. `Interpolated` maps it to 0..1 across the status type's clamp range (inverse lerp), so the modifier works with a normalized fraction rather than absolute units.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusModifier.BaseStatusValue: Constant added to the status's raw value before it is converted per ValueType, shifting the status reading up or down.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusModifier.StatusType: The status whose current value drives the modifier. The modifier only takes effect when this status is present and valid on the target, otherwise it leaves the value unchanged.

Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.T:: Maps a status value from `RemapFrom` onto `RemapTo` before applying it, and can skip values that fall outside that range entirely.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.RemapFrom: Input range of the converted status value that gets mapped. A value at RemapFrom.Min maps to RemapTo.Min and one at RemapFrom.Max maps to RemapTo.Max. Also the range compared against by IgnoreValuesBelowRange and IgnoreValuesAboveRange.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.RemapTo: Output range the status value is mapped onto. The mapped result becomes the modifier value that ModificationMode then combines with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.Clamp: When true the status value is clamped to RemapFrom before mapping, so values outside the input range produce RemapTo.Min or RemapTo.Max rather than extrapolating past them. When false the mapping is unclamped.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.IgnoreValuesBelowRange: Whether to skip modification when the input value is below the RemapFrom range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.IgnoreValuesAboveRange: Whether to skip modification when the input value is above the RemapFrom range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusRemapModifier.Exponent: Power curve applied to the remap interpolation, biasing where the input maps within RemapTo. At the default of 1 the mapping is linear.

Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusToggledRangeModifi.T:: Applies one of two fixed values depending on whether the status value falls inside `AffectedValueRange`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusToggledRangeModifi.AffectedValueRange: The status value range, inclusive of both ends, that counts as inside. The modifier value is InsideRangeValue when the status value falls within this range and OutsideRangeValue otherwise.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusToggledRangeModifi.InsideRangeValue: Modifier value used when the status value is within AffectedValueRange. ModificationMode combines it with the running value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.StatusToggledRangeModifi.OutsideRangeValue: Modifier value used when the status value is outside AffectedValueRange. ModificationMode combines it with the running value.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ConstantValueMo.T:: Moves a status value by a fixed amount each tick, used for a steady burn down or build up.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ConstantValueMo.Value: The fixed amount fed into `ModificationMode` every tick, independent of the current status value. With `Add` and `ScaleByDeltaTime` on, this is a change per second.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ConstantValueMo.AffectedValueRange: The status values this modulator applies to. The lower bound is inclusive and the upper bound is exclusive, so adjacent bands can be written back to back without overlapping.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateSine.T:: Moves a status value by an amount eased along a sine curve across `AffectedValueRange`, so the change tapers off at one end.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateSine.InterpolationRange: The output values produced at the bottom and top of `AffectedValueRange`, with a quarter-sine curve in between instead of the straight line an `Interpolate` modulator would use.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateSine.InvertCurve: Swaps the easing while keeping the same endpoints. Off, the output rises quickly and flattens near the top of the band, on it starts slowly and accelerates.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateSine.AffectedValueRange: The status values this modulator applies to, and also the range the sine curve is measured across. The lower bound is inclusive and the upper bound is exclusive.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateValu.T:: Moves a status value by an amount interpolated across `AffectedValueRange`, with `Exponent` bending the curve.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateValu.InterpolationRange: The output values produced at the bottom and top of `AffectedValueRange`. Combined with `ModificationMode` `Add` this gives a rate that ramps across the band, and the two ends may be written in either order.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateValu.Exponent: The power applied to the position within `AffectedValueRange` before interpolating. Above 1 keeps the output near the Min end for most of the band, below 1 pushes it toward the Max end early.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.InterpolateValu.AffectedValueRange: The status values this modulator applies to, and also the range the interpolation is measured across. The lower bound is inclusive and the upper bound is exclusive.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.MultiValueModul.T:: The ordered list of modulators a status runs each tick, stopping at the first match unless `ContinueAfterFirstModulation` is set.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.MultiValueModul.ContinueAfterFirstModulation: Whether the remaining modulators still run after one has matched. Left off, the list behaves like a first-match chain, which is how vanilla fire selects one curve per value band.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.MultiValueModul.Modulators: The modulators tried in order against the status value. Each entry picks its kind through a `Type` field, one of `Constant`, `Interpolate` or `InterpolateSine`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.PartStatusToggl.T:: Turns on while the named status on the part sits between `MinStatusValue` and `MaxStatusValue`, letting other components react to a burning or scorched part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.PartStatusToggl.MinStatusValue: The lowest combined status value on the part that switches the toggle on, inclusive.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.PartStatusToggl.MaxStatusValue: The highest combined status value on the part that switches the toggle on, inclusive.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.PartStatusToggl.Invert: Flips the toggle, so it is on while the value is outside the range and off while inside. A part with no instance of the status at all reports the inverted state too.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.PartStatusToggl.StatusType: The status whose value on this part drives the toggle. It must be a `Part` layer status, a tile layer status throws at runtime when the part is built.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusCustomSha.T:: Plays a status' continuous media effects from a single node that picks random points across the area the status covers.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusCustomSha.StatusValueToEffectValueType: The status value conversion type, if any, to return as the value of Rand).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusCustomSha.RectSizeFactor: The value that the status' rect size is multiplied by when retrieving a random point for particle spawning.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusCustomSha.Effects: The media effects driven by the custom shape. A bare list can be written here in place of the whole group, in which case the other fields keep their defaults.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusResistanc.T:: How strongly a part shrugs off a status, given as a cut to its value and a cut to its duration. A single number or range sets both.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusResistanc.Value: The resistance to the applied status value, where 0 lets it through unchanged and 1 blocks the application entirely. The Min and Max ends are interpolated by the part's DamageFraction, so a damaged part can resist differently from an intact one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusResistanc.Duration: The resistance to the applied status duration, on the same 0 to 1 scale and interpolated by DamageFraction the same way as `Value`. Writing the whole StatusResistance as a single value or a single range sets both fields at once.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.T:: One named status such as `cosmoteer.fire` or `cosmoteer.heat` sitting on a part or tile, fixing how it combines, ticks, spreads, is resisted and what effects it plays.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ID: The identifier other rules use to refer to this status, for example the `StatusType` field of a StatusApplication hit effect, a StatusToggle component or a StatusValueRegulator. Vanilla ids are namespaced like `cosmoteer.fire`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.IndicatorSprite: The sprite displayed over instances of this status.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.Layer: The layer that instances of this status are applied to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.StatusCombineMode: How applications of this status are handled when another status of this type exists in the same location.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ValueCombiner: Provides the final value when combining multiple status instances.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ValueClampRange: The range that instances of this StatusType will have their values clamped to.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.RemoveAtMinValue: Whether an instance is deleted as soon as its value reaches `ValueClampRange` Min. It also stops diffusion and status application from creating an instance that would start at exactly that minimum. See `TriggerEffectsOnMinValueRemove` for whether `RemovalEffects` fire in that case.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.TriggerEffectsOnMinValueRemove: Whether `RemovalEffects` and `RemovalMediaEffects` are performed when an instance is deleted by `RemoveAtMinValue`. Has no bearing on removals from any other cause.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.TransferToUnderlyingOnPartDestroyed: Whether tile-based statuses will transfer to underlying parts when the part they're on is destroyed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.NegativeCombineIgnoresResistance: Whether combinatory status applications with negative values will ignore value resistances.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.CrewSpeedFactor: The range value to multiply crew speed by, sampled by interpolated status value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.JobInterruptionSeverity: The severity value used to determine whether certain jobs should be cancelled by this status, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.Filter: Restricts which parts and cells this status can be applied to. The same filter also decides whether a status may transfer onto a replacement part under `TransferToUnderlyingOnPartDestroyed`, and whether diffusion may seed a new instance in a cell.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ResourceSink: The rules defining the status' resource sink behaviour, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.SoftRepair: The rules defining the status' soft-repair behaviour, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.Diffusion: Makes the status spread between neighbouring cells each physics tick, the way heat conducts through a ship. Only works when `Layer` is `Tile` and `StatusCombineMode` is not `ApplyNewInstance`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ValueModulators: The value modulators applied to the values of this status' instances.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ValueModulationResistanceRange: The range that status resistance values are clamped to for ValueModulators.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.TickInterval: The interval between each call of this status' TickingEffects and TickingMediaEffects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.RequireValueRangeForTick: The status value range that ticking effects will be performed for. Statuses with values outside this range will be ignored.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ClearPlayerSourcesOnAggressionLoss: Whether the instances of this status should have their source player cleared on loss off aggression (e.g. truces).
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ClearOnShipJunked: Whether the instances of this status should be removed (without triggering effects) on the ship being junked.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.MediaIntensityValueType: Whether the status value handed to media effects as their Intensity is the raw value or interpolated into a 0 to 1 fraction. Interpolation uses `MediaIntensityInterpolationRange` when set, otherwise `ValueClampRange`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.UseDurationForMediaIntensity: Whether the media effect Intensity is derived from the status' remaining duration in seconds rather than from its value. Vanilla fire foam uses this so the foam effect fades out as the foam expires.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.MediaIntensityInterpolationRange: The value range mapped onto 0 to 1 when `MediaIntensityValueType` is `Interpolated`. Leave unset to reuse `ValueClampRange`, which is what you want unless the visual should saturate well before the gameplay maximum.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ClampMediaIntensity: Whether the interpolated media Intensity is clamped to 0 to 1. Only has an effect when `MediaIntensityInterpolationRange` is set, since the fallback to `ValueClampRange` always clamps. Vanilla heat turns it off so the glow keeps intensifying past 1000 heat.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ParentMediaEffectsToShip: Whether media effect nodes are attached to the ship and positioned in ship-local space, so they move and rotate with it, instead of being spawned at a fixed world location.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.StatusResistances: The status resistances provided to underlying parts by instances of this status type.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.DamageResistances: The damage resistances provided to underlying parts by instances of this status type.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.PenetrationResistanceModifier: The modifier applied to the penetration resistances of parts underlying instances of this status type.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ApplicationEffects: The hit effects performed when this status is applied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ApplicationMediaEffects: The media effects played when this status is applied.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.TickingEffects: The hit effects performed on each tick of this status.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.TickingMediaEffects: The media effects played on each tick of this status.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.ContinuousMediaEffects: The media effects played continuously on application of this status, and stopped on status removal.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.CustomShapeEffects: The media effects played continuously using a single effect node with an ICustomEffectShape. Supports only a subset of media effects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.RemovalEffects: The hit effects performed on removal of this status.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType.RemovalMediaEffects: The media effects played on removal of this status.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Base.T:: Settings shared by every resistance entry, deciding whether the value is spread over the part's tiles, counted once per status instance, and how it folds into the existing figure.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Base.DivideByPartArea: Whether to divide the resistance value by the tile-area of the part.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Base.MultiplyByStatusCount: Whether to multiply the resistance value by the instance count of this status type on the part. If this is false, this resistance is applied once, regardless of status count.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Base.ModificationMode: How the resistance value from this rule is folded into the part's existing resistance. `Add` and `Subtract` shift it, `Multiply` and `Divide` scale it, and `Replace` discards the part's own value.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.T:: Lets the status bleed between neighbouring tiles until levels even out, with per-part speed factors for parts that conduct better or worse.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.Basis: The value that cells with no status instance are treated as holding, and the value that partly empty cells drift back toward. For heat this is 0, the ambient temperature.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.SpeedFactor: The fraction of the difference between two neighbouring occupied cells that moves across per tick, before the per-part factors are applied. The final factor is clamped to 0 to 1, and each of the four neighbours exchanges one fifth of the gap, so 1 means near instant equalization.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.MinDeltaThreshold: The smallest per-tick transfer that is actually applied between two occupied cells. Anything smaller is dropped to zero, which keeps tiny residual values from spreading forever. It is not applied to transfers into empty cells.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.EmptyCellSpeedFactor: The speed factor used when the neighbouring cell holds no part, and also for the dissipation of partly occupied cells back toward `Basis`. This is how a status bleeds off into space at the hull edge. Vanilla heat uses 0.004 against 0.01 for cell-to-cell conduction.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.PartSpeedFactors: Per-part-type overrides of the diffusion speed, keyed by part id. Vanilla heat gives structure an `Occupied` factor of 25 so heat conducts through armor far faster than through machinery.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.T:: How fast the status diffuses through one part, given separately for tiles that are occupied and tiles that are empty.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.Occupied: Multiplies DiffusionRules `SpeedFactor` for transfers between this part and a neighbouring cell that also holds a part. The two cells' factors are averaged, then the product is clamped to 0 to 1.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Diff.Empty: Multiplies DiffusionRules `EmptyCellSpeedFactor` for transfers from this part into a neighbouring cell that holds no part. Only the losing cell's factor is used, there is no averaging.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Simp.T:: A resistance given as a plain value range, sampled by how damaged the part is.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Simp.Resistance: The resistance value, sampled by the part's DamageFraction.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.T:: Decides which parts the status can land on, by part category, by whether crew can walk there and by operational or structural health.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.PartRectType: Which rectangle of a part is consulted when looking up the part occupying a cell. `Normal` uses the part's full footprint, `Physical` uses the smaller PhysicalRect a part may declare, so cells inside the footprint but outside that rect count as empty.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.NonWalkable: Whether the status may also be applied where crew cannot walk. Setting it false rejects parts with a zero CrewSpeedFactor and cells that block crew travel, which is how a status is kept to walkable floor only.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.OnlyPartCategories: Restricts application to parts that carry at least one of these part categories. Unset means no category requirement.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.ExcludePartCategories: Rejects any part that carries one of these part categories. Applied after `OnlyPartCategories`, so a part matching both lists is rejected.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.OperationalHealth: Whether the status may be applied to parts whose HealthType is `Operational`, meaning most functional parts. Set false to make the status affect structure only.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.StructuralHealth: Whether the status may be applied to parts whose HealthType is `Structural`, meaning armor and structure. Set false to make the status affect functional parts only.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.T:: The resistance this status hands the part beneath it against another status, cutting both that status' value and its duration.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.Resistance: The resistance values, sampled by the part's DamageFraction.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.T:: Makes the status ask crew to carry a resource to it, such as fire extinguishers to a fire, and names the job and its priority.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.Resource: The requested resource type of the sink.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.AssociateJobWithPart: The PartRules to associate with the sink's delivery jobs, if any.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.JobNameKey: The key for the delivery job's priority name.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.PrioritySortOrder: The sort order for the delivery job's priority.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.DefaultPriority: The default priority for delivery jobs to this sink.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.ValueChangePerResource: The change in status value per resource delivered.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.TargetValue: The value that resources will be delivered in order to reach.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.AlwaysRequestMaxResources: Whether the status sinks will request the maximum amount of resources that crew can carry, regardless of remaining capacity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.DeliveryMediaEffects: The continuous media effects to play while delivering resources to the sink.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.DeliveryHitEffects: The hit effects to perform on delivery of resources. EffectScale is set to the resource quantity.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.ReassignmentSearchIterations: The number of search iterations to perform when reassigning crew from removed sinks. Behaviour is disabled at 0.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.T:: Makes crew work the status down by hand like a repair job, setting the work per point of value and the range that puts a status on the repair list.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.TargetValue: The status value crew repair work drives the instance toward, in raw status units. Vanilla fire, heat and scorched all use 0, meaning crew work the status away entirely.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.WorkPerValueChange: The crew work units needed to move the status value by 1. Vanilla heat uses 0.02 and scorched 0.1, so a scorch point costs five times as much crew effort as a point of heat.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.CrewRequestCountOverride: Replaces the number of crew the repair job asks for, which otherwise defaults to the area of the repair grid rectangle. Overrides from several soft repairs blocking the same part are summed.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.RegistrationValueRange: The range that a status' value must be within in order to be registered for repair.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusType/Stat.DeregistrationValueBuffer: How far outside the RegistrationValueRange a repair-registered status' value can be before it is deregistered.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusTypes.T:: The full list of statuses in the game, together with the atlas settings their indicator sprites are packed with.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusTypes.AtlasTextureParams: The parameters for creation of the status indicator atlases.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusTypes.Statuses: Every status type in the game, keyed internally by each entry's `ID`. Vanilla includes one file per status here, covering fire, scorched, heat, fire foam, shield overload and disruptor drain.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueFilt.T:: Only lets a rule apply while the named status on the part sits between `MinValue` and `MaxValue`.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueFilt.MinValue: The lowest combined status value that still counts as a match, inclusive.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueFilt.MaxValue: The highest combined status value that still counts as a match, inclusive.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueFilt.StatusType: The status whose combined value at the location is tested. A location with no instance of this status never matches, whatever `MinValue` and `MaxValue` say.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.T:: Pushes status values in a region around the part towards `TargetValue`, paying for the change out of a resource storage or banking it into one.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.Trigger: The component trigger that runs one regulation pass. Nothing happens until it fires, so the trigger's timer or toggle sets the regulator's rate. Vanilla's heat exchanger drives it from a timer component.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.Region: The region that the regulator affects.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.RegionHighlightID: The part highlight preset used to shade `Region` in the build view. `Falloff` shapes the highlight intensity the same way it shapes the actual effect.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.Falloff: The exponent on the distance factor across `Region`, which weakens `ValueDelta` toward the region's outer edge. 0 disables falloff and treats every cell in the region equally.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.PickingMode: The order in which the statuses at one location are worked through when several are stacked there. `MinValue`, `MaxValue` and `Random` visit every candidate, `First` and `Last` walk the list from one end. `Last` stops one entry short and never touches the first status in the list, so on a location holding a single status it does nothing at all.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.TargetValue: The value to move status values towards.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValueDelta: The amount that each status' value may be moved towards the target.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValueDeltaPool: The total amount of value that may be added or removed
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValueSourceStorage: The resource storage that the regulator will draw from.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValuePerSourceResource: The conversion rate of ValueSourceStorage resources to status value.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.LimitBySourceResources: Whether the regulator requires available resources in the ValueSourceStorage in order to function.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValueTargetStorage: The resource storage that the regulator will deposit into.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.ValuePerTargetResource: The conversion rate of status value to ValueTargetStorage resources.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.LimitByTargetFreeSpace: Whether the regular requires free space in the ValueTargetStorage in order to function.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.AllowedChangeDirections: Restricts the regulator to only raising or only lowering status values. `Positive` blocks decreases, `Negative` blocks increases, and `Any` allows both.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.MediaEffectsOnIncrease: The one-shot media effects played at each affected cell whose status value went up. Their Intensity is the magnitude of the change.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.MediaEffectsOnDecrease: The one-shot media effects played at each affected cell whose status value went down. Vanilla's heat exchanger uses this for its absorption particles and sound.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.StatusValueRegu.StatusType: The status this regulator reads and writes. Both `Tile` and `Part` layer statuses are supported, and the regulator does nothing if the ship has no handler for the type.

Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ValueModulatorR.T:: Changes a status' own value over time, run each tick from the status' `ValueModulators`. Write `Constant` for a flat change, or `Interpolate` and `InterpolateSine` for one that varies across the value range.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ValueModulatorR.StatusFilter: An extra condition on some other status at the same location. The modulator is skipped unless that status is present and its value falls in the filter's range. Vanilla fire uses it to burn itself out faster once the part is scorched.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ValueModulatorR.ModificationMode: How the modulator's output is applied to the current status value. Resistance is honoured correctly only for `Add`, `Subtract` and `Replace`. With `Multiply` and `Divide` the whole result is scaled by one minus the resistance, so a fully resisting part drives the value to 0 instead of leaving it alone.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ValueModulatorR.ScaleByDeltaTime: Whether the modulator output is per second rather than per tick. For `Add` and `Subtract` the value is multiplied by the tick length, for `Multiply` and `Divide` the distance of the multiplier from 1 is scaled instead.
Cosmoteer.Ships.Statuses.ValueModulatorR.OutputValueType: How the modulator's own output is read before it is applied. `Raw` uses it as a status value directly, `Interpolated` treats it as a 0 to 1 fraction of the status' `ValueClampRange`.

Cosmoteer.Ships.ValueModifier.T:: Bends a number at runtime using a buff, a status or the effect intensity. Write one of the concrete modifiers in a `ModifiableValue`'s `Modifiers` list.

Cosmoteer.Ships.VitalCategoryInfo.T:: Warns the player in build mode when a ship carries no part of the given category, such as a missing airlock or reactor.
Cosmoteer.Ships.VitalCategoryInfo.Category: The part category the ship is expected to contain. If the ship has no parts in this category, its warning is shown in the build UI.
Cosmoteer.Ships.VitalCategoryInfo.WarningKey: Localization key of the message displayed when the ship is missing any part in Category.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.T:: Stores rules for the in-game camera.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.PixelOrthographicFactor: Pixels-per-world-unit factor for the orthographic viewport, divided by the global UI scale before use. Sets how many screen pixels one world unit spans at camera scale 1, shared by the simulation, galaxy map and editor viewports.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.DefaultScale: Initial camera zoom (uniform scale) applied when the camera node is created, and its starting target zoom. Clamped between [[MinScale]] and [[MaxScale]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.MinScale: Smallest allowed camera zoom scale, the most zoomed-in the player can go. Exposed as the scene's minimum camera scale and the view controller's minimum zoom. Pairs with [[MaxScale]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.MaxScale: Largest allowed camera zoom scale, the most zoomed-out the player can go. Also used as the reference zoom for music parameters and nebula rendering. Pairs with [[MinScale]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.MousePanBorderThickness: Thickness in pixels (scaled by the global UI scale) of the screen-edge band where holding the mouse triggers edge panning of the camera.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.MouseWheelZoomSpeed: Base rate multiplier for mouse-wheel zooming. Multiplied by the square of the player's own mouse-wheel zoom sensitivity setting when the zoom scale moves toward its target, and also factored into the zoom sound volume.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.BorderClampPanSpeed: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.FollowFactor: Smoothing factor for how the camera follows its focus target. Fed into a SmoothDamp so lower values give looser, more gradual following and higher values snap the camera to the target faster.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.AutoTrackRampTime: Seconds for auto-tracking of on-screen ships to ramp fully in or out. The tracking weight moves between 0 and 1 at a rate of delta time divided by this value.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.DirectControlOffsetFactor: Multiplier on how far the camera shifts toward the cursor during direct control when "view follows cursor" is enabled. Larger values push the framing further off the ship toward the mouse.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.DirectControlZoomFactor: Upper bound on the automatic zoom-out applied during direct control when "auto zoom view" is enabled. The zoom eases from 1 up to this factor (or the max zoom, whichever is smaller) as the cursor moves toward the screen edge.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.DirectControlZoomDeadZone: Normalized cursor distance from screen center (0..1) below which direct-control auto-zoom does nothing. Auto-zoom eases in over the range from this dead zone out to 1. Works with [[DirectControlZoomFactor]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.DirectControlSmoothStrength: Rate at which the cursor position used for direct-control aiming is smoothed toward the real mouse location each frame. Higher values track the mouse more tightly, lower values add lag.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.ScreenShakeExponent: Exponent shaping the screen-shake response curve. The summed shake amount is clamped to 1 and raised to this power before driving the shake, so values above 1 suppress weak shakes and emphasize strong ones. Only applies when the player has screen shake enabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.LinearShakeAmount: Maximum positional offset of the screen-shake, before scaling. The curved shake value multiplies this and is divided by the camera's zoom scale, then offsets the camera along both axes via [[ShakePerlinNoise]]. Rotational shake uses [[AngularShakeAmount]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.AngularShakeAmount: Maximum rotational offset of the screen-shake in degrees, before scaling. Multiplied by the curved shake value and divided by the camera zoom scale, then applied as a rotation sampled from [[ShakePerlinNoise]]. Positional counterpart is [[LinearShakeAmount]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.FTLZoomOutBufferMult: Multiplier on the extra framing margin the camera zooms out to when lining up a local FTL jump, so both the ship and its jump destination fit on screen with padding. Only applies when the player has zoom-out-on-FTL enabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.ShakePerlinNoise: Perlin noise generator sampled over clock time to produce the screen-shake motion. Separate noise channels drive the X offset, Y offset and rotation so the shake looks smooth and non-repeating. Amplitudes come from [[LinearShakeAmount]] and [[AngularShakeAmount]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules.ZoomClickSound: Looping sound played while the camera is zooming with the mouse wheel. Its playback speed scales with the current zoom, and its volume tracks the zoom rate against [[MouseWheelZoomSpeed]].

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.T:: Stores rules for a crew doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.Name: Display name given to the spawned crew member. When omitted the game generates a random name for the crew soul.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.BodyTypeIndex: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. The spawned crew's body type is derived from a random seed rather than this index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.SkinColorIndex: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. The spawned crew's skin color is derived from a random seed rather than this index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.HairColorIndex: Has no effect. The game reads this value from the rules but never uses it. The spawned crew's hair color is derived from a random seed rather than this index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.CrewDoodadR.Allegiance: Player index that owns the spawned crew member. Defaults to `-1` (neutral) when omitted.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.T:: The base class for different types of doodads.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.ID: Unique identifier for this doodad type. Must be in the form `author_name.doodad_name` (it must contain a dot with text on both sides) or loading throws an error. Other doodads and spawners reference this ID.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.OtherIDs: Additional IDs that also resolve to this doodad type. Useful as aliases so that saves or spawners referencing an old ID still load this doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.Icon: Sprite shown for this doodad in the creative-mode doodad toolbox button.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.DescriptionKey: Localization key for this doodad's display name. Shown in the toolbox tooltip, as the POI mouseover label, and used as the spawned ship's name for ship-based doodads. See [[UndiscoveredDescriptionKey]] for the name shown before a POI is discovered.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.UndiscoveredDescriptionKey: Localization key used in place of [[DescriptionKey]] while a point of interest has not yet been discovered by the player.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.CategoryKey: Localization key for the collapsible category the doodad is grouped under in the creative-mode toolbox. Doodads sharing the same key share one category box.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.HideInCreativeMode: When true, omits this doodad from the creative-mode doodad toolbox so players cannot place it manually.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.SpawnRadius: World-space radius reserved around this doodad when it is placed by a spawner or generator, keeping other objects from spawning on top of it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.DoodadRules.Tags: Set of spawner tags attached to the spawned doodad. Other systems match against these tags, for example planet damage zones use them to decide which ships should avoid the area. Tags supplied by the spawning context are merged with these.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.FtlGateDood.T:: Stores rules for an FTL Gate doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.FtlGateDood.JumpEffectsSource: Ship-local point on the gate from which FTL jump-in and jump-out media effects emanate. It is transformed to world space when a ship jumps through the gate. When omitted, the gate ship's center is used instead.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.GeneratedSh.T:: Stores rules for a doodad that is actually a randomly-generated ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.GeneratedSh.Allegiance: Player index assigned to the generated ship. Defaults to `0` when omitted.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.GeneratedSh.Generator: Ship generator that procedurally builds the ship this doodad spawns.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.LandmarkDoo.T:: Stores rules for a landmark doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.LandmarkDoo.IsFtlPoint: When true, the landmark counts as an FTL point that ships can jump to. Passed to the landmark component created for the spawned ship.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.NebulaDooda.T:: Stores rules for a nebula doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.NebulaDooda.NebulaID: Nebula type to paint into the sector at the spawn location. Placing this doodad sets the nebula cell under the point rather than creating a standalone object.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.T:: Stores rules for a point of interest doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.HudIcon: Icon shown on the HUD indicator that marks this point of interest. When omitted, no indicator is created for the doodad. Its size also sets the indicator's UI size.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.UndiscoveredHudIcon: Icon used in place of [[HudIcon]] while the point of interest is undiscovered. Falls back to [[HudIcon]] when not set.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.OverrideHudIconColor: Color for the HUD indicator. When omitted the indicator uses the player's current neutral color.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.DefaultToUndiscovered: When true, the point of interest starts undiscovered so it shows the [[UndiscoveredHudIcon]] and undiscovered description until the player reveals it. A per-instance parameter can override this.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.POIDoodadRu.IndicatorSort: Adjusts the HUD indicator's sort order relative to other point-of-interest indicators. Higher values draw on top. It is added to a large negative base so these indicators sit below most others by default.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.T:: Stores rules for a planet doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.StyleID: Planet style used to procedurally generate the planet's appearance. Resolved against the registered planet styles.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.TextureSize: Base resolution in pixels of the generated planet texture. The effective size is this multiplied by the doodad's texture scale and the player's planet-resolution graphics setting. Larger values give a sharper planet at higher memory cost.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.ScaleRange: Minimum and maximum world size the planet may take. A spawned planet's scale is picked from this range (or from [[RandomScaleRange]] if set), and manual resizing is clamped to it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.DefaultScale: World size used as the starting scale when the player places this planet manually in creative mode. It is also the reference scale for computing the planet's level-of-detail texture resolution during random spawning.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.RandomScaleRange: Overrides [[ScaleRange]] as the range a random scale is drawn from when the planet is spawned by a generator. Manual placement and resize limits still use [[ScaleRange]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.DistanceRange: Range of parallax distances from the gameplay plane the planet may sit at. Greater distance means slower parallax and a smaller apparent size. A spawned planet draws its distance from this range unless [[RandomDistanceRange]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.RandomDistanceRange: Overrides [[DistanceRange]] as the range a random distance is drawn from when the planet is spawned by a generator.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.DefaultDistance: Parallax distance used as the starting value when the player places this planet manually in creative mode. It also acts as the reference distance for the texture level-of-detail calculation when [[DistanceRange]] has a positive minimum.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.RenderStage: Render layer the planet draws on. `Lower` renders it behind gameplay objects, `Upper` in front. The stage only applies in-game, and planets fall back to `Lower` outside of a game (such as in menus).
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.IsLightSource: When true, the planet acts as a light source, contributing to the lighting normal used to shade ships. Suns set this.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.MinimapColorScale: Tint applied to the planet when it is drawn on the minimap. Defaults to white. An alpha of zero keeps the planet off the minimap entirely.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.ProximityEffects: Configures damage and visual effects inflicted on ships that come near the planet, such as a sun's heat. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDoodadRules+ProximityEffectsRules]].

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.T:: Stores rules for any proximity effects caused by a planet.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.InstantKillRadiusFactor: Multiplier on the planet's radius defining the inner zone where parts are destroyed outright and space crew are killed each tick. The zone radius is this factor times the planet's scale divided by two. It also marks the inner edge of the falloff used by the raycast effects (see [[EffectsScaleOverDistance]]). Ships treat this zone as an area to avoid.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.EffectsRadiusFactor: Multiplier on the planet's radius defining the outer zone where raycast damage and effects apply. The zone radius is this factor times the planet's scale divided by two. Ships treat this zone as an area to avoid, and the warning circle is drawn at this radius.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.EffectsRadiusFactorShipQueryBuffer: Extra world distance added when searching for ships to affect, so ships whose hull sits just outside the effects radius are still processed. Vanilla suns set this to a large shield's radius so shielded ships are caught.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.RaycastsPerDiameterPerSecond: Density of damage rays cast against each affected ship, expressed per unit of ship diameter per second. No raycast damage or effects occur when this is zero or negative.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.HitOperationalEffects: Hit effects applied when a damage ray strikes a part with operational health.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.HitStructuralEffects: Hit effects applied when a damage ray strikes a part with structural health.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.HitShieldEffects: Hit effects applied when a damage ray strikes a shield.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.EffectsScaleOverDistance: Effect strength interpolated across the falloff zone, from the inner instant-kill edge to the outer effects edge. Defaults to `[1, 0]`, so effects are full strength close to the planet and fade to nothing at the outer edge. The interpolation position is shaped by [[EffectsDistanceExponent]] and scales the hit effects and media intensity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.EffectsDistanceExponent: Exponent applied to the normalized distance before it indexes [[EffectsScaleOverDistance]], shaping the falloff curve. Values below one keep effects strong further out, values above one concentrate them near the planet.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.IgnoreShipTypes: Ship types exempted from the proximity effects. Vanilla suns list asteroids, megaroids, and ancient ships so they are not damaged.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.MediaEffects: Continuous media effects played on each affected ship, with intensity accumulated from the raycast effect strength at the points that were hit.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.WarningCircle: On-screen ring drawn at the [[EffectsRadiusFactor]] radius to warn the player of the danger zone. Rendering of the danger zone requires both this and [[EffectsRadiusFactor]] to be set.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.WarningCircleThicknessZoomExponent: Exponent applied to the camera zoom scale when computing the [[WarningCircle]] thickness, controlling how the ring's thickness responds to zooming.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.PlanetDooda.WarningMinimapCircle: Ring drawn at the effects radius on the minimap. Requires [[EffectsRadiusFactor]] to be set.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ResourceDoo.T:: Stores rules for a resource doodad.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ResourceDoo.ResourceType: Resource type of the nugget this doodad spawns. Resolved against the registered resource rules.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ResourceDoo.Quantity: Range from which the spawned nugget's resource amount is randomly picked. Defaults to `1`.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.T:: Stores rules for a point of interest doodad that also has a ring around its area.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.RingCircle: Circle renderer that draws the ring around the point of interest's area. Its thickness and texture drive the ring's appearance, including the dashed look in vanilla.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.DefaultScale: World radius given to the ring when the player places this doodad in creative mode, used for both the placement ghost and the spawned doodad's scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.CameraRelativeThickness: When true, the ring thickness scales with the camera zoom so it stays a constant apparent width on screen. When false the thickness is a fixed world size.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.DynamicUPerCircumference: Number of texture U repeats per unit of ring circumference, controlling how densely the ring texture (such as dashes) tiles around the circle. When unset the texture is drawn without dynamic tiling.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.MinimapThickness: Thickness in minimap pixels of the ring when drawn on the minimap. A value of zero keeps the ring off the minimap.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.MouseHoverColorFactor: Color multiplier blended in while the mouse hovers the point of interest's indicator. Defaults to white (no change).
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.MouseHoverColorTweenTime: Duration over which the ring tweens toward [[MouseHoverColorFactor]] as the mouse enters or leaves the indicator.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.DiscoveredAlphaTweenTime: Duration over which the ring fades in after the point of interest is discovered.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.RingedPOIDo.FadeOutSizeRange: On-screen ring size range over which the ring's alpha fades out. Rings smaller than the range's low end fade toward invisible, which hides rings that shrink too small to be useful at the current zoom.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ShipDoodadR.T:: Stores rules for a doodad that is just a pre-designed ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ShipDoodadR.Ship: Pre-designed ship blueprint that this doodad spawns. The blueprint is loaded and initialized to full health when the doodad is placed.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Doodads.ShipDoodadR.Allegiance: Player index assigned to the spawned ship. When omitted the ship keeps the allegiance from its blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.T:: Stores rules for filtering hit and media effects.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Ships: Whether ships and their parts can be affected at all. When false, every ship and part check fails regardless of the allegiance fields. True by default in every effect's built-in filter.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OperationalHealth: Allows the effect to hit parts with operational health (the normal health pool of most functional parts). A part is filtered out when the flag for its health type is false. True by default. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.StructuralHealth]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.StructuralHealth: Allows the effect to hit parts with structural health, such as armor and structure. True by default. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OperationalHealth]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OnlyPartCategories: When set, only parts whose type declares at least one of these part categories pass the filter.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.ExcludePartCategories: When set, parts whose type declares any of these part categories are filtered out.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Shields: Whether shields can be affected. Shield hits still respect [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.IgnoreInvulnerability]] and the allegiance fields, judged by the ship the shield belongs to. True by default.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Bullets: Whether projectiles can be affected. A projectile's allegiance is judged by the ship that fired it, so a projectile fired by the effect's own source ship falls under [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Self]], not [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies]]. Projectiles whose firing ship no longer exists skip the allegiance check entirely and always pass. True by default for most effects, but `AreaImpulse` presets it to false.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OnlyBulletCategories: When set, only projectiles declaring at least one of these categories in their `Targetable` rules pass the filter.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.ExcludeBulletCategories: When set, projectiles declaring any of these categories in their `Targetable` rules are filtered out.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OnlyStatuses: When set, only parts matching at least one of these status filters pass the filter.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.ExcludeStatuses: Intended to filter out parts matching any of these status filters. The current game code inverts the check, so in practice it behaves exactly like [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.OnlyStatuses]] and rejects parts that do not match.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Crew: Whether crew floating in space can be affected. Crew allegiance uses their home ship while it still exists, otherwise the crew member's own player. True by default.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Nuggets: Whether loose resource nuggets can be affected. Nuggets have no allegiance, so this flag alone decides. True by default.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.IgnoreInvulnerability: When false, ships flagged invulnerable are protected from the effect. Checked for ship and shield hits. False by default for most damage effects, but `AreaImpulse` and the bullet and crew collision filters preset it to true.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Self: Whether the effect's own source ship can be affected. This also governs projectiles fired by the source ship when [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Bullets]] filtering runs, so an effect that should not touch its own projectiles needs `Self = false` even when [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies]] is false. When unset, falls back to [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies]] and then to the game mode's normal damage rules. No effect presets this, so it is unset unless written.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.TargetedSelf: Overrides [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Self]] when the source ship is also the effect's target ship. When unset, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Self]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies: Whether allied ships (same team, including other ships of the same player) can be affected. Does not cover the effect's own source ship, which is [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Self]]. When unset, falls back to the game mode's normal damage rules. Most effects leave it unset, but `AreaImpulse` presets it to true, so it must be written as false there to spare allies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.TargetedFriendlies: Overrides [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies]] when the hit ally is also the effect's target ship. When unset, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Friendlies]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Enemies: Whether enemy ships can be affected. When unset, falls back to the game mode's normal damage rules, which normally allow damaging enemies. `AreaImpulse` presets it to true, and the bullet and crew collision filters preset it to false.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.TargetedEnemies: Overrides [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Enemies]] when the hit enemy is also the effect's target ship. Enemy projectiles targeting the effect's source ship also check this before [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Enemies]]. When unset, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Enemies]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Neutrals: Whether neutral ships (neither allied nor enemy) can be affected. When unset, falls back to the game mode's normal damage rules. `AreaImpulse` presets it to true, and the bullet and crew collision filters preset it to false.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.TargetedNeutrals: Overrides [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Neutrals]] when the hit neutral ship is also the effect's target ship. When unset, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Neutrals]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Junk: Whether junk ships (derelict debris) can be affected. When unset, falls back to the game mode's normal damage rules. `AreaImpulse` presets it to true, and the bullet and crew collision filters preset it to false.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.TargetedJunk: Overrides [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Junk]] when the junk is also the effect's target ship. When unset, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Junk]] applies.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.EffectFilter.Deconstruction: When true, only hits caused by part deconstruction pass the filter. When false, deconstruction hits are filtered out. When unset, the distinction is ignored.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.T:: Stores info for a particular speed that can be selected by the player.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.Speed: Clock scale multiplier this preset selects, where 1 is normal speed. The speed bar steps through the presets in ascending order of this value, and the current label is matched by comparing the confirmed clock scale to it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.NameKey: Localization key for the short name shown on the game-speed bar when this preset is active. Falls back to the numeric scale when unset or unmatched. See [[LongNameKey]] for the longer label.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.LongNameKey: Localization key for the longer name used in the PvP setup game-speed drop list. Companion to the shorter [[NameKey]] shown on the speed bar.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.DecreaseToSound: Sound played when the clock scale drops to this preset (the new speed is lower than the confirmed one). Counterpart to [[IncreaseToSound]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed.IncreaseToSound: Sound played when the clock scale rises to this preset (the new speed is at or above the confirmed one). Counterpart to [[DecreaseToSound]].

Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.T:: Knocks out every crew member within `Radius` of the impact for `Duration`, with the stun weakening toward the edge.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Duration: The stun length, in seconds, rolled at random between Min and Max for each affected crew member and then multiplied by the distance falloff factor. A Max of 0 or less disables the effect. Stunning an already stunned crew member keeps the longer of the two times unless [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrewStunEffectRules.Cumulative]] is set.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Radius: The radius, in tiles, of the world-space circle around the impact point within which crew are stunned. At 0 or less the effect does nothing.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Falloff: The exponent shaping how the stun duration weakens with distance. The base factor runs linearly from 1 at the epicenter to 0 at the edge of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrewStunEffectRules.Radius]] and is raised to this power, so values above 1 concentrate the stun near the center while 0 stuns everyone in range at full duration. Defaults to 1.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Delay: Seconds to wait after the hit before the stun is applied. During the wait the effect point follows the motion of the ship that was hit. Defaults to 0.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Filter: The filter deciding which ships and which crew's current parts can be affected. Defaults to enemy ships only. The vanilla cannon deck's overclock self-stun sets `Friendlies = true` and `IgnoreInvulnerability = true` so it can stun its own crew.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.Cumulative: Adds the new stun time onto a crew member's remaining stun instead of keeping only the longer of the two. The vanilla cannon deck uses this so repeated overclocked shots stack up crew stun.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaCrew.HitShipOnly: Restricts the stun to crew on the ship that was actually hit. When false, the default, crew on every ship intersecting the circle can be stunned.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.T:: Damages every part within `Radius` of the impact at once, weakening toward the edge by `Falloff`.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.Damage: The damage dealt at the epicenter, in health points. Unlike the `ExplosiveDamage` effect there is no shared pool, every tile, bullet, and crew member in the circle is damaged independently, scaled down by [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDamageEffectRules.Falloff]] with distance and multiplied by the game mode's damage factor. Against shields it acts as damage per meter of shield arc inside the circle. The effect is skipped entirely when both this and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDamageEffectRules.DamagePerTileHealth]] resolve to 0.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.DamagePerTileHealth: Extra damage dealt to each affected tile equal to this fraction of the hit part's per-tile health (its max health divided by its footprint in tiles), defaulting to 0. Applied without falloff or damage-factor scaling, so `1` wipes out a part's tile-share of health outright. Only applies to ship parts, not shields, bullets, or crew.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.DamageType: The damage type of the inflicted hits, checked against the resistances of the parts, shields, and targetable bullets that receive them. Defaults to the default damage type.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.SpawnUnderlying: Whether parts destroyed by this damage spawn their underlying part (normally structure) in their place. Set to false to make destroyed parts vanish outright. Has no effect when the triggering hit already forbids spawning underlying parts.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.Radius: The radius of the damaged circle, in tiles. Tiles whose centers fall inside the circle are damaged, processed nearest to the epicenter first. Nothing happens when it is 0 or negative.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.RectType: Which footprint is used to find the part occupying each damaged cell. `Physical` respects a part's `PhysicalRect` when it declares one, so cells outside that rect hit nothing there. `Normal` matches every cell of the part's full footprint. The vanilla overclocked large laser bolt uses `Normal`.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.Falloff: The exponent shaping how damage drops from full at the epicenter to zero at the circle's edge, defaulting to 1. The linear distance fraction is raised to this power, so `1` is a straight linear falloff, `0` disables falloff so the full damage applies everywhere inside the circle, and larger values concentrate damage near the center. Does not apply to [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDamageEffectRules.DamagePerTileHealth]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.Delay: Seconds waited before the damage is applied, defaulting to 0. While waiting, the blast point stays anchored to the hit ship, or keeps drifting at that ship's last velocity if the ship ceases to exist. Vanilla railgun parts delay their death blast by 0.15 seconds so destruction visibly chains from segment to segment.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.Filter: Which kinds of objects the blast can damage. Defaults to enemy ships (both operational and structural health), shields, crew, and nuggets, with bullets excluded. Vanilla railgun parts add `Friendlies = true` to their death blast so a destroyed segment damages the neighboring segments of its own ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaDama.CrewKillChance: The chance, as a 0..1 fraction defaulting to 1, that a crew member in the area is harmed at all. Rolled once per crew member, and crew that fail the roll are skipped entirely. Crew that pass take the normal falloff-scaled damage.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.T:: Shoves nearby ships away from the impact point with a single physics kick.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.Impulse: The strength of the impulse. Ship hulls receive it per part tile within the radius, applied at each tile, and shields per tile of arc length within the radius. Bullets, crew, and resource nuggets each receive the full amount. Negative values pull toward the center instead of pushing away. At 0 the effect does nothing.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.Radius: The radius, in tiles, of the affected circle around the effect point. Nothing happens when 0 or less.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.Falloff: The exponent shaping how the impulse fades with distance from the center, multiplying its strength by `(1 - distance/radius)^Falloff`. Defaults to 1, a linear fade to zero at the rim. 0 removes the falloff entirely.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.InvertFalloff: Reverses the falloff to `(distance/radius)^Falloff`, so strength grows from zero at the center to full at the rim. The overclocked vanilla tractor beam emitter pairs this with a negative [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpulseEffectRules.Impulse]] for its pull burst.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.Delay: Seconds to wait before the impulse is applied. During the wait the effect point follows the hit ship's movement, or drifts on at that ship's last velocity if it is destroyed.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.HitEffects.AreaImpu.UseEffectDirection: Pushes everything along the hit effect's world direction instead of radially away from the center point.
