Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Dynami.ZoomFalloff: Exponent shaping the volume fade between [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.DynamicVolumeRules.MinZoom]] and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.DynamicVolumeRules.MaxZoom]]. 1 fades linearly and higher values fade out more quickly as the player zooms out.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Dynami.PlayAtZeroVolume: Starts one-shot sounds even when their computed volume is currently 0, which would normally skip the play entirely. The sound can then become audible if the camera moves, zooms, or regains sight while it is still playing.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Dynami.ExteriorVolume: Volume multiplier blended in proportionally to the roof opacity of the relevant ship. At full roof opacity the sound plays at exactly this multiplier, and with the roof faded out it plays unmodified. Vanilla interior ambience uses 0 so machinery is only heard while the interior is visible. Defaults to 1.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.T:: The named draw-order slots visual effects sort into, running from under the ship up to over the roof. An effect picks one by name in its `Bucket` field.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.LowerBuckets: Declares the named effect buckets that render below ships' floors but above their base structure layer, mapped to render buckets -1000 upward in list order so later entries draw on top of earlier ones. Holds at most 1000 names, and every bucket name must be unique across all five lists. The first bucket declared here is also the default bucket for `Particles` effects that specify none, which is `BulletLower1` in vanilla.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.InteriorSurfaceBuckets: Declares the named effect buckets that render above ships' floor layers but below their walls, doors, and crew, mapped to render buckets 1 upward in list order. Holds at most 97 names. Vanilla uses this band for interior effects such as fire, smoke, foam, and scorch marks.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.MiddleBuckets: Declares the named effect buckets that render above ships' walls and crew but below their weapons and roofs, mapped to render buckets 100 upward in list order. Holds at most 1000 names. Must contain the `default_bullet` bucket, the default render bucket for bullet sprites.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.SurfaceBuckets: Declares the named effect buckets that render above ships' roofs and roof turrets but below their fancy roof lights and crew in space, mapped to render buckets 2000 upward in list order. Holds at most 1000 names. Vanilla uses this band for on-hull effects such as thermal laser hits and scaffolding glows.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.UpperBuckets: Declares the named effect buckets that render above everything ship-related, including roof lights, space crew, and part indicators, mapped to render buckets 4000 upward in list order. Holds at most 1000 names. Vanilla puts muzzle flashes, beams, thruster plumes, and most explosion flashes here.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.T:: One piece of the sound and visuals an event produces, such as a sprite, a beam, a particle system or a sound. A modder writes one of its concrete types.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.Delay: Seconds the effect waits after being triggered before it actually plays. Applies only to one-shot playback, continuous playback always starts immediately. Being modifiable, it can be driven by buffs carried in the effect's parameters.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MediaE.IgnoreIntensity: Has no effect. The game stores the value but no media effect type ever reads it.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MultiM.T:: A list of media effects that all play together for the same event.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.MultiM.Effects: The sub-effects making up this media effect, each a group whose `Type` picks the effect kind: `Beam`, `Quad`, `PartQuad`, `TileQuad`, `ArcShield`, `Particles`, `Audio`, `ScreenShake`, or `Random`. All entries are created on the same node and play in unison whenever the containing effect is triggered. Because the field's serialization alias is empty, the list is normally written directly as the containing field's value, as in `HitEffects [ { Type = Particles ... } ]`.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.T:: Draws a sprite stretched across a whole part, for glows and overlays that ride along as the part moves.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.RectType: Which rectangle of the hit part the quad covers, either the part's full footprint (`Normal`, the default) or its declared PhysicalRect (`Physical`). The effect requires a hit part in its parameters and fails without one, so it is only usable in contexts that hit a part.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.Inflate: Distance, in tiles, the part's rectangle is expanded on every side before the quad is drawn. The vanilla ship salvage progress glow inflates by 0.5 so the glow bleeds past the part's edges.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.Z: Has no effect. The part quad renderer never reads it, it builds the quad from the part rect alone. The identically named [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEffectRules.Z]] on a plain quad effect is the one that works.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.ColorOverIntensity: A color multiplier sampled between Min and Max by the effect's current smoothed intensity, applied on top of the sprite's vertex color and the effect's color parameter. Defaults to a constant white. The vanilla salvage progress glow samples from transparent black to white so the quad brightens with salvage progress.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.PartQu.ColorOverFade: A color multiplier sampled by the fade progress, at Min when fully faded out and at Max when fully faded in, following the fade-in, hold, and fade-out times inherited from the base quad effect. Defaults to transparent white through white, a pure alpha fade.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Plays a particle system at the effect's position, pairing a shared `Def` that describes the particles with an `EmitterDef` that sets how fast they come out.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Def: The definition of the particle system the emitted particles live in, containing the initializers, updaters, and renderers that drive their behavior and appearance. Emission counts declared inside it are ignored because the system's own emission is disabled. All particles come from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.EmitterDef]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.EmitterDef: The emitter that feeds particles into the system, carrying the per-second emission rate and the burst size per one-shot. One-shot plays emit a single burst from it while continuous plays run it every frame until the effect ends. Its output is multiplied by the `ScaleEmissionWith` fields.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Bucket: The effect bucket the particles render in, which determines their draw order relative to ships and other effects. Bucket names are declared in the ordered lists of `common_effects/effect_buckets.rules`. Defaults to the first bucket in that render order.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UseRealTime: Updates the particle system with the real-time application clock instead of the simulation clock, so the particles keep animating while the simulation is paused or its speed is changed. The vanilla mine's range ring uses this.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.EmitImmediately: Whether the emitter should be created with 1 accumulated particle emission.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.PenetratingBucket: An alternate bucket used instead of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.Bucket]] when the effect is played with the penetrating flag set, which happens when a projectile hit penetrates through the part it struck. Most vanilla projectile hit effects switch to `Middle2` in that case so the hit visuals render at interior depth.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.MinIntensity: The effect intensity below which no particles are emitted. A continuous effect keeps updating its existing particles and resumes emission once the intensity reaches this value again.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IsFancy: Marks the effect as a fancy version that only plays while the Fancy Particles graphics setting is enabled. Pair it with a fallback effect that sets [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.IsSimple]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IsFancyLight: Marks the effect as a fancy lighting version that only plays while the Fancy Lighting graphics setting is enabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IsSimpleLight: Marks the effect as a lighting fallback that only plays while the Fancy Lighting graphics setting is disabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IsSimple: Marks the effect as a fallback that only plays while the Fancy Particles graphics setting is disabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ToggleWithRoofOpacity: Ties emission to roof visibility. When set, no particles are emitted while the roof of the relevant ship (the hit ship unless overridden) is fully faded out, as with the vanilla resonance beam's hit smoke that stops while the ship's interior is shown.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Sharing: `None` gives each play of the effect its own particle system attached to the effect's node. `Global` emits into a world-space particle system shared by every effect with the same [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.Def]], bucket, real-time flag, and back-buffer flag, which batches frequently spammed effects such as the vanilla tractor beam glints and resonance beam hit sparks.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UnsharedRenderInWorldSpace: Renders an unshared particle system in world space instead of the local space of the node the effect is attached to. Only applies when [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.Sharing]] is `None`, since shared systems always render in world space.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DontEmitWhenOffScreen: Suppresses emission while the effect cannot be seen, meaning its location is outside the inflated main view and miniview rectangles or outside the local player's sight range. Particles that were already emitted still update normally. Vanilla part explosions disable this so the debris exists when the player pans over to the wreck.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DontEmitWhenOffScreenSizeInflate: The margin in tiles added around the view rectangles for the off-screen emission check, and also the radius of the circle used for the player-sight check. Only relevant while [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleEffectRules.DontEmitWhenOffScreen]] is enabled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UseCustomShapeForOffScreenCheck: Runs the off-screen and sight checks against the custom shape supplied by the effect's source, such as a beam's line or the tiles covered by a status effect, instead of the effect node's single point. Vanilla fire particles use this so a fire spanning several tiles still emits when its origin point is just off screen.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.MaxEmissionZoom: The camera zoom scale above which emission stops, where a higher scale means the camera is zoomed further out. Lets fine detail effects stop emitting once they would be too small to see, as with vanilla fire particles at 15 and the shield overload sizzle at 30. Unset means no zoom limit.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.MaxParticleCount: A soft cap on the number of live particles in the effect's particle system. Emission is multiplied by the remaining fraction of the cap, so it tapers off smoothly as the count approaches the limit. The vanilla fire base effect caps at 10000.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleEmissionWithIntensity: Multiplies the emission amount by the effect's current intensity. Vanilla fire particles use this so more intense fires emit more.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleEmissionWithBeamLength: Multiplies the emission amount by the beam length supplied by the playing weapon, so longer beams emit proportionally more particles. Used by the vanilla tractor beam glints.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleEmissionWithWorldVelocity: Multiplies the emission amount by the speed of the effect's world velocity, typically the velocity of the projectile or object playing it. The vanilla EMP missile's thruster lightning uses this.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleEmissionWithPartSize: Multiplies the emission amount by the hit part's area in tiles (width times height), falling back to 1 when no part is involved. Vanilla salvage and construction poof effects use this so larger parts make larger bursts.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleEmissionWithPartPhysicalSize: Multiplies the emission amount by the area of the hit part's physical size rather than its full logical footprint. The vanilla shield overload sizzle scales with this.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.CaptureBackBuffer: Captures the scene rendered so far and binds it as the `CapturedBackBuffer` shader texture before the particles draw, letting distortion shaders sample and warp the image behind them. Used by vanilla shockwave and heat distortion particles.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Filter: A filter matched against what the effect hit, such as the hit ship, part, shield, bullet, or crew member. When the filter rejects the target, the effect does not play. Vanilla fire sparks restrict themselves to ship hits this way.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Draws the particles into the light buffer so they light up what is around them instead of only being drawn over it.
Draws particles as quads shaded by the scene lighting, taking each particle's surface normal from `LightNormalIn`.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LightNormalIn: The data that stores the particle locations.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DiffuseShader: The shader used when rendering to the diffuse target.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.NormalsShader: The shader used when rendering to the normals target.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Draws each particle as a jagged lightning bolt running from `SourceLocationIn` to `DestLocationIn`, with noise bending the segments.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LineSprite: The sprite drawn for each segment of the bolt, tinted by the sprite's vertex color times the particle's color. Each segment advances the texture's V coordinate by one UV-rect height, walking down the texture along the bolt. When unset, segments are drawn as plain untextured quads in the particle's color.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LineThickness: The thickness of the bolt, in tiles, tapering from Max at the bolt's source to Min approaching its destination and multiplied by the particle's scale data from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ParticleRenderers.ParticleLightningRenderer.ScaleIn]]. The vanilla FTL charge lightning tapers from 1.5 down to 0.1.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.EnableLightningShaderAnimation: Enables animating the vertex color along the entire bolt for use by the lightning shader.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BlendLightningShaderAnimation: If lightning shader animation is enabled, enables blending between it and the original vertex color over the lifetime of the bolt.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UseSameSeedForEntireBolt: When not enabled (the default behavior), changes the noise seed per bolt segment so each segments motion is more random.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IgnoreBoltEndingOverride: If lightning shader animation is enabled, disables the default behavior of overriding the animation for the bolts ending segment with values to make the bolts ending fade smoothly.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IgnoreBoltStartOverride: If lightning shader animation is enabled, disables the default behavior of overriding the animation for the bolts starting segment with values to make the bolts start fade smoothly.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LightningShaderAnimationSegments: If lightning shader animation is enabled, controls the number of animated slices (bright sections) the bolt should have.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.TimeShiftPerSegment: Shifts the perlin noise sample forward or backwards in time incrementally for each bolt segment.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.AnimationIntensity: If lightning shader animation and blending are enabled, controls the intensity of the lightning shader animation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.SegmentOverlap: Shifts the endpoint of each segment forward by this amount.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.SourceLocationIn: The data that stores the particle source locations.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DestLocationIn: The data that stores the particle destination locations.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleIn: The data, if any, that stores the particle scale factors.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ColorIn: The data, if any, that stores the particle colors.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UVRectIn: The data, if any, that stores the particle UVs.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.TimeIn: The data that stores the particle time.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.SeedIn: The data that stores the particle seed.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DistPerSegment: The approximate distance per segment which will determine how many segments to use.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.XOffsetPerlin: The perlin noise to add to the lightning's point X offsets.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.YOffsetPerlin: The perlin noise to add to the lightning's point Y offsets.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BulgeExponent: The amount that the lightning bolt will "bulge" near its center.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Draws particles as quads that carry a second color as well, for shaders that blend between two tints.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Color2In: The data that stores the 2nd set of particle colors.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Adds the motion of whatever the effect is riding on into each particle's velocity, so a trail drifts along with its ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityInOut: The data that stores the converted location.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Turns each new particle to point the way it is travelling, so streaks and sparks lie along their own motion.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityIn: The data that stores the particle's velocity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RotationInOut: The data that stores the particle's rotation.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Hands out `Vector2A` and `Vector2B` in turn to successive particles, the way the chaingun ejects casings to alternating sides.
Writes each particle's index into a variable so later updaters can vary a value from one particle to the next.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IndexOut: The data that will be set to the particle's index.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Stops particles at a barrier plane the game moves at runtime, which is how a bullet trail is cut off at the point of impact.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BarrierIDIn: The index of the particle barrier.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationIn: The data that stores the location of the particle.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Tints each new particle with the color of whatever spawned the effect.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ColorOut: The data that stores the particle color.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Packs two float variables into a single Vector2 variable.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DataXIn: The data used for X in the output Vector2.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DataYIn: The data used for Y in the output Vector2.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Tints each new particle with the current crew member's color.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ColorOut: The data that stores the particle color.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at the far end of the effect's shape, such as the point where a beam terminates.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the end point.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Spreads a frame's worth of new particles back along their velocity so a stream does not clump into blobs at low frame rates.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationInOut: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityIn: The data that stores the particle's velocity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Mode: The particle location compensation mode to use.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Strength: The strength of the FPS compensation.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Writes the surface normal of the impact into a variable, so sparks can spray back out off the surface that was hit.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.HitNormalOut: The data that will be set to the hit normal.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Adds the world velocity of the effect's source into each particle's velocity, so a muzzle flash carries the ship's motion.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityInOut: The data that stores the converted location.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Works out each particle's lighting normal from where it sits in the world, feeding a renderer that shades particles to match the scene.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationIn: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LightNormalOut: The data that stores the particle's light normal.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Stops particles at a barrier plane whose position and facing come from other particle variables, with no help from the simulation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationIn: The data that stores the location of the particle.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BarrierLocationIn: The location of the particle barrier.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BarrierNormalIn: The normal of the particle barrier.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.InvertNormal: Whether to invert the barrier normal.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at a random point on the effect's shape and reads out the value the shape carries there.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ValueOut: The value associated with the particle's location.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at a random point on the effect's shape, such as somewhere along a beam or across a burning tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at a random point inside a part's rectangle, in ship coordinates so the particles ride along with the ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RectType: Which type of part rect to use.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Inflate: The amount by which the part's rect is inflated.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RestrictToPartColliders: Whether the particle locations should be restricted to the part's collision geometry.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.SubtractPartCenter: Whether the particle locations should be ship or rules relative.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RotateByDirection: Whether the part rect should be rotated by the part direction in ship space.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at the point the effect was spawned from.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Turns a rotation variable into a unit Vector2 pointing that way.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RotationIn: The data that stores the particle's rotation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.NormalOut: The data that stores a normal representation of the input rotation.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Shifts a particle variable by `Offset` times the particle's index, to step a burst out in even increments.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.DataInOut: The data that will be offset based upon the index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IndexIn: The index that will be used to offset the data.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Offset: The offset that will be multiplied with the particle's index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Modulus: The value by which the index will be modulo'ed before being multiplied with Offset. Use 0 to disable.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Spreads rotations evenly around the circle by particle index rather than purely at random, so a burst of debris leaves no gaps.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.SafetyMargin: The margin that is used to restrict the rotational slice to avoid similar end rotations.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Turns a Vector2 direction into the rotation angle that points along it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.NormalIn: The data that stores a normal representation of the input rotation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RotationOut: The data that stores the particle's rotation.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Sizes each new particle by the current camera zoom, keeping an effect readable whether the view is close in or far out.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleOut: The data that stores the particle's scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleFactor: The factor by which the zoom will be scaled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ZoomExponent: The exponent that will be applied to the zoom.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Sizes each new particle by the effect's current intensity, so a stronger effect throws bigger particles.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleOut: The data that stores the particle's scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.ScaleFactor: The factor by which the intensity will be scaled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IntensityExponent: The exponent that will be applied to the intensity.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Copies the firing bullet's barrier id onto each particle, pairing a trail with the barrier that will cut it off when the bullet lands.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.BarrierIDOut: The index of the particle barrier.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Mirrors a particle's texture coordinates left to right or top to bottom, so one sprite frame can be reused flipped.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.FlipXYIn: The data that stores the particle's sprite index.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.UvRectInOut: The data that stores the particle's UV rect coordinates.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Launches each new particle at a speed scaled by the effect's current intensity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityOut: The data that stores the particle's velocity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.VelocityFactor: The factor by which the intensity will be scaled.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.IntensityExponent: The exponent that will be applied to the intensity.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.T:: Places each new particle at a random point inside a part's rectangle, in world coordinates so the particles are left behind as the ship moves on.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RectType: Which type of part rect to use.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.Inflate: The amount by which the part's rect is inflated.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Partic.RestrictToPartColliders: Whether the particle locations should be restricted to the part's collision geometry.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEf.T:: Draws a single sprite at the effect's position, for muzzle flashes, glows and impact flares.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEf.Z: The depth coordinate given to the quad's vertices, passed through to the sprite's shader.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEf.IntensityScaleFactor: Scales the quad with the effect's intensity. When nonzero, the quad's world size is the sprite's size times the intensity raised to [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEffectRules.IntensityScaleExponent]] times this factor. At 0, the default, intensity does not affect size and the sprite draws at its natural size. The vanilla resonance beam's hit flash uses 4.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEf.IntensityScaleExponent: The exponent applied to the effect's intensity when computing the quad's size with [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEffectRules.IntensityScaleFactor]]. Values below 1 damp the growth, as with the 0.5 used by the vanilla ion and resonance beam hit flashes.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEf.RandomTimeOffset: The range, in seconds, from which a random time offset is rolled each time the quad starts playing. The value is passed to the sprite's shader per vertex, letting shader animations desynchronize between quads. Defaults to `[0, 1]`.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.T:: Picks one of several media effect sets at random every time the effect plays, weighted by each option's `RandomWeight`.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.RandomOptions: The candidate effect sets. Each time this effect plays, one set is picked at random with probability proportional to its [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.RandomMediaEffectRules+EffectSet.RandomWeight]] and all of that set's media effects are played together.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.Deterministic: Draws the random pick from the simulation's deterministic random stream instead of the purely visual one, so every client and replay picks the same option. The stream's state is restored afterwards, leaving simulation behavior unaffected.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.T:: One weighted option inside a random media effect, holding the effects that play when it is the one picked.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.RandomWeight: The relative likelihood of this set being picked, proportional to the summed weight of all entries in [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.RandomMediaEffectRules.RandomOptions]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Random.MediaEffects: The media effects played when this set is picked. They all play together, and the surrounding Random effect counts as finished once every effect of the picked set has finished.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.T:: Shakes the camera, harder the closer the view is to the effect and fading out over `Duration`.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.ShakeAmount: Strength multiplier for the shake fed into the camera's screen shake controller, which converts it into positional and angular jitter. The applied amount is further scaled by the effect's intensity, the distance factor, and the remaining-duration falloff. Defaults to 1.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.Duration: Seconds the shake lasts after it starts, decaying to nothing over this time following [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.DurationFalloff]]. A continuously played shake instead holds full strength until ended and then decays over this duration. Defaults to 1.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.DurationFalloff: Exponent applied to the fraction of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.Duration]] still remaining when computing the shake strength. 1 decays linearly to zero and higher values fade the shake out sooner. Defaults to 1.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.MaxDistance: The distance from the camera center at which the shake has no effect. Distance is measured in view-relative units where 1 spans from the center of the screen to its edge, so the falloff region scales with zoom. The float-max default disables distance attenuation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.MinDistance: The view-relative distance up to which the shake applies at full strength. Between here and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.MaxDistance]] the strength falls off along the [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.DistanceFalloff]] curve.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.DistanceFalloff: Exponent shaping the strength falloff between [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.MinDistance]] and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScreenShakeEffectRules.MaxDistance]]. 1 is linear and higher values fall off more quickly.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.Screen.Filter: Conditions on what the effect hit, such as ship allegiance, part categories, shields, bullets, or crew, that must pass for the shake to occur. The filter is re-checked every frame while the shake is active, dropping the strength to zero whenever the conditions stop holding.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.T:: Draws a sprite over a single ship tile, for per-tile overlays such as fire, foam and scorch marks.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.Inflate: The value to inflate the quad's rect by.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.Z: Has no effect. The tile quad renderer never reads it, it builds the quad from the ship cell rect alone. The identically named [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.QuadEffectRules.Z]] on a plain quad effect is the one that works.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.ColorOverIntensity: The color range to sample by the intensity.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.ColorOverFade: The color range to sample by the fade value.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.MediaEffects.TileQu.DisableQuadRotation: Whether to keep the quad rotationally aligned with the world-axes instead of the ship.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules.T:: Stores rules for the networking logic.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules.InputTicksPerSecond: Rate of lockstep input ticks per second for multiplayer simulation. The interval between ticks is its reciprocal, and it converts input delays measured in seconds to a tick count.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules.MinInputTickDelay: Smallest number of input ticks that player commands are buffered ahead of execution. Used as the starting delay and as the lower clamp on the latency-derived delay.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules.MaxInputTickDelay: Largest input tick delay allowed. Upper clamp on the latency-derived delay so a bad connection cannot push command lag arbitrarily high.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules.InputTickDelayLatencyFactor: Multiplier applied to measured network latency when the host computes how much input delay to use. The scaled latency is converted to ticks via InputTicksPerSecond and clamped to MinInputTickDelay..MaxInputTickDelay.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.T:: Stores the definition for a three-slices capped line and exposes methods to render it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.LineSprite: Sprite drawn as the middle segment of the line, stretched between the begin and end points as a single rotated quad whose height is [[LineThickness]]. When omitted, no line body is drawn and only the caps appear.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.LineThickness: Height of the line body quad in world units. Also feeds the render bounds, which grow to the larger of this and the cap sizes.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.LineBeginOverhang: Pulls the begin point inward toward the end by this many world units before drawing, shortening the line at its start. Negative values extend it past the begin point. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.LineEndOverhang: Pulls the end point inward toward the begin by this many world units before drawing, shortening the line at its end. Negative values extend it past the end point. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.LineUPerLength: Scales the line sprite's U texture coordinate by the line's length so the texture tiles or scrolls along the line instead of stretching once. When nonzero, the UV width is multiplied by length times this value and the U origin is offset by the caller's length offset times this value. Zero leaves the sprite's UV untouched.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.BeginCapSprite: Sprite drawn as an end cap at the begin point of the line, sized by [[BeginCapSize]]. Omit for no begin cap.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.BeginCapSize: Width and height of the begin cap quad in world units. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.BeginCapOverlap: Shifts the begin cap toward the line center by this many world units so it overlaps the line body rather than butting against it. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.EndCapSprite: Sprite drawn as an end cap at the end point of the line, sized by [[EndCapSize]]. Omit for no end cap.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.EndCapSize: Width and height of the end cap quad in world units. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.CappedLine.EndCapOverlap: Shifts the end cap toward the line center by this many world units so it overlaps the line body rather than butting against it. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.T:: Stores the definition for a nine-sliced sprite and exposes methods to render it.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.TopLeftSprite: Sprite for the top-left corner cell of the nine-slice, drawn at a fixed size given by the left and top [[Borders]]. Corner cells never stretch. Omit any slice to leave that cell empty.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.TopSprite: Sprite for the top edge cell, spanning between the left and right corners. Stretches horizontally with the rectangle unless [[EdgeCenterUPerWidth]] makes it tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.TopRightSprite: Sprite for the top-right corner cell, drawn at a fixed size given by the right and top [[Borders]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.LeftSprite: Sprite for the left edge cell, spanning between the top and bottom corners. Stretches vertically with the rectangle unless [[EdgeCenterVPerHeight]] makes it tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.CenterSprite: Sprite for the center cell, filling the area inside all four [[Borders]]. Stretches in both axes unless [[EdgeCenterUPerWidth]] or [[EdgeCenterVPerHeight]] make it tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.RightSprite: Sprite for the right edge cell, spanning between the top and bottom corners. Stretches vertically with the rectangle unless [[EdgeCenterVPerHeight]] makes it tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.BottomLeftSprite: Sprite for the bottom-left corner cell, drawn at a fixed size given by the left and bottom [[Borders]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.BottomSprite: Sprite for the bottom edge cell, spanning between the left and right corners. Stretches horizontally with the rectangle unless [[EdgeCenterUPerWidth]] makes it tile.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.BottomRightSprite: Sprite for the bottom-right corner cell, drawn at a fixed size given by the right and bottom [[Borders]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.Borders: Left, top, right, and bottom inset widths in world units that mark where the nine cells meet. The corner and edge sprites occupy these insets while the center fills what remains. Scaled by the caller's border scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.Bleed: Left, top, right, and bottom amounts by which the drawn rectangle is expanded outward before slicing, so the sprites bleed past the nominal bounds. Scaled by the caller's border scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.EdgeCenterUPerWidth: Tiles the horizontal-spanning cells (top, bottom, center) along U by multiplying their UV width by the rectangle width times this value, instead of stretching a single copy. Zero stretches the sprite to fit.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.NineSlice.EdgeCenterVPerHeight: Tiles the vertical-spanning cells (left, right, center) along V by multiplying their UV height by the rectangle height times this value, instead of stretching a single copy. Zero stretches the sprite to fit.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.T:: Defines, builds geometry for, and renders a three-slice capped line with an additional horizontal slice allowing rendering of one or both of the top or bottom halves of the sprites.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.LineSprite: Sprite drawn as the middle segment of the line, stretched between the begin and end points as a single rotated quad whose height is [[LineThickness]]. The sprite is sliced horizontally so callers can render its top half, bottom half, or both. When omitted, no line body is drawn and only the caps appear.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.LineThickness: Height of the line body quad in world units.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.SplitRelativeThickness: Whether the line thickness and cap sizes are halved when rendering only one half of the horizontally sliced sprites.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.LineBeginOverhang: Pulls the begin point inward toward the end by this many world units before drawing, shortening the line at its start. Negative values extend it past the begin point. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.LineEndOverhang: Pulls the end point inward toward the begin by this many world units before drawing, shortening the line at its end. Negative values extend it past the end point. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.LineUPerLength: Scales the line sprite's U texture coordinate by the line's length so the texture tiles or scrolls along the line instead of stretching once. When nonzero, the UV width is multiplied by length times this value and the U origin is offset by the caller's length offset times this value. Zero leaves the sprite's UV untouched.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.BeginCapSprite: Sprite drawn as an end cap at the begin point of the line, sized by [[BeginCapSize]] and sliced to the same top/bottom half as the line body. Omit for no begin cap.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.BeginCapSize: Width and height of the begin cap quad in world units. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.BeginCapOverlap: Shifts the begin cap toward the line center by this many world units so it overlaps the line body rather than butting against it. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.EndCapSprite: Sprite drawn as an end cap at the end point of the line, sized by [[EndCapSize]] and sliced to the same top/bottom half as the line body. Omit for no end cap.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.EndCapSize: Width and height of the end cap quad in world units. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.Overlays.SplitCappe.EndCapOverlap: Shifts the end cap toward the line center by this many world units so it overlaps the line body rather than butting against it. Scaled by the caller's thickness/cap scale.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.T:: Stores rules for the in-simulation gameplay GUI and overlays.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipTextColorFactor: Multiplied into the color of ship name text shown in the world, such as ship indicator labels and mouseover names, after the allegiance or indicator color is chosen. Vanilla uses it to make ship text slightly transparent.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectionOutlineSprite: The border of the rectangle drawn while dragging a box selection around ships. Its color is tinted by the local player's color. When the camera focus mode is active, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusOutlineSprite]] is drawn instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectionFillSprite: The translucent interior of the drag selection rectangle, tinted by the local player's color. Drawn together with [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectionOutlineSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusOutlineSprite: The border of the drag selection rectangle while the camera focus cursor mode is active, replacing [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectionOutlineSprite]]. Unlike the normal selection rectangle it is not tinted by the player color.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusFillSprite: The interior of the drag selection rectangle while the camera focus cursor mode is active, replacing [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectionFillSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCircle: The circle drawn around a ship under the mouse cursor that is not yet selected, previewing what a click would select. Tinted by the ship's allegiance color. Ships concealed inside a nebula use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HiddenTentativeShipCircle]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HiddenTentativeShipCircle: Replaces [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCircle]] for hovered ships that are hidden inside a nebula. Vanilla gives it a different dash pattern to signal the contact is concealed.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCrewCircle: The circle drawn around each crew member who is assigned to a hovered ship but currently outside it in space. Crew whose distance warning is active use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningCircle]] instead. Selected ships use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCrewCircle]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeScheduledNuggetCollectSprite: Icon drawn over each nugget that a ship under the mouse cursor has already been ordered to collect, previewing that ship's scheduled pickups before you select it. The equivalent icon for ships you have selected is [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedScheduledNuggetCollectSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeNuggetCollectSprite: Icon drawn over a nugget that the selected ships are able to collect, shown when hovering the nugget and over each nugget inside the drag selection rectangle in salvage collection mode. Swapped for [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeNuggetCantCollectSprite]] when collection is not possible.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeNuggetCantCollectSprite: Icon drawn over a hovered nugget when none of the selected ships can collect it, for example because they lack storage capacity or are too far away. The collectable counterpart is [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeNuggetCollectSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCancelCollectSprite: Icon drawn over a nugget whose scheduled collection would be cancelled, shown when hovering a nugget with a pending pickup in cancel mode and over nuggets inside the cancel drag rectangle in salvage collection mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCrewLine: The line connecting a hovered ship to each of its crew members who are out in space, drawn from the ship's bounding circle to the crew member. Shown only when the show space crew lines setting is enabled, except that crew with a distance warning always get [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningLine]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipVelocityLine: The arrow line drawn from a selected or hovered ship's selection circle in its direction of travel, indicating current linear velocity. Its length comes from the velocity times [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipVelocityLineScale]] and it fades out at very low speeds. Also drawn for all on-screen ships when the velocity indicator display setting is set to all.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipVelocityLineScale: Multiplies the ship's linear velocity to get the world-space length of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipVelocityLine]]. Because velocity is in tiles per second, the value is effectively the number of seconds of travel the line's length represents.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityCircle: The arc drawn just outside a ship's selection circle to indicate its current rotation speed and direction. The arc's angular width is the angular velocity times [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityScale]] and it fades out at very low rotation speeds. An arrowhead from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityArrow]] is drawn at its far end.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityArrow: The arrowhead sprite drawn at the leading end of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityCircle]], pointing in the direction of rotation.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityScale: Multiplies the ship's angular velocity in radians per second to get the angular width of the [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipAngularVelocityCircle]] arc. The value is effectively the number of seconds of rotation the arc represents.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircle: The circle drawn around each ship the player currently has selected, tinted by the ship's allegiance color. When first selected its color tweens from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenFromColor]] over [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenTime]]. Ships concealed inside a nebula use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HiddenSelectedShipCircle]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HiddenSelectedShipCircle: Replaces [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircle]] for selected ships that are hidden inside a nebula. Vanilla gives it a different dash pattern.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenTime: Seconds over which a newly selected ship's selection circle color fades from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenFromColor]] to its normal color, producing a brief flash on selection.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenFromColor: Multiplier applied to the selection circle's color at the moment a ship is selected, which then fades back to the normal color over [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCircleTweenTime]]. Vanilla uses an over-bright alpha so the circle flashes when selection starts.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCrewCircle: The circle drawn around each crew member who is assigned to a selected ship but currently outside it in space. Crew with an active distance warning use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningCircle]] instead. Hovered ships use [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCrewCircle]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCrewLine: The line connecting a selected ship to each of its crew members who are out in space. Shown only when the show space crew lines setting is enabled, except that crew with a distance warning always get [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningLine]] instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedScheduledNuggetCollectSprite: Icon drawn over each nugget that the currently selected ships are scheduled to collect. It animates in per [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledNuggetCollectTweenDuration]] and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledNuggetCollectTweenFromScale]] after the collect order is issued.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledNuggetCollectTweenDuration: Seconds over which the scheduled collect icon and its resource pickup line fade and scale in after a collect order is issued. Applies to both [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedScheduledNuggetCollectSprite]] and [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeScheduledNuggetCollectSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledNuggetCollectTweenFromScale: Starting scale multiplier of the scheduled collect icon when a collect order is issued. The icon grows or shrinks from this value to 1 over [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledNuggetCollectTweenDuration]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningCircle: Replaces [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCrewCircle]] or [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeShipCrewCircle]] around an off-ship crew member whose distance warning is active, meaning they are straying too far from their ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipCrewWarningLine: The line drawn from a ship to an off-ship crew member whose distance warning is active. Unlike [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedShipCrewLine]] it is drawn regardless of the show space crew lines setting.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusShipCircle: The circle drawn around ships under the mouse cursor while the camera focus cursor mode is active, previewing which ship a click would focus the camera on. Not drawn when the camera is already focused on or inside that ship. Drawn at 1.5 times the ship's bounding radius.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeAttackCommandCircle: Circle drawn around a hovered enemy ship to preview that a right click would issue an attack command, tinted with the player's enemy color. Also drawn around each target while dragging an attack command.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeFollowCommandCircle: Circle drawn around a hovered friendly or neutral ship to preview that a right click would issue a follow command, tinted with the player's own color. Also drawn around target ships while dragging a move command with collision avoidance active on them.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeFtlCommandCircle: Circle drawn around an FTL gate under the mouse cursor when the selected ships have FTL drives, previewing a jump command through the gate. It replaces the default attack or follow context circle.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeSalvageCommandCircle: Circle drawn around a hovered derelict or enemy ship that the selected ships can salvage, previewing a salvage command. Its color is tinted by the target's allegiance.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageCommandCircle: Circle drawn around a hovered ship that a selected ship currently has a salvage command against, previewing that clicking would cancel that command.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusModeCursor: Mouse cursor shown while the camera focus input mode is held, where clicking a ship focuses the camera on it. Also used by mission GUI elements that focus the camera on a mission target.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.PartModeCursor: Mouse cursor shown while the part selection input mode is active, where clicks select individual parts inside ships instead of whole ships.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCollectCursor: Mouse cursor shown while hovering a nugget that the selected ships can collect. Swapped for [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCantCollectCursor]] when collection is not possible.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCantCollectCursor: Mouse cursor shown while hovering a nugget that none of the selected ships can collect, matching the [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeNuggetCantCollectSprite]] overlay.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageCollectCursor: Mouse cursor shown when a click would cancel salvage or collection, while hovering a ship, part, or nugget with a pending salvage or pickup and while holding the cancel modifier in salvage collection mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCollectionSelectionOutlineSprite: The four edges of the drag-select rectangle while box-selecting parts and nuggets to salvage in salvage collection mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCollectionSelectionFillSprite: The interior of the drag-select rectangle while box-selecting parts and nuggets to salvage in salvage collection mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageCollectionSelectionOutlineS: The four edges of the drag-select rectangle when the cancel-salvage input is held in salvage collection mode, replacing [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCollectionSelectionOutlineSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageCollectionSelectionFillSpri: The interior of the drag-select rectangle when the cancel-salvage input is held in salvage collection mode, replacing [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCollectionSelectionFillSprite]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetLocationOverlaySprite: Icon drawn over every visible nugget while the salvage collection tool is active, marking where collectable resources are. Nuggets of resource types banned on all selected ships are skipped.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.BlueprintTransitionDuration: Seconds for blueprint, redprint, and prohibited-zone overlays to fade fully in or out when their visibility toggles.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.BackgroundTransitionDuration: Seconds for the space background dim to fade in when a toolbox opens and out when it closes. The dim fades toward [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.BackgroundDimOpacity]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.BackgroundDimOpacity: Opacity, as a 0..1 fraction, to which the space background is dimmed while a build, paint, crew, or resources toolbox is open. The dim fades in and out over [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.BackgroundTransitionDuration]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.GridTransitionDuration: Seconds for the build grid drawn over the selected ship to fade fully in or out when it is shown or hidden.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipGridLiveModeColor: Line color of the build grid drawn over the selected ship's maximum build area when viewing the live ship. Blends toward [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipGridBlueprintModeColor]] as the blueprint view fades in.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipGridBlueprintModeColor: Line color of the build grid over the selected ship while the full blueprint view is shown. The grid blends from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipGridLiveModeColor]] as the blueprint fades in.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipDarkenColor: Color factor that unselected ships fade toward when the background is dimmed by an open toolbox, and that ships fade toward as the blueprint view fades in. White means no darkening.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SelectedPartNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around each selected part, tinted with the player or neutral faction color. Fades out as the build grid fades in.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativePartNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around parts inside the current selection rectangle that are not yet selected, tinted with the player or neutral faction color.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FocusPartNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around parts under the cursor while in focus mode with the camera focused inside the ship.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HealthBarBlockSprite: Sprite tiled horizontally across a part's health bar, one repetition per [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HealthBarHPPerBlock]] hit points, so the bar reads as discrete blocks. Tinted from green toward red as the part takes damage.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HealthBarHPPerBlock: Hit points represented by one block of [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.HealthBarBlockSprite]] in the health bar shown above a part. Vanilla uses 1000, so a 4000 HP part shows four blocks.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around each part that a selected ship's crew has been ordered to salvage. Appears with a shrink animation controlled by [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSliceShrinkDuration]] and fades out as salvaging progresses per [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageProgressFadeRange]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeScheduledSalvageNineSlice: Has no effect. The game requires and stores the sprite but no code ever reads it, so it is never rendered.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeSalvageNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around parts that would be salvaged, shown when hovering a salvageable part, around parts inside the salvage drag-select rectangle, and around the existing salvage targets of ships under the cursor.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageNineSlice: Nine-slice box drawn around parts whose salvage order would be canceled, shown when hovering a part being salvaged with the cancel input held and around such parts inside the cancel drag-select rectangle.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSliceShrinkDuration: Seconds after a salvage order is issued during which [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSlice]] fades in while shrinking from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSliceShrinkFromInflate]] down to fit the part exactly.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSliceShrinkFromInfla: Distance in tiles by which [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSlice]] starts inflated beyond the part's rectangle when a salvage order is issued, shrinking to 0 over [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSliceShrinkDuration]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageReticleSprite: Icon drawn centered on each part that a selected ship's crew has been ordered to salvage, alongside [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageNineSlice]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeScheduledSalvageReticleSprite: Icon drawn centered on the salvage targets of ships under the cursor, alongside [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.TentativeSalvageNineSlice]], previewing which parts those ships are set to salvage.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ScheduledSalvageProgressFadeRange: Range of the part's salvage effect intensity, a 0..1 value, over which the scheduled-salvage box and reticle fade out as crew salvage the part. With the vanilla `[0, 0.5]` the overlay is fully faded once intensity reaches 0.5.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCursor: Mouse cursor shown while the salvage collection tool is active and when hovering a ship or part that can be salvaged. Replaced by [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.CancelSalvageCollectCursor]] while the cancel modifier is held.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipSelectSound: Plays when the player selects one or more ships, whether by clicking, drag-selecting, recalling a control group, or clicking a ship logo in the FTL jump window.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipFocusSound: Plays when the camera locks focus onto a ship or group of ships, such as after a double-click. Distinct from [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.ShipSelectSound]], which covers plain selection.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.PartSelectSound: Plays when one or more parts are added to the current part selection, including selection via part control groups and the parts card.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.PartDeselectSound: Plays when parts are removed from the current part selection or the part selection is cleared.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.FtlReadySound: Plays in the FTL jump window at the moment every selected ship with a jump command finishes charging and becomes ready to jump. Fires only on the transition from not ready to ready while the jump button is active.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCollectSound: Plays when the player successfully orders crew to collect one or more resource nuggets, including multi-nugget collection via double-click.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.NuggetCollectCancelSound: Plays when the player cancels pending nugget collection jobs, either by clicking a nugget already being collected or by drag-selecting nuggets in cancel mode. In a cancel drag that also cancels part salvage, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCancelSound]] plays instead.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageCancelSound: Plays when the player cancels scheduled salvage on one or more parts, by clicking a part already marked for salvage or by drag-selecting in cancel mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageMineSound: Plays when the player issues salvage orders on ship parts, whether by clicking a part or by drag-selecting an area in salvage mode.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.GatherFloatingResourcesSound: Plays when a drag-selection in salvage mode issues collection orders for floating resource nuggets and no parts were marked for salvage in the same drag. If parts were also marked, [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules.SalvageMineSound]] plays instead.

Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.AudioSpeedIncreaseDuration: When the simulation clock speeds up, game audio ramps toward the new pitch over this duration. The change rate is the speed difference divided by this time. Paired with [[AudioSpeedDecreaseDuration]] for slowdowns.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.AudioSpeedDecreaseDuration: When the simulation clock slows down, game audio ramps toward the new pitch over this duration. The counterpart to [[AudioSpeedIncreaseDuration]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.PhysicsUpdatesPerSecond: Fixed physics tick rate of the whole simulation. The simulation root steps at an interval of `1 / PhysicsUpdatesPerSecond`, and many other per-second budgets (crew updates, job assignments, network timing) are divided down from this rate. Changing it rescales the core simulation timestep.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.CCDThresholdVelocity: Speed above which a physics body switches to continuous collision detection so fast movers do not tunnel through thin objects. Applied to crew bodies directly and to ship bodies scaled by the ship's uniform scale.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.SightCircleFadeDuration: Seconds a sight circle (a unit's vision area) takes to fade in when it appears and to fade back out when it disappears. Alpha lerps over this window from the circle's appear and disappear times.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.SightCircleSizeTweenSpeed: Rate at which a sight circle's rendered radius moves toward its true radius each frame. Higher values make the circle resize more quickly as vision range changes.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.StasisCellSize: Side length in world units of one cell in the stasis spatial grid. Object locations are floored into cells of this size to partition which stasis spawners are woken or slept. Related to [[StasisLiveRange]] and [[StasisPreloadRange]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.StasisLiveRange: Distance in world units from a root location (such as a player ship or camera focus) within which stasis spawners become live and spawn their contents. Spawners farther than this stay asleep. Compare [[StasisPreloadRange]], the larger radius at which content is prepared ahead of time.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.StasisPreloadRange: Distance in world units within which stasis spawners are preloaded, ahead of the smaller [[StasisLiveRange]] at which they go fully live. Measured against root locations and temporary preload points.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.StasisUpdateInterval: Simulation time between stasis manager update passes. Each interval the manager re-evaluates which spawners are in live or preload range and advances stasis spawner updates by this amount.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.StandardLightHeight: Z height fed into the light normal computed for flat objects that opt into standard lighting (bullets, crew, resource nuggets). A larger height flattens the normal toward straight down, making those sprites light more top-down and less from the world light's direction.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.ShipHideAlphaTweenDuration: Seconds over which a ship's rendered alpha tweens between fully visible and fully hidden when it is hidden or unhidden (for example under a fog overlay). The move rate is scaled by clock speed.
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.Network: Nested rules for the multiplayer networking logic, such as input tick rate and input delay bounds. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.NetworkRules]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.Grid: Nested rules for rendering the background reference grid to the camera, including line color and desired line density. See [[Cosmoteer.Backgrounds.GridRules]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.Camera: Nested rules for the in-simulation camera, covering zoom range, panning, follow behavior and screen shake. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.Cameras.CameraRules]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.SimGui: Nested rules for the in-game gameplay GUI and world overlays, such as ship label colors. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimGuiRules]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.GameSpeeds: The ordered list of selectable simulation speed presets, each pairing a clock multiplier with display names and transition sounds. The speed control bar steps through these entries. See [[Cosmoteer.Simulation.GameSpeed]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.DebugPointLightSprite: Sprite drawn at the mouse for the debug point-light tool, which places a movable test light to inspect normal-mapped lighting. Only used by the in-game debug tools, not during normal play. Paired with [[DebugPointLightHeight]].
Cosmoteer.Simulation.SimRules.DebugPointLightHeight: Z height of the debug point light placed by the debug tools, passed to the point-light shader constant. Debug-only, alongside [[DebugPointLightSprite]].

Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.IPa.T:: Defines a ship-local region relative to a part.

Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.T:: An IPartRelativeRegion describing a rectangular region.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.Area: The rectangle of cells the region covers, in un-rotated cells relative to the part. It is transformed by the part's placement, so it rotates and flips with the part. The distance factor for effects that use one falls off from the rectangle's bounding circle center to its radius.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.BlueprintMaterial: The material used to fill the region rectangle in the build view. Unset means the region draws nothing in the blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.T:: An IPartRelativeRegion describing a region within a distance from a rect.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.Distance: How far, in tiles, from the part's edge a cell can be and still count as inside the region. The distance is measured from the part rect chosen by [[Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.PartRelativeEdgeDistance.RectType]], and the falloff factor runs from 0 at the edge to 1 at this distance.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.RectType: Which part footprint the edge distance is measured from. `Physical` uses the part's `PhysicalRect` when it declares one, `Normal` uses the full tile footprint.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.BlueprintMaterial: The material used to fill each in-range cell in the build view. Unset means the region draws nothing in the blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.T:: An IPartRelativeRegion describing a region within a certain grid distance.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.GridDistance: How many cells out from the part's physical footprint the region reaches, counted in whole grid steps. A cell touching the part is distance 1.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.AllowDiagonals: Whether a diagonal step counts as one cell of distance rather than two. When false the distance is Manhattan (horizontal plus vertical steps), when true it is Chebyshev (the larger of the two), so the region becomes a square instead of a diamond.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.BlueprintMaterial: The material used to fill each in-range cell in the build view. Unset means the region draws nothing in the blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.T:: An IPartRelativeRegion describing a circular region.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.Radius: The radius, in tiles, of the circular region measured from the part's center. A cell counts as inside when its center is within this distance, and the falloff factor runs from 0 at the center to 1 at the radius.
Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.Par.BlueprintRenderer: The circle renderer that draws the region outline in the build view, its thickness set to [[Cosmoteer.Source.Ships.Parts.Regions.PartRelativeRadius.Radius]]. Unset means the region draws nothing in the blueprint.

Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.T:: Sets a particle's initial location to the center of a part.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.LocationOut: The data that stores the particle's location.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.CenterType: Which type of part rect's center to use.

Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.T:: Sets a particle's initial scale to the size of a part.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScaleOut: The data that stores the particle's scale.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.ScaleFactor: The factor by which the intensity will be scaled.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.Inflate: The amount by which the part's rect is inflated.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.RectType: Which type of part rect to use.
Cosmoteer.Source.Simulation.MediaEffects.UseMinDimension: Whether the smaller of the two part dimensions should be used instead of the larger.

Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.T:: Adds a new status value onto the existing one with diminishing returns, so stacking fire onto an already burning tile adds less each time.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.ValueRange: The range to use for lerp and inverse-lerp operations.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.InverseValueExponent: The exponent applied to (1-normalizedBaseValue) before multiplication with the normalizedOtherValue.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.ReducePositiveValues: Whether positive input values should be reduced by the inverse value.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.ReduceNegativeValues: Whether negative input values should be reduced by the inverse value.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.NormalizedAdd.MinFactor: Floor on the inverse-value reduction. The reduction factor is `pow(1 - normalizedBase * (1 - MinFactor), InverseValueExponent)`, so when the base value sits at the top of ValueRange the other value's contribution is retained at MinFactor rather than dropping to zero. Defaults to 0, allowing full reduction.

Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.SimpleValueCo.T:: Merges the old and new status values with one arithmetic `Mode`, either `Max`, `Min`, `Add` or `Multiply`. It can also be written as just the mode name on its own.
Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.SimpleValueCo.Mode: The arithmetic used to combine two values into one. `Max` and `Min` take the larger or smaller, `Add` sums them, and `Multiply` takes their product.

Cosmoteer.ValueCombination.ValueCombiner.T:: How a freshly applied status value merges with the value the target already carries. A modder writes one of its concrete types, or just a combine mode name.

Halfling.Audio.FilterParams.T:: Contains parameters that specify how a sound instance or audio group should be filtered.
Halfling.Audio.FilterParams.FilterType: Specifies whether and how frequencies of audio will be filtered.
Halfling.Audio.FilterParams.Frequency: Specifies the cutoff frequency used by the filter.
Halfling.Audio.FilterParams.QFactor: Specifies the Q factor used by the filter. This value controls how rapidly the audio will be reduced. It is not used by the LowPass or HighPass filters.

Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.T:: Exposes methods for retrieving the Sound, volume, and speed properties of a sound effect.
Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.Sounds: A collection Sound objects from which a random Sound will be selected to play.
Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.VolumeRange: The range of volumes in which the actual volume of the sound effect will be chosen at random.
Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.SpeedRange: The range of speeds in which the actual speed of the sound effect will be chosen at random.
Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.StartRange: The range of possible start times in which the actual start time will be chosen at random.
Halfling.Audio.ISoundEffect.Filter: The filter, if any, to apply to the sound.

Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.Seed: A value used to hash the input coordinates. A PerlinNoise1D with the same seed value (and other properties) will always produce the same output for a given input coordinate.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.GridSize: The size in units of the underlying Perlin noise grid.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.Repeat: If not zero, the outputted values will repeat every this number of coordinate steps.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.Octaves: The number of iterations used to generate the final noise value.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.Persistence: The factor by which the strength each further octave iteration will be multiplied.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.OutputExponent: The power to which output values are raised before they are scaled, shifted, and clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.OutputScale: The factor by which output values are multiplied after they are exponentiated and before they are shifted and clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.OutputShift: The amount added to the output values after they are exponentiated and scaled and before they are clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise1D.ClampOutput: The range to which output values will be clamped after they are exponentiated, scaled, and shifted.

Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.Seed: A value used to hash the input coordinates. A PerlinNoise2D with the same seed value (and other properties) will always produce the same output for a given input coordinate.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.GridSize: The size in units of the underlying Perlin noise grid.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.Repeat: If not zero, the outputted values will repeat every this number of coordinate steps for the corresponding dimension.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.Octaves: The number of iterations used to generate the final noise value.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.Persistence: The factor by which the strength each further octave iteration will be multiplied.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.OutputExponent: The power to which output values are raised before they are scaled, shifted, and clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.OutputScale: The factor by which output values are multiplied after they are exponentiated and before they are shifted and clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.OutputShift: The amount added to the output values after they are exponentiated and scaled and before they are clamped.
Halfling.Generation.PerlinNoise2D.ClampOutput: The range to which output values will be clamped after they are exponentiated, scaled, and shifted.

Halfling.Geometry.Arc.0: The near edge direction when the arc is written in list form `[nearEdge, width]`, as in the vanilla `Arc = [22.5d, 360d]` in command_attack.rules.
Halfling.Geometry.Arc.1: The angular width in the list form `[nearEdge, width]`.
Halfling.Geometry.Arc.T:: Stores the direction and width of an arc in 2-dimensional space.
Halfling.Geometry.Arc.NearEdge: The direction of the arc's starting edge. 0 points along +X and positive angles rotate toward +Y, which is clockwise on screen since the Y axis points downward.
